title: Taste is OK, Nothing Special
text: Because of all the great reviews, I had high hopes for this coffee. Upon opening the package, which by the way, was not vacuumed sealed even though a valve is in the bag, I noticed immediately that the grind was somewhat coarser than I expected. The color was good, sort of on par with Peete's Major Dickinson, but again just standard looking coffee. I made the coffee using a Melitta filter in the pour-over method which produced a drinkable cup of coffee which was on par with what you would find in a better diner. if you're a coffee aficionado or a coffee snob, this is not the coffee for you. And it's not the coffee for me. I quickly came to realize that, for a few dollars more I could buy a much better Bean or pre-ground coffee. Again, this is not to say that it's a bad cup of coffee, it's just an average cup of joe.

title: Essential ingredient for Chinese cuisine.
text:
This is what you are looking for if you are trying to recreate your favorite American Chinese takeout dishes. Also essential for many Thai dishes. Pad Than and Drunken Noodles! The list goes on and on for what this is used in, but broadly, very common ingredient in East and Southeast Asian cuisine. I am still learning myself, but it is essential and if you are where I was a few year ago and confused about what to get, then you are on the right track.

Use sparingly. A good start for something like Chicken with Broccoli is a cup of good chicken stock, a few tablespoons of this stuff, a little black soy sauce, and some thinner soy sauce to adjust salt. That's just a base for something to get you going if this is what you are looking to do.

Update:
I had a chance to compare the milk chocolate received in this package with ones my mother-in-law brought (bought at a national chain store). The ones I received in the order were darker in color, had a tougher shell and were not nearly as creamy inside. They were also much sweeter than the grocery store ones. The good news it that when I contacted Amazon immediately after opening the box and reporting my issues, they were very prompt in issuing a refund. Thank you Amazon for that element of good customer service.

title: Not spoiled, not awful--just not good. I won't buy this again!
text:
I bought this ricotta to make a couple of special treats: lasagna and stuffed shells. I have made these dishes a few times a year for many years and basically never have had a failure. Not this time. Both the lasagna and the eggplant Parmesan which I made with it were quite disappointing. The ricotta was flavorless and its texture was not the smoothness I expected. It was grainy coming out of the tub, but I thought, optimistically, that the baking process would put that right. It didn't. And the flavor? Rather than the mild, slightly nutty cheesiness I expected, it had almost an anti-flavor, leeching out the flavor of the other cheeses, the herbs, and the sauce. In our house leftover eggplant has never stayed around to be thrown out. Our eggplant lovers are close to fanatical. But what came out of the kitchen this time produced no enthusiasm and no desire for leftovers, most of which did indeed age out and get thrown away.
I have given this product two stars because it wasn't awful. It just--wasn't good. Not at all.
Not buying this one again. The price was attractive, but yep, we got what we paid for.

title: The powdered cheese sauce for this lentil rotini is chemical tasting
text:
There are four 11 ounce boxes and at the current price of $18.99 it comes to $4.75 per box which makes this extremely expensive. I personally would not pay that high price. Nevertheless, the price is up to how much the purchaser wants to pay.

Each box supposedly makes three servings but I feel it is more like two servings or even one serving as it is easy to overeat this. In fact, I turned this into two servings for me.

All I had to do is dump the rotini into two quarts of boiling water and cook for nine minutes. At first, I thought I got the wrong pasta because the raw noodles are red in color; however, it changes to white after it is cooked and looks like what is on the front of the box. Once the pasta is cooked and drained, I stirred in two tablespoons of butter, a half cup of milk, and the two seasoning packets. I then blended it and let it stand for two minutes before serving.

The last picture shows it plated and what is equivalent to one serving which is 450 calories, with 840 mg of sodium, and 30% saturated fat. The second photo shows the nutrition facts and ingredients list.

Overall, this is very expensive and I do not care at all for the flavor of the powdered cheese sauce. I would not buy this blend.

title: Tea, Please!: An Ito En Oi Ocha Unsweetened Green Tea Review
text:
Ito En Oi Ocha unsweetened green tea is made in Japan from purified water, 100% Japanese grown tea leaves, and ascorbic acid. This recipe results in a crisp and clean green tea served from a can.

The oddest thing about this drink is the warning on the can indicating it cannot be microwaved. That made me laugh and wonder who made an attempt to make the warning necessary.

If you like the flavor of green tea and need the convenience of a canned beverage, the Ito En Oi Ocha unsweetened green tea is a great tasting option to consider.

► PROS:
0 calories
Crisp, clean flavor
No artificial flavors, colors, or preservatives

► CONS:
The can is not microwavable

There’s also a fatal flaw with the dough. As instructed, I always let this pizza brand thaw for 15 to 30 minutes, otherwise the dough will stay raw in the middle. title: Sustainable Gum: Glee versus Simply Gum (both get 5/5 green stars).
text:
I bought variety packs of both Glee and Simply Gum to stock up and figure out which is my favorite. Yes, perhaps I have too much time on my hands ;) First, here’s my overall summary of the two for quality and price:

Glee Gum (3/5 gold stars):
• Glee Gum is tasty when you first chew it, but the flavor disappears quickly.
• The texture of Glee is also a bit dense and rigid for my liking – especially after a minute when the sugar is gone.
• Overall, Glee is economical and fine for people who don’t want to chew for very long.
• The flavors are all quite good - my favorites are tangerine and mixed berry. The peppermint is fine too.

Simply Gum (5/5 gold stars):
• Simply Gum took me a little while to get used to (my initial rating was 4/5).
• Now that I’ve adjusted to the softer, stickier texture, it’s my favorite gum and I find it hard to go back to regular gum.
• The flavors are all appealing to me – subtle but interesting – like the “real food” equivalent to regular gum.
• The flavor is integrated into the gum (rather than just in a coating) so it’s not overpowering and also lasts quite a long time.
• It seems more expensive, but with about 20 pieces per box (one piece at a time is sufficient) it’s actually not bad. A serving of Glee is 2 pieces, so a box of Glee gum contains 8 servings.
• The packaging design is beautiful and functional. It makes me a little happy whenever I use it.

I’d much rather chew either of these gums than go back to a major brand like Trident, etc. This is partly because I prefer Glee and Simply Gum and partly because they are more sustainable. Most leading brands of gum list a “gum base” on their ingredients. This gum base can include polyethylene (plastic), polyvinyl acetate (wood glue), paraffin wax, fats (hydrogenated vegetable oil) and talc. Glee and Simply Gum are both made from natural tree gum (chicle), harvested by tapping Manilkara trees that grow in the rainforests of Central America. I think that both of them are far superior to the big commercial brands of gum and both deserve 5/5 green stars for social and environmental impact. Here is some more info on these two brands:

• Harvesting natural gum from trees can help protect rainforests and support a sustainable practice that has gone on for thousands of years.
• Natural gum also has a lower carbon footprint than petroleum-derived ingredients that are used to make the “gum base” of commercial gum.
• Natural gums (Glee and Simply gum) are also biodegradable – reducing biological hazards (and ugly pavements).
• In Simply Gum, most of the ingredients (sugar, glycerin, rice flour) are organically grown.
• In Glee Gum, the sugar is not organic but it is Fairtrade certified.
• Both Glee and Simply Gum are packaged in recyclable cardboard boxes – no plastic.
• Both companies and woman-owned and based in the US.
• Glee Gum works with people with disabilities and supports Trees for the Future and scholarships at the Maya University in Mexico.
More info on sustainable chewing gum is available on my site – greenstarsproject. Interested in writing green star reviews? If so, contact me!

title: Thin, tasteless and boring
text:
Thin, tasteless and boring. That pretty much describes this sauce (and the pink vodka sauce by this brand). It's so bad I'm shocked that Mario Batali put is name on this!

The Pros: The sauce has a nice color and a nice texture with some chunkier peices in it.

The Cons: The sauce is thin in between the chunkier bits so it doesn't cling well to the pasta. You can see bits of garlic, onion and (minimal) spices in the sauce but the flavor has been completely boiled out of it to point that all that's left the bitter part of the garlic and the acidic part of the tomatoes. To say the flavors don't blend is an understatement. There are any flavors to blend in the first place.

I would be embarrassed to be Mario Batali right now. Obviously he has traded his expertise and food quality for the money making machine.

I severed this to good friends and they all agreed it wasn't a good sauce and that they would prefer not to have it again. I'll be writing a similar review for the pink vodka sauce which was also a disappointment.

title: IS SAID TO FIGHT BACTERIA & VIRUSES!!!
text:
Love the flavor of this honey.. Heard it has many benefits too!!!!
One health article stated, "Manuka is perfect to treat and shorten the length and severity of a sore throat,’ ...‘It fights bacteria and viruses while also boosting the immune system. It’s incredibly soothing; take a spoonful by itself or with warm water and lemon juice (not boiling)"..
Another article also stated, "Its antiviral and antibacterial properties can reduce inflammation and attack the bacteria that cause pain.
Not only does manuka honey attack harmful bacteria, it also coats the inner lining of the throat for a soothing effect.
A recent study in patients undergoing chemotherapy treatment for head and neck cancer observed the effects of consuming manuka honey on Streptococcus mutans, a type of bacteria responsible for sore throats.
Interestingly, researchers found a significant decrease in Streptococcus mutans after they consumed manuka honey.. manuka honey decreases harmful oral bacteria that causes mucositis, a common side effect of radiation and chemotherapy. Mucositis results in inflammation and painful ulcerations of the mucous membranes lining the esophagus and digestive tract... various types of honey have been touted as natural cough suppressants...
One study found honey was as effective as a common cough suppressant.
Although manuka honey wasn’t used in this study, it’s likely to be just as effective at suppressing coughs."

title: Aromatherapy!
text: I am new to bean roasting, this is my second bean sample.  The previous was a Mexican bean, I found it ok but weak.  I bought this one based on the reviews.  I agree, this is some amazing coffee.  It's also good cold, and reheated in a microwave. This batch was 3/4 cup, roasted in cast iron, stirred constantly with a wire whip.  Heat setting was slightly cooler than for a steak.  Time was 13 minutes in preheated pan.  Almost every bean popped loudly, given enough time.  If it seemed too hot, I backed the heat down to the six o'clock setting for a minute.  Once it cooled off, heat was turned back up.  There was some chaff, most of which was completely charred by the end.  When done it was sifted in a metal colander, and I fanned it by hand to speed cooling.  I would rate this as a medium-dark roast.  It has now been 24 hours, the aroma is the best I've ever smelled, bar none.  A fascinating, complex, indescribable sensation.  It seems to change and draw you in.  The beans are beginning to ooze oil droplets.  I am going to give it 2 more days, then grind half of it.  The remaining sample will age a full 6 days.  Am looking forward to the results.  Get this coffee, you already have all the gear needed to fire it up like a pro.

title: I found this to be a superior brand of ghee
text:
I have had a few health challenges in the past, and when I found out some of them were due to being lactose intolerant I shed a few tears because I have always loved dairy products. This has led me to not only change what I eat, it has forced me to get creative in the kitchen. There are many things I used to cook or sauté in butter, but I now find I really prefer using ghee. It has a much higher smoke point and this is important for me since I am not the greatest at making sure my stove burner is set at the exact right temperature, and I get distracted easily. I have burned more things than I care to admit when I used to use butter, and then the burnt butter taste wasn't so good. Now, with the ghee, it has improved my cooking, hah. Anyway, it is more forgiving.

I find this brand of ghee to be awesome. I only buy grass fed beef for my family, and so this product is the only type of ghee I would consider using. "Certified organic" is an actual government guarantee, so it is the most valuable statement for consumers. Bottom line is that not only is this brand healthy and safe to use, it tastes good. It doesn't add any funny or overpowering flavor to the food, and it solves the high temperature burnt oil taste in my recipes. I have used other brands that are also good, with one exception, but I find this to be the best I have tried so far.

title: Flavored coffee.... is it for you?
text:
I made a dumb mistake when selecting this item for review... I thought it was "regular" coffee, and not a blueberry-cinnamon variety. My bad!

However, even though I'm not a fan of flavored coffees per se, they do wind up in my house from time to time, and what I like to do is mix the beans in with one of my other regular coffee beans, arabica usually, as being able to control the amount of extra flavoring is a lot of good ol' fashioned coffee fun.

So that's what I did with these beans, and I found a mixture that allows me to get a hint of those fruity, toasty blueberry cinnamon flavors but not be overwhelmed by them.

I look forward to trying other types of beans/coffees from this company. I appreciate their retro design, thoughtful packaging and fresh product. Although it's a touch on the pricey side, it's worth trying. What an exciting thing it is for the coffee lover to have access to all these small brands you wouldn't normally find in the grocery store.

title: Mild taste of corn, plump and fresh
text:
Wandering through every kind of unpopped popcorn Amazon sells, but my search may have ended with Bob's - I was already impressed with their fresh tasting medium grind cornmeal.

Bob's white popcorn is outstandingly tender with a subtle taste of sweet corn; the yellow I found to be more robust and a bit more chewy - almost like mushroom corn. Fat winged puffs with an actual taste of corn.

I like both; think the yellow is the most all-around as it would stand up to syrups and making popcorn balls. Just depends on what mood I am in. Popped well in my easy-going stove-top method of peanut oil in old saucepan, heat until 2 kernels pop, add 1/2 cup popcorn, shake, remove from heat when popping slows. Add melted butter or margarine and white cheddar and garlic parmesan popcorn seasoning.

The folks at Bob's seem to know and care about their grains! Only nit is I wish they would not use plastic bags, as these are hard to find a place to recycle. Recyclable bottles would be better.

title: Happy Cashew Junkie
text:
Salt plus nuts. Add beer. Happy.

Make those nuts cashews. Ecstatic.

That's where the Planters Cashew Halves and Pieces come into play. These are roasted, not raw, with just enough salt.

You get the idea. I like cashews a lot. When I was a kid, they were too expensive for us to have regularly, so we lived on peanuts. While I love peanuts, cashews are better.

About these in particular, they are halves and pieces. Come on, if you are just munching them, do you care if they are whole? I don't. The only time I do is if I'm serving them at a party. If it's just me, I'm good.

I buy the smaller container for the freshness factor. Once opened, they start losing their magic. I like having some ready mid-day when I need a boost but don't want to ruin dinner, or when I've fired up the grill.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

Of course, the package had to travel through the Puerto Rican heat to be delivered, so I guess that can be expected. And the cans weren't delivered in a fridge pack as shown. They were just lose in a random box.
And the biggest positive? Caffeine Free Diet Dr. Pepper in a land without such an option - a little taste of home!
Due to the cost, I won't be ordering very often, but when homesickness strikes, you can bet I will be ordering again!

title: Organic Tao Chai
text:
First off, let me say this is truly a lovely blend of chai ingredients. I was a little hesitant at first about buying this brand of chai because of the mixed reviews. But I honestly have no regrets. The only thing I'd say about this is that the packaging should let its tea drinkers know that the tea needs to be brewed and not steeped. Not all loose leaf tea needs to be brewed and not all needs to be steeped. So placing this up would be helpful. I'm glad I read the reviews or I may had made the honest mistake at first and steeped my loose leaf chai rather than brew it. Apart from that I saw some complaints about the tea being bitter that I would like to address. Black tea depending on the type from English breakfast to earl grey ect, can be quiet bitter. Especially if you drink it black. The intensity of the bitterness at times depends on the manufacturer or maker if you will. Some chai brands are smooth, mild and creamy while others may be bold, bitter and a tad sweet. Chai over the years has been tweaked differently depending on the brand. But one thing to keeps in mind is that black tea to some degree always has a bitterness to it. Whether it's light, or heavy on the pallet. Also something to consider with loose leaf is the water to loose leaf ratio before you brew. If you're not certain experiment with it or simply look up a recipe for better measurement. Because depending on how much loose leaf you add to your water your tea may end more on the bitter side since the ingredients are more on the intense some what bitter side for this brand. The chai ingredients for this brand do contain spices. But if you're looking for that certain spicy kick you get from other brands you may not receive it with this one because there is no black pepper and the ginger isn't immensely strong. The flavors for this brand are very well balanced so they compliment one another. So feel free to add black pepper in if you'd like. If black pepper is currently not a house hold item for you, try a little smidge of cayenne it goes a long way and should give you the spicy kick you desire.
One more thing, in the event that you accidentally brew your tea too bitter balance it out with a milk of your choice and add the sweeter you fancy.
Happy Sipping!

title: Just try it.
text:
“Normal” American soy sauce is an entirely chemical mix. The hydrolyzed soy is soy mash left over from oil production and it’s soaked in hydrochloric acid and then the acid is neutralized with lye, leaving water, protein, and salt. Corn syrup is usually the sugar of choice, and it too is a chemical product. Caramel color is no longer just brown burned sugar, but is a chemical product made with a combination of sulfuric, sulfurous, phosphoric, acetic, and citric acids; ammonium, sodium, potassium, and calcium hydroxides; and ammonium, sodium, and potassium carbonate, bicarbonate, phosphate, sulfate, and bisulfite salts. It has been accused of being carcinogenic. Then there’s a preservative which is itself a chemical additive. Put all this together and feed it to your family!

This product here is brewed with real soy and real wheat and has a trace of alcohol, presumably from the fermentation stage. It also has a very different taste (no judgement of better or worse here), even if it keeps the salt burn of the chemical variety while increasing the savory umami levels a good deal. Get a bottle and just try it. This one’s bottle is clear but keep it in the dark and keep it very cold otherwise the lack of chemical preservatives may have you tossing it out long before you use it all up.

title: Did The Flavor Change With The Can Redesign?
text:
I’ve been enjoying Zoa over every other energy drink for the last couple years. Of all the flavors of all of the energy drinks, “tropical fruit” or “fruit punch” flavors are my favorite. Zoa’s Tropical Punch went to the top of my list at first taste. I like that they keep their drinks natural and low-to-no sugar.

I do have some issues with their recent can redesign, though. Having that bright red and black can was easy to spot while shopping. In my mind, red equals tropical/fruit punch. Changing to a blue can design for this flavor doesn’t make sense to me as far as having a customer quickly and easily identify flavor.

More importantly, the first batch I ordered post-red cans tastes like a different formula. Has it changed? No clue. But now I’m always going to wonder if the flavor was intentionally changed along with the can.

I’ll still order these, but probably less frequently than before. Rockstar Fruit Punch has a better chance of being ordered as my primary energy drink of choice now.

text: I made the mistake of going to the grocery store when I was hungry so I picked this bit of convenience food. This Hawaiian Luau sauce was on sale at Aldi for less then two dollars; at that price I thought I could set aside my hatred of pre-made sauces and give this a whirl. I put 4 lbs of pork butt in the slow cooker with this (almost twice the suggested amount) and it still permeated all the meat with it's distinctly un-Hawaiian flavor. I took the meat out and shredded it without mixing in the remaining sauce, and found the artificial taste of pineapple almost overwhelming. I dipped a bit of pork into the remaining sauce, shook off the excess, and found it to be cloyingly sweet. My significant other and I were able to get some down with a healthy dose of steak sauce and some Ciabatta bread, so in the end it didn't destroy the meats utility as food, merely hampered it.

title: Why the need to wash?
text: We ordered the salsify because we like it better than the white asparagus, the type usually consumed in Europe. Salsify does not have the somewhat bitter taste typically associated with asparagus. We prepare the salsify (cook or reheat) in a white sauce, using a package of "asparagus" cream sauce mix and meat balls. The salsify is then eaten together with potatoes of choice. In Europe we bought the salsify packed in a glass jar. Here it came in a can. The can's label had a precautionary note advising to wash the salsify before using it. That threw us for a loss because in Europe there was no such precaution and we actually used the water the salsify was packed in as liquid to prepare the sauce or gravy in which the salsify was served. Because of the washing requirement, we believed that the water in the can also was not fit for consumption. Hence we discarded the water as well. We used a can of cream asparagus soup mix and meatballs. The result was 99 percent of what we were used to. The four-star rating instead of five stars is because we had to wash the salsify and discard the water.

(Another reviewer commented on the name of the coffee, suggesting that it is awkward. Negro just means "black" in Spanish, though, and this is a very dark coffee. The name fits.)

It's a very bold flavor, and they are not kidding it has a high caffeine content. A cup of this gives me a much more noticeable jolt than usual.

I've ground it for use in an espresso machine, and also used it as regular drip coffee. I like it both ways, though I think I prefer it in my espresso machine. There's no indication on the package of when it was roasted.

Unlike some other reviewers, I do detect a hint of bitterness in the aftertaste of this coffee. I don't mind that, but it does seem to be there. Other than that the flavor is rich, and ... can I say "roasty"? ... with just a hint of dark chocolate. It's good coffee.

text:
I bought these because xylitol mints came highly recommended by Ellie Phillips DDS in her new book [[ASIN:B009LPLMRU Kiss Your Dentist Goodbye: A Do-It-Yourself Mouth Care System for Healthy, Clean Gums and Teeth]] The key ingredient in her mouth care system is xylitol (a natural product sometimes known as wood sugar) which she says "could be the ultimate magic bullet for tooth decay, working with nature to change the chemistry and biology of a dentally dangerous mouth to bring it back to health in less than a year." She recommends "ending every meal, snack or drink with about one gram of xylitol: either coated on chewing gum, as a breath mint or eaten directly off a spoon."

Since I'm not a gum chewer I decided to opt for mints and have so far tried two Spry flavors, "Berryblast" and "Power Peppermint." I like both, not just for the taste but even more for their calorie counts of just 1.2 per piece. As an added bonus, because they're sweeter tasting, I find nibbling a few pieces of "Berryblast" a great way to end meals on a sweet note without caving in to my lifelong cravings to end meals with dessert. The Peppermint flavor's plus is that it makes one's mouth feel really fresh and clean.

I also recommend Dr. Phillips's book.

Update 1/17/13: Since posting the above, I've also tried the "Lemonburst" flavor and find that it makes a VERY nice accompaniment to a cup of tea.

title: If you have a sensitive stomach like me, you might not want to buy this.
text: Bought these because why not, I wanted to try them and they are less expensive than the vegan mock-meats, and gluten free which is great for celiacs like me. Also, not many ingredients, so I guess minimally processed. First time I made these I made "beef" and broccoli and it came out good. The taste takes a little getting used to but that's about par for the course with these type of things. I ate the whole batch of food, and then proceeded to be sick for two days. So I didn't use them again for a while because I wasn't sure if they made me sick or if it was something else and I didn't want to find out. I also ate A LOT of them, so was wondering if that was just "too much to handle." Last night, I felt brave and rehydrated a 1/2 cup to have with dinner. Now, versus before, I'm on a strict cutting diet and have essentially been eating the same things over and over, so now I know it wasn't something else, and I also cut way back on the portion. They still are making me feel not quite right. I don't know what it could be, I thoroughly rehydrated them, even threw them in with my peas and brought to a boil before I drained it. I'm not dying over here, but I'm puffy and gassy (TMI, I know, deal with it) and it has to be from this stuff. My stomach is also singing the song of its people. I had wanted to try other derivations of this type of product from this company and others but I don't know now. I don't think I'll throw it away. I think I'll probably take them to my father's house and only eat it there. I'm still just puzzled by it because I eat tons of soy based stuff and it doesn't bother me. I seriously have a reaction similar to a mild gluten exposure for about 1-2 days after eating this.

title: Don't Push the Fruit Chamber Too Deep in the Bottle
text: This bottle is really nice! It's a hardy plastic that doesn't produce condensation with cold beverages & survived a hard drop on the floor. My only problem with it is the fruit chamber/top area of the bottle. The first time I wanted to use it with fruit I placed the chamber in the bottle but I couldn't remember if it's only placed near the rim of the bottle (it is) or closer to the part where the plastic widens inside. I thought the latter and wow, was that a mistake! The fruit chamber fell inside the bottle & I couldn't get it out. I tried pulling it out with rat-tooth forceps and my fingers with no success. Finally, an hour later, my dad somehow screwed the top of the chamber off with his tools & got both pieces out. It may seem straight forward to not push the chamber as deep as I did but I wanted to warn others just in case someone might think similarly to me. title: I am thoroughly impressed!
text:
I recently tried the Oatsome Barista Organic Oat Creamer and I must say, I am thoroughly impressed! As someone who is dairy-free, finding a creamer that froths and steams like cow's milk has been a challenge. But this oat beverage has definitely exceeded my expectations.

First off, I love that it's made with organic oats and doesn't contain any dairy or nuts. It's also free from any artificial ingredients, which makes me feel good about what I'm putting into my body. The taste is really smooth and subtle, without any overpowering oat flavor.

What I love most about this oat creamer is its versatility. I've used it in my coffee and lattes, and it blends really well. It also froths beautifully, which is great for making latte art. I've also used it in my baking and cooking recipes, and it's worked really well as a substitute for cow's milk.

Overall, I highly recommend the Oatsome Barista Organic Oat Creamer for anyone who is dairy-free, vegan, or simply looking for a healthier alternative to traditional creamers. It's delicious, versatile, and a great addition to any pantry.

title: We all taste things differently.
text: It's tricky to try to tell you whether this syrup tastes "good" or not because we all taste the same thing differently. To some of you, the chemical element of the syrup will dominate, to others the sweet element will be all you notice. I have a unique way of tasting things because I have no sense of smell. So I was able to taste the salty aspect of the salted caramel, as well as the sweet. Sometimes the chemical ingredient will affect me in a physical way - a tingling or sharpness somewhere on my tongue, or as a "fume" sensation in my inhalation. Crazy, huh? So all I can say about this syrup is that I tasted caramel, I tasted salt, the chemical aspect was almost non-existent (as opposed to other calorie-free syrups I have tried) and I love it in my coffee and shakes, and drizzled over fruit and oatmeal, and other items too numerous to mention. Yes, it is very sweet, which it is supposed to be, so use accordingly.

title: A bit of smoke is a good thing... update, this is now my go-to
text:
[[VIDEOID:27e91395a8af2f20bd615bc23442b49e]] EDIT:
After going through a few dishes, I can say that Liokareas glaze is now my go-to. I've grown to like that slight smoky flavor, enough to kick Nonna off the shelf. I wish Amazon would include this as a subscribe and save item because I am going to be going through a lot of it.
END OF EDIT

So 100% of my lifetime experience with Balsamic Glaze is with the brand they carry at my grocery store. I love it, and go through a ton of it, mostly putting it on salads but sometimes vegetables too. So when I had a chance to try this Liokareas glaze, I thought it would be a good idea to expand my horizons.

I have to say that I was pretty happy with it. It has the same core Balsamic Glaze texture I'm used to, but there is just a hint of smokiness there that makes a bit of a difference - and smokiness is usually a good thing.

The big question is this: when I make it through this bottle, will I switch back to the old reliable or will I stick with the newcomer Liokareas? Right now I'm inclined to think I'm going to make the switch, this stuff is pretty good!

I bought this sweet tea liquid to put in my 72-hour kit. I'd never actually used it so I decided that I should prior to adding it to my 72-hour kit. I'm glad that I decided to try it. I quickly realized that there's no way to know how much to use, or how much is a serving. I added it to my bottle of water. It looked like tea, but it didn't taste like tea. It tasted like water. I squeezed more of it into my bottle. It still didn't taste like tea, only lightly sweetened water. So I added more of it. It looked like strong tea, or weak coffee. It tasted like weak tea. Since I'd already used 1/4 of the bottle I decided to give up and drink it.

The bottle says that it's 24 servings. Huh!!!! I seriously don't see how I'll get 10 servings. I don't know if any of the other flavors are as disappointing as the sweet tea. I definitely won't purchase it again.

text:
I want to start by saying I did review the Organic Assam as well. While more expensive, this one (Assam Exotic) is worth the extra money if you want the best tasting tea.

SO, I recently had a insatiable craving for milk tea, developed from the days I bought canned milk tea from Kirin (Japanese company, I think). It comes and goes and Kirin doesn't produce the same milk tea they used to anymore, so it's hard to come by the kind I like unless I go to those dreadful bubble/boba tea places and pay top dollar. No thanks.

Looked into it, and found that it's easier to make than I thought! Assam tea for stronger/darker milk tea, so I went all in. The packaging for this is insane, in a good way. It's vacuum-sealed, air tight, and they provide a second bag to move the tea to after you open the vacuum-sealed bag. The taste? WONDERFUL. Worth it all the way. But if you want a more price-efficient option, the Organic Assam from Vahdam is also good. Not as good, but still good.

text:
Absolutely delicious, light, gluten-free, low calorie, inexpensive lunch! I am on a perpetual diet, and nothing has made me happier than this soup. I like ramen soup, but the problem with regular Maruchan ramen is that it has msg and wheat (gluten) and also twice the sodium per packet and its preserved with TBHQ. All of which is bad for me. Also ramen is fried, these rice noodles are steam cooked, not fried. And I like the fact that they put two flavor packets, one is the soup mix and the other is the spicy oil, so if your kids don't like hot spicy, they don't have to add the spicy oil packet. Great, right?

The price works out best if you get the box of 72 from Amazon. This package of 12 actually works out to be a little more expensive than the supermarket, but still worth it if your supermarket doesn't carry it.

title: Pleasantly surprised!
text:
I've been trying jerky in all it's forms on Amazon, mainly because I like it, but partly because I'm on a quest to find the good and the bad ones. They can be expensive so I don't want to see money wasted on bad jerky.
These were really good! You're getting two of each of the three flavors in this pack, and I will break down each one below.

Classic flavor. This one was the thickest jerky of been the two. It's neither sweet nor spicy in but has a soft dry texture and a distinct flavor I find it hard to describe, other than to tell you I could eat this all day. Loved this one.

Mustard. Bit let down by this one. I was expecting it to pop with the mustard and BBQ flavors but it just didn't. At most I felt a sort of tingling sensation on the sides of my tongue. It's honestly not bad, but I was expecting more.

Sesame and garlic spice. This is where you will find the action. It has a kick to it that just builds up and then explodes in your mouth with a spicy hot flavor. Best part is the heat doesn't overwhelm the flavors. Though I don't love super hot because I'm a big sissy, I found I could tolerate this one and even enjoy it.

It's really not the best jerky I've come across but considering you get six packs for $35 it has a good bit of value for money and it is absolutely worth trying.

title: Smells great, tastes decent, makes killer iced tea
text:
I’m a big jasmine green tea fan and LOVE my Rishi loose jasmine green tea, but it’s gone up a lot in price so I’ve been looking for decent, cheaper jasmine green teabags and given the reviews here I was hopeful this might be it. I was further encouraged when I opened the package and was hit immediately by a strong jasmine scent reminiscent of my excellent loose jasmine green. Unfortunately, in the all-important flavor area this tea falls a bit short. Despite the wonderful fragrance, very little jasmine flavor makes it into the actual tea so it tastes more like a mild green tea than a true jasmine green tea, but I will say this is still much better than most other bagged jasmine green teas I’ve tried and it’s organic, used bags without bad chemicals, and is environmentally conscious. So all this on balance this will be my new, cheaper daily drinker until I can find something better.

But another use for these teabags is in making really good, healthy, and cost-effective iced tea. Put 6 teabags into a glass pitcher and heat 6 cups of water to 180 degrees (a full boil will cook the green tea leaves and spoil the flavor. I highly recommend using filtered or bottled water in an electric kettle with temperature control (filtered/bottled water tastes MUCH better than tap water with delicate green tea and doesn’t leave sediment in the kettle). Pour the hot water over the teabags and let steep for 10-20 minutes depending on your desired strength and level of caffeine — most of the health benefits of green tea infuse fairly quickly into the hot water, and the longer it steeps the more caffeine you’ll get. Let the tea cool in the pitcher for about a half hour before putting it in the fridge unless your glass pitcher can survive going from hot to cold without cracking, and when it’s cold you’ll have delicious tasting, healthy, and zero-calorie iced tea you don’t even have to add anything to due to the jasmine flowers providing a nice yet subtle hint of flavor that makes it incredibly light and refreshing. I much prefer this to regular black iced tea, and you’re getting the superior health benefits of organic green tea. Try it. You’ll love it!

title: Flavorful with Romantic Aroma!
text:
Amaretto smells so wonderful. I poured about a 1/2 cup of the beans into a decorative cup and set in my office so that I can enjoy the pleasant scent.

The bag does not seem to state the weight or volume of beans. However, it does seem to be about 12 ounces ( I did not think to weigh it when I received it and have been drinking for about two months so too late to weigh it now!).

I use a Kruegg coffee maker and have brewed my cup both with only 1 tablespoon and with 2 tablespoons per 6-8 oz. Both ways taste delicious to me. The 2 tablespoon method does leave a stronger lingering coffee flavor in the mouth. It is not bitter, but it is strong/bold. Made with 1 tablespoon, the flavor is mild and goes down smoothly.

There is no way to express in words the delight of my nostrils while brewing this coffee. As with most, if not all coffees, the smell is so much more potent than the actual flavor. But the flavor is there, just not strong which means not overpowering. I usually drink my coffee with creamer and sugar, but this one I can actually drink black.

The comments on the bag state to store in an airtight, cool dark place and to use clean filtered water but not distilled. I do not know why it suggests to not use distilled. I have brewed it with both waters and do not really taste a difference.

Last note, the bag had a sticker on it stating that Best Used By date was approximately 3 months after I received it.

title: Ordered to wear, not as cake toper.

Thought perfect for my tiny one's second birthday as I have a crown (yes, I know) that she loves!!! But too large for her little head, but this looked to fit perfectly, and I think it will fit perfectly on her!
Substantial in weight but not cumbersome & has the inner circles for attachment to the head inside the crown & lovely in the scarlet rhinestones.

But? I was surprised that two (2) larger clear rhinestones had detached when opened? Shown in several pictures attached & although simplistic to glue back in? I was just taken by surprise that they separated before use.
As for use as a cake topper? I have no idea, not the intention personally. But as weighted as it is, I would be surprised if it would lay on regular icing well? Perhaps more of an on top of fondant success.
I think charming for my tiny one, as I know she will adore her crown, but did not put the five (5) stars as I would have had not the stones been detached from the beginning. Reason in four (4) stars.
I also plan on enforcing the others as little ones can be hard on headpieces & I know she would be distraught if others removed themselves & could not be located. Better safe than sorry about when it might happen! Other than that? Quite pleased and think the tiny one will be ecstatic!

title: Hooked on Honey Almond and Bob's Red Mill
text:
Before I begin, I should make it clear that I am not a fan of breakfast cereal -- or even breakfast in general. I don't care how much the nutritionists wail and gnash their teeth. Breakfast is not the most important meal of the day in my book. Give me coffee and kick me to my desk, please!

But for Bob's Red Mill Honey Almond Granola, I make an exception. I would eat this as a cereal seven days a week from now until Bob's Red Mill runs out of oats. It's not too sweet, not too crunchy, not loaded with ingredients I don't know or can't pronounce (or both), not too hippie, not too yuppie, not too sun-drenched fields of happiness commercials.

What's in it? Oats, honey, canola oil, almonds and vanilla. That's it. That's plenty.

How to serve it? That depends on your schedule. Out of the bag and into the right hand, on the run - that works if you're in a mad-dash hurry. Right-handed? Use your left hand to catch the granola. Ambidextrous but drive a stick shift? Use either hand. If, however, you prefer milk on your cereal instead, use a bowl. And a spoon. And wait until you've parked, please.

Not in a hurry? Pour a few ounces into a bowl, bury it in water and nuke for 2-3 minutes. Voila - almost-instant hot breakfast.

Need a snack? Grab a handful out of the bag.

Hate raisins like I do? No worries! There aren't any of those pesky little former-grape critters to pick out and destroy.

Love raisins? Add 'em in! They'll be right at home, whether you're serving your breakfast or lunch granola or snack hot or cold. Amazingly versatile product!

So Bob's Red Mill, employee-owned Oregon Nirvana, has moved yet another person closer to a healthier lifestyle. They're to be commended, not only for having some of the best granola on the planet, but for holding to the highest standards of product quality and customer service known to mankind. Yep, I'm a fan of both their granola and their corporate mindset.

title: Nostalgia achieved! First cookie order and will definitely repeat 😊
text:
I'm so glad to have found these! I'm an 80's kid from Hawaii, so we didn't have the variety growing up. The first time I ever had these was at my grandparents house and I loved it!

My grandma always had 3 kinds of cookies for my grandpa - Tru Blu sandwich cookies, Hydrox, and Vader's Dutch Shortbread.
Being kids, grandpa shared his Hydrox cookies - but we could have 2, and had to eat them at the table. Then there were Oreos and Hydrox became unavailable in Hawaii. Couldn't find them except for one time in the 2000's before they disappeared.

I've finally found them after all these years! So delicious and just like I remember. Same chocolate flavor and the cream filling doesn't make my tongue feel oily.

I will definitely be ordering these again. I hesitated because I wasn't sure about the cookies' state upon arrival, but they arrived intact and in their own box.

title: Took Forever To Review But It Was Worth It
text:
Disclosure: This was sent to me for free via the Vine program. I did not receive monetary compensation to write this review, just the product itself.

So I put in for the Jamaican Coffee Club in...June. Shortly after doing so, I had to put an embargo on drinking coffee. I figured it'd be a month at least but no, no, it was 3 months. So that puts us to September. September comes around and it's all coffee all the time mood so I busted out this to give it a try, only to realize that I didn't have a coffee grinder and this was whole bean coffee. I couldn't afford another coffee grinder so now I had to dig through my storage unit to find my hand-crank Hario Skerton just to do the review. After several sweaty days of digging, I finally found it. This week. MAN, my lead time on reviews is poor sometimes. I'm so sorry. Enough of me blathering, let's get into it.

Coffee arrives double wrapped up in a bubble mailer. The outer layer is a jute bag which gives it a nice touch of homespun-y charm but the inside is your standard coffee-protecting bag. I opened the bag to find gorgeously oily beans with a heady aroma. This was done SCA (Specialty Coffee Association) cupping style, with 8.25g of ground coffee (ground in a Hario Skerton set to a mid-grade grind) to 150mL of water (recipe doubled in this case) in an SCA approved cupping bowl with an SCA cupping spoon. Trust me, I planned for this one. It took awhile so I was doing it right. Infusion was done with just-off boiling water (208F) and let set for 3 minutes before the crust was broken and the coffee evaluated. The aroma of it was extremely decadent and the creaminess they talked about evident in the nose. It was sweet cream, chocolate, dark fruits like plum, and toasted cereal and nuts on the nose. Dipping the spoon in and giving it a hearty slurp (slurping encourages aeration of the coffee and also drives my roommate nuts so win-win after he ate my pad thai a few nights ago), the taste follows. It's rich and full bodied without any charcoal or off-gas notes. Baking chocolate and cream are big flavors on this one, making it almost like a choco-coffee milkshake at times. It has some acidity that balances the brew out but not too much to make you pucker. It says that this is a medium roast but I'd put it closer to a medium-full roast but without the scorch you get from darker roasts so it's...expertly roasted. All in all, a delicious cup of coffee.

Delicious cup of coffee? Yes. Affordable cup of coffee? No, not by a long-shot. 8 oz of beans is nearly a whopping $37, or $4.63 an ounce of coffee. So this IS a GREAT cup of coffee and would do well as a gift, I suppose. But this, for me, is a "once upon a Vine" kind of item: I'd only ever be able to afford this via the Vine program because it's just so far out of budget. But if you have a loved one that likes coffee, nay, LOVES coffee, this isn't a bad cup to pick up for them. Provided they have a grinder. Unlike me. Whoops.

title: Less caffeine than straight-coffee, confusing 4/3 measurement
text:
This Focus Mushroom Coffee is a blend of Instant Coffee, Reishi, Lion's Mane, Cordyceps, Chaga, Turkey Tail, and Maitake mushrooms, and Assam Black Tea. It's supposed to have a medium roast flavor. When I open it up, it has a decidedly "earthy" and slightly burnt aroma. Definitely a little funky and you can tell it's not just coffee.

The directions on the label for this instruct you to: "Simply add 4/3 tsp of FOCUS COFFEE (3g) to 6-8 oz hot water..." I'm not sure if they meant 3/4 tsp or 1 and 1/3 tsp and I'm not about to pull out my kitchen scale and actually measure out 3g of instant coffee... but either way, I can confirm that 1 heaping tsp per cup of water works fine! The instructions want you to use hot water, but I've blended it straight into cold water for instant iced coffee and it dissolves just fine with a brisk stirring.

It tastes a LOT better than it smells. Mostly just like medium-roast instant coffee, not too much of that earthy funk. Maybe a bit of a burnt-toast note.

The best thing about it, to me, is the low 30mg of caffeine per serving. I've been trying to cut back on caffeine to get my resting heart rate lower, and this gives me just enough caffeine for a little boost and my fitness tracker doesn't detect any increase in my heart rate from drinking it!

title: Tastes like regular peanut butter!
text:
This is amazing stuff- the protein to calorie ratio is amazing and the sugar levels are reasonable. Imagine eating peanut butter but only consuming 1/10th of the calories! This is essentially peanut butter that has been slow roasted for long enough that the fats are cooked off. The result is peanut butter that has really low calories and low fat compared to the normal stuff. It also has lower sugar levels compared to the regular jar stuff. You just have to add water to reach your desired consistency.

I find this stuff really tasty and love both the regular and chocolate flavors. Like one of the other reviewers suggested, I made PB&J sandwiches using Sara Lee Delightful oatmeal bread (40 calories per slice, as opposed to 120+ calories per slice for regular bread) and sugar free jam with fiber added. Hello high fiber, high protein, low calorie snack that keeps you full! I also like to make the chocolate PB2 a little more watery and add it to Fage 0% fat plain greek yogurt for an extra high protein, low sugar and low calorie snack. Watery PB2 also makes for a great dip to dip your banana or apple in. I use My Fitness Pal to track my macros, and this is really nice for adjusting my macros for days when I need more protein without a lot of calories. I still eat regular peanut butter for days when I do need the calories, but PB2 holds dear to my heart. For fitness fiends like me who track their macros, this is a godsend. For peanut butter lovers, this is also a godsend.

The prices on Amazon are comparable to the prices I see at my local King Soopers in Colorado, I don't think you can find them for much cheaper out in the wild (ahem, Walmart).

title: Horrible for your teeth or any dental work, avoid this candy!
text:
Pearson Candy Company, BIT O' HONEY, should at least put a disclaimer; if you had any dental work at all please be aware that it could, (and does) rip out, break and destroy your teeth as well as costly dental work you ever had. After chewing a couple pieces of Pearson Candy Company, BIT O' HONEY, It felt like I crunched a tiny rock, the combination of hard taffy and tiny slivers of almonds had broken my porcelain crown, as well as, the post and the small tooth inside. The candy had stuck to my dental work and yanked it loose, the almond felt like I bit into a tiny rock. I had to gently remove the candy off it without further trauma. MY crown was dangling like a hook on the ceiling. I wrote a paragraph to Pearson Candy Company to let them know what happened and that my crown wasn't even loose or decayed before eating their candy. My mouth on one side was swollen and I couldn't eat on one side for weeks. I had to get the tooth extracted and replaced with a costly dental implant or bridge, the bridge was less expensive, so I chose that.

They responded with a letter and return envelope to mail a claim form in, from what I believed was reimbursement or help to pay for that missing tooth. Pearson Candy Co. sent me a box of candy, which would have been nice, if I could chew. They asked for my personal information, dental records, dental insurance, and estimate of cost to fix broken tooth, I even added the box of candy and piece I had to un-grip off my tooth in a Ziploc bag. When I sent it all in, they immediately denied my claim. The insurance company they use, said that because there was no foreign object in the candy, (which I never said there was or wasn't), that I don't have a case. I told the insurance company for Pearson that I sent them the piece and asked if they examined it, they said they hadn't received it, then 18 min. later when I called back, they told me they did examine it and found nothing wrong with it, obviously they lied about that. Then I told them I'm 48 yrs. old take care of my teeth, have all of them, except for the one their candy irreparably broke. They told me the tooth was decayed, I told them it was not. My dentist said," there was no decay and it was a perfectly good porcelain crown, that Bit o' Honey was a strong piece of candy to rip off your crown, break the post and tooth, the way it did. Also, to never eat that kind of candy if you have had any dental work at all.

I wasn't looking for a big payout or expensive dental implants, which could be $6-9,000. I would have just settled if they at least offered to pay half of what a less expensive bridge would cost to replace that one tooth. They reached out to me to send in all the information and denied my case immediately, falsifying on their end, that my tooth had decay or that it didn't have a foreign object in the candy, which they never checked in the 18 min. time that they said they didn't receive it and then said they had it tested, by who? An independent examiner, I think not. It's a .99 cent candy, that is costing me $1,000's. I will be sharing this info. on every site I can find to get the word out, as well as, repeat this story to my 1,000's of customers as a warning, as a bartender for Navy, my reach is far.

title: Excellent, fresh and grassy olive oil
text: This is a very good premium olive oil with a beautiful, light, and grassy flavor. In a lovely glass bottle with a pourer top, the oil is a deep yellow-green in color. The flavor is mild and ethereal for such a high-quality and ultra-fresh oil; it's intensely grassy and vegetal — one of the "greenest" in taste I've ever had — with only a light touch of peppery aftertaste that connotes great freshness. There is very little bitterness to the aftertaste at all; it's flavorful without any of the harsh or zingy notes that sometimes come with ultra-fresh oil. As a result, it seems like a great choice for topping or finishing — particularly with the easy-pour top that will allow it to be drizzled lightly over things just before serving. For dressings, bread dipping, or as a finishing oil on pasta, it's a wonderful, premium choice. I would definitely not cook with it, since it'd be a total waste of the oil's brilliant fresh flavor. This is a great oil and it's highly recommended for the right use.

title: Yes, it Matters
text:
I love coffee. Love the flavor, love experimenting with different coffees, and even collect various types of coffee makers. They go in and out of rotation because each one brings its own unique nuance to the bean.
So naturally, I jumped at the chance to try this product.
Does it make a difference?
Yes, it certainly does, but it's not going to matter much if you are the sort of person that just drinks coffee, as opposed to someone that savors it.
If you make your coffee with spring water because you don't like the taste of filtered water when making coffee, this product is definitely going to be something you'll want to try.
Naturally, I tested this by making two cups, one with and one without, having my spouse switch the cups around, so I could blind taste the two.
The difference is a whisper, not a shout. It's a richer and smoother flavor, and after finishing it, it seemed to be even easier on my stomach, although that could be simply a result of any one of a number of other factors.

For the serious coffee drinker, or as a thoughtful gift for someone that loves coffee.

Update: I continue to be impressed by this product. It's amazing what a tiny packet of minerals can do to give your coffee a lift. Having tried it in numerous coffee makers, including pour-over, espresso machine, French press, Keurig, and even a Vietnamese phin, it makes every cup more enjoyable. Doesn't matter if you enjoy a black espresso or a milk and sugar donut shop coffee, it's more delicious.

title: Great pasta
text:
A friend of ours, who also teaches at a cooking school and has a line of cookbooks, recently took a "cooking tour" of Italy and this was one of the many items she brought back. She made us an excellent traditional Italian meal that incorporated this pasta and we loved it. I'm sure the amazing flavors of the dish had more to do with the ingredients and her hard work than the pasta, but the pasta added a flare of something different. It was very memorable and as they say, you eat with your eyes first. We have since started purchasing Bucatini and was excited to find this brand on Amazon (also surprised to see other brands). We stayed with this brand. The diameter is about 1/8 of an inch, 12 inches or so long and the center is hollow. It's not hollow like Macaroni. The hole is much smaller, almost a pin hole. It's a very hearty pasta. Doesn't take much longer to cook (15-20 min?). Kids tend to get a kick out of it as well.

FYI....I found that some of the pictures shown on Amazon from Cav. Giuseppe Cocco don't match the actual item. So don't buy the item based on the photo or the label you see in the photo. I almost made that mistake. In this case, make sure the item description says "Bucatini", otherwise you might end up with a different pasta.

title: I am really enjoying this.
text:
I experimented with several different combinations of rum, wine, and sweetener. I tried black rum, gold rum, spiced rum, and white rum. I tried Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Pinot Noir. For sweetener I tried, honey, date syrup and agave.

They were all good (except for the first two batches which had too much wood taste). However, the combination I liked the best is as pictured, Captain Morgan Parrot Bay rum, White Zinfandel wine, and a light agave for sweetness. I found the agave dissolved much easier than using honey.

I use equal parts rum and wine and around four ounces of agave. In the half-gallon Don Ramón bottle the liquid required and the yield are right about 1 liter. I usually let it age for at least a week before transferring it to another bottle.

title: Blackcurrant seems quite good for my use
text:
I bought the blackcurrant variety for rather an offbeat use. I’m fond of Kir, which is white wine (or Champagne or similar sparkling wine) flavored with creme de cassis: blackcurrant liqueur. I’m trying to cut down on sugar, though. A teaspoon of this (5ml or so) to a 750ml bottle of wine, artificial sweetener to taste (might not need much), is a pretty good low-sugar version of Kir. Not as good, of course, but drinkable. To me, anyway.

The flavor seems about right, it’s a lot cheaper than creme de cassis though it might seem a bit expensive, and I’ll probably buy more. If I still brewed beer, and this flavor is typical for this product, I’d probably buy a lot of the flavors for flavoring my brews.

title: not bad at all but there are better lower priced ways to do kalua pig imo
text: I have made kalua pork in slow cooker and instant pot many times and prefer to use my $ to buy the red salt, some black and some green bamboo salt, and the much less expensive  Mrs. Wright's mesquite liquid smoke, (sometimes add a drop or 2 of hickory-but I want to try the applewood also) and toss in 1-2 washed whole in their peels very ripe bananas with just a small slit in the peel on one side of them remove and throw away when done cooking before pulling the pork. A part of my family is 2nd generation HA and say my version here on the mainland is very close to the luau pork in HA. It has been many years since I was on the islands so I wasn't sure until I tried it on the family when they were here. This liquid smoke is ok, and many sites advocate it as THE thing to use, but we like the flavor from the above combination better, and per pot full of pork, it is less costly too. Still, if you like kalua pork, try both ways and see for yourself which you prefer.  Both are American products- Mrs. Wright's liquid smoke was created in 1895 in KC, Missouri to help preserve pork and other meats because smoke-infused liquid does have some anti-microbacterial properties, and brining or topically applying liquid smoke to meat can extend its shelf life.

title: This is a tasty, large variety in a great little cooler
text: So my wife and I have two different "takes" on jerky - she is far more adventurous when it comes to what animals are included, and the heat. But when I had a chance to grab this Buffalo Bills 18-Piece Hot & Spicy Lovers Jerky 6-Pack Gift Cooler I thought I'd be getting it for her - I mean, the "where" part wasn't that daring, but the "hot" part made me nervous. The package arrived earlier today and we have already had two types - a Hot Venison and Black Pepper Beef jerky and both are delicious! Okay, so we started with things we thought I would be okay with and I was right... Not only did I find them very flavorful, but the "hot" was not overwhelming or bad for me - I handled it and thought it was just right on both. So... have NOT tried any of the others, but I will have bites - as I always start out - though I have every confidence my wife will love them if they continue to be anything like these have been. So backtracking... the kit comes with the cooler - a good size for a few cans of something or lunch when further used. We'll keep it around as it seems good enough to toss stuff into when we don't want to take our regular, large coolers, or as an add on. Inside you're/we're a little surprised by how much jerky comes in the kit. We both felt like the portions are right on with normal bags of jerky we have seen or gotten before. Check the ingredients for your needs - there is a good amount of salt, but most jerky is that way. We both felt like the venison was a "normal" amount of "tough," while the black pepper was a bit tougher. But again, we are both really pleasantly surprised by how tasty this stuff is - I mean it is filled with flavor. title: From the looks this is a healthy snack with minimal processed ingredients, delicious if you like whole foods
text:
Purchased these bars for the first time and received them this weekend. I really like kind of sticky consistency and the plain simple packaging. When I say Plain and simple packaging I mean the front of the bar tells us exactly what is in it. If you are one of the many people who are increasingly health conscious I would suggest these bars.

What these bars are not though is a super sugary candy bar masquerading as a nutritional supplement. The bar has a solid feel to it, which has the consistency of things that are made with figs, (because this is) it is a bit sticky and has a nice amount of chunks from the nuts in it. You can definitely taste the blueberries but that flavor is that of real blueberries not artificial sugar loaded ones.

All in all I really like these bars because I don't have to feel guilty about eating the artificial sweeteners or too much sugar.

A couple things to note about the macros:

9 grams of fat
110 milligrams of Sodium
23 grams of Carbs
15 grams of that is Sugar
4 grams of Dietary Fiber
12 grams of Protein

title: OH MAN!
text:
Ok, here it is... BEST COFFEE I HAVE EVER BREWED AT HOME HANDS DOWN!! There you go! Seriously, I love dark coffee, dark beer, dark.. well nevermind the rest, but you get it. This coffee (as others have stated) is glossy, oily and dark. Smells good looks good and then you taste it!
First the grind... if you are not grinding at home before you brew, you don't love coffee... sorry that's the truth. You may think you do, but you don't. And if you are not using a burr grinder, you are missing all of what your coffee has to offer. Ok sorry about the soapbox... When you grind this coffee, you notice something lacking that I have noticed with a lot of other coffee beans... the chaff. Little brown flecks that end up in the grind that is not coffee. Well there is little to none with these beans which in my book gets an A++
Secondly, the taste... I have never had a smoother cup of coffee. I would say anywhere not just at home. This truly is a remarkable cup of coffee to be had. I have yet to try it in a French press, but I use a drip brewer as my everyday maker so I am going to get on that and let you know. Dark brew, smooth to the palate, goes down very nicely.
Highly recommend this if you like dark coffee...
This is now become my coffee of choice... the hunt is over... I have found it... Try it for yourself, if you don't like it, send it to me!

title: Not the real deal - I don't think I'm even going to make anymore
text:
I mistakenly interpreted "No artificial flavors, no artificial sweeteners, colors from natural sources" to mean this was somehow authentic Horchata. It is not. Horchata is primarily a rice drink with sugar and cinnamon. This is not that, going by the ingredients. Note that ingredients have to be listed in order based on the amount used, from most to least.

"Colors from Natural Sources" is Titanium Dioxide (for color). Titanium, like copper, iron, dog feces, and plague, is natural. Titanium dioxide is the rusted form of titanium. So this is a natural source, but probably not the one you were guessing (either rice or milk.) Many would consider this a chemical.

"No artificial flavors" must be true because the main flavor ingredient is "natural flavor". What might that be? We are just left to wonder. The main ingredient, but far, is sugar, which is OK. This is a sweet drink. Then Titanium Dioxide, the milk blend, the silcon dioxide (sand!), ....... keeps going and going and, middle of the fourth line "rice flour". So there are 9 other things, including guar gum, that are more prevalent that the traditional main ingredient in horchata.

"No artificial sweeteners" because we all love "steviol glycosides". To be fair, it is a natural sweetener, but it gives the drink a chemical taste. Yuck!

All said - if this tasted halfway decent I'd give it three or four stars, but it very hard to get right. It is so sweet that if you water it down to make it tolerable, there is no flavor but sweetness. One can smell some cinnamon and maybe the "Natural Flavor" but it is just a sweet flowery drink that's kind of gross and not the horchata we know.

title: Versatile, Delicious, Fresh, Quality Tahini!!! Recipes Below!!!!
text: This is great tahini. Not too bitter. I use this to make a simple dressing....1/2 cup of fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp sea salt, 1 cup of this tahini, 3 cloves minced garlic (I use the jar type in water it's more mild), and 1/2 cup of water...blend together and adjust the thickness of the dressing if you want to use as a dip or a salad dressing less or more water respectively. This will keep for about 2 weeks in the fridge. Great with falafel (eggplant based with chickpea), Jerusalem salad, or even to dip warm, crusty bread in. I also use this to make a fresh hummus in which you want customize with extra lemon, kalamata olives, chitpotle peppers or whatever you prefer. I use 1 can of chickpeas, half the can of the liquid from the chickpeas (put the rest aside for later), 1/4 cup of this tahini, 1 tbls of jarred minced garlic in water, 1 tsp sea salt, 1/2 tsp cracked black pepper, 1 tbls fresh lemon juice, 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil and blend till smooth, adjusting with the leftover rest of the liquid from the chickpea can. Top with a sprinkle of dried parsley, paprika, and a drizzle of olive oil. This recipe is a bug hit in our condo building!

title: I'm Very Happy With Them
text:
I'm very happy with them. There is a good mix of types. No one of them predominates. They are indeed salty, but it's not oppressive, and if you send me a wet bag of something, it had better be salty enough to avoid biohazards. I feel no inclination to rinse them for regular snacking, but might for some dishes. They are slightly oily, maybe more so than most branded jars of olives. Would probably put an oil slick on your martini, although I don't think you'd be ordering these for that purpose.

I broke the bag down into quart Mason jars and refrigerated them. No reason that they won't keep as well as any other open jars. (If you're buying this size bag, I suspect olives don't last long at your place, anyway.) The price easily beats the local grocery store olive bar bulk price. This is the way olives for the open olive bar come packed, anyway.

I've seen people complain about springs of herbs in other types of "country" olives. They are not obvious in this pack. They say there are herbs, and the flavor suggests there are, but they are well ground and integrated.

UPDATE; I am on my second bag, and it is exactly identical to the first, so points for consistency. Still very good.

UPDATE: On my fifth or sixth bag, and exactly the same. Very good quality and price.

Even worse, the texture is waxy and because they are so flat the non-pareil ratio is very high so any creaminess you could get out of this experience is destroyed by millions of little Pebbles rolling around in your mouth. The mint is weak and unexceptional, the colors aren't even as pretty as they once were. I would be totally fine with this if it meant that they were probably less toxic but who's to say? For $28 I expected a much higher quality of candy in original packaging not this bulk 2 lb bag of distinctly lackluster mints. Certainly does not even resemble my childhood favorite Easter candy.

The only reason I'm giving MM 4 stars instead of 5 - is because they took a LONG time to get me my cookies. They sent me an email saying they shipped my cookies when in fact, they hadn't. title: Not the best in my opinion.
text:
This coffee alternative is not my favorite. It has a funny aftertaste like burnt bread. But if you are a black coffee addict and like the taste of old black joe, this is probably your best bet. I myself have never cared for the taste of unsweetened, uncreamed coffee anymore than I prefer unsweetened cocoa. To me, it's not good coffee unless it tastes sweet and creamy. I realize that this is not what most coffee hounds prefer, but I also know that a lot of us like cream and sugar in some degree. Another problem with this otherwise excellent blend of roasted grain and herbs, is that it soaks up a lot of water and tends to clog paper filters, not allowing all of the hot water to brew through to the cup. It swells up quite a bit more than coffee, and tends to overwhelm paper filters.

One of the best alternatives to coffee, but not the best I've tried.

title: Maybe it's a cilantro thing, or, mebbe you ain't got 'nuff Moxie!
text:
I'mma love me some ginger beer, and not that fake SUPER HOTTEST EVAH carp! Here, I'll target myself so you can tell if you might like Maine Root ginger beer. I find Bundaberg surprisingly underwhelming: too sweet, insufficient fizz. Reed's Strongest is acceptable. Fentiman's is delicious (which made my disdain for Fentiman's Pink quite a surprise). Gosling's? Can't remember last time I had some. Most root beers (but not all birch beers) are too sticky sweet. Oh, and ginger ale? A joke.

Outside of ginger beer: Fentiman's Curiosity Cola is curiously fascinating. I have a nose for juniper, uh, botanicals (or even the odd Rīgas Melnais balzams) and other strong flavors (I'm a square-foot Islay leaseholder, know what I mean? Anyone?). I like cilantro and I *love* Moxie.

So, with that in mind, does Maine Root smell a bit like dirt? Yer darn tootin' it does! And why? 'Cause that's what *ginger* smells like, that's why! Where do you think ROOTS come from? Hmm?

So, I praise Maine Root for being the real thang. And if the likes/dislikes above are in your bailiwick, then maybe this made-me-sneeze ginger-binger is for you, too. But if you hate cilantro, Moxie, and cats, then just steer clear, buddy--and skip the Maine Root, too.

title: Bad Kisses
text:
Introduction: I am a Prime member, and I made some recent Amazon purchases for a friend, for products they needed to do an Appreciation Luncheon for volunteers in their church. The volunteers work really hard, and invest their own money and time, to serve meals to the families of deceased persons in their church. All seemed to have gone well for the luncheon, so it was viewed as a great success, at the time. Now, that it is over, a very embarrassing and sad element has been discovered. My friend who put the luncheon on, called and shared some bad news with me about the products I had acquired on Amazon, for the luncheon. Being a reviewer, and user of reviews, I see that I too overlooked warnings by previous people who had bought from this supplier. I would normally have caught the negative replies and have taken heed, but was in a hurry. The old saying "Hast makes waste", is so true. It caught up to us here.. And, so, I ask my friend to write up her review so that I could add it to the negative reviews shared by others. Below is her email note to me, to share with other would-be purchasers:

Recently purchased 4 pound bags of chocolate candy kisses. I was putting them into a white Organza bag for favors that were given out to a large group of ladies for their volunteer work at our church that was held on Nov. 13th this year. I had several of the favor bags left over and for the first time today, I decided to treat myself to some delicious chocolate but unfortunately discovered that all of them that I unwrapped and ate were grainy and had an unpleasant texture and taste. VERY DISAPPOINTED. While I understand that chocolate can last for a year, it definitely needs to be stored in a cool dry environment. While it did not smell bad, I felt that due to incorrect temperature change, it caused the sugar to crystallized and was stale. In my case, I am unable to send them back as I explained that they were given out to over 90 ladies last week.

Once again, very very disappointed in the quality of the product and a warning to others that they need to understand how chocolate can go bad if not stored properly even though the expiration date is still good.

title: An authentic experience
text: As I unsealed the nitrogen flushed package, closed my eyes, and took my first whiff of those polished white grains, I was instantly transported to a world of samurai, shogun, and fair noblewomen transported by palanquin. I found myself mounted on a mighty steed, leading my men in a pitched battle against the neighboring clan. It came down to single combat between me and my rival daimyo. Our katana clashed furiously as our fight raged up and down the hills around Kumamoto. Finally, my sword came crashing down on his, cleaving it in two. He wrote a quick death poem and drew his wakizashi, prepared to commit seppuku and counting on me to deliver the coupe de grace. Rather than taking his head, though, I took his hand in friendship, an equal in a remarkable combat experience. I offered him a steaming bowl of Tamaki Gold rice and as I raised my hashi to my mouth to enjoy those perfectly cooked grains, I opened my eyes. My kitchen was a mess. Five stars.

title: Large bag, small seeds -- good for various recipes
text:
I've used these sesame seeds to top baked pizza crust as well as process to make tahini (which ultimately makes hummus.) These are untoasted and hulled so typically have a light taste. The seeds baked just fine on top of the pizza for a little crunch, while the small size of the seeds meant that the food processor had to work harder to make a creamy tahini (and I cheated by added a little olive oil to macerate easier.) Toasting in the oven or quickly on a frying them might give you a bit more flavor, but otherwise, no big taste surprises here if you're used to the sesame taste.

These are imported specifically from mediterranean Turkey (but are produced in either India or Paraguay), a place where foods like hummus are commonly made, so no surprise they have a good quality source for sesame seeds. The seeds are smaller than the average American consumer may be used to (that are typically produced domestically or in Mexico.)

Prices can vary a lot by vendor, and whether you want toasted, unhulled, or organic (of which these are not.) In any case, this larger resealable bag (which does a good job of keeping the seeds fresh) will be a better deal than the small packages sold in most grocery stores. Plan for some interesting cooking and baking!

title: Having celiac disease makes my food options pretty limited. Ever since I was diagnosed early last ...
text: I'm a college student that works full-time. Having celiac disease makes my food options pretty limited. Ever since I was diagnosed early last year and went gluten-free, I never really found the time to plan out my meals and ensure I was getting enough carbs to make it through the day. I ended up dropping to 95lbs (I'm 5' 7") because I'd slip into only eating one measly meal a day for weeks at a time. For awhile I survived on almost nothing but potatoes, cheese, and meat. I have tried many different mixes and all of my efforts to regain "bread" into my meals were a complete waste of time and money... Until I tried King Arthur's GF mix. I got it, followed the gluten-free bread recipe from their website, and TO MY AMAZEMENT, it freaking worked without a hitch! The texture was a bit off on my first try, but I finally made something that was edible. Suddenly I'm eating sandwiches at work, sandwiches at home, biscuits for breakfast! Tonight is pizza. I'm now at a more healthy weight of 115lbs. Having this stuff is life changing for someone without a lot of free time to experiment or make my own mix. I just wish it was available at my local grocery store.

title: Nobody Wants to Try My Nuts
text:
I bought the Wild version and had them shipped to my work, which came sooner than originally expected. I opened the bag and let the air out before smelling the bag. You could get a hint of something spicy, but it mostly just smells like peanuts. I threw one into my mouth and started to chew, very little heat up front, but as others have mentioned, the heat comes after swallowing. Definitely spicy, it hits the back of your throat pretty hard and stays there awhile. I popped another after a minute or two and it was equally spicy.

For what they are, they taste really good. I think most foods like this are just hot for the sake of being hot with little to no thought given to flavor. While you chew, you actually enjoy the flavor for a good few seconds until the heat kicks in. I decided to throw 7 at once into my mouth and again, I wasn't feeling anything until I finished eating them and then the heat hit really hard and lasted a good 15 minutes. They're not unbearable, but they do pack a punch. I'm tempted to try the Death Nut challenge, just to see how hot things can really get.

Still waiting for my co-workers to try one, but they don't seem too interested...
