title: Tasty
text:
I have purchased these olives before, and I enjoy them. There’s like three or four different types of olives in the mix, so different textures should be expected. I haven’t ever had any that I would describe as mushy. Some are softer than others. They’re so good. Since they are soaked in a salt brine, they are salty!

I take enough out of the jar to fill a pint size Mason jar about half way full. I use a slotted spoon so the brine stays in the container. I cover the olives in the Mason jar with cold water and soak them overnight in the refrigerator to leach some of the salt out of the olives. If they are still too salty for me, I drain off the water, fill it with cold water and let it sit for a few more hours or overnight in the refrigerator again. Afterwards, I drain the water and add in enough brine from the container to cover the olives. Sometimes I add a lemon slice and a smashed garlic clove. I store it in the refrigerator. I like doing it this way because I eat a lot of olives and want to minimize my salt intake. Reusing the brine adds some salt back, but the olives are not salty like when taken straight from the brine.

My favorite snack is a few olives, black walnuts and havarti cheese.

text:
First of all, I liked the flavor of this. I felt that the basil was at the right level and the other seasonings were on point. You don't even need to salt this. It is very tasty as it is. I was also very pleased with the protein and the ingredients list. I love rice, mind you, but it's nice to get something more out of the experience. This was also simple to prepare, and maybe that is where the texture goes amiss.

I followed the directions on the package precisely and the result was on the soupy side and a bit "gummy". It seemed more starchy than rice does. I felt like it could have used some rinsing and soaking before being cooked to wash off any external starches which contributed to the texture issues (as is the case with actual rice), but I don't know if that is the way this works. I would try soaking it next time, but I'm afraid of turning it to mush. I think a little less water than the instructions suggest might not be a bad idea, but it's really hard to know what will happen given that this is an unusual type of "rice." So, while I loved the flavor and ease of preparation, I was less of a fan of the texture and am unsure how it can be improved (or if).

title: I don't know if coconut oil can do all the amazing things people claim
text:
I was a little skeptical about all the rave reviews. I still am; I mean, I don't know if coconut oil can do all the amazing things people claim.
(Hair growth? Blood pressure improvement?)
But after using it for a few weeks I DO like this product. Added to my coffee in the morning is my way of taking it as a dietary supplement.
It took me a few days to get over the oily consistency: it was like a coconut oil slick floating on my coffee, but it doesnt taste bad so I've
kept it up. I admit I feel more energetic taking this. I'm planning to continue and see how it goes long term.
As a deodorant, it doesn't really work for me. I can't use it and go about my day in the summer; I still smell. So back to Secret.
I used to bake some blueberry muffins in place of vegetable oil and the muffins were delicious. I will keep using it to bake as well.

title: EXCELLENT!  The taste that was missing!
text:
First, let me say that I love my popcorn. I really love the taste of movie theater popcorn.
I have tried a bunch of toppings to get the "taste", but this stuff is the best!
Here is what I use:
Whirly pop - popper
[[ASIN:B00004SU35 Wabash Valley Farms 25008 Whirley-Pop Stovetop Popcorn Popper]]
Great Northern pop corn, 4 oz. portion paks:
[[ASIN:B000PDY3P0 Great Northern Popcorn, 4-Ounce Portion Packs (Pack of 24)]]
This stuff is great...more pricey than doing it yourself, but worth it, for no hassle.

Just the combination above, works fantastic. I felt it was missing, just that "extra" flavor.
I first used topping oil...ok, but not great.
Then I tried Whirl buttery flavor cooking oil. This stuff is good, almost there.
Then I bought the Odell's. Wow! What a difference! Sure it's expensive, but worth it. You don't need much.
The tubs come in a 3 pak, pretty small, but sealed in the tub, so no leaking. You don't need to refrigerate it, even after opening.
The popcorn is a little more salty with this topping, so keep that in mind in your usage.

Good stuff!

title: Yummy rice noodles
text:
I got these to make the Vietnamese soup Pho with.

Pros:
- Yummy thin rice noodle
- Takes only a few minutes to cook in boiling water
- Denser than the see through rice noodle so good with stir fries or even gluten free Italian dishes

Cons:
- I think all rice noodles come this way but not sure...There are 4 servings in 1 package and the noodles are so wrapped together that you have to make a mess pulling apart the portion you will use. My dog loves this as he munches up all the little noodles bit that break apart to the floor. To make this less annoying...
1)Put a large tupperware dish in your sink that will fit the remaining dry noodles and the pot you will cook them in next to your sink
2)Pull the whole clump of noodles out of the package over the sink and place in dish
3)Tear out the portion you want and place it in your pot then cook as usual

This greatly cuts down the mess of noodles all over the counter, floor, stove top. My pup isn't quite as happy with the results but I am :)

title: Sun Crystals work well in Baking
text: I am not a fan of any sugar substitutes.  I have tried using Splenda and other substitutes in the past but have always been disappointed by the aftertaste.  After all the hype of Stevia I was excited that I had a chance to try the Sun Crystals.  I love to bake and decided to use the Sun Crystals in my low fat banana bread recipe that doesn't include much sugar.  I followed the measurement / substitution guidelines and my banana bread turned out beautifully!  It cooked even and browned on the top perfectly.  I had a nice warm slice of the bread and instantly could taste that something was off.  I gave my husband a piece without informing him of my sugar substitute and he asked if I used a different recipe.  I was extremely disappointed by the aftertaste of the Sun Crystals.  We tried the bread after it cooled but could still taste the difference.  We ended up not eating the rest of the bread.  I am giving this 3 stars because it worked well and baked nicely I just don't prefer the aftertaste of the Stevia.

title: 4/5 from a meat eater, only real downside is the price comparison.
text:
This is one of the better fake meat products I've tried, for certain. If someone gave some to me without telling me it was fake meat, and asked what I was eating, my guess would definitely be "some kind of sausage". I wouldn't say they're amazing; when cooked, I'd say they're around the mark of what I'd consider low-mid quality Italian sausage. Considering they're vegan though, it's straight-up amazing how close they've gotten with the texture, taste, etc. Not 100%, but damned close.

The only real issue now is the same issue with basically all fake meat products; the price comparison. At $5-$6 for a 9 0z bag, that's very steep. You can get two 14 0z kielbasas from Aldi for less than that, or like 2-3 pounds of tofu. If Gardein could somehow drop the price drastically, make it like $1.99 a bag without dropping the quality, then these would be an instant staple. I'd be ordering them every week and stocking my freezer with them.

title: DISGUSTING!!  And I LOVE Coconut water! Just not Zico's
text:
I've recently started consuming Coconut water daily. We live in Bahrain, and I was buying Taste Nirvana brand on the military base, but they sell out as soon as they come in. I'm also spending close to $9 sometimes on the fresh young coconuts from the grocery, but realized that was quickly adding up! So, I thought I'd save money, and keep my supply filled with an automated monthly shipment.

BAD IDEA.

Since, my shipment of 24 came, I am disgusted everytime I try and drink one. Thinking that maybe they were just "bad" sour coconuts, I've kept trying. After 6, from different packages... I've come to the conclusion, it is NOT just a fluke, and Zico's coconut water is horrible! It tastes SOUR and filthy! I wondered why Zico and other companies sell the coconut waters flavored with other so called "juices", because coconut water in and of itself, is refreshing, & simply delish! Taste Nirvana is comparable to fresh! (Sidenote: I bought the plain "Pure Premium Coconut Water")

So, with that said, I wanted to make sure I put a review out there for everyone to read. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT! It tastes as if it could be dangerous, or toxic if consumed.

AWFUL! AWFUL! AWFUL! I think the coconut water was expired prior to bottling. YUCK!!!!

P.S. The positive reviews obviously came from either people who don't have tastebuds, or DO NOT know what FRESH COCONUT WATER should taste like. THIS IS NOT COCONUT WATER!!!!

Danielle H.

title: My kids like it
text:
I mix this sometimes just with butter and milk, sometimes with other shredded cheese. Either way my kids seem to enjoy it. Does have a flavor similar (but not quite the same) as Kraft or similar boxed mac-and-cheese varieties.

It can be difficult to mix in thoroughly if you don't do it right though. It is easy to get chunks if you do it like traditional mac and cheese. My advice:

1) Perform the following after the noodles are cooked, but while they are draining.
2) Start melting some butter in a separate pot (to taste, I usually use about 2-4 tablespoons worth for 2 servings of macaroni.
3) Pour in milk (usually I use somewhere around 1/2 cup) and start to warm it, but not to boiling.
4) Whisk in the cheese powder. Gradually add powder until the cheese sauce achieves the desired thickness. A whisk combined with moderate heating is your best bet to get it mixed well. It might take a minute to get all the chunks thoroughly mixed in.
5) Once thoroughly mixed, THEN add the noodles back into the sauce and mix well to coat all the noodles.

This process seems to work well for all the Hoosier Hill Farm cheese powders I've tried.

title: first time buying ghee, lactose free, tastes and smeels wonderful!
text:
I love butter but I am lactose intolerant, so I searched for butter alternatives
and got cacao butter which works well for baking but I missed the real butter aroma and flavor.

I didn't know about Ghee until two days ago while searching for lactose free butter
and I had to try this ghee.
When I opened the jar, it smelled so good like butter but just way concentrated and rich in aroma.
I just baked some chocolate chip cookies using this ghee and almond flour; they smelled good while being baked
and it tastes great.

I think since it's in a jar, it would be too hard to scoop out if refrigerated.
Since it's still cold here, I am keeping it in a kitchen shelf.

Besides the higher price compared to butter, I now have no reason to go back to normal butter :)
if you are lactose intolerant but still love butter like me, try this.

text: I got this to test my bizarre and sudden increase in heat tolerance.  To give somewhat of an idea of my tolerance, I used to struggle eating a bag of Flamin' Hot Cheetos, but about a few weeks ago they're suddenly like a regular bag.  Figured I'd test and also up my tolerance by getting this.  Tested with a toothpick first, very spicy, but not uncomfortable.  Just finished eating (1.45oz of) shredded chicken and (1 cup of) rice with this sauce drizzled on and mixed in.  Probably put about a teaspoons worth mixed in, but that flavor was still strong enough to taste.  Spice levels climbed to uncomfortable levels also, but only enough to have to pause a minute between bites.  If you can get past the spicy it's actually really good.  Best tasting hot sauce I've ever had actually (I've had most the ones in regular grocery stores).  A bit of a BBQ-ish, chilli kinda taste?  Regardless, will 100% be buying more when this bottle gets close to running out.  Though as little as you need per meal that may be awhile.

title: Best gummy!
text: So here is the deal - we're old enough that gummies were simply not one of our candy types growing up and to this day, neither of us hardly ever eat anything gummy unless you count a few vitamins and and then. I hate the texture, hate the synthetic taste and in general would simply rather have chocolate. BUT...I like cinnamon candy and although we both try to avoid any excess sugar in our diet, a tiny sweet treat is nice now and then. The organic, no dyes, kosher (ie no dead pig gel) etc made this an easier than average concession to our sweet tooth but frankly, I still expected these to be tough and gross like most gummies - well I was wrong. These are not only very tasty but the texture is totally different than standard gummies in a GOOD way - very good. We both immediately ate four each ( a lot for us) and it not only satisfied the sweet craving but there was also less guilt. I'm curious to see what these will sell for and would consider purchasing again in the future.

title: Very Sweet, Hard to Dissolve, Plastic Bottle
text:
I have arthritis issues and drink tart cherry daily. I've tried several brands available on Amazon and I find this one to be a little too sweet and the syrup seems oily and difficult to dissolve in water compared to other brands. Trying to dissolve this in seltzer leaves the drink flat because of excess stirring required. I like to mix one cup at a time and because of the lack of solubility I always find syrup concentrate at the bottom of the glass.

So far the best I've found is "Dynamic Health Organic Certified Tart Cherry Juice Concentrate" that comes in the 16 oz. bottle. It is not too sweet and is not oily, which means it mixes readily in water or seltzer.

Update: After consuming a bottle of this I have to say the taste grows on you. And it somehow has a less processed taste than the others I've tried. Will give it another try maybe.

The Fruit Fast and all the other brads on Amazon seem to come in plastic bottles, so there's BPA and other plasticizer issues. However, this item comes so well packed that they could easily bottle it in class without risk of breakage during shipping.

title: Delicious and crispy!
text:
I received Lawry's Crispy Oven Bake free as a BzzAgent. I was excited to try it as I'm familiar with the seasoned salt and require it on my fries at all times. I decided to try the bake with pork chops instead of chicken, as it was all I had in the house at the time. I have a habit of seasoning my meats prior to adding any breading, so this time was no different. I seasoned my pork chops with Lawry's garlic salt (which I also received in my free kit, and I love it), black pepper, and onion powder. I followed the remaining directions on the box and placed the chops in the oven for 30 minutes. Not only were they beautiful but they were absolutely delicious! The coating was perfectly textured and not mushy or soggy like some breadings tend to become after baking.

I would definitely recommend using this, but you probably need to season your meat first. I believe that it would've been a bit bland had I not pre-seasoned my chops.

title: Okay Chocolate; Would Make a Good Gift
text:
When it comes to chocolate, I’m a take-it-or-leave-it kinda guy. I enjoy it occasionally in a low-key sorta way, but I don’t crave it uncontrollably. I never buy it; the only time I have any around the house is when Amazon offers it as a Vine Program selection, which was the case with these MiLanGo Chocolate Hazelnut Truffles.

With that said, I can’t rave enthusiastically about any subtle nuances of aroma, texture or flavor that these little semi-spherical treats may exhibit to those of more refined sensibilities, or offer an expert’s opinion on their ingredients, composition or quality. What I CAN say is that they’re bite-sized morsels of melts-at-a-touch, light-hued chocolate studded on the outside with crushed hazelnuts and with a center that’s very soft, almost airy, despite the fact that it contains a whole hazelnut. To my pedestrian tastes, their flavor is okay but not special; I would say the chocolate is of candy-bar quality. The packaging is nice enough, with each spheroid individually wrapped in foil and then ensconced in a form-fitting plastic tray, to make this an attractive gift option.

As a product of Turkey, they contain some ingredients that I’d rather not see in my foodstuffs, such as palm oil and artificial flavors. I don’t know if such ingredients are common in higher-grade chocolates, but be aware that they’re in these.

Overall, I rate these at a middle-of-the-road three stars. They’re okay for what they are, but I won’t really miss them when they’re gone.

title: Not very sweet
text:
If what you are after is a prominent cocoa flavor with a little saltiness and not too much sweetness (think more bitterness), then this is the bar for you. I love dark chocolate, but I, also, love the sweetness that we get here in the US. This chocolate bar is the bitterness I love in dark chocolates, but it lacks the sweetness of a candy.

The bar claims to be Keto friendly and low-carb. The nutritional data is geared to 1/2 bar as a serving size and shows 19g of carb of which 8g are fiber and 7g is erythritol - if I get this right, that means a 4g net carb effect for 1/2 bar and 17g of fat, so in a controlled individual this can be low-carb and keto friendly, for me it fails to satisfy my need for something a little sweet and is a non-consideration for a keto / low-carb diet (I'm not wasting my few carbs on a bitter candy bar, sorry).

Perhaps I can break them up into pieces and sprinkle the bits over something else like adding a little dark chocolate to some low carb raspberry torte. P-)

title: Delicious and Quality Tea
text:
The tea is marketed to promote a healthy mood. Although this claim is not FDA approved and elsewhere on the package, it says “to maximize benefits, drink three cups of tea daily for two weeks followed by one-week break. With that recommendation and the recommendation of using 2 grams per cup this package isn’t even a 2-week supply. The claim of promoting a healthy mood is pretty vague as well. Like am I supposed to feel less anxious? Happier? I think they count on the power of suggestion and hope people think this tea is supposed to make me feel good, so I feel good. It is independently tested for ph. Eur. Potency. The label also says that it is USDA organic, gluten free, certified vegan, and paleo friendly.

This tea is caffeine free and smells pretty good. The tea is loose-leaf and comes in a foil packaging with an easy rip tab. However, it is super inconvenient and poorly designed because once you rip the tab, it is super difficult to store/poor the leaves in the tin. The package opens down the side which in my opinion is really annoying (pictures attached). The package comes in a nice tin that seals securely. I have never had this flavor of tea or this product in any other form to be able to say how strong it is or that it does/doesn’t taste as it should.

I would recommend this tea for the taste and smell mainly and not because of improving your mood and things like that.

title: much too sweet
text: I have never purchased this bar from Amazon, but I felt it needed a review. I first purchased the dark variety of these bars at WF and loved it so much I have since bought boxes of it to share with friends and family. I have since found, however, that this company is grossly inconsistent with the sugar levels of their different bars, specially considering that they are marketed towards the health-minded consumer and sold in health food stores. While the dark chocolate bar is pure heaven, with an elegant, full, boldly aromatic chocolate taste and very little sugar, this white (coconut) bar is extremely cloying, and their crispy (milk) bar is even more so. I purchased two whole boxes of these white bars as a theme for the holidays, and had my kitchen pail full of half-eaten bars at the end of the evening, with even a few of the kids saying they were too sweet for them. I wrote a letter to the company commenting on how wonderful (and healthy) their dark flavor is and how much sweeter (and very unhealthy) their other two bars are, and never heard back. I thought I would give them another try a year later, and found that they have actually increased the sugar content in this bar, which I hadn't thought possible. So, though this company claims to be healthy and considers its bars a "superfood," be mindful--they are not. They are candy bars made with natural ingredients, that is all. This snow angel bar (and the milk chocolate "crispy" bar) will raise your glucose to dangerous levels, so please stay away from it. Instead, I highly recommend their dark bar, which actually is quite good, and which is also available here (you will love it enough to wish there were more than 12 in the box). Angell Bar White Chocolate Bar, Coconut, 1.4 Ounce.

title: Taste Good and Shipped Safe and Quick
text:
(Quick review/Overall Feelings at bottom)

Been Looking for some good fruit cream filled candies(mainly orange), and stumbled across these on amazon. They got to the house a lot quicker than they said they would so that was a pleasant surprise. They also got shipped in very nice packaging. Came in a nice insulated bag that actually sat on the porch for about an hour before i was able to get home and get them, but the box and candies were still nice and could inside even though they had been left in the heat(being left in the heat had nothing to do with the candy people themselves , but whoever delivered them). I got the assortment because I wanted to try everything, even though I was looking for mainly fruity ones. Everything tasted great, I think the plain cream ones were my least favorite but still very good. Wish they had more fruit cream chocolates in the box, but that really isn’t taht big of a deal. They were a bit pricey with the shipping and everything totalled together, but after seeing how well they were packaged It helped me feel better about the whole price. I will definitely be buying more now that I have finished the box(they also last quite long so I Was able to snack on them for quite a few days). If they have a box that is only fruit flavors, or orange cream I’ll probably shoot for that option, but either way all the chocolates were good so even if i just get this box again I will be happy.

Overall Feelings-
—PROS—
-Very good flavor
-Great packaging and shipping, arrived quick and cold.
-Can last a while if you pace yourself
-Would make a great gift.
—CONS—
-A bit pricey, but for decent reasons. Would still buy again

text:
The Product doesn't taste bad it just is bad for you. Instead of using the natural olive oil that comes with olives, they add highly processed sunflower oil. Many PUFAs (polyunsaturated fatty acids) such as canola, cottonseed, safflower etc. cause health problems including chronic inflammation. Why add oil to a product that has its own healthy oil?
I think it's because the 0lives used are left over from the last press (3rd or 4th) and what is left is overprocessed olive husks to which oil has to be added to make it palatable. Safflower oil is cheap. The end product does not taste bad just rather insipid, like tea out of a twice used tea bag.

I've purchased whole coffee beans from Atlas Coffee Club before and was excited when I saw that they have K-cup pods. I love the idea of single origin coffee and like trying coffees from around the world to understand and compare flavors. I'm not a coffee connoisseur by any means, but this Rwanda medium roast coffee is awesome! It has a nice, rich flavor and isn't too bitter which I love. The coffee tasted relatively fresh, even though it's packed in a pod (one of the tradeoffs for convenience). I used it to make a latte with a bit of steamed milk and sugar. Delicious, and I'm looking forward to having more of this coffee.

It is a little more expensive than other K-cup brands, but I like the fact that these are single origin. It also comes in a beautiful box that I wouldn't be embarrassed to display on my countertop, and a card that tells you about the origins of the coffee and the cause that you're supporting with your purchase. I'm looking forward to trying some of their other products too and doing a comparison.

title: Great option for avoiding corn (grits) or oats (oatmeal)! Gluten Free!
text:
Love this stuff! I found this a while back and thought it would be interesting to try as a subsitiute for grits or oatmeal. I can't eat oatmeal as I am allergic to it and corn grits are yummy but as well seem to bother me. I used to not do so well with rice but seem to be ok with it now. So I tried this with the kids as an oatmeal substitute and it was ok, but it really works more like a savory dish like grits especially yummy with cheese. I like to eat it with eggs and sausage like I grew up eating with grits. It cooks super fast and easy, for a more creamy texture i like to whisk it while it cooks and also add a little butter which also keeps it from sticking to the pan. I just bought a pack of this to send to my dad because he tried it at our house when he stayed with me but he couldn't find it locally anywhere. And of course Amazon has it at a great price! It was double the price for a package at our local natural food co-op. I want to try it as rice pudding and see how that turns out.

It really is amazing how this does not taste like typical rice would. I mean if I had a bowl of this and a bowl of rice side by side it would be hard to know they were the same thing. You would swear this was just good ole fashioned grits.

Depending on your tastes and needs and perhaps humidity and location you may have to alter the cook time and/or water level. Also do NOT forget to SALT it. It would be very bland otherwise, just like grits or rice or anything else.

title: Extra es su sabor duradero y refrescante.
text:
Recientemente compré la goma de mascar Extra Libre de Azúcar y debo decir que estoy muy satisfecho con mi compra. Este paquete de 15 unidades es perfecto para llevar conmigo a cualquier lugar y siempre tener una goma de mascar fresca y sin azúcar a mano.

Lo que más me gusta de la goma de mascar Extra es su sabor duradero y refrescante. La menta fresca es perfecta para refrescar el aliento después de una comida o simplemente para mantener un aliento fresco durante el día.

Además, el hecho de que sea libre de azúcar es una gran ventaja para mi salud dental. Puedo disfrutar de una goma de mascar sin preocuparme por el daño que el azúcar puede causar a mis dientes.

Otra característica que aprecio de la goma de mascar Extra es su facilidad de uso. El paquete es fácil de abrir y las gomas de mascar son fáciles de sacar y masticar. También aprecio que la goma de mascar sea suave y no se vuelva dura después de un rato de masticarla.

En resumen, recomiendo altamente la goma de mascar Libre de Azúcar a cualquier persona que busque una manera fácil y conveniente de mantener su aliento fresco sin preocuparse por el daño del azúcar a sus dientes. Su sabor duradero, facilidad de uso y beneficios para la salud dental lo hacen una excelente opción para cualquier persona que desee disfrutar de una goma de mascar fresca y sin azúcar.

title: Beautiful lustre dust, works well but best on dark colors.
text: This dust comes in a small container, a lot smaller than I expected. It works very well for powdering desserts gold depending on the color of the item you're dusting. I used a small brand new makeup brush that I had on hand to powder a dozen or so white chocolate roses for wedding cupcakes and they turned out beautiful, though it had more of a copper gold tint to it. The thing is, it works so much better on regular brown colored chocolate and I found that out too late. Using regular brown chocolate would of saved me a lot of time from all that powdering, would of given the roses a more realistic gold look and I also would of used less of the lustre dust. I also used it on some white fondant butterflies and flowers, gives it a beautiful copper gold touch and made everything look professionally made. This dust works best on darker colors unless you don't mind a copper gold looking presentation. I am overall happy with the results though and would purchase this item again if I ran out.

title: best I've found for brewing tea...
text: while I don't much care for the taste/texture of the water as is due to it's specific mineral content that is exactly what makes it the best for brewing tea.  the strength, flavor and color of the brewed tea is considerably more than twice that of distilled and pretty close to twice that of other spring water as the mineral content (as well as a porcelain vessel as a proper catalyst) of the water is essential to brew tea to it's full potential.  i brew it extra strong and then dilute with my favorite water (distilled has the most, well, clean taste and therefore does not interfere with the flavor profile of the tea; just make sure to buy it at a market with a high turn over and not somewhere it sits on a shelf for ages for use in an iron-steam function to de wrinkle cotton-cuz that tastes dreadful).  afterwards save the little bottles in a cool dark cabinet for use as a mid afternoon hand bag size pick me up of said tea; alternatively use to freeze one quarter to one half full (top off with fresh beverage of the same so stays cold for later consumption) of the bottle-or even 5/6ths if somewhere hot and will melt by then-with your desired beverage depending on how long before you wish to drink it.  if going to freeze it is imperative to remember that the fluid will expand while freezing so leave at least one inch of head space and only partially close the lid until solid and then tighten.  works great with chocolate  milk too :)  mind the condensations while thawing-wrap with cloth or paper towel which can double for hand/face cleanup after snacking-and also possible pressure buildup from expansion/contraction during the freeze/thaw cycles so can be messy if filled too full.

title: HORRIBLE Texture, But 2 Stars For The Nutty Grain Flavor; Would NOT Recommend For Pasta Lovers
text:
This was incredibly disappointing. As a sufferer of Celiac (and one that remembers the taste and texture of 'regular' pasta), I'm always on the hunt for gluten free substitutes for my favorite food. After reading the glowing reviews for this one, I was excited to try it. And I hate to give a good company a bad review, but it really was pretty awful.

My main issue with it is the texture. It actually TASTES semi decent, which is why it got 2 stars instead of 1. It has a robust, nutty, grain flavor with a slightly sweet aftertaste. Fairly pleasant, although not really something I'm looking for in my pasta. But the texture RUINS it for me. I tried it al dente, super overcooked and every way in between. There is no way to make the texture palatable. It's a lot like I remember whole wheat pasta being, but much stiffer and grainier with very little flexibility. It was unappetizing and nothing like pasta should be.

I would not recommend this product. I bought one other bag of pasta from this company in a different shape to see if it improves, but I'm not hopeful.

title: Great Flavor, Excellent for soups
text:
I received McCormick Gourmet Collection Thyme for free to try and review. All opinions are my own.

I've been using the McCormick Gourmet Thyme for a few weeks now and I love the flavor. It helps that this is the time of year I make more savory poultry recipes and soups and thyme is a must have for those recipes. I was amazed at how the flavor really boosted the flavor of my homemade chicken noodle soup. I've added the same amount of other brands of thyme and the McCormick Gourmet Thyme had a definite flavor boost that made my soup even more enjoyable.

I did compare the McCormick Gourmet Thyme to another brand of thyme for a visual comparison. For the most part they looked the same. The color was the same, scent was equally powerful. One thing I did notice is that the McCormick Gourmet thyme seemed to have less crushing to it. The brand I compared it to had more smaller, almost powdered crumbs to it, while the McCormick seemed to be less processed. I don't know if this affected flavor or not, but it was a visual difference I noticed and if you are looking for those beautiful herbed looks for your food, such as if you're a food photographer or if appearance in this way is important to you, then I would go with the McCormick Gourmet Thyme.

Overall this is product has a great flavor and can be used in any dish you are looking for a full, savory thyme flavor.

A friend of mine in the medical field said that oatmeal is good for your cholesterol. I told him I couldn't stand oatmeal, and he recommended this brand and flavor. I liked it from the first bite.

Preparing the oatmeal is really simple. I use the microwave. The package that each serving of oatmeal comes in has a water line on it. You pour the oatmeal in your bowl, pour water into the package to the water line, pour the water from the package into your bowl of oatmeal, and microwave. It's so simple, so affordable, so delicious, and so much better for me than going out for breakfast.

title: RESTAURANT QUALITY SAMOSAS
text: I have been an aficianado of Indian food for more than thirty years, thanks to my now-fiance who introduced me to it when we were quite young, and have eaten in many fine Indian restaurants. I decided to try these samosas even though I was not familiar with the TANDOOR CHEF brand. I am extremely pleased with the taste and quality. They are as good as those you get in a high-quality Indian restaurant, actually better than most I have had, and rival the very best. The outer shell of the samosa is crispy yet tender. It's not greasy and has a lovely flavor. The filling of potato and peas is almost perfect. The taste is fresh with complex flavors and the proper spicing. Just the right amount of heat and celantro as well. The addition of packets of mint chutney is a nice touch. The chutney is a proper bright green and has a vibrant, fresh mint flavor. It's not too salty as many are either. My only criticism is that they should have supplied more of it. The two packets are quite small. The samosa boxes arrived in a styrofoam box packed with dry ice and all were still frozen. They cook-up in about 15 minutes in a 350 degree oven. If you like Indian food you absolulutely cannot go wrong with these samosas. They are delicious.

text:
I used to go through life in a sluggish, mediocre manner. I used to wear earth toned clothing, and used to only see the world in a chalky dull way.

One day I ran out of coffee pods at work, and while I frustratedly balled my fist at my own incompetence, a man in a hoodie emerged from the shadows of my work break room. He asked "Hey bro, you looking for a pick me up?" I looked left and right, and then behind me, thinking he was offering me cocaine, "Sure!" I jump on the offer.

Just then he reached into his WuTang clan cooler and pulled out a miracle orange can. This may sound odd, but the air around the can sparkled as he presented it, as if I were watching a TV commercial.

He handed it to me, I cracked it open, and tilted my head back to gulp it down like Popeyes eats a can of spinach. By the time I brought my head back eye level, the imam of energy has disappeared. He left me only with this story and a new addiction.

I now live my life riding a tidal wave of enthusisim, energy, and passion. Thanks Monster energy!

title: Simply Amazing!
text:
Ok, first off, I didn't know what to expect, I thought "maybe" one or two items would be good to eat, possibly even just passable, little did I know the amazing amount of taste headed my way!

First off let me walk you through each item, and what I thought of each.

The main item in this package (the one that delivers the most bang for your buck nutrition wise) is the Seapoint Farms Dry Roasted Edamame, 1 oz: A high-energy crunchy snack with over 14g of protein and 8g of dietary fiber per serving.

This stuff is amazing, you either love it or you hate it. After I ate this kit I immediately went out and ordered the auto ship from amazon for just the edamame's.

They taste like peanuts, but each one almost has a different taste, from nice and salty, to hmmm can't believe it's not a real peanut.

Bottom line? I LOVE IT. Nutrition wise it's a 6 out of 5! Taste wise it's a 4 out of 5 (rounding up on the 4).

Next is the Wild Garden Original Hummus Dip, which is high in protein & fiber.

I used this in conjunction with the Pita Break Flax & Honey Lavash Crackers, which are pretty tasty on their own.

The dip tastes like this amazing bean dip you'd find at an authentic mexican restaurant, 100% good. I love it a lot. Never have I had hummus before, but after this... I will again.

The crackers are pretty good, a little hard, but taste pretty good themselves. They are high in flax and have a faint honey taste.

Next up is the cranberries, these are just amazing, some of the best dried fruit I've ever had.

Last (and my personal favorite) is the Almond Roca Candy, Toffee Candy

Never before has my mouth tasted such luxury. This is the best tasting thing you could ever put in your mouth! Holy "mouth watering candy" Batman!

The only bad thing is? Amazon does NOT offer this for sale separately, and you CANNOT find it in any of the stores near me. Some third party people sell it here, and it's around 40 for a jar. Worth it? You bet!

The package has a whole? All things considered this is a great package, and a filling meal. It comes to about 4 bucks for the whole meal, which is a little bit on the high side. It's worth it as a weekly indulgence (for me), but not quite the daily picnic I hoped for.

If the price per serving was around 2.50$ I'd buy it every day.

Instead I bought the full sized edamame's from amazon (subscribe and save) for about 14 bucks a month for a bunch of bags. As these are the major super food in this package, I recommend doing the same. And if you can ever find a place online to get those Almond Roca's, DO comment on my review so I can pick some more up!

5/5, as a weekly treat, daily is just a bit high. Bottom line? I highly recommend it!

text:
I bought these because I was looking for the much-loved Callard & Bowser licorice toffees my mother used to treat me to every so often as a child. I haven't had one for about 50 years, and today, when my package of toffees arrived from England, I eagerly ripped open the bag and popped one in my mouth. At first, I was thinking, no, these seem very much harder than what I remember, but it's very cold outside today, and the package was sitting on my doorstep for hours, so the candies were unusually hard. Within about 20 seconds, the candy started to soften and I was able to chew it and move it around in my mouth. My knees nearly buckled. It was every bit as good as what I remember from my childhood. I savored the one and quickly popped another. I can tell these are going to be habit-forming.

If you're looking for a replacement for Callard & Bowser licorice toffees (who are out of business), you will find these completely acceptable as a substitute, just as other reviewers have said. Excellent!

title: Lovely bouquet
text:
The bouquet is lovely. My son often sends us flowers from Amazon and so far we have always been pleased. This bouquet is no exception. I must say I was a little concerned when it was delivered. The temperature outside was in the 90s. It was obvious to me the delivery truck was not refrigerated. The box was warm and when I opened it, the moisture wrapping around the bottom of the cut stems was HOT. I honestly felt there would be no hope for these flowers. However, we immediately cut the stems, prepared the water and set the flowers in the vase. So far they are not showing any stress from the excessive heat. I am not sure what would have happened if we were not home and they were left on the porch.I am afraid they may have been damaged.

The only "complaint" I have about mixed bouquets purchased through Amazon, is all the flowers do not bloom at the same time. For that reason your bouquet will often not look exactly like the photo. Right now my lilies are not blooming. By the time they do bloom the roses will likely be spent. I just wish they could figure out how to make up the bouquet so all flowers are in fresh and full bloom at the same time.

title: Very tasty, kind of like a vegetarian chilli...
text:
This is a very tasty and hearty soup. The broth is pretty thick; it actually reminded me of a vegetarian chili more than a soup due to the thickness and southwest spices. Adding a little shredded cheddar and a dollop sour cream would make this soup extra delicious. I thought it was pretty filling by itself, though.

Of course, the whole can is supposedly two servings, though I don't see how an adult human could only eat half the can and be full. I ate the whole thing. But pretty much all canned soups pull the same "2 serving" thing so I can't really fault this one for doing it too. So a full can is 340 calories. Sodium is high, as with all canned soups, but the protein and fiber numbers were very good. I'd say it is pretty healthy soup as far as canned soups go and it tastes good too.)

title: Whoa! Stop the press!! This is AMAZING!!! Top coffee reviewer here.. THIS IS COFFEE!!
text:
Ive reviewed SOOO many coffees!!! Most were good. A few not so much, some stand out here and there. This is certainly in the top 5% WOW category!
OK I think its important to state a few things. First off, a long time ago I watched a TV show that most of you know and love hosted by a man named Alton.. Yeah, that one. Science. Anyways he used the equasion 2 tablespoons of coffee per 6 fluid oz of water as his "go to" measurement for a truely amazing cup of coffee. I actually wrote it down inside my cabinet so I wouldn't forget it.
The cup i made I used that exact measurement. I made a 12 - 14 oz cup of coffee and used 5 tablespoons of this A&P Coffee, and I made it in my French press. I tasted it just plain black. I watched the socks fly across the room. Im not a black coffee drinker, (usually I hate it just black; nods to Captn Janeway..) but I think I could actually drink it this way. Next i added some oatmilk. Now Im REALLY floored. Then, I tried it again, and again, and had to push the cup away, because I wanted to drink it like you guys probably would, so i added a tablespoon of sugar. (I try not to consume any sugar..)
I was floored at how amazing it was. Like I literally sat there saying Ohhh my this is AMAZING over and over. Without any doubt one of the best cups of coffee Ive had in around a year, and Ive tested and reviewed dozens in that time. I could still taste the insanely rich bold burnt flavor of this coffee 45 minutes after I drank it.. and once again I mumbled something about how amazed I was. Yeah.. that good.
My wife made it in an espresso machine, and it was good... but NOTHING like the cup I made. So HOW you make coffee is as important as what brand and flavor you try. I put this coffee up there with my favorites which I probably shouldn't mention due to guidelines, but check out and rate my other reviews as helpful if you want to know more on that. Now that being said, the above measurements are a bit steep on the pocketbook, so I don't always drink coffee that strong. Depends on the circumstances.
The taste... burnt. YEAH i LOVE burnt coffee!!! The more burnt it tastes the more i like it!!! It had VERY VERY strong flavors of dark chocolate and maybe a hint of toffee? Kinda like those Score dark chocolate toffee bars?? Anyways it was AMAZING! I cant stress it enough. JUST BUY IT!!! NOW!!! Dont even close the window!!! And you owe it to yourself to try it in a french press with the strong amounts listed above, if only once. If made in an espresso machine, its still good... just not nearly as good. Ive had some coffee flavors that were better in the espresso machine. This one SOARS in a french press so I recommend that.
It takes time to write these... and its fathers day, so Im spending my fathers day helping you guys make a decision, so please rate this review as HELPFUL by clicking that button. Thanks for reading!

title: This will change the way you think about tuna salad and potato salad
text: This is a great find. A supermarket staple in Japan (grocery stores there sell it in every size imaginable), more and more American chefs are discovering the tangy goodness of Kewpie Mayonnaise. It's made with rice vinegar and and has a distinct flavor far from the blandness of many American mayonnaises. It's great as a mayo replacement in sandwiches, but it really comes into its own as a major flavoring agent in dishes like potato salad and tuna salad. The price is very good for the quantity, and from a quality standpoint it stands alone.

title: Creamy, tasty, and fresh. Great for those with peanut allergies.
text:
This cashew butter contains only three ingredients: cashews, sunflower oil, and sea salt. It may also contain trace amounts of almonds since their almond butter is processed on the same line. The product is also gluten-free. You may experience some separation of the oil from the nut butter, so stir it up good. It's not as thick as peanut butter, which makes it easy to stir into other ingredients but tricky to keep on a cracker. If you want it firmer, just refrigerate, and that'll harden the fats. Storing these in a cold, dark refrigerator would also extend the freshness of the product.

The 66 ounce product contains six 11-ounce PETE #1 containers. At the current price of $58, that's less than $10 per bottle. The safety seal is firmly attached to the bottle, which means they used the right adhesive to prevent oxygen from entering and damaging the fats. The expiration date on my bottles is May 23, 2018, so there's no fear of these going bad.

I think this cashew butter is delicious. A friend concurs. I would definitely buy it again.

title: Sweet 'n Salty and Healthier than my normal snacks!
text: I was paying $1 a piece for these out of the snack machine at work. Buying online I got them for less than half that price delivered. I stocked one of my drawers at work, and snack on these whenever I need a little "pick-me-up". Some people call this M&Ms with obstacles, but I love them. Just the right mix of nuts, seeds, raisins and chocolate. One of these easily holds me over until my next scheduled meal. And even though one of these is more calories than I need in a snack, it is a healthier choice and MUCH less calories than some of the other offerings in the snack machine that I was giving in to before I started buying these. I take these with me all the time on long trips or scout outings. One word of advice, when you get these, go through them and look for the packets that are void of excess air and eat those first, as they are usually the ones with a tiny hole in the packet somewhere that has let the extra air out, and will go stale first. Even the ones that were in this state, which were few, tasted fine.

text:
My family has used a Whirly-Pop popper for several years and was happy w/ plain "Jolly Time" popcorn from our local grocery store. Over the last 6 months or so we've had more and more of a problem with hulls and "old maids". Our view was the popcorn quality had diminished and the only other choice at the local stores is Orvil Redenbacher, so I looked at Amazon.

We are very pleased with both types of Fireworks Popcorn that I ordered (White Birch and Red River). White Birch is a slight favorite in our house, but both are much better than "Jolly Time". Hardly any hulls and only a couple of unpopped kernals.

We are eating popcorn about every other day now as opposed to once a week, so the minimum order isn't too large a quanity. There is a subtle difference in taste and we are looking forward to trying other varieties. I highly recommend this product and will be ordering more in the near future. title: IF YOU WANT THE DEFINITION OF DELICIOUS Mozzarella CHEESE LOOK NO FURTHER YOU FOUND IT HERE.
text:
No I am a total freak for good Mozzarella cheese and this is some of the best I've tasted. Some Mozzarella has a subtle smell of chemicals that remind me of disinfectant. Some Mozzarella lose their taste of milk and taste more like plastic. I love Mozzarella and I'd enjoyed some of the best in my travels. Sometimes mass produced Mozzarella has an engineered taste I can spot instantly.

I was surprised that this 365 by Whole Foods Market, Mozzarella Shred had an honest clean fresh taste absent the nasty hallmarks I described previously. The best part of eating this cheese was the lack of the chemical after taste. This 365 by Whole Foods Market, Mozzarella Shred melts beautifully and its flavor is both subtle and genuine at once. This 365 by Whole Foods Market, Mozzarella Shred is equally at home on a pizza or an cheesy egg with awesome toppings omelette. Make a grilled cheese or Ruben sandwich with this cheese and send your taste buds in to blissful rapture. I kid you not it is that good.

So yeah I love this and have no negative issues to report with this cheese except that the bag is too small maybe.

The Checkerboard one was excellent. NOT much chocolatey-ness, but the texture is a lovely biscuity cookie texture and the taste is very subtle and pleasant. Not overly sweet.

The chocolate one was a waste of calories and time. The texture was not great and there was no distinct chocolatey-ness. I expect a strong chocolate flavor when a cookie calls itself "crispy cocoa." It is crispy, but not a crispyness that made my day. Nothng special. I can eat it, but it doesn't make me smile.

Big thumbs up for the Checkerboard and "meh" for the Crispy Cocoa. I do hear that the ginger one is great--but I'll leave that for others to decide.

I am wheat sensitive, but heard this einkhorn wheat was less distressing. I still got some eczema from eating these, so they have to be an occasional treat. I don't like itching, ya know? But for those who can handle this over regular wheat, I definitely say if you like biscuity cookies, try the Checkerboard.

title: Astonishingly good mac-n-cheese, even if you don't know its gluten-free
text:
I am reviewing a single box of Horizon Organic Gluten-Free Macaroni and Cheese that I received at no charge through the Amazon Vine program.

I have to eat a gluten-free diet and it can make for some complications in prepared foods. While I don't like to rely upon processed foods, sometimes they're necessary, and mac-n-cheese happens to be a favorite of mine. Usually I use a brand available on a private label through a local store because its cheap and I know waht to expect - that brand isn't the greatest (the sauce is always soupy) but again I know what to expect.

I'm astonished by how good this Horizon Organic Mac-N-Cheese is. Preparation went exactly as was instructed, and I was rewarded with a plate of truly creamy cheese sauce covering small but al dente macaroni noodles. The sauce was called white cheddar but it struck me as closer to a smoked cheddar (or maybe I burned the milk a little?). While the noodles were too small to fit on the tines of my fork (call it childish but it is how I've enjoyed mac n cheese since i was a kid) they went perfectly with the sauce. The recipe makes exactly the right amount of sauce, too, not too soupy or too sparse, and I ended up eating the entire box in one sitting. Okay, I know that's kinda gross when you think about it, but man it was good.

Five stars for doing it perfectly.

title: A fun and interesting game to play with an adventurous group.
text:
Fun game with seriously accurate flavors (even if the bad ones are really nasty).
I purchased this, I am going to call it a booster pack, for the actual bean boozled game that I purchased at the same time as this on the recommendation of a friend of mine. He played the game with just a booster pack, his 10 year old son, and his mother and they had a great time. I thought it sounded fun, so I purchased the game and this booster pack to play with teenagers (14, 18, and 19) and we had a blast! I think it would even be fun to play with adults. In the version with the spinner, each player takes turns spinning and then choosing the bean that matches the picture from the spinner. Since the unpleasant flavors look exactly like their tasty counterparts, it can be truly hilarious when you start chewing. When we played we started by assigning points for swallowing, completely chewing, etc., but after a while it became more like a russian roulette sort of game and we had a great time. Oddly enough, fresh mowed grass turned out to be an interesting and tolerable flavor (for me it actually tasted like cut grass smells). Of course, the yummy flavors were spot on and, well, yummy as usual.

title: Don't bother - new China owner - not Malaysian - changed recipe - not the same !!!!!
text:
After buying the latest bottle in a local 99 Ranch Market, this is what I found... it tastes terrible !!! I had my husband taste it, he's the hot sauce connoisseur, and as soon as he smelled the bottle, he said something's different. The color is now dark brown, almost as dark as oyster sauce. I still have a bottle from 3 years ago, after sitting around aging, is still more red than this brand new bottle.

That was why I couldn't find it anywhere for a long time (I used to get it from Hmart Supermarket). Hmart doesn't even carry it anymore, saying that customers returned their bottles. Secondly, it's flavor now is too sharp and pungent, almost straight vinegar smell, and very little sweetness smell. This is supposed to be the original Sweet & Spicy recipe!

After talking with the store manager and researching online, I found that a CHINESE COMPANY FROM CHINA bought the company and they CHANGED the recipe !!!!! Not only the ratios of vinegar and sugar is different, the type of chilis they use is also different (DEFINITELY NOT the Malaysian chilis).

Another one bites the dust! Do yourself a favor; only buy if you can return after opening. Otherwise, don't bother.

title: Very good but not as good as the 'Swiss Water Processed' decaf coffees also here at Amazon - needs good brew temps
text:
I have tried this as well as several of the "Swiss Water Processed Decaf Coffee" from "Fresh Roasted Coffee LLC" which are also sold here at Amazon. While this is a good decaf, I find that I prefer the other decaf coffees prepared with the so called 'Swiss water process' from the other company (at least 3 of them). The coffees from the other company decaffeinated in the same manner have much more aroma as beans and seem to have improved flavor. I give them 5 stars. I give this one 4 stars because it is still good but not quite as good.

UPDATE March 04 2015

I have since gotten one of the insulated French Presses which has helped this coffee improve a lot (the others, interestingly were good before and are still good but not hugely improved with the new French Press). Having the insulated press keeps the brew temperature (with a pre-heated press) from about 204 to 194 at the end of the brew process, and this coffee seems to need that to get the best out of it. I previously was using a regular glass press which was not insulated and of all the coffees this one seemed to suffer the most from that.

I attach a photo of the four fresh brewed coffees from Fresh Roasted Coffee LLC (sold here at Amazon and purchased through Amazon). Of those four, the Mexican is by far my favorite with Colombian and Sumatra seconds and a possibly defective batch putting the Indian Monsooned a distant fourth. I have to be suspect of the Indian, as compared to the others from the same company it has absolutely no Crema whatsoever and has a very limited and short flavor profile.

title: mild, lightly nutty, lightly sweet, very mellow; not at all bitter.
text:
5 stars: no issues or concerns on quality. Love the transparency of information, and the mini lesson on the product page. The matcha smells good, is a light fine powder, and makes decent hot tea, or blended into smoothies or other foods. Comes in typical pressure zip mylar bag.

I drink coffee, love my coffee, but consuming matcha lends to a more sustained caffeine feel with no jitters. So I drink a cup of beloved hot coffee, and since I usually dont eat breakfast, I will make a matcha latte mixed with non dairy milk and some protein powder or liquid. This provides some extra caffeine and allows me to fast longer. Also regular consumption of matcha decreases if not eliminates my need for sweets. I've always experienced that, and rely on matcha to keep me in control.

Overall.. kinda, no different than other brands I have purchased over the years. I have been drinking matcha on and off for 15 years or so. Unlike then, it is so easy to find now! I think I have only used culinary matcha powder, from super cheap to quite pricy. From various regions. This one is on the pricier side for me. I dont rate on price though- we all have different budgets, and some peoples taste buds are more discerning that others. I have to say, I really dont notice a difference.. especially when being added to a smoothie. I will say that I tend to use a lot of matcha at once and sometimes it takes extra preparation to mask some of the bitterness in many of the matcha I have. I dont need to do that with this. It stands out in that this does seem to have a little more mellow and sweet taste, even mildly nutty, and has a brighter green color than some, and I dont need as much extra stuff to mask it. It isn't bitter. So yeh, this is fantastic, but I find many brands to be really good. I have yet to meet one that I dont like.

title: Very Nice (If Pricey)
text:
I decided to splurge a little on some actual tea sugar instead of dumping in a spoon of the white stuff per usual. I even went the extra step and got both cane and beet sugar to see if I could tell the difference.

And yes, you can definitely tell the difference. Just opening the bags gives you an entirely different aroma between the cane sugar and the beet sugar. I never realized just how strong an aroma cane sugar has until I had both side by side for comparison.

The beet sugar aroma isn't nearly as powerful, letting the tea shine all on it's own. As someone who'd unconsciously gotten used to the subtle caramel notes of cane sugar it threw me off a bit at first, but it definitely helps you taste more of the tea itself and less of the sweetener inside it. So if you don't mind the cost it's definitely worth the splurge on that first flush darjeeling or the like. If you're just making up a gallon of sun tea though, not so much.

title: Delicious set of organic spice blends!
text:
Avid organic spice user, and it's been fun to mix it up with this set and let someone else do the driving. I've tried 3 of them on hard-boiled eggs: first I grabbed was the excellent taco blend, and I'm a salt junkie so I had to add some sea salt for the egg to be to my preference but looking forward to using this one in a slow-cooked ground beef recipe for sure. The New Mexico chile, ancho, and cocoa really make for a nice kick that's well rounded.

Once I opened them all, the Greek blend was the one that smelled the most outstanding to me and really loved it when I tried it on the egg. Today I had the seafood blend and that was a surprise hit, kinda tangy and didn't need extra salt. Thinking I'll use the poultry blend on a whole chicken tomorrow in the smoker bet it'll also be fantastic like the rest. Tried to capture the ingredients of each one in case you're curious like I was - no sugar :) and a bonus sample packet of the as-yet-unopened Divine Bovine. I'm most often using spices on beef so that little pouch will go fast but overall I'm getting a great introduction to Flavor Seed.

These particular gummies are nice and soft once you get them to your mouth, but they are extremely sticky and hard to actually get out of the container. This stickiness also ends up leaving an annoying residue on the fingers once you're done. In this regard, It's not really as convenient as other brands I've tried. It also has the downside of having a strong ACV smell to it once you get the bottle open, but it's not really a big issues, since the gummies still don't actually have a strong vinegar taste.

Overall these are an ok brand of gummies. But for me personally, while the taste is good, it doesn't really make up for the inconvenience of the stickiness.

title: Sweet Home Louisiana
text: I have been living in California for 30 years now, but never forgot the coffee my Mom used to fix when I was a kid in New Orleans, half coffee & Chicory and half boiled cows milk, what the french call Cafe A'Lait.  Of course I also remember drinking that same coffee and stuffing down biegnets at the Cafe DuMonde and the Morning Call in the French Quarter.  Now being in California this long you tend to get Californicated, you know, premium wines, exotic coffee beans, etc., etc.  But when I happened on the old familiar can of CDM on Amazon I thought, what the heck, lets see if it brings back any memories, so I ordered a few cans.  Am I glad I did.  Not only did it bring back memories, but it made me realize that I would have never have found the taste I had been looking for in all those exotic beans I bought because there is no coffe bean in the world that can match the wonderfully strong and complex body of Coffee and Chicory.  Probably not for everyone, but absolutely indespensible for us old New Orleans boys.

title: Makes "Homemade" Taste "Store-Bought"
text:
Y'know that, like, non-dairy dry powder creamer some places have for their coffee? Well, let's just say I made some coffee meringues with them, and the taste reminded me of a million breakfast buffets all at once.

It's not a *bad* thing exactly? But it's just way more difficult to control for flavor, even using something as bitter as black coffee.

If you have a mean sweet tooth, go for it (but get the biggest bag; trust me, I went through this WAY faster than expected). But if you want to cut the sweetness a bit without destroying the meringues, I'd just grab some cream of tartar and practice doing it the old-fashioned messy way. Trust me, it's not as difficult as it's made out to be.

I like the fact it’s an all purpose rub; I think it’s one of my favorite things from this one. In my opinion, all purpose rubs provide a neutral taste; this provides a variety of options on what you can put it on. The label says steak, chicken, pork, beef, and vegetables. The only reason I took off one star was because of its saltiness; this particular seasoning has a super salty taste. You need to make sure and use just the right amount. Combining this with additional flavors may help compliment the flavor; overall, it’s great you can use it on a lot of food. Just make sure to watch that salt. title: Tasty, chewy, satisfying snack
text:
These remind me most of the Fast Break candy bar, except less sweet and more interesting. I like that you can see each layer of the ingredients in this, and that the entire thing is not enveloped in chocolate. These are soft, easy on the teeth, and quite satisfying.

I like peanut butter and chocolate, and combined with the salty pretzel, and peanut and granola layer, these easily hit the salty and sweet mark for me. The peanut butter layer is noticeable and smooth, covered in salty pretzels. The pretzels here are actually tiny little pretzels made just for this purpose, not crushed up pretzels, which is what other brands try to offer. The middle layer is a granola blend, possibly with more pretzels and peanuts combined, which is then dipped at the bottom into chocolate. So while this is not a chocolate bar, and there isn't a thick layer of chocolate at the bottom, there's enough chocolate to satisfy that "chocolate and peanut butter" craving.

I like that these are only 180 calories. They are high in fats, but that's to be expected with the peanuts and peanut butter. You'll get 5g of protein from these, but little else in terms of real nutrition. Interesting for me is 91mg of calcium and 1mg of iron. I like that "peanuts" is the number one, first ingredient. So I'd put these in the "OK for a mid-afternoon snack" with a cup of coffee or tea.

Really pleased with these, and will not hesitate to pick them up again.

title: Makes fantastic soup but is extremely over priced compared to standard 4 pack of same product
text:
Stock makes fantastic chicken soup but extremely over priced compared to standard 4 pack.
With the standard 4 pack I add 3 chicken breasts, 4 -5 cups of water to the crock pot and leave it to cook either 2 hours for defrosted chicken and add 1/2 to 3/4 cups Jasmine or brown rice and cook until the rice is done. I like to dice or shredded the chicken breasts and this makes a hearty soup without tons of liquid. If I didn't defrost the chicken breasts first, I just throw them in the crock pot with stock, and let it cook all day, adding the rice after work. If I want to expand the recipe to feed more people I use 5-6 breasts, 7-8 cups of water (max my crock pot will hold), and increase the number of stock packets to 6. 1 cup of rice if I want about 1/2 or so of the soup to be liquid or increase rice to 1 1/3 cups and shredded chicken for a heartier soup. I've never used minute rice so I can't give a cooking time but Jasmine or brown rice takes 20 to 40 minutes to cook with crock pot set to high. Basically a really great soup with about 5 minutes total for prep and 3 ingredients because the knorr sock tubs have the seasoning already perfectly done. Adding a thickened would turn the recipe into stew. Adding vegetables if you'd like. Could add color and additional nutrition. We prefer the basic stock, water, and chicken breast recipe.

text:
About six months ago I switched to drinking low-acid coffee because of some acid reflux problems I was having. Trader Joe's low acid French roast is probably the best tasting low-acid coffee I've tried, but unfortunately Trader Joe's doesn't make a decaf version and I'm trying to cut down on my caffeine. For decaf low-acid coffee I've tried [[ASIN:B001P28DHY HealthWise 100% Colombian Supremo, Decaffeinated, Swiss Water Process Low Acid Ground Coffee, 12-Ounce Cans (Pack of 3)]] and Puroast (both purchased off Amazon). Neither one is great, but HeathWise is better. HealthWise is bland, so you have to use more coffee to get a good-tasting cup (I usually mix a scoop of decaf with a scoop of the Trader Joe's, and that helps), but the Puroast decaf smells and tastes off. I can't describe what's off about it--it's just not pleasant. It certainly doesn't have that rich coffee aroma and flavor we coffee-lovers love. Perhaps the non-decaf version is better. If you need low-acid decaf and you're desperate, this will do--hence the three stars. But I would never serve this to a guest in my home, and I really can't recommend it.

UPDATED REVIEW
After drinking this coffee on and off for a couple weeks, I've come to the conclusion that it's actually causing me intestinal distress. title: Excellent Decaf for a Reasonable Price
text:
This is my favorite decaf version of Central American coffee, likely because it is roasted darker than some others. As a result, there is a fuller, smokier flavor that is missing from some Columbian coffees, and it still maintains the smooth finish that Central American coffee is known for.

This company is a small roaster, so you are buying artisan coffee, for which you might expect to pay a premium. It is also organic. And the goal here is to help those in need, so all the profits go to a good cause—care for the poor in Africa.

But all those things don’t make this any more expensive than other premium brands. Sure, you might find excellent coffee on sale for less at your local grocery store, but the retail price here is very much in line with what you would expect to pay.

The packaging is nice—it seals the coffee well, and it is easy to open (no small accomplishment, by the way!) The seal is especially important if you buy ground coffee, because it tends to go bad. (For the record, my experience with ground coffee from small roasters has been uniformly good—likely because it is so fresh. So even though I normally grind my own, I am highly pleased with the freshness of this ground coffee).

Highly recommended.

title: No Lobster Taste
text:
I cannot taste lobster in this product or in the broth of the bisque I made with this product.

I made a lobster bisque last night. There is a photo of the jar in this listing which shows a recipe for the bisque, but my jar didn't have the recipe on it. However, the ingredients list does show that "cooked lobster" is the first ingredient, and salt is the second ingredient, so I would expect there to be a strong taste of lobster, or at worst, a weak taste of lobster. But I cannot smell or taste any lobster and neither can my wife. The contents of the jar smells more like a soy sauce.

Nonetheless I made the bisque and I even added a half cup of cooked lobster tail. I could not taste any lobster in the broth at all and neither could my wife. The broth was not unpleasant to eat - it just didn't taste like lobster - not even a hint of it. Interestingly, I noticed that the website on the jar in the photo of this listing which is superiortouch.com does not come up. On my jar, the website is listed as betterthanbouillon.com so I went there and found the lobster bisque recipe. However, the recipe is a little different - the one shown in the photo on this listing shows that 1 cup of white wine is needed with 1 TBS of the lobster base. But the recipe on the betterthanbouillon site says I should use only 2 TBS of white wine and then 1.5 TBS of the lobster base, which is 50% more than the early recipe. But if that's true, then why do both jars indicate 38 servings are in the jar??? Doesn't make sense. Since it's an 8 oz jar, there should be 16 TBS of lobster base. Anyway, I used the website version recipe which calls for 1.5 TBS of the lobster base, and when all was said and done, we couldn't taste any lobster in the broth at all, even though I added my own fresh cooked lobster tail meat to the bisque. Very odd, especially since adding lobster meat is optional. It's as if they forgot to add the lobster meat to the product. I will try this bisque recipe one more time and edit the review if needed, but I'm not optimistic. If it fails again, I'm not going to throw it out - I'll use it mixed with a BBQ sauce for chicken or something... and cook some thighs on the Weber. :-)

title: Energizing - unsure? Relaxing, Soothing - definitely.
text:
Over the past couple years, I have been drinking more of these tea blends as I attempt to balance my lifelong coffee addiction. The endless varieties of tea/herbal combinations creates some truly wonderful (and a few truly horrific) combinations.

ElevaTEA from Serenergy falls into the wonderful camp. The challenge with these multi ingredient loose leaf blends is delivering a consistent experience, but that is also part of the fun - you are never sure exactly what you are gonna get. For example, one cup I brewed had deep reddish color and a strong Rooibos flavor with a little extra sweetness and an undercurrent of orange. Another cup had a lighter, almost honey-like complexion - the rooibos was less dominant but the undercurrent was definitely peppermint. Both were equally enjoyable to drink and left me feeling soothed and relaxed.

The recommended serving size is 1 teaspoon - though the directions on the package suggest 1/2 teaspoon which I think must be a mistake. I have been using just over 1 teaspoon in all my brews so far and using water heated to 195F as the directions suggest using water just shy of boiling.

In summary, I cannot testify to the energizing effects of this tea - but I have thoroughly enjoyed every cup - and as stated above, left me feeling soothed, relaxed and perhaps a little refreshed. Maybe the refreshed feeling is close to being a little energized.

title: Outrageously good flavor!
text: UPDATE:  Amazon now tells me I have re-purchased 7 times!  Not only are these Oregon Porcini incredibly delicious in so many dishes, they're easy on the tummy.  I switched to these after experiencing severe gastric distress from other non-U.S. dried shiitake mushrooms, have used them many times with no ill effects.  I first immerse in (you don't need to bother with warm) room-temp tap water in a 2-cup measuring cup, pressed down with a small ramekin or glass.  After half an hour, I strain the broth into whatever I'm cooking through cheesecloth, then I mince the mushrooms themselves (because the large pieces can be tough).  Although I do strain through cheesecloth, these usually have zero grit--whereas the dried Porcini I used to buy in the supermarket typically had a lot of grit.  For Thanksgiving my hosts asked if I would make vegetarian gravy, which I did with these + fresh mushrooms, and everyone exclaimed how delicious it was.  One little bag goes a very long way, and I always want these umami bombs in my pantry!

title: Where've you been all my life?
text:
IBS and gastric bypass pretty much poo poos my ability to enjoy ANY coffee. The acid, the caffeine? Who knows that trigger is, but I also can't drink tea or other drinks (can't have bubbles), water is good but boring after a while. Can't do juices/sports drinks because diabetes, and the artificial sweeteners give me migraines. I'm stuck for a beverage other than water, I missed coffee!! But it was killing me softly.

Then I found you!!! Low acid, caffeine free? Can't possibly taste that good, all decaf doesn't taste like real coffee right? Wrong.

This coffee is so good & so smooth. I don't need as much sweetener either, I think I needed the sugar to cut the acidity? No stomach cramping, no sour burning stomach situation, no churning sensation. It still triggers bm(s), as I think coffee just does for some people, but I'm so happy to have my cuppah (or 5) pain free and without wanting to launch myself into space from the caffeine. Thank you for being you Cafe Don Pedro, I think I love you.

I'm able to lock this away from my thieving co-workers and look like the hero when I do share. With the 2 pack it takes a while to run out, so sharing and keeping my hero status is easy.

A word of warning - it does not travel well once you insert the pump. We moved offices mid-bottle and I could not get the pump to lock. In the move some concentrate leaked out of the pump, but not a big deal if you're not planning on moving around a lot with the bottle.

text: Due to current health issues, eating fruits or vegetables is impossible (I cannot digest them - anything with seeds, skin or a peel), I've tried everything and my body is unable to process them. Applesauce isn't considered fruit and I'm so tired of a liquid diet - the thought of another smoothie makes me want to vomit! These are the greatest thing I have came across! My packages all contain full pieces (no smashed crumbs) of Fuji apples with a hint of cinnamon. The fact that each pouch gives you a full serving of fruit, only contains 40 calories AND no added sugar, makes these great snacks to take to work, to put in lunches or grab if you want something sweet. The boxes fit perfect in my pantry and are cut so you can just grab a pouch and go. I love to let a piece melt in my mouth - it's just like a soft, yummy apple! Since I'm about to have $25,000 worth of dental work - I'm already placing another order. Might be adventurous and try the pear, but the apple and cinnamon is AMAZING!

title: My Pop Tart addiction story....
text:
"Hello my nickname is Ragepoppa and I'm a Pop Tart addict."....that's really how it should go. My family has had countless interventions with me about my "Pop Tart problem" (so they call it). I say they just dont understand, mind their own business...let me be. It could never be so easy I say. I call it a devine love for gooey, sugary, frosty fruited, tangy-ness (yes tangy-ness) that only a Kellogs Pop Tart can deliver. I guess the real problem here is the fact that i've dragged others into my realm of over indulgence, namely my dog "Pop Tart" (thats really his name). The "crackling sound" of a Tart wrapper on the verge of being opened gives me such a rush and as far as eating Pop Tarts is concerned this (on any given night) is usually how it goes down.....

Let me tell you this...

Ok...In the middle of the night when everyones asleep (best time to eat a Tart) I am quite oftenly awakened from my sleep by the Pop Tart gods. I throw on my robe. I slowly sneek to the back of the house to the pantry as I can hear the gods calling me with every sneaking step. As I slowly, silently open the door the inner light of the pantry comes on, its like a beam of bright sunlight being shun upon me by Pop Tart heaven (sometimes i pinch myself to make sure that I havent actually met my calling cuz that's really how it is when we die right...bright light..colorful boxes of differnt flavored Pop Tarts everywhere inviting us, surrounding us, telling us its ok to just come to the light) anyway...As I "slowly" grab a package out of the box my dog (Pop Tart) can hear the "crackle" of the wrapper from the other side of the house while in a dead sleep (remember, my dog Pop Tart he has the same problem I do) It's like he's programmed to awaken from Tart package crackling...jeeze! By the time I'm in the kitchen and throwin these badboys on a paper plate (to microve for exactly 16 seconds I might add cuz thats how I roll with my Tarts) He is literally doing "flips" cuz he's so excited by what is about to follow (as am I). As always I silently wave my arms back and forth in a wild fashion trying to "hush" him as to "not wake momma" for she could bring a real damper to the pleasure for which we are about to engage in. Youd think by now he'd know the routine but "Noooooo.." Pop Tarts gotta do flips and run in circles and growl happily ("No Pop Tart No!!") as I find myself recklessly waving in silence in my boxers and robe and before you know it the microwave has already went "ding" and I find myself doing the same dance as him in the middle of the night in the kitchen trying to silence him while everyones trying to sleep so my wife and kids dont get up!!! This has become properly termed as the "Pop Tart kitchen dance" by my wife and kids as they know the sounds oh too well from being awakened so many times over the years by this embarrasing display that my dog and I have subjected ourselves to just to try to enjoy a good evening snack..

Long story short....

Sometimes we get busted and our Pop Tarts are taken from us (depending on how much noise we have just made) before we can enjoy them (bummer man...) Other times...and I mean the best times, we chill on the couch while Sports Center whispers on the T.V., a cold glass of milk is also in hand for the ride along and we really bond man...we really bond....its special..a man and his best friend enjoying a moment together. A moment that no one can take from us that we share.... A man, Pop Tarts and his dog. Sometimes I say to him..."We really did die and go to heaven didnt we Pop Tart."
