title: Good Tea, Almost Perfect
text:
This was delightful tea from the onset, as soon as I opened it, it smelled like a bag of fresh oranges. When you look in the bag you see bits and chunks of orange peel, so this was very promising. I have really been drinking a lot of rooibos blends lately, so I couldn't wait to brew up a cup of this tea.

I used about 10 ounces of water in my cup and 1 1/2 teaspoons of tea and let it steep for 5 minutes. It came out very tasty, a smooth mild orange taste, borderline tangerine, no tartness, not sweet, but solid orange tea. What would have made this perfect for me is adding a little tartness to it, maybe adding some hibiscus to the mix.

It came in a nice resealable bag, and had an expiration date of September 2024, so it was plenty fresh. This is a very enjoyable tea on its own or with a meal, I do recommend it if you like orange teas.

I am a big fan of Brazil nuts because they are such a great source of Selenium and other nutrients. We eat one or two every morning, so a big bag goes a long way. We keep them in the refrigerator to extend their shelf life.

As far as quality, these rate right up with the best I have ever tried. Occasionally in a bag this size you will find a few tat seem stale or almost a moldy taste. That has not been the case with these. I rate them 5 stars for quality.

I rated them at 4 stars because of the price compared to other similar products. Since I am also budget conscious, I have found that there are other brands that come in 2 pound bags for a better price. We usually freeze half of them to keep them fresh.

title: The Best of Prepared Pies, Goes Bye Bye!
text:
Let me start here.

Description online:

• A holiday must-have.
• Sweet apples and warm spices cradled in a tender, flaky crust.
• Serves 6

Ingredient List online:
Ingredients
Sliced Apples, Wheat Flour, Sugar, Palm Oil, Water, Salt, Corn Starch, Dextrose, Rice Starch, Citrus Fiber.
Adapted from the song by the Kingston Trio and showing my age: Where have all the warm spices gone? Long time passing.

I regaled the takeover of WF by Zon, but slowly, not so sure. In America, two things you don’t do
1. You don’t mess with the flag
2. You don’t mess with the best prepared apple pie recipe in da business

Whenever I wanted a good, comforting slice of apple pie, WF AP was my jam. At first I thought it was me when I noticed the taste difference. But alas the reviews confirmed it.

I mean I use to look forward to warming up a slice as a special treat and pairing it with its ride or die, gooooood vanilla bean ice cream. I now feel like an unsuspecting spouse in a divorce…….shattered.
Please WF/Zon reverse the curse! Please allow me to stop saying, “Alas poor WFAP I knew it well.” ☹

title: Healthy, portable, non-perishable(ish) product that tastes good
text:
There are a lot of conflicting views about soy but one dietary rule of thumb experts often agree on is most foods are safe in moderation.

If you are on the run and need something to eat, there are very few options that are portable, non-perishable, and healthy. I've spent significant time researching foods that meet these three categories and one of the select few options I identified was nuts. Of course, only soy nuts have all of the amino acids to qualify as a complete protein. Beyond their value as a quality protein source, soy nuts also provide a good balance of carbs, protein, and fat, one of the strongest of any single whole food. This balance is important to maintaining blood sugar levels and deriving a sated feeling from the food, and it also conforms to various diet plans, i.e., the Zone. These soy nuts provide all these benefits without even the negative of added salt/sodium.

Conclusion - it's worth researching whether substitution of soy nuts, especially on an infrequent schedule, for other types of snack food is right for you. I happen to think it is.

I received this product fairly quickly and it met the description on Amazon. I'm deducting one star only because the taste of these soy nuts is not quite as good as green soy beans that i've roasted at home myself. However, the taste isn't bad, in fact it's reminiscent of popcorn kernels without the toughness if you've ever accidentally eaten one of those.

I’ve even added in a drop or two of my favorite essential oil to give a little extra umph, but honestly this has so much flavor, you don’t need to add anything to it! Also be sure to eat the citron and ginger left in the bottom of your cup! (so good, and so good for you!) Mix w cold water for a refreshing drink, especially in the morning, but also all day long!
Read up on the benefits of ginger, honey, and citron, and you'll understand why you should try this. For me, I feel I’m strengthening my immune health and improving my digestion and metabolism w this tea!
I’ve bought jars for everyone in my family, given jars to my friends, given it as hostess gifts, and recommend it to everyone I know….AND I drink about a jar a week.

title: Terrific For Fast, Easy, "Homemade" Taste
text:
As the temps outside drop, I love baking bread... but don't always feel up to the time or mess involved. Something I've discovered is an all purpose biscuit and baking mix (Bisquick is a favorite) makes a super fast and simple loaf of beer bread. In a mixing bowl, stir together 2-1/2 to 2-3/4 cups Bisquick All Purpose Mix and 1/4 cup granulated white or brown sugar; add one 12 ounce bottle of light beer and beat together until combined. The batter will be lumpy. Pore and spread batter into a well-greased loaf pan and bake in a preheated 350 degree oven for 40-45 minutes. Remove from oven, cool a few minutes and turn the loaf out onto a cooling rack. You can enjoy the bread warm or cooled to room temperature. Substitute up to 1/2 cup of Bisquick All Purpose Mix with quick cooking oats for a heartier bread. Stir a small amount of dried herbs into the dry ingredients before adding the beer for herbed bread. Play with the recipe!

What's nice about Bisquick All Purpose Mix is how versatile it is. It can be used to coat boneless meat before pan frying, makes a terrific crust-less quiche, becomes the basis for yummy cookies or muffins, and of course makes biscuits, shortcakes, pancakes and waffles. During cooler months when I bake more often, it's handy to have on hand when I want homemade taste without a lot of hassle.

title: A Very Nice Tea
text:
I am a jenny come lately to tea. I grew up with Greek herbal teas and demitasse coffee. Any other tea was the ubiquitous bagged tea you see in the grocery. My first cup of loose leaf brewed tea was from Asian friends I was visiting. That was when I understood the love for tea.

The tea is long leaves, no sticks so far and brews up without bitterness. It stands up to milk and sweetener. I let it steep a little longer and I use a teaspoon per cup plus 1 for the pot. It is even enjoyable plain.

I read the more critical reviews and I suppose I got lucky to some degree with my purchase. Tea production is a pretty labor intensive process. My guess is that quality control is always a challenge.
My only complaint if you will with the product is that the box and bag are not resealable hence the 4 stars. It otherwise is a very drinkable tea.

title: Focus
text: This was actually a mispick that was shipped to someone as a gift.  Amazon has such excellent customer service!  They sent the correct flavor to the recipient and allowed them to keep the mispick! So glad they did, as the recipient gave me the box of Focus tea. Focus is a mixture of moringa, black tea, ashwaganda root and turmeric root.  It has a very earthy flavor to it. It is a bit strong and a tad bitter to taste.  Some may consider it  a little bit of an aquired taste because it is earthy and a little bitter. That being said, it's not jarring and it does brew up to a smoothe enjoyable strong cup of tea.  I add a splash of milk and honey to it, but,  I have had it with plant based creamers and it was fine. I did find that it actually was relaxing, which did allow me to focus on my work.  There are medicinal benefits to the ingredients, if you are diabetic you may want to check with your doctor before drinking this tea, moringa is known for lowering blood sugar.  Glad for the mis- ship, in this case, as I plan to order another box for myself.

title: It's cocoa crazy!
text:
In my Keto journey, I've been trying out several types of keto/paleo friendly cereal's. Being a child who grew up eating lots of breakfast cereals, I missed that milk/cereal/crunch type of meal.
This is pretty close to the mark.

The cost to portion ratio threw me off. You get 5 packets in your box and for the cost of a small cereal box you get one individual bag of cereal. At first I was put off by this until I realized that based on ingredients, distribution and the audience, it's not a terrible price point. Sure you pay a bit more, but we generally pay more for healthier substitutes in our foods. At least, from my own experience.

Now the big thing... taste.
The initial taste if fantastic. It tasted like a I was eating a certain name brand chocolate cereal puff. It was great!
But then I added almond milk for most of the meals, and another time 2% milk because I was out. It was great for the first minute or two. Then the cereal got soggy quick and the taste was not as potent. It was there, just not as in your face "yum" I experienced on the first couple of bites. Minor quibble.

Would I recommend these? Yes.
In fact, I just finished my last bag yesterday and am debating on ordering more before the holidays. I've tried the other "rice crispy" brand of keto cereals, and I've enjoyed them, but this... ho boy... this one is amazing in comparison.

I'm looking forward to trying their other flavors and maybe even trying this one again.
So if you're a keto, paleo or just a low carb conscientious eater, I spoonfully recommend this product. I've enjoyed it and I hope you will as well!

title: I prefered the old recipe, but the new recipe is more keto-friendly.
text:
I bought these before I realized that they changed the recipe; I had not had them in a few years because I moved to a place where no grocery store stocks them. Originally, these nuts were an excellent tasting, low calorie snack that was sweetened with sucralose and contained modified food starches. At some point in the last few years, they changed the recipe and replaced the sucralose with natural sugar and stevia, and the modified food starch with potato and corn starch. There may have been other changes, but I could not identify them.

As a result of those changes, these nuts now have less flavor, fewer net carbs, but more calories per serving. They're not as good as I remember. They're still decently tasty but they don't hit my sweet tooth like the original ones did. I probably won't buy these again and will instead switch to a trail mix to get my healthier sweets.

title: No big deal if you enjoy to eat spicy foods
text:
I'm guessing the folks who think this is insanely hot are not used to spicy foods i.e. not from the Southwest where things like red/green chile (not "Texas" chili) and jalapeno peppers are a staple of pretty much every dish.

The chips are hot but nothing to write home about. I've had many salsas and meals served at local restaurants that were just as hot. If you want hot, come to a chile cook-off here in New Mexico and you'll have lava coming out your other end the next day. These chips didn't even burn on the way out. The only thing surprising about these chips was that there was a mild burning sensation that lasted much longer (about 30 mins) than traditional hot chile peppers.

Everyone in my office that tried the chips just kind of shrugged them off, with a few taking handfuls of them and crunching into them as they walked back to their offices, remarking that they would be better with some good salsa hahaha

That all being said, I can see how these would catch folks by surprise if they live in other parts of the country where their only experience with spicy food is canned chili. For those of us who buy, roast, peel, and hoard bags of Hatch green chile in our freezers, this stuff just didn't do much for us.

Throw this in the toaster oven at like 250 for a min and just get some heat into it and enjoy dont try to brown this. It's great. title: The only thing that gets me off the couch after work
text:
I'm an evening runner. Yeah, I know it makes me much less likely to run my miles, but I hate waking up early. These sport beans are often the one thing that gets me up off the couch to hit the road. Eat a bag (or, really, for shorter distances you can just use a half bag) about a half hour before you need to go and boom, you have energy enough to keep going. I also bring an extra bag on longer distances. It's caffeine, so if you don't really partake you may get jitters. I'm a coffee person so this is pretty smooth for me.

The taste isn't terrible, but there is a definite twang of salt/electrolyte?. Be aware. Sometimes you can get a few that taste pretty close to regular jelly bellys though, and that's nice.

I prefer these to Clif ShotBloks, but the shotbloks taste better. These sport beans are easier to open and get at while you're on the run with sweaty hands, and you can just pour them out rather than tearing at a plastic package like a starving raccoon.

title: Oh Yes!
text:
I have been drinking Reed's Ginger Beer for a long time, because it is widely available here in our city and nearly everywhere else I visit. It also contains no artificial additives or so-called "natural flavors", and only uses real cane sugar. You can also see the real ginger settle on the bottom.

Bundaberg is also one I drink a lot since it is available at Costco for a very reasonable price.

So Reed's and Bundaberg are really good, but Bruce Cost's IS far better. No question. I bought two bottles today at the local Cracker Barrel, and I am sitting here falling in love with this drink. I normally let the bottle of the Ginger Beers I drink sit in the freezer for no longer than two hours, and then I take it out to where it thaws to just the right point. Best way to drink it.

Sadly, I have never seen Bruce Cost available anywhere else in our city, and looking at Amazon now, I know I would never buy it from here unless they slash the price significantly. The Cracker Barrel I got these bottles from sell for less than half what a bottle goes for here. Absolutely ridiculous.

All good things are not meant to always be within easy reach, so it is what it is. I do not go to Cracker Barrel very often, so it may be that I will cross paths with Mr. Cost somewhere else. At least I know that it is out there and tastes great. Hakuna Matata. No worries.

text:
Looking at all other reviews after making the purchase, I set myself for a disaster but after cooking it not sure what everyone is talking about.
It is a frozen pasta dish from grocery store. For the price, what else are you expecting? Its priced well and packaged well - there was a review about using too much plastic but not sure why you are shopping frozen aisle if you worried about waste and packaging.

Meal itself is good enough by its own - I did add some parmesan once its cooked and I added more meatballs - however you only get like 8 meatballs which is not enough for anyone.
I think there is plenty of sauce but it is kinda weak in terms of flavor. I would have liked more tomato in the sauce which would have make the end product tasty and have more of a vibrant color.
They can also add some toppings like parmesan or chili flakes as finishing touches.
All in all for what it worth, it is definitely a good buy for the nights you can’t cook or want something quick. I probably would buy it again for rainy days when I can’t cook.

title: I'm Italian.  I cook.  I love this.
text: I can sometimes find passata locally but if I want Mutti Passata I have to order it online.  My order came on time, well packaged, and worth the cost and shipping.  I recently made two recipes with Mutti Passata.  One is Italian Sugo (sauce, gravy whatever you like to call it) which was phenomenal and the other was a braised Brisket in Barolo or red wine and passata.  I've been making both recipes with other canned tomato sauce, jarred tomato blends or what have you, but the texture and flavor of passata is much better for these dishes.  If you have a true Italian grocery in your town you can probably find a lot of different brands, or if there is a Whole Foods you can sometimes find it there.  Since I only needed three bottles for a large (huge really) batch of sugo, and 1 for the braised brisket, it's worth the cost per bottle.  I don't know if I'm allowed to share my recipe blog where you can find these recipes, but it is foodflirtation dot wordpress dot com. title: If you are using these to make something like Rose Hip Oil
text: If you are using these to make something like Rose Hip Oil, I would use fresh Rose Hips. After all the research I did on making Rose Hip oil, nothing I found gave any warning to the fibers inside the package or inside the Rose Hips. Its very much like fiberglass if you have ever experienced that on your skin. Not fun. So IF you decide to get dried Rose Hips here is the solution I figured out. Be VERY careful handling the bag and pour them into a freezer bag (they are tougher than sandwich bags), Once in the bag start crushing with a rolling pin or other something similar. These things are TOUGH despite being dried. Then place the contents of the bag into a metal mesh strainer. Once everything is in the strainer start shacking it back and fourth to sift out the fibers. Don't wash the crushed Rose Hips. Afterwords, wash the fibers down the drain and pour the crushed Rose Hips into a clean bag. I was so happy that this ended up working, so I am passing that knowledge onto all of you. TRSUT ME, you do not want this stuff on your skin.

title: Worked great!
text:
This worked perfectly for my son's science fair project. Although it came with no instruction booklet in my pack I had found a review on a similar product with detailed instructions it worked perfectly.
We used 200 grams of sprite 2 g of sodium alginate mixed thoroughly.
In another bowl mixed 2 cups of water, weighed it out, which was 470 grams and mixed it with 4.7 grams of calcium chloride till dissolved. Then had a bowl of plain water last.
Used syringe to suck up a little of the sprite mixture, then slowly dropped in to the calcium mixture. Let sit for 1 min. Then removed and put into the plain water for a quick second to rinse off. Then eat!
We didn't use the calcium citrate at all.
We used coke, sprite, and Gatorade and all worked perfectly.
You must use 1% of the food liquid and the water in sodium alginate and calcium chloride. Ex. 300 grams of juice to 3 grams of sodium alginate.
Good luck!

title: Well balanced buttery macadamias!
text:
So following Paul Saladino's Animal Based diet I have eliminated all nuts due to high linoleic acid content but macadamia's are high in monounsaturated fats (like olive/coconut/meat) and half only 2% LA profile just like beef so I have been enjoying macadamias for my fat macros for a good half-year now and have enjoyed a wide variety from Winco bulk-bins to Sam's Club's (my fav) and these are right up there at the top.

They are perfectly salted for my tastes although I tend to prefer salt. Although since going Animal Based I don't think I oversalt like I used to on keto. But if you like macadamias you either like them unsalted and raw or salted, there's no in between! Some other brands leave you asking what happened to the salt. These are not oversalted, not undersalted, but perfectly balanced.

With respect to roast, if you consider coffee, I'd equate the vast majority of these (~80%) to the perfect macadamia "medium" roast. However, I do very much enjoy the 10% darker roast macs and the other 10% that are slightly under-roasted. It just gives a nice variety in the crunch and texture. Couldn't be better balanced if you asked me.

$$$ wise these are also very affordable. Issa (the owner) is also awesome and has some amazing customer service. If you're a macadamia snob I recommend giving these a shot. Only thing better would be if there was a subscribe and save option on these

When I suddenly couldn't get the 2.1 oz soup cups, and this appeared (1.8 oz soup cup), I bought 3 boxes of 6. I ate the first one a few days ago, and barely could choke it down.

The broth in no way resembles chicken broth, it's brown and watery and has a slight trace of miso or soy flavor, with a bitter after taste.

title: Made in Italy. Misleading advertising. Tastes great.
text: I like the texture and taste of this oat milk. We drink it straight from fridge. And the package size is perfect for everyone to enjoy a single glass of chocolate milk with no left overs to have to refrigerate. With 25 grams of carbs and 16 grams of sugar per serving, we treat it like a dessert, similar to ice cream. Oats require 80% less water to grow than almonds and are a direct way to impact environment, the packaging touts. **HOWEVER, since this product is MADE IN ITALY, you don't reduce any carbon footprint, or reduce your impact AT ALL. It's produced in Europe, shipped over on a container, trucked to a warehouse, packed in a cardboard box once your order it, then driven to you via ups after you order it. And then you get to dispose of the box and packaging it shipped in. So, don't feel like you're making a positive impact to the world simply by ordering this. If you want yummy, italian oat milk though, here's your product!!

title: Tastes minty cool...
text: I almost gave it 4 stars based on the presentation of the tea box. There was a huge dent in the side of it, which is kind of an eyesore for me because I typically keep the boxes until the tea is all used up. I suppose the dent happened during the shipping process or during delivery so why penalize the seller for this? Now let's get to the flavor. As seen in my photo, the first ingredient is Green Tea. After that is: Spearmint, Lemongrass, and Peppermint. If you don't know about order of ingredients, the first one on the list is what it contains the most. So this is mostly green tea with other herbs mixed in. I'm guessing its for flavor purposes, as some people cannot handle the potent taste of pure green tea, the way I can. Green tea is an acquired taste for sure. What I get from the taste of this tea is very minimal traces of the green tea although it's there, it's not pronounced. Then the mint and slightly citrus taste from the 🍋 lemongrass kicks in. You would almost miss the lemongrass if you weren't looking for it in the taste. I also got a tiny bit of a woody flavor from the tea. Overall, I'd say it has more of a minty taste to mask the green tea flavor. But again, I can tell the green tea is subtly there. The aroma of this tea is minty. If you didn't know that it was "green" mint tea, the aroma would probably make you think it's peppermint tea. All in all, it's a good mild tasting tea and definitely at a great price.

title: Best Soup I've ever had from a package/can!
text:
I have tried a lot of canned soup over the years for an easy and quick lunch and none of them compare. This is the first soup I've had in ages where the chicken isn't tough or dry. It tastes like real chicken and doesn't have that icky soup texture that most canned soups w/ chicken have. Also, the vegetable and beans - they give you a good mix of all items. It's not loaded w/ the cheapest ingredient and only give you two chunks of the good tasting veggies that cost more. Plus the flavors are well rounded and it doesn't have that chalky canned soup taste that most soups have.

I like to squeeze in some fresh lime juice and add a small spoon of light sour cream and this is a great, satisfying lunch that will stick w/ you. I will be putting this on my subscribe and save plan when I need to order next - so yummy!!

Also, if you have dietary restrictions like I do - I cannot eat gluten or yeast - this soup fits the bill. Thank you, Pacific, for making quality products that aren't chock full of stuff that doesn't need to be in them!!

title: This is FOOD GRADE 100% pure orange oil.  Use it sparingly.
text:
I see a lot of people complaining that this is more expensive than other orange oil products. You know why? Because it is exactly what it says on the label: Pure 100% orange oil. It is as far as I can see the ONLY orange oil on the market that is safe to use in food. THAT is why it is much more expensive than those others.

You look closely at most of those other "pure orange oil" products, and you know what the first ingredient is? PETROLEUM DISTILLATES. (I found one orange aromatherapy oil where the first ingredient was sunflower oil, but it was honest enough not to claim to be pure orange oil.) You can polish your furniture with them, and that's as close to food as they'd better get.

Boyajian's is the real thing. You can bake with it, you can add a drop or two (NO MORE, or it'll be overpowering) to your tea or coffee, you can add a spritz to orange sauces, you could flavor vodka with it to make your own orange vodka, add a spoonful to homemade orange sorbet ... the sky's the limit.

Those OTHER products — the ones where the first ingredient is petroleum distillates — are fine for putting a shine on your table. But seriously, don't put them in or on anything that's going in your mouth. SERIOUSLY. I'm not joking here. This is a public service warning. If it has a published MSDS sheet, IT DOES NOT GO IN FOOD.

Seriously.

title: good product, just not balanced enough for my taste.
text:
i got mine in today. My opinion is that they are OK. Don't get me wrong. I love chocolate covered stuff, but my problem with these was that they did not have a good balance. I think the problem stems from the type of chocolate that they used to cover the fruit. At first, I was biting them in half when I ate them, and I thought that the chocolate was overpowering the fruit. But then after eating the fruit in full, or at one time, I found that what I think the problem is, is that when you eat them, the chocolate does not tend to, I guess you could say, dissolve, like the fruit does. Which means that one flavor does not mix completely well with the other in a constant balance. Think if it this way, you can get chocolate that melts easily in your mouth, where just sucking on it, it creams up, and then there is chocolate that melts in your mouth more like hard candy does. This is the type of chocolate that is more like hard candy. You need it where one flavor does not overpower the other, and on these, it seems like about 2/3's of the flavor is coming from one or the other, because of the type of chocolate used.

If you just toss the full thing in your mouth and start chomping away, then you probably will not notice it much, but if you take your time at eating them slowly, you will notice this much more. It may be due to the fact that they are in a bag like this that they could not use a better type of chocolate for them, because maybe they had a lot of problems with them sticking together and stuff, if they did. plus adding in that these are dark chocolate and not milk.. They are not bad, and I have no problem eating them. I just don't think that they did a good job on balancing the flavor. I have some dove chocolate covered fruit (cant remember if they were milk or dark chocolate), and I think they did a better job at balancing the flavor of the fruit with the amount/type of chocolate on them.

They are good, and worth the money that I paid. They are just not my favorites.. Overall, I think the quality was good, but not great.. I think the chocolate was a decent chocolate, but not the best.. but hey, for the price, not bad.. and was worth trying. Like they say, you get what you pay for, and these were definitely on par with that saying. They are definitely a lot better then some other ones I have tried. I was looking for chocolate cover cherries when I came upon them and just bought them to give them a try. But I still think that cella's makes some of the best chocolate covered cherries. but to be fair, cella's has a different kind of chocolate covered cherry too. In the end, yes I would say to give them a try, as your tastes may be different them mine, and you may like them. Other then that, I have no complaints about the product.

One thing I can say about these that is not very common to see is that they have multiple fruits in this bag. Most of the time, you get just one fruit in a chocolate cover fruit bag, where this one, you get 3 different types of fruit, which gives you a good variety. and that, I would say, is a major plus to these. Also, the balance between the flavor and the fruit on these, is the same, no matter if you pick of the blueberry, or the cherry, or the cranberry. So for the price, I would say that these are well worth the money, and considering they are not really expensive, it is worth trying them too. Just one side note, if you, like me, saw the chocolate covered cranberries in there and kinda wondered about how good they will be.. like I did.. well, dont worry too much. I thought that the flavor would be weird or not very good thinking about the cranberry, but I would say that they were just as good as the cherry. Maybe it has something to do with them being dried fruit, and not fresh. But I would say that all 3 fruits were equally good.

final verdict, yes worth trying, worth the money, and I may or may not buy them again. i just am not sure, but no real complaints about them.

I took it and shared it with the owner of the local Chinese restaurant and he was surprised. It just goes to show that the new ways are not always the best ways. I think also it shows that we lose something when we don't take time to hand craft things. We get so used to the lesser quality that it becomes the norm. title: Healthy, tasty and easy to cook meal
text:
These Madras Lentils are a tasty and easy-to-cook meal. Both my parents are Indian, so I grew up eating spicy, flavorful Indian food. While I can't cook much, I can still have a healthy meal with authentic Indian flavors in minutes.

I normally make 2 cups of brown rice and mix it with these lentils for a meal cooked in under 15 minutes. The lentils can be heated in the microwave in just one minute, and are packed with protein. They are flavorful but a little mild, so I like to add in a dash of red chili powder.

They are very similar to the Indian dish dal makhani. They have a long shelf life, are quick and easy to cook, and are very healthy. Highly recommended for busy, health-conscious professionals.

I have been known to stock up on a half dozen Farmer's Brand peanuts when I go to the Ranch 99 for my Asian groceries run. Imagine my absolute DELIGHT to find the Phong Kee peanuts at my local supermarket in the Asian foods aisle. Not only at the Five Spice peanuts remarkably similar in flavor profile to the Farmer's Brand (you know - that kind of spicy, salty, savory flavor??), the Phong Kee peanuts are all de-shelled already, so they're super easy to pop in your mouth.

I love these and am so glad I gave them a shot. Last time I went back to the supermarket, I picked up five bags of Five Spice and also tried a bag of the crunchy Hot peanuts. (Those are good, too, by the way.) But yes, the Five Spice is amazing and I can't wait to share them with my family, who got me started on the Farmer's brand peanuts to begin with.

It also feels great to support a small, minority owned business. Give these peanuts a shot - they're SO worth it.

title: Having just eaten this for dinner, I have advice and raves
text:
First of all, don't be put off by the price. If you've kept track of grocery store receipts lately or the sharp increase in basic foods over the last year, you may see how this product could save you time, gas and MONEY.
At the time of this writing, it cost about $16.88 for four packages of this mix. EACH package easily serves 8-16 people with soup left over.

While the instructions note to add 4 cups of water or a water and broth combo, we quickly discovered we had to double or even triple the liquid added. No problem there, because we had more soup!

If you don't have fresh veggies or spices around, this will suffice as is and it is thick and satisfying. If you garden, you'll improve the taste by adding fresh chopped parsley, garlic and whatever veggies you want. A can of tomatoes (or fresh, chopped ones) does no harm. This is a mix you can play with, add ingredients and spices.

IMPORTANT: this is not a salted mix. It is full of split peas, barley, lentils, whole wheat pasta, dehydrated spinach, tomato, onion, etc. If you don't use salt, consider adding a salt substitute. I also added basil. It was delightful, quick and is now a pantry staple.

Nutrition: 330 calories (1/2 cup) only 20 calories from fat. Significant source of iron at 22% of the Daily Value. Protein: 20 grams. Fiber - 8 grams. Add some bread and you have a meal, rounded out with some greens, perhaps.

title: I was on the fence but I'm glad I ordered these!
text: I saw a few reviews saying they didn't like the taste of these so at first I was hesitant to order them but I'm glad I did. I wanted to support a small business rather than some of the larger brands and I liked the ingredients used especially since a lot of supplements contain iffy ingredients. I only ate 2 the first two days because eating 3 for a breakfast seemed like too much (plus I have oatmeal every day for breakfast anyway) and after that once a day and I think they've made an increase in my milk production. I've had to mostly stop breastfeeding because my baby has latching issues and does better with a bottle so I pump a lot rather than feed and I'm happy being able to see a couple extra ounces per day after about 5 days of eating these and it has kept going now that I'm down to one cookie. I do think that if you really like sugary processed treats you may not love these but I don't have a sweet tooth so for me they're perfect. They're only subtly chocolatey and the peanut butter isnt overpowering and I like the texture and visible oats. I kept mine in the fridge which I think keeps them fresher and helped them stay nice and chewy without drying out. They're a little above my budget but I'm taking a chance and ordering the large pack for next time. Definitely worth a try.

title: Good pu-erh, worth trying
text:
I discovered and got hooked onto pu-erh during a recent trip to China and have only had the teabag variety thus far. Among the 3 brands I have tried thus far, one store bought, one an international brand, this is the best tasting pu-erh in a bag I have found. I intend to try couple other brands available on Amazon.com or if I see in any of the local Asian grocery stores.
One thing that could be better about this brand is the bag around the tea bag, which is a bit hard to open (even though it has the guide slit). On the brigther side, each tea bag is individually wrapped in a 'plastic like' silver cover, which helps seal in the flavor very well.
Characteristics of this tea:
- 'fishy' like smell when you first dunk into hot water (not overpowering or nasty by any means)
- steeps fully in about 4-5 minutes
- neither bitter like the stronger black teas nor mild like the greens. perfectly balanced somewhere in-between.
- satisfying flavor, makes me feel good about drinking a cup of tea.
If you have not tried this brand, worth giving it a shot. I typically drink 4-5 cups every week and will likely get a refill ordered soon, unless I find an even better pu-erh out there. Giving it a 4 star rating since this is a good buy, and my reference point is limited at present.

text: Glad to find this organic light rye flour from Doves Farm, UK, as I could not find a similar product anywhere in the US. One would think that Bob's Red Mill would carry such a product; they make a non-organic light rye flour and an organic dark rye flour, but no organic light rye flour. Go figure... At any rate, this flour is used in my organic artisan sourdough breads and pizza crusts and I can now proudly say that my culinary creations are 100% organic! Light rye comprises about 8% of the total flour volume in these sourdough baked goods, but that 8% combined with organic unbleached white bread flour produces the perfect flavor profile that has resulted in a legion of fans. Looking forward to reordering this product soon!

title: Real Weak Coffee; Too Expensive!
text:
Whenever I contemplate the last twenty years of my life, I don't think I've ever gone a day without drinking coffee or tea. Caffeine is essential for my survival. Therefore, I was pleased to have an opportunity to review a two-pound bag of 100% Arabica whole bean coffee from Real Good Coffee Company, Peruvian Light Roast, from Seattle, Washington. I received a sturdy, thick, brown bag that was easy to open with its notched indentations at the top and easy to close with its resealable Ziploc closure.

The coffee beans smelled fresh and aromatic. The beans have a very good best by date of 080923 on the back of the bag, in the lower right-hand corner, near the barcode. This bag has a one-way air vent through which I could smell the coffee beans, which were easy to grind. Unfortunately, these coffee beans make weak coffee. My dad complained about it. Mom didn't complain because she likes weak coffee. I don't. I had to use at least one-a-half coffee scoops per cup of brewed coffee. This depletes the coffee quicker, making a cup of my coffee more expensive. Therefore, the price of this whole bean coffee ($34.99 at the time of this review) is too expensive for me. When I first requested it for review one month ago, it was only $24.99, which is more reasonable. I don't understand the sudden price hike.

Because this Peruvian light roast from the Real Good Coffee Company produces weak coffee, I cannot recommend it to my family and friends; most of whom, like me, prefer to drink coffee with more kick to it. I need all the kick I can get in the morning, especially when I don't get enough sleep the previous night.

title: Oh my god.
text:
I love coconut, but when I bought this product, I still wasn't entirely sure what I planned to do with it. Living in cold, northern climes, smoothies aren't that appealing for many months a year. Now, I know. I'm going to eat it out of the jar on a spoon.

Like I said, I live in the cold north, and this product was indeed rock solid when I first opened the jar. I boiled some water for tea, then after the leftover water had cooled down for a few minutes, I pour it into a bowl and set the jar of Coconut Manna in it. I confess I forgot about it for a little while and it probably sat in the hot water for 10-15 minutes. After that, it was no harder to stir than a new jar of natural peanut butter. When I licked the stirring spoon, it was so delicious my head nearly fell off. I ate a couple spoonfuls and then put the jar away.

A few hours later, I opened the jar again out of curiosity. Though starting to solidify around the edges, it was still mostly soft. Good to know that after you go through the trouble to process it, it stays usable (eatable) for quite a while.

title: Excellent South Africa style condiment
text:
I ordered the two 470 gram bottles instead of the big jar due to previous issues with the big jars comming apart during shipping. These arrived intact. Yay. Gave one to my business partner to try, he loved it.
Unlike Indian and Ceylonese chutneys, this is focuses more on sweet, and not the tangy heat. So, far less confusing to the average Western palate.
While in RSA, I always enjoyed Mrs. Ball's on a variety of foods from chicken and beef to fish, cheese, Biltong and Woers.
If you like more heat like I do, it is easy to add a bit of habanero sauce to the mixture. Pro tip: do not go to RSA without some quantity serious hot sauce if you are from the Southwest USA. The food will bore you to death. Their idea of "very piquant" is a paprika sauce milder than we feed babies in Arizona and Texas. You can also wake them up big time when they want to try your Death Sauce or Ass Reaper!
I have a daughter who dislikes chutney, and so I gave her some of this on a cracker without telling her what it was. She loved it.

title: I love these
text: So I was a little bit skeptical of these concentrated water additives. I didn't really know how it would taste, or how well it would perform. Let me tell you, after having used it for many weeks now, I am in love with these. The black cherry tastes really nice, and it only takes a small squirt to properly flavor my 750 milliliter water bottle. I take a water bottle to the gym, and now always flavor it with this Mio energy drink. It's like making your own Gatorade I guess, and is really nice to have at the gym. It gives me that extra little boost that I always require during my workouts, and is very helpful when I'm feeling fatigued. Though I've been using it for many weeks, actually maybe even several months come to think of it, I'm still on my first squeeze bottle. I think this eight pack will last me years. I don't like it to be too flavored, so obviously you just add as much as you want to flavor it to your tastes. For my taste, a small squirt will do for 750 milliliters. So, they'll last a very long time, and be a great replenisher for working out or any athletic activity. I'm really very happy with these, and would most certainly recommend them.

title: People love Van Leeuwen but they aren't my favorite
text: I'm a vegan, and often I feel that many things out there that are vegan aren't made necessarily by a vegan or had a vegan try them first. I'm just over everything having coconut of some sort in it. I don't mind a bit of coconut milk or cream in things, however, my preference is not usually being coconut heavy or when there is no need to add the coconut if there is another vegan base being used. Coconut has a tendency to overpower IMO, and as I'm getting older well having too much coconut is too much fat for me. So I often lean more toward looking for oat, nut base, soy, or pea protein bases, but the occasional coconut milk is fine, just don't get why it seems Van Leeuwen always has coconut in their products. The size is ok but the flavor I feel just gets a little lost with the coconut added and with some tweaking I think could be great ice cream not 'Ok' ice cream which is how I often feel no matter how many times I try this brand. I really want to like it, but I usually get it and find myself going back to my usual go-to ice cream brands. I know it can be better, well at least to my liking it just often leaves me feeling underwhelmed. i also think whether it's in the store or at one of their shops it feels too pricey for me.

title: Happy morning drink for combating anxiety
text:
I'm a happy home herbal-medicine user, both using and making for myself, my family, and others. I even grow my own medicinal herbs and wild-harvest some. However, I like knowing that Rasa used actual practicing herbalists in creating this blend, so I know it's as good or better than anything I'd come up with myself.

I bought this blend as a splurge birthday present for myself and my family; I was pursuing adaptogenic herbal therapy to combat anxiety. I used the blend for two months, getting two steeps out of one tablespoon (a great tip for reducing the cost!).

I'm not a coffee drinker but adore chocolate; drank "black," this blend unsurprisingly has no sweetness, but all the herbal goodness. My favorite way to drink it is blended with a teaspoon of coconut sugar, a scoop of collagen protein powder, and teaspoon of coconut oil, and a little coconut-milk creamer to gild the lily. Spin it up in a blender and it was a well-rounded, super-health-promoting drink.

Only removed one star because cost of regular use is high. However, I understand why it's priced as it is and respect the knowledge and research which went into this excellent product.

If you're looking for a nourishing way to support mental health, this is a great choice. Make sure to use it regularly to see benefits.

title: High price, but delicious and nutritious!
text: These superfood bars are delicious and packed full of goodness, but they very pricey for the size of the bar. They bars themselves aren't very big but they are satisfying for the size. The ingredient list is all real food with no added filler. They're plant based, grain free, gluten free, non GMO, and sweetened with coconut nectar instead of added sugar. The Almond Crunch ones remind me of cookie dough flavor and are very good! I like that they're easy to bring along anywhere I go for a quick snack that's super healthy. I don't like that each bar has 270 calories as I'm not looking to add more calories to my diet but I can substitute a meal for these and then it's not so bad. I also like that theres a good bit of protien in them which I'm always looking to add more of to my diet anyway. I had my daughter try one as I thought they were so good, but she didn't like them at all. I guess it's all in your flavor preferences. They do come in a cooler type bag that's chilled but they don't have to be refrigerated. I do prefer them refrigerated though but again another personal preference. All in all, they're delicious and nutritious but be prepared to spend a good chunk of change on them.

title: Great Deep Fryer Oil
text:
Here is me, trying to do the right thing form a health perspective. I paid double in cost what I would have paid to deep fry (so far) 4 turkeys and 2 chickens had I used off-of-the-shelf cotton seed or canola oil. But, the taste and texture with this coconut oil is markedly better than the other cooking oils I have used. And, supposedly, the coconut oil is actually pretty good for you (unlike cotton seed and canola oil which are practically poison).

One thing you'll want to prepare for is the consistency of the product. Coconut oil is hard and white when below 80ish degrees (F). If it is over that temperature it will be clear and liquid. Prepare to scoop in a hardy manner if the oil is in it's white, solid state.

The only reason I am not giving it 5 stars is price. But, at least I can reuse the oil many, many times.

title: Economical AND allows me to have my favorite brews!
text:
My review leans towards supporting the use of ANY refillable K-cup in a Keurig machine, although this is the specific brand I first purchased. I have since also purchased a different brand 4 pack at Stop and Shop. The price per refillable "pot" was about the same.

I received the Keurig as a gift and LOVE using it, but having 2-3 cups/ day meant I was constantly running out of K-cups and the cost was adding up.
The refillable option that comes with the Keurig is inconvenient - you fill the "pot" with grounds, insert it into a chamber, twist on the separate cap, and THEN have to switch the insert for the one already in the machine. I don't know why the Keurig brand itself would have the least convenient refillable cup of all!

I purchased these refillable cups about 6 months after getting my Keurig and wish I had done it sooner!! Now I can get my favorite Starbucks or locally roasted coffee beans, ground slightly coarse for the flat bottomed K cups. A pound of coffee lasts about a month, so Im getting about 60-75 cups of coffee for $15, easily a third of what the K cups were costing me (in bulk!)

The only benefit I can see to the KCups, besides variety in flavors, is the ease of clean up. I loved not having grounds all over my sink, even with disposable filters. So the refillable cups bring me back to that mess, which Is why I chose to purchase even more cups. Only 1 of the 6 I own had the lid break off, but it is still usable, it just tends to get a few grounds in the coffee. I am going to purchase another set so I can refill enough for the week and only empty them once/week.

Hint: Filling the cups when they are still wet from rinsing tends to get coffee grounds stuck everywhere, which end up in your coffee. This is nearly eliminated when the cup is dry - another reason to have more than one.

These are dishwasher safe, although they easily rinse under running tap water.

title: Wagyu & Me: Together Forever
text:
Did I slather this wagyu beef tallow on my ten-hour smoked beef brisket just before wrapping it in butcher paper for its final few hours of cooking? Yes. Did said brisket turn out juicier than that gossip I heard about your Aunt Tilly? Yes, again.

Did I use this wagyu beef tallow to stir-fry a chow mein my son declared was the best he’d ever eaten? Yes. Did it have more flavor than that dude with a giant clock around his neck? Yes, again.

Do I use this whenever I need to add a little fat to anything I’m cooking? Yes. Does that anything I’m cooking end up tasting better? Yes, again.

Some reviews mention short expiration dates, so I feared I may have to drink a shot of it each day to use it in time. While that wouldn’t be the worst thing in the world, that’s not the case with the product I received. The expiration is a full year into the future. Right around the time we’ll have flying cars and robot butlers.

So, do I recommend this wagyu beef tallow for all your cooking needs? Only if you have tastebuds.

title: Expensive, but delicious and so worth the boost to my mental health
text:
I love this product. I've tried Dry January, Sober September, etc and while I can last the whole month, by the end, I'm so bored with sparkling water and fruit juice that I can't wait to drink real cocktails again. But I've been looking for something that while help me cut back on alcohol for good.

Let me say that I totally understand where some of the negative reviews are coming from. It is really expensive flavored water.

However, the taste of the Garden flavor is bright, herbaceous, and so interesting. I mixed it with lime sparkling water and a small squeeze of lemon juice. It was so amazing to have a drink that has all of the complex flavors of a cocktail with none of the guilt or health consequences.

And that's how I justify spending $35 on a bottle of flavored water. If this can help me lose weight and improve my mental health by helping me stay sober, then it's worth it to me. Also, with the money I'm not spending on alcohol, I think I can afford this. I figure, it costs the same as a few cocktails at my favorite restaurant or the bottles of wine/Iiquor that I normally get somewhat regularly. So, why not splurge for my health?

Also, if you add a few drops of ashwaganda, you get a similar feeling of relaxation from your mocktail with none of the hangover. I look forward to trying the other flavors!

title: Flavor has changed - so disappointing
text:
I discovered this tea on a trip to Ireland a few years ago. After I used up the box I bought there, I ordered more from Amazon. The next few boxes had the same good flavor as the box from Ireland, although at some point the packaging did change. I ran out last fall, and it wasn't easily available for a while, so I was very happy to see it back in stock in March, and ordered a box. The box was wrapped in plastic, as always, and the carton was very securely packed. There was an expiration date long in the future.

Unfortunately, the flavor has changed. Instead of the appealing unique flavor of the prior boxes, this tastes like plain Lipton tea, a flavor I don't care for. I tried different steeping times, in case that was the issue, but I found the tea undrinkable each time. I'm hoping this is perhaps due to a lack of supply of the usual tea because of the pandemic, and not a deliberate decision to change the flavor. I'll wait a while, and if I have a chance to just try one cup in the future, I'll see if the good flavor is back. I am still enjoying another Bewley's flavor, Dublin Morning tea, and the box of that tea that I bought last fall tastes the same as prior boxes. I'll stick with that flavor of Bewley's for now.

title: Total Waste of $
text: I love truffle oil and have been using different brands for a few years now. Some are better than others but this stuff is a total rip-off. There was NO flavor of truffles at all. The front of the bottle says Porcini Mushrooms & Truffle Flavour Infused Oil but under ingredients it shows sunflower & olive oil, mushrooms, flavors. What kind of mushrooms? At least if it tasted like Porcini mushrooms I wouldn't be quite as annoyed- but nothing. I have bought the Roland white truffle oil as well as La Tourangelle black truffle oil in the past and liked both of those. Now, none of these oils is going to have a really intense flavor of truffles- they're all based on truffle flavor or extract- but they also don't cost $100 per portion as fresh truffles would and still polish off a dish! If Drogheria & Alimentari has any "T" extract whatsoever -it's of such a small amount it can't be tasted. It says they've been in business since 1880- WHERE I can't imagine Italian cooks putting up with this quality!

For a dry pasta that is widely available this has a wonderful flavor and very enjoyable.  All you need for an easy week night meal is 20 minutes and a jar of sauce.  So glad that I received a full size sample as part of BzzAgent.  I have since tried other Barilla Collezione pasta's and loved them all.  They have a much better texture than normal dried pasta.  It's a definite keeper in the pantry!

title: Good Alternative to Regular Standard Pasta
text:
This multicolored pasta shell product is not made with the usual ingredients (flour) but out of vegetables. This is one of those ultra healthy pastas that are good for those who, because of health reasons, can't tolerate "standard" pasta. But it is good?

While it tasted kind of bland straight from the pot, it's really not that different in taste from regular pasta, which gets its flavoring from the sauce. In this case it's about equally tasty. Once I added some sundried tomatoes and sauce, it was delicious. The only thing is that it's softer and doesn't have that crispness you sometimes get from pasta cooked al dente.

Overall this is a good healthy alternative to regular pasta.

title: Affordable introduction
text:
This is not the best cut of Spanish ham, but it is affordable and works well for tapas. I purchase mine locally at a better price point, but know that this is the least expensive (and flavorful) cut from the 'black hoof' ham.

Although this is not strictly acorn fed like the premium [[ASIN:B002BL9ZQ6 Jamon Iberico de Bellota]], it is still an experience that will develop and refine your palate for Spanish black hoof style hams. It's a little thicker than prosciutto, and with a different texture. The flavor is what sets this apart from its distant Italian cousin. This one has a more pronounced flavor that is hard to describe. It's less salty to my palate.

A major difference between this and the Bellota (aside from price) is this one is made from grain fed pigs whereas the Bellota is from acorn fed ones. The flavor is totally different if you have a refined palate, and for me there is no real comparison. However, since I cannot afford Bellota more than once a year, this is a nice substitute for setting out a tapas and enjoying with queso Manchego and a glass of Tempranillo or Garnacha.

This extra large size of Frosted Mini Wheats is an economical, tasty way to get a whole bunch of fiber into your diet. Mini Wheats are a great deal like Triscuit crackers, only the biscuits are sweet instead of salty. The cereal appears to be some kind of extruded wheat threads stuck together into a tiny pillow and baked. That sounds horrible, but these are among the tastiest of breakfast cereals.

One gotcha is that they become soggy in milk in a very short time, but it's an easy matter to eat the cereal dry with milk on the side. Dunk if you wish.

That's about all I can think of to recommend a breakfast cereal that you have probably eaten since you were a child. Back then, you ate Mini-Wheats because they tasted good, and now you eat them because they are good for you. Pity that there isn't a little plastic toy in the package. :-)

title: Wish it Was Sweetened With Something Else... Tastes Great Though!
text: I tried these with much fear and trembling. I saw sugar free and decided to give them a try... Never did it occur to me that perhaps companies are still sweetening sugar free products with malitol now that we have so many other great, healthy options. Once these arrived, I, like a conscientious consumer, checked the ingredients list. *Cue panic mode* Oh. No. What have I done. My parents went on the low carb Atkins diet waaaaaaaaaay back in the day, and back then candy sweetened with malitol was all the rage. It tastes just like the real deal! But oh man, I'm still scarred by watching the after effects my parents dealt with as a result of consuming malitol sweetened candy. (Spoiler alert... You've never seen explosive gas like malitol gas!) So, When that word malitol showed up on the ingredients list, I stopped in my tracks, unsure if I actually DID want to try these after all. I finally decided to give it a go, and ever so cautiously ate one piece. I watched the clock and was in slight terror until a few hours had passed with nothing even approaching the gastrointestinal distress I remember my parents being in. Maybe one piece at a time is safe? I'm definitely not trying more than that! I was super impressed by the flavor! It really doesn't taste any different to me than regular Special Dark Hersheys. I wish it was sweetened with something else, but honestly, the terror of the possible effects are a good thing to keep me from binging the whole bag.

title: Jumbo sunflower seeds you say? Sign me up!
text: Oh how much I love these darn seeds. I'd be a fool not to say that every time I take a handful of this tasty treat I am not reminiscent of the one and only Fox Mulder[[ASIN:B000JJ6K1U The X-Files - Seasons 1 - 9]] who brought sunflower seeds into the cult following status of greatness they so rightly deserve. I could wax on poetically for hours on how delightlful it is to be hungry late at night and to find the inviting blue and red bag of David's original jumbo seeds staring at you through the darkness behind the glow of the television screen. Shining on like a crazy beacon answering all of your hungry needs. I love these not only for their saltiness and roasted quality but for a nice lazy Sunday afternoon activity. Also, their boxes are TINY, TINY. 5 cups of cereal in one box. That's literally 5 servings... one box will last you 5 days if you ONLY EAT 1 cup.

For the magic spoon experience imagine a plain , stale, rice cake that's then covered with a protein shake from the 90s (the ones where you get that gritty texture feeling on your teeth) now box that up and shape it like cheerios and charger $10 for 5 cups of cereal and you have magic spoon. The magic is in how they got all these great reviews.

So for $40 this could feed one person for 20 days eating ONLY 1 cup per day. If you have a family or are a couple, your monthly cereal bill is about to explode! 7oz cereal box for $10...magic!

title: Nothing less than five stars...it's Hershey's cocolate!
text:
I admit to being a little puzzled when I saw this 33-ounce bag of Hershey's chocolates among the Vine offerings. I thought Vine offered new products for folks to try in exchange for their reviews. Of course, Hershey's chocolates are as entrenched in our culture as apple pie. But perhaps the bundling of these three flavors (or perhaps the bag size) is a new initiative. In any event, I immediately ordered one. When they arrived, I tore into them, gobbling down 4 or 5 in quick order.

There really isn't too much to say about this product. Delicious Hershey's chocolate, perfect for any sweet tooth. I admit that I prefer the milk chocolate and chocolate with almonds better than the cookies 'n' creme flavor, but when a powerful case of the munchies hits, they do just fine.

It's hard to imagine giving anything less than five stars for a two-pound plus bag of Hershey's. Try 'em, you'll like 'em.

The alternative is to try skimming the water out instead of draining it completely, but you will end up with soupy, diluted cheese. title: Flavor is nothing but BEET
text:
First I just want to say that I did not buy this product on Amazon; I bought it directly from the company. I spent close to this amount ($6) because I thought it sounded really tasty and convenient and I was willing to give it a try even though the price was a little high.

When I first poured the water and it turned a deep purple color (Turmeric Reishi) I was very surprised and confused, expecting a yellowish broth due to the turmeric. When I took a sip, the ONLY thing I tasted was BEET (which I personally find really nasty and dirty).

I decided to try ginger basil to see if it was any better and I am not kidding-- the flavor is indistinguishable. It is also a deep purple and tastes exactly like beet. Ginger and basil are both very distinct flavors and I didn't even get a hint of either.

If I had to describe the flavor, it tastes like beets (most prominently) with a grainy mouthfeel and an aftertaste of onion powder, salt, and pepper.

Haven't tried the third yet, but I don't have high hopes.

Bottom line: these flavors may be palatable to some people, but in my opinion, the company falsely advertised the flavors. I'm glad I didn't buy a bigger bundle!!

title: Nice everyday teay that's easy on the wallet
text:
Appropriate disclosure - I have not (as of yet) bought any of this tea off Amazon. I usually buy it locally.

UPDATE - 11/4/2020

I just bought 2 boxes of the Earl Grey from Amazon. They arrived quickly (thanks to me paying dearly for fast shipping) and the tea was everything it should be. I buy this tea regularly in local stores. I ordered it from Amazon because of the current pandemic. It's best not to go in stores if you don't have to. Everything was as expected. There's no difference between the Amazon version and the store bought version. Just nice Earl Grey tea for a reasonable price. Captain Picard would approve.

END UPDATE
-----------------------
ORIGINAL REVIEW
I have been drinking tea for a while. Several years. When I first started, I was drawn to loose leaf because I tend to be a purist in all that I do. Unfortunately, after a while, all the extra trouble of dealing with loose leaf just started to wear me down. I drink a lot of tea and frankly, it's often more of a hassle than it's worth.

When it comes to bagged teas, a tea like Twinings English Breakfast seems to hit the spot for me most of the time. It's not too strong. It could be considered really light if you steep it in a 16 ounce cup like I do but I think it's acceptable. I'm not a huge fan of really strong teas anyway. A lot of them tend to make me a little nauseous or something.

Anyway, this English Breakfast is pretty smooth. I'm not sure what the blend is but I think I detect a bit of Keemun (Which I do love) in there. I don't get that Ceylon flavor that you get in a lot of black tea blends. I'm really not a fan of Ceylon at all (This blend may have some but if it does, it doesn't punch you in the face like it does in some other blends).

I suppose this tea could be just a tad bit stronger and I wouldn't complain. The key with this (or any tea) in my opinion is to let it cool down enough so you can drink it without burning your mouth. I have found that most tea is almost tasteless when it's too hot to drink comfortably. Then, as it cools down, the flavor and aroma starts to really come out.

Anyway, this tea surprised me when I first tried it because I had completely ignored bagged teas, thinking they were all terrible. I guess this is far from great tea but for the price, I don't mind taking a bit of a hit in the quality department. It's a reasonably good product. I think I just got a box of 25 for $2 at the grocery store.

Twinings has several good bagged teas.

title: Amazing TRADITIONAL Croatian Christmas Snack!
text:
I grew up near the original Strawberry Hill povitica bakery in KCK and baked it a lot with my Croatian family. This is a tradition in KC that is delicious and I was excited to introduce my husband to it. We buy it at the local grocery store, and it’s still overly expensive buying it locally. Some of the flavors are too dry and sadly since they moved to their bigger location the quality has suffered a little. For some of the reviewers who are “traditionalists”, if you know you like a single log and not the S, and can see that they use the traditional Croatian S log, don’t complain about it after you buy it when the picture shows what it is. You get a lot of filling in relation to the dough, and that’s the point.
That said, if this is your first time buying, definitely try the English walnut. It’s never dry and perfect if you warm it up in the microwave for 30 sec. It is a staple around Christmas for us. For the other flavors, if they seem dry, try nuking them under a slightly damp paper towel, that usually does the trick for us.

title: Good Quality Red Reishi
text:
So, first off, I’m not going to get into a lot of the benefits of Reishi mushrooms. Do your own research on that if you’d like to. I will instead be focusing on flavor and the like instead.

This is a finely milled powder made of dehydrated Red Reishi. According to the manufacturer, this is organic, non-GMO, vegan, kosher, gluten and dairy free. All these are good marks, given the mushroom it’s not surprising, but good.

It does not really disperse easily in all liquids, so you might want to get something like a milk frother or a blender that will really agitate it if you want it in liquid form. This is common to a lot of fine milled powders that don’t actually dissolve, which this is. Thicker liquids, like say a smoothie, it will disperse in much easier. It will also drop out of suspension much easier in thinner liquids, so you want to mix it, then drink it right away.

It does not have any added sugar or anything to it, so drinking or eating it plain is gonna be a little unpleasant if you’re not into the taste of reishi. Which is definitely an acquired taste. I find it very bitter and just not great on its own. Of course, no added other ingredients is a good thing, because then you can add it to varying things and are not shoehorned into something. I personally tend to not drink a lot of coffee or drinks that this would mix into alright, so that’s nice. Instead, I’ve tried using it as more of a seasoning type flavor boost when cooking or baking, where I feel it works a lot nicer. I feel it just helps to add just a little extra something in the flavor department. Or you can hide it completely so you don't taste it.

Overall, if you like this type of supplement powder, and believe it’s a good fit for you, then this should be a pretty good option.

title: My all time favorite hot sauce-- get it while it is here!!!!
text: This is the sauce I used to drive over an hour to buy, and even scrounged up many ( I mean many!)  close to date glass bottles of online when my favorite online retailer was going to stop carrying it.  I can't exaggerate how happy I was to see it here in a plastic bottle. I suppose it is a bit less hot than rooster sauce, but I am not one to shy away from heat. Heat level was not my draw. For me, what makes this one worthy of hunting down and hoarding is the complexity of the flavor. It would be like adding the world's best habanero mash to a less chili-bright rooster sauce. I don't think it actually has habanero in it, but that is the best way I can think of to explain it. The flavor is rich and deep. For people who hate bland food, it's akin to what ketchup is to people who eat fries just for ketchup.  I add this hot sauce to everything: soups, cooked meats and veggies, salad dressing. If you like genuinely spicy food with complex flavors ( not too sweet, not vinegar forward, not a joke hot sauce with the worse arse in the title), you have to try this one. You can check out my other reviews to see that this is honest and I am all about spice. This is the gold standard for flavor. You can bring some to any dinner you are expecting to find bland and still enjoy your food.

title: Time to readjust your expectations and prejudicies.
text:
Fruitcakes have been the butt of jokes for years, and not totally undeserved. Most are dry blocks of artificially preserved 'food-stuff' that seem to have more in common with gastro-archeology than joyful snacking.

Collin Street Bakery in Corsicana, Texas has produced a product that remains true to its founders' German heritage (think of a Stollen cake with pecans on top instead of powdered sugar). Fresh, high-quality ingredients make this cake a delight. For over 100 years, their Deluxe Fruitcake has been delivering joy one bite at a time (hint: you can now order their cakes pre-sliced... a nice convenience).

The only alternative source for fruitcakes that I trust are the ones made by Gethsemane Abbey in Kentucky (Thomas Merton's old hangout). While the cake isn't quite as good Collin Street's, the bourbon they pour over it compensates wonderfully.

P.S. Don't be put off by the green-dyed candied cherries. Just think "festive!"

title: Great quality and taste!
text:
I love this stuff! If you taste it on its own, it has a fragrant coffee-like bitterness from the reishi that honestly is nice in combo with stuff like coffee or chocolate. (From what I’ve heard you want your reishi to have a bitterness because that means it has potent levels of beneficial compounds.) Serving size is a 1/2 tsp, but in my hot chocolate recipe I only use 1/4 because I like the flavor balance better. I’m not a coffee drinker but would definitely recommend it in coffee — I think it would complement quite well.

It’s a fine powder, appears fresh and high quality, and the company is really detailed about their process and quality on their site. Really appreciate them and this was a great intro to adaptogenic mushrooms!

Be aware that the powder could stain as it’s very sensitive to moisture. Also you probably want to take a toothpick to the teeth of the ziplock when you first open it, because the powder is so fine that it really packs in there. I had trouble on first opening but after clearing it I’ve had no issue closing it. Just pay close attention to make sure it really closes, or just transfer to another container.

5/5 easily!

title: I have found that I do have a reaction to allulose
text: There are cold days that I drink quite a bit more hot tea than others and I do like my tea sweet.  Now, I am a horrible aspartame sweeter user - yes, I know that it is not good for me, but of all the sweeteners out there, it is the one that satisfies my tastebuds the best.  So, I tried the allulose and at first it seemed to be a good substitute for my regular sweetener, but then...because we had a cold snap and I did my thing of drinking way too much tea to warm me up (so I can keep the heat in my house lower and save energy/money).  What followed was an evening spent in the bathroom!  Apparently the allulose disagreed with my insides when introduced in a larger quantity than normal.  Not like I went from one cup of tea to three gallons of tea, mind you, but that was the ONLY difference from the last time it was cold and I drank an equivalent amount of tea sweetened with aspartame.  So, I will say that will a cup or two of tea, the allulose was a good substitute, but in my case, if I go beyond that I'll switch back to aspartame so I don't spend another evening sitting on the porcelain throne!

title: surprisingly good for shelf-stable food
text:
I have been to many Indian restaurants and make my own Indian dishes and I found the flavor of this to be quite impressive. It is as good as some of the lentil dishes I've had in restaurants. The flavor is complex with a lot of spice and a touch of heat at the end of every bite. The rice is fluffy and well cooked. The grains aren't mushy or gummy and each was separate. The portion of curry to rice was pretty much perfect. The only tiny quibble I have about this is there is a bit of oil present in the curry that separates out, but it is easy to stir it back in. The lentils are also a bit grainy, but that's not uncommon in all lentils. I would have preferred that they have a bit more tooth, but that's a personal preference. The nutrition information says this is two servings. It is absolutely only one. Even a child might need more than half of this and it's not a huge portion for one person (especially at only 240 calories for the entire thing).

The container was easy to open and heat. You have to remove all of the plastic film for heating so there is a chance of the curry bubbling up and spattering so I recommend cover it with a silicone lid. The containers are easy to eat out of without spilling or other problems. As an emergency or lazy day food, I thought this was one of the best options I've ever had.

title: I almost don't miss my Tassimo any more!!!
text:
Years ago I had a Tassimo machine. The discs for those are able to use liquid so they could make some amazing latte's - they were SO good. When I moved it stayed with it's owner (since technically - I didn't have it - I just had access to it). I bought a Keurig about 2-3 yrs ago & have missed my lattes tremendously. I never even bothered to try any other versions of these since I knew it wouldn't compare to the Tassimo. But I have a lot of faith in the Gevalia name - and love their other coffee's - so despite the price I went ahead & tried these out. And I'm SO glad I did!! They're awesome!!

Here's how they work - it's 2 steps:
1) pour the powder packet into your cup (I use scissors despite their 'open here' tear strip - cause I've had way too many explode on me, probably something i"m doing wrong).
(2) Brew the cup & once complete stir it a bunch.
The instructions say to use the smallest cup size - the 6oz. If your cup is large enough you can also use the 8oz - that what I use & can't taste any difference. But keep in mind - it's a LOT of powder (and the powder still takes up space - even once it's dissolved into your coffee). I've never tried it with the 10oz so can't say much here.

I've tried all three - here's what I think:
Mocha - definitely the sweetest of all three - and my personal favorite. I like my coffee sweet (I use 4 splenda's with my regular coffee - which is the largest one - I think it's 10oz). With these I don't use any sweetener - they're sweet enough (not the same kinda sweet though - but still very sweet...it also may be that these use real sugar I assume).

Caramel - sweet - but not nearly as sweet as the Mocha. Much subtler taste to it...not my style - but I'm sure others would enjoy it.

Cappuccino - definitely the least sweet of the bunch. When I'm not in the mood for my regular sweetness, this is what I go for (& I still add about 1/2 a splenda).

So if you're looking for a frothy drink out of your keurig - I strongly recommend these!! And if you're using Amazon Subscribe & Save the price is the best one I've seen yet.

title: I used it to cook with and didn't like that too much
text: I purchased a 3 lb. bag for $25 of a different brand of xylitol from Amazon.  It was one of my first purchases on Amazon.  I used it to cook with and didn't like that too much.  I went too fast (I guess) because it hurt my tummy.  I was used to fiber in my body, so... I thought I could last... but it really upset my tummy, but the wonderful thing that I wanted to write a review about will follow... not that I've written that con.  So, basically, I did a lot of research.  I like to keep my teeth.  Anyway, I heard about xylitol and it's benefits and did the research and bought some of the mints (which really taste like candy, because xylitol is a sweetener) because they are so good for your teeth, but you have to remember to use them.  They work!!!  I loved them, but like I said, you have to remember to use them, after brushing or whatever, and I've bought gum with xylitol as well... but what I wanted to rave about is... I had 3 lbs. that I purchased and I was like how am I going to use all of this?  I thought it was going to be such a waste.  I was trying to figure out a way to use it and in fact I have purchased xylitol toothpaste (as well) among the other products mentioned, but it is quite expensive.  Well, it's not that it's expensive per se, but that you use toothpaste on a regular basis and upgrading to a more expensive product that you use regularly is expensive, because it's a regular upgrade (paying more for a product regularly)... anyhow I thought I could use my xylitol that I bought for cooking in my toothpaste.  I didn't buy it for that because I bought a tube of xylitol toothpaste when I wanted and it really tastes the same as regular toothpaste.  But I have noticed something spectacular and that is... since I have been using xylitol in combination with my regular toothpaste my breath has been amazing (no matter what I eat).  It really does it's job...  what I do is this...  I have my own bathroom and thus, do not share toothpaste.  So, what I do is squeeze the amount I want in my mouth (not on the toothbrush) because of what I'm going to do next... then, I wet my toothbrush and then... I put the wet toothbrush in a jar where I have the xylitol.  It's really neat because my brush is wet and so, it's going to just pick up the xylitol and cover the brush with it.  Yes, xylitol is a sugar, but it's so great for your teeth.  And I put the 3 lb. bag of xylitol in small jars and I'm still on my first small jar and haven't finished it yet. title: Horrible rip off!
text:
They throw together a couple of jars and a recipe card and call this a meal kit. First, they don't include the proteins. I'm ok with that as it makes it flexible and the kit can have a much longer shelf-life. However, be aware that that means the kit only has a few cheap ingredients that you're paying $35 for. But then you say it must be gourmet ingredients that are hard to get. No, they're things you could buy anywhere. Yes, but what about the saffron? Saffron is really expensive. The amount of saffron they give you is microscopic. Online recipes call for a teaspoon of it. This little plastic bag they included had about 1/1000th of a teaspoon. There's no way that amount could affect the flavor of all that rice, tomato, etc. It is just this company ripping off its customers.

Now let's talk about the flavor. It was nothing like paella. Way too much tomato sauce and chicken broth concentrate, not enough spice. Tasted more like some kind of tomato rice.

Stay as far away from this product as you can. I suspect this goes for all their other kits as well but I'm certainly not going to waste my money finding out.
