title: I like them as an alternative refreshment and occasional energy drink
text:
I normally like my morning cold brew or sometimes a hot coffee in the winter but there might be some days I skip either of those. On 2 such occasions I skipped the morning stuff and through the morning I was fine but with some running around and caring for newborn twins, I wanted some later afternoon pick me up. I have cans of Monster on hand and do tent to enjoy the taste even of the 0 cal offerings. But I didn't think I'd want to slug one of those and opted for these on both occasions

I like how they have a light but pleasant flavor and are a more simple and less artificial option to traditional energy drinks. Whether it was the caffeine or some placebo, I don't know but I felt it perked me up a bit to carry on through the day and some of the draining things I have to handle.

I don't feel that I'm too sensitive to caffeine so I don't usually have jitters or sleep issues if I have something caffeinated late morning or mid-day. This was no exception to that but I can't say how others would handle the caffeine but I enjoy these and for the price , they are a cheaper than a 24 pack of Monster at the wholesale club and probably a lot better for me in comparison. That's not to say I'll never touch the artificiality sweet energy drinks but its good to know there is a 'cleaner' option that I still can enjoy with Perrier!

title: Plump And Juicy Whole Peeled Tomatoes In A Balanced Tomato Puree Based Sauce With Bright Basil
text: If you are planning to make a homemade tomato sauce or a large batch of homemade tomato soup the  L'Oro Del Sud Italian Whole Peeled Plum Tomatoes are a must have ingredient. The 6lb 10oz can holds plump and juicy canned tomatoes in a thick tomato puree based sauce. The whole peeled plum tomatoes are tender and full of flavor. As I divided the tomatoes for multiple recipes, I found basil leaves sprinkled throughout. The tomatoes and sauce have a delicious flavor where the tomato is the star. It is perfectly balanced with natural sweet notes and acidic notes. I liked that I did not have to add any sugar to make it sweeter or baking soda to balance the sour notes. It is just perfect! I used some of the tomatoes in a sauce recipe and others for a tomato soup recipe. It was delicious in both applications. These tomatoes can also be frozen into portioned servings if you don't plan to use all the tomatoes at once. It is a high quality product with a tasty flavor. The ingredients for this product are all clean and recognizable. They include peeled tomatoes, tomato puree, salt, basil leaves, and citric acid. There are 24 servings per container. One half cup serving size includes 30 calories and 1g Protein. It is a Product of Italy. I loved these tomatoes and definitely plan on adding another order to our Amazon cart when we run low.

title: Tasty for Keto but bit dry
text:
We've tried 3 bags of different products from Orchard Valley Harvest. All 3 are good, tasty and fresh. 2 out of the 3 are more similar, which is the anti-oxidant mix and this keto mix. So am comparing the two.

If you are on a keto diet, this is a great trail mix, with some chocolate along with nuts. With myself not being on keto, I would not likely purchase the keto mix as it was overall a dry mix. Taste was good but it gets bit dry and bland after a while. I liked the anti-oxidant mix more as it had some dried fruit and salted dark chocolate almonds which was a great balance of flavors. The keto mix had dark chocolate almond butter almond which was not as good as the salted one, perhaps it just lacked that salty/sweet contrast that the anti-oxidant mix had.

That said, despite the clear favorite between the two for me, if I had a restricted diet, I would happily munch on OVH keto mix.

title: Fantastic oatmeal!
text:
I hate the glue-like consistency of rolled oats, and even the pulverized flavored oats with tons of sugar are pretty nasty to me. I love the texture of steel cut oats, and McCann's is one of the better brands (not all steel cut oats are the same). They taste great and are easy to prepare, either by using a rice cooker, slow cooker/crockpot, or preparing the night before by boiling half the required liquid, adding the oats, then cover and remove from the stove and let it sit overnight. Add a little more liquid if needed the next day, nuke in the microwave and its good to go! Try adding peanut butter and cocoa powder with one packet of Splenda per serving, dried fruit, cinnamon and brown sugar, or even a spoon of canned pie filling such as apple or cherry.

Others have mentioned problems with the packaging and receiving dented cans, but I think Amazon has fixed that problem. My 4 cans came shrink-wrapped together, along with a sturdy cardboard bottom. That was inside a larger box with a bunch of air pillows for padding, so the cans are completely unblemished.

title: Un gran caffe !
text:
I bought the four-pack two months ago. I brew espresso with a 15-bar De'Longhi espresso-making machine, and consistently have a fine "crema." The packaging of these four packs has English and French text; although from Italy, they may have been diverted from a run intended for the French market. The packaging states that this espresso is a blend of robusta and arabica coffees, but does not give the proportions of each.
The Lavazza 'Crema e Gusto' that I buy locally (sometimes hard to find) has its verbiage in English and Italian, and in addition, has a little dial printed on the back, showing that the blend is 70% robusta and 30% arabica.
Some coffee nerds think that the robusta component improves the 'crema', and ensures that the brewed espresso will have the requisite high caffeine content. (Espresso brewed in a 15-bar espresso maker is in contact with the almost-boiling water very briefly; the argument is that water that is forced through a robusta blend will brew an espresso with more caffeine than water forced through 100% arabica).
Some coffee nerds (snobs?) swear by arabica for everything, including espresso. Lavazza, also sells a 100% arabica espresso blend, and Illy makes makes a fine 100% espresso.
These claims could be tested by someone with the appropriate scientific apparatus. But I do very much favor Lavazza's 'crema e gusto'.
It works fine with a stove-top Moka pot, which is probably what most Italians use at home. But with the Moka pot, you don't get much, if any, 'crema."

title: Heavy on the spice, lacking in the pumpkin
text:
I bought this syrup along with several other Torani brand syrups to go with my brand new espresso machine I got for Christmas. I had read all the previous review that had warned about the lack of pumpkin flavoring in the syrup. I figured the product manufacturer had been made aware with all the previous complaints and had made improvements to fix the flavoring. Well I guess I was WRONG in my assumptions.

The product comes in very nice looking packaging and Amoretti is nice enough to supply a pump with your bottle of syrup (very nice touch). However the flavor of the syrup is like drinking a hot mug of nutmeg, cinnamon, and ginger. I thought I might have tasted a bit of pumpkin but then again I may just be associating those other spice flavors as ones you find in pumpkin pie and it was in my head. I ended up having to throw out the three cups of cappuccino I made and likely will have to dispose of this product all together as I have no other use for it.

So buyer beware, heed the previous reviews. This product should be labeled Autumn spice or something similar but certainly not pumpkin.

title: This product was great, while it was available
text:
After years of buying the adulterated stuff sold in supermarkets by the major brands, I was really happy to receive this 100% pure tea.

It was a little difficult at first to adjust to using so little of it per glass, but since it's pure tea, not mostly maltodextrose like the "big brands", you need to use far less of it. I finally settled on using a 1/4 teaspoon measuring spoon per glassful.

At first it looked awfully expensive, because the 8oz. bags appeared pretty small for the price, but once I realized how little needed to be used per glass it was easy to see that it was far more economical than the 3oz jars of adulterated stuff in the supermarkets. I never did stop to calculate how much I saved over the life of two 8oz bags, but it was substantial.

Sadly, when I came back to order more, it appears not to be available any longer, and I haven't been able to find another product like this one. :(

text:
What a treat - 55 pieces of candy that all contain caramel. Even better - the bag itself arrives in a huge box that contains a soft inner packaging, like a spongy layer of cardboard padding, and a reusable ice pack too. This had defrosted and was mainly liquid, but it’s a thick plastic bag and there were no leaks. It’s a nice touch and makes sure the chocolate is delivered in tip-top condition.

Of course the chocolates all disappeared in about 2 days, the whole family reluctantly agreed to ‘test drive’ these caramel creations and provide their feedback. No surprise that it was a thumbs-up all round, especially for the M&Ms, we had not tried these before and found them chewier and more satisfying than expected.

The bag is also excellent value, works out to be exactly 20 cents per item and you get to freeze the gelpack and use it again.
Would it be churlish to point out that there are too many Snickers and not enough of the Milky Way Simply Caramel? Probably.

title: Energy Drink Without The Jitters
text:
Wow! The flavors are right on the money. The blue can tastes just like blue raspberry. The red can tastes like carbonated [cherry] Robitussin (the only one I didn't like the flavor of). The yellow can tastes exactly like the flavor of a freshly cut sweet pineapple as you chew it, not a hint of tartness. And the green can tastes like classic Mountain Dew.
Nevertheless, the food coloring is so heavily saturated that you'll have to drink these sodas with clothing you don't want permanently stained.
That said, I'm not exactly sure what these drinks were designed to do but from my experience these drinks kept me wide awake without crashing afterward. I'm usually quite clumsy but under the influence of these energy drinks I had no jitters and my hand and eye coordination were spot on all day long, not a single thing in my house tipped over or dropped because of my clumsiness. It definitely came as a relief to my family when for the past week I didn't utter a single curse word. This drink was created for gamers (at least that's the impression I got from the graphics on these cans). I'm not a gamer but I am a huge fan of flavorful energy drinks - and of Mountain Dew. Whether this drink is designed for gamers or not, it definitely beats the tastes of the G Fuel lineup (even though they have way more flavors than Game Fuel). And if Faze Rug happens to read this (or fans of Faze Rug like the Rug Rat that I am), my deepest most heartfelt apology to you on my opinion.

title: Well, it tastes like Recaldent...
text:
I work in a dental clinic and have been using Recaldent for many years. I have easy access to it for myself, but it's disappointing that the powers at be have lobbied to make MI Paste, Trident Xtracare, and other Recaldent products unavailable in America. CCP-ACP is far superior at remineralizing teeth when compared to Fluoride. Plus it's safer!! It's derived from milk. (Don't get me started on fluoridation of our water).

That said, this gum definitely tastes like Recaldent. It causes the mouth to salivate strongly for the first 5-10 minutes. I generally have to use a spittoon once or twice before I can sit back and enjoy chewing the gum. -- The flavor is OK. It tastes like purple grapes covered in MI Paste.

I can't read anything on the label. I truthfully have no idea what all is added to this gum. However, based on the strong taste of CCP-ACP, I would assume that you're getting your money's worth on that substance...... which is why I bought this gum.

I had no side effects to name and usually right after I wake up and get out of bed, I could feel the grogginess fade away rather quickly. I recently started drinking large amounts of green tea after reading about the health benefits (around 6-8 packs per day). Since I drink so much, I wasn't going to bother with the fancy expensive green teas and just wanted something that was cheap. I first tried the green tea from Costco, but wasn't very happy. Costco's green tea tends to be pretty messy, and there is a lot of powder in the bag (which is supposed to be added to the tea I guess). I wasn't overall happy with the flavor. I then saw this on Amazon and decided to give it a try. The price is comparable to Costco (I think slightly cheaper even). The packaging for the tea feels much better than Costco and isn't messy like the Costco tea.

Last but certainly not least, I think this tea tastes better than the green tea bags from Costco. I have started mixing the Costco bags with these to try mask the Costco tea flavor, but still use it up.

title: Wonderful texture, ok flavor
text:
This mix is pretty good! I’ve been making a lot of keto desserts, almost all almond flour based, in my quest to soothe my poor deprived sweet tooth. Mine invariably end up super crumbly, and taking a bite - or even taking them off the cookie sheet - scatters crumbs everywhere. This mix does NOT have that issue - the cookies were fluffy and almost cake-y and soft, no issues with crumbling or falling apart. Great texture that I was missing!

Flavor-wise they are ok. Snickerdoodles don’t normally have a strong flavor, but I didn’t taste any cinnamon at all, just kind of a sweet almond flavor. Not bad at all, but not remarkable. They did satisfy my sweet cravings, and let me feel like I was eating a real cookie.

The mix was easy to make, although the “dough” is really sticky. Scooping it out with a spoon was easy enough, but it says to flatten them and that only happened through gravity rather than pressing down. I used coconut oil rather than butter, I’m not sure if that makes a difference.

Overall, great! I definitely want to try more varieties from Kiss My Keto, these were good!

title: Bad Smell, Worse Aftertaste
text:
This sauce is not nearly hot enough to justify such a poor aroma and flavor.

The smell is extremely pungent but not with notes of chili or spice but more akin to cheap vinegar or spoiled wine with strong notes of loam or decaying forest. This alone I imagine would be more than enough to turn most people away.

Visually both the bottle and sauce are very appealing with a modern design and deep burnt red marbled color respectively. Also, once it is on your tongue and you get over the initial negative reaction to the scent it is not entirely offensive however it does not taste good by any stretch. There are definite notes of mushroom flavor present but they are heavily overpowered by an almost rotten vegetation flavor. Given I have only tried truffles a few times in my life but never have I had an experience similar to this. The heat has a delay and is similar in intensity to normal Tabasco.

The aftertaste, similarly to the aroma, is dominated by a flavor of spoiled sweet wine and decay. This is easily the most unpleasant part of the overall negative experience.

Please, save your money and buy a bottle of Tabasco, Cholula, or Sriracha instead. Any of those are leagues better than this and at a more reasonable price.

title: Refreshing and delicious
text:
I drink tons of tea daily and I actually study what tea is. I ordered this & I wasn't sure what to expect. I have drank really poor quality tea in the past. When this showed up, I was very pleasantly surprised by the scent. A good balance of sharp peppermint and mellow spearmint. Very harmonious.
I brewed close to a gallon of this tea. I tried some hot & the rest went into a large pitcher of iced tea. It's gorgeous hot. Most excellent as a palate cleanser and handles being sweetened with sugar or even honey. If your tummy is gassy or if you feel nauseated, brew it & sweeten it some. Cool to lukewarm and drink. That should help enough to make you more comfortable.
As iced tea, I brewed a concentrated infusion & then added cold water and plenty of ice. It's delicious and not at all "in your face". I didn't sweeten it & it works well with a bit of lemon. Very refreshing and tasty.

This is a genuinely good tea. Try it and you won't be disappointed.

title: Caution
text: Touting this product has 33% less sodium may be true but the reason that claim can be made is because the granules are 33% finer than regular salt. Each grain of salt is 33% smaller - thus 33% less sodium, however,  with the granules being so fine a lot more comes out of the salt shaker - quickly! Even covering some of the holes in the shaker lid does not help much. Consequently, you are getting 33% more granules from the shaker which translates to 33% more sodium. So it is a wash. A person could make the same claim by using 33% LESS regular salt. This is not worth the money when you can adapt sodium intake, by that percentage, with your own salt shaker.

title: So adding 1/2 scoop to 16 oz of juice works a lot better. I've added it to a orange/celery/carrot/apple/beet/kale juice and ...
text: So I wanted to write this review on the reboot with joe website, but can't figure out how to do it. I ordered it from there. Anyways, here's my experience with the protein powder. I found that the whole scoop just is too grainy in 16 oz. So adding 1/2 scoop to 16 oz of juice works a lot better. I've added it to a orange/celery/carrot/apple/beet/kale juice and a carrot/apple/beet juice. The powder in both juices I have found complement the taste very well. The powder makes me feel fuller too. I also added the protein powder to a cucumber/spinach/lemon/celery/kale juice and well I don't really enjoy the taste of that particular juice in the first place, but adding the protein powder made it so much worse in my opinion. So I would stick to just adding the protein powder to the juices you enjoy already. I don't think that the protein powder makes juices taste better in any way. Also, I pour in the protein powder first, then dissolve it with a little water first before adding in the juice and shaking it up. I found that's the best way to get it to dissolve completely. It tasted fine when added to a cucumber/spinach/ginger/celery/grape/kale/apple/chard/parsley juice as well. So although I personally thought it went well with beet juices, it doesn't take away from other juices you already enjoy which is nice. Love that it's vegan and packs a lot of protein! The added vitamins for the immune system and making hair, skin, and nails healthy is really great too!

title: Made in Michigan since 1866
text:
I like "Vernor's", and drink it all the time. It is old fashioned drink from Michigan, since 1866, and the labeling was known for its lovely green and gold colors and the gnome character. If you look at the can it is actually called ginger soda instead of ale and is different than typical ginger ale in taste. Vernors has a strong vanilla presence, is smoother and more moist, and sweeter than a ginger ale. It is closer to a cream soda than ginger ale, very good. A ginger ale is more dry, higher in carbonation, and has a spicier bite to it. Vernors has 39 grams sugar per can, versus 33 grams per can for Schweppes Ginger Ale. Neither has caffeine.

The recipe has changed a bit over the years mostly in the choice of sweeteners. They use the same high fructose corn syrup that the cost-cutting mega soda companies use, rather than the cane sugar they used to use. The down side to that is that the corn syrup syrup drowns out some of the flavors. Many microbrews are using cane sugar again, although it costs more, to get a better taste. Vernor's is still aged in oak barrels for 3 years, no doubt accounting for the smoothness. All in all a great soda for anytime. The soda is also known, like other ginger drinks, for its use as a home remedy for an upset stomach.
Vernor's is a regional soda, and there are many areas of the country you can't find it in. That is why it sells here. They may be selling it in glass bottles again soon, at least there is a page that says so the day I am writing this comment. Search at Amazon for ASIN: B001JK2SEG to see what I mean. Vernors has quite a history, and there are two books at Amazon about the soda. The first is Vernor's Ginger Ale (Images of America: Michigan) ISBN-10: 0738551856. The second book is "The Vernor's Story: From Gnomes to Now" ISBN-10: 0472066978 a book about the company's marketing green and gold packaging with the famous gnome, and Vernor's fans.

title: 8000lbs Deadlift: Confirmed
text: Great tasting organic tea, whether it’s hot or cold outside. Before trying this product I could barely deadlift a standard barbell. I drank Jock White Tea for the first time on the way to the gym and I could tell a noticeable difference in my output. I was suddenly able to “Get After It” and no exercise or weight seemed too much. Since I was feeling so great in the gym, I decided to see if I could set a new PR in deadlift.  I slapped a plate on each side of the bar and prepared for the lift, to my surprise it was extremely easy, so I put two more on and two more and two more. I repeated the lift with easy despite the weight that I continued to add. Soon I had maxed out the bar, but it was still too light. I asked two ladies if they could stand on the plates at either end of the bar for added weight, skeptical at first, but they eventually went along with my crazy plan. I prepared for the lift with each woman balancing on the stack of plates loaded onto the two ends of the bar. After numerous reps that continually increased in weight, I was still able to lift the weight with easy. By this time everybody in the gym was watching the madness that was going on and a small crowd gathered to watch. I asked the two biggest guys I could find to stand on the plates, just as the women had done the set before. These guys were huge, I’m talk some true monster, real silverbacks. With the added weight I prepared for my next set. Ready, lift...still I found the lift to be easy, so I asked the women to sit on the shoulders of the men for my next set. With spotters standing by to catch the men and the women should they lose their balance (safety first), I completed my final set with ease. Long story, short: 8000lbs deadlift confirmed. Standby: Get Some!

title: The perfect sandwich cookie.
text:
As a child I remembered liking Hydrox better than Oreo. But it seemed like I was the only one.

20 years later, would that still be the case? Would these recapture the taste I remembered?

I think it's unfair to try and compare something to a memory. Anyone who says these don't taste like they remembered is setting an almost impossible bar. Something could be the exact same, but may not taste like you once thought. I know Mac & Cheese hasn't changed but the way I experience it does. So the only fair comparison is to Oreo. Is this a better sandwich cookie? Yes. In every way.

Hydrox smells of rich cocoa. You take a bite and get a satisfying crunch. It tastes of real chocolate. The cream tastes like a real cream filling. The texture of the filling is superior as well. I never had a problem with the sweetness of Oreo (we're talking about chocolate cookies here) but the sweetness of Hydrox is perfect as well.

10 times out of 10 I would choose Hydrox over Oreo. It's just a better cookie in every way.

title: Great Coffee, not so great design. UPDATED! AWESOME!
text:
This is my second go round ordering this product. First time I had the issue with the exploding K-Cup and coffee grinds in the brewed cup of coffee. The coffee itself is great if you are able to brew it correctly. I stayed away my past few orders and had other brands and even variety packs with no issues at all. I checked back in with this product saw the reviews and figured maybe they corrected the design of the K-Cup but I was wrong. A work around for it for me at least is to put the K-Cup in the machine and press down so the bottom is punctured then close the lid to puncture the top to brew. If I just place the cup in the machine itself the bottom doesn't get punctured leading to a bad brew and wasted coffee (I've tried this on 3 different machines).The variety and quality of the coffee itself is great so I don't mind the extra step in brewing, just hope it's corrected someday.

**Update 10/22/13

I have been in touch with customer service and they've been great and responsive. Came home from work today with a new set of K-cups, went straight to my brewer to give it a shot and they were perfect! New packaging and new design works great. I'll definitely be a repeat customer again!

title: Fresh, great tasting slivered almonds that come in a resealable package
text: This review if for Fisher Slivered Almonds.  To start with I was very pleased with the packaging.  The bags of almonds came packaged in a cardboard box (inside a shipping box) and that packaging kept the bags and contents from being crushed.  The almonds in each bag were fine. Because these are slivered almonds a 10 oz. bag is actually quite large.  The bags open easy (just tear off the top) and have a zip lock seal to retain freshness.  Normally I use slivered almonds on salads and definitely with green beans but I tried these as a snack too. Very fresh and very tasty!  I've seen comments in other reviews that indicated the taste is bland and they don't crunch enough.  I love almonds but if you want a crunch you should go with roasted or even natural whole almonds.  Slivered almonds have a softer consistency and they definitely don't have a roasted almond taste.  There are definitely different products for different uses so choose accordingly. If you're looking for slivered almonds these are packaged  well, taste great and a great choice!

title: Varied, but not in a good way.
text:
I've purchased Jamaican Blue Mtn, Brazilian, Columbian(twice) , Guatemalan, Costa Rican, and Malawi...all peaberry.
I have my own highly reliable source for peaberry Kona that I will always use, so no reason to buy it from Volcanica.

JBM: It's expensive, but the quality was worth it to me. I've never had JBM in Jamaican-brewed style, so my assessment may be a little amateur.
Columbian: first purchase was rich, robust, flavorful, and what I remember in a good Columbian. And it was peaberry...I looked. On my second purchase, I received a mis-pick of Columbian Supremo with a little barcode sticker for peaberry on it. I had already started brewing my first pot before noticing...and, believe me, there's a difference between supremo and peaberry. They should correct mistake if you contact them.
Brazilian: Good for the price, especially for my first time trying it.
Malawi: Not bad. More citrus-y, so not my favorite. Luckily it is priced with the less expensive range beans.
Costa Rican: Good flavor that builds as it sits on your tongue. Worth the price.
Guatemalan: Better than other brands I've purchased, even for the price...which is acceptable range.

title: Try it , you might like it
text: What can I say about this product except I love it and I am so happy I found it. I came about this product because I spent my 50th birthday in the ER with kidney stones. Driving home that night with my nursing student daughter I knew I has to give up my gallon a day Iced Tea habit with Soda mixed in on occasion and switch to a life of water. I never want to go through all that pain again. So I had her stop at a c-store to look for a bottle of lemon juice toadd to my water because if I enjoyed the taste of jst water I would not have been in the situation I had just gone through. Well she cane out with several bottles of flavored water , which I knew I did not like and she could tell I wa not going to drink these. So on the way home she remembered she had some "lemon packets" from the hospital she worked at. She said give them a try and gave me the 4 she had in her purse. They were True Lemon packets and I tried them and liked them. I went searching and found them here on Amazon for cheaper then the price on the True Lemon website. So I had gone through 2 boxes of 500 when I decided to try the True Lime. WOW! I liked the True Lemon but I LOVE the True Lime. I have ordered 2 boxes of the 500 and have ordered a box for my youngest daughter at college and we both love it, including a few of her friends at school. I use it at work and keep it in my desk.I have it in the car glove box and take it on vacation with me. I use about three packs per 16oz. bottle of water. the packet says it is equal to a wedge of lime and that might be true. I just prefer the stronger lime taste to my water. I am now on the subscribe and save program for this item and well not stop using it. I have gone cold turkey on soda and Iced Tea and with using these true lime/ lemon packets it has not been one problem for me. I have cut out massive daily amounts of calories and caffeine and I have noticed I dropped a few pounds. ( Just a few.)  I believe that this item has actually contributed to my having a better state of health and trust me I am no heath nut. Give it a try and you might be surprised by how well you like it.

title: My favorite protein bar (and I've tried several)
text:
I started out my protein bar journey trying *multiple* brands of chocolate mint bars, and this is by far my favorite: in taste, ingredients, and nutrition. With Subscribe and Save, I was able to bring the price down (including the multiple items discount). I took a gamble and ordered the variety box to try all 4 kinds.

Now, the bars are different in texture depending on the flavor (see below). I would say that the two with coconut taste more sweet, even though the raspberry has 5 grams of sugar and all the others have 7. This is the same or well below the other bars I've tried, and they do not have a strong Stevia/diety aftertaste (I hate Stevia and can usually notice it right away, but I don't notice it *while* eating these bars, I just need some water afterward, and it dissipates quickly).

Dark Chocolate Coconut: Tastes straight up like a (dark chocolate) Mounds candy bar.

Chocolate Raspberry Coconut: Tastes like a raspberry Mounds bar, if that existed.

Chocolate Almond Crunch: Nice and dense and chewy, reminiscent of an almond butter cookie dough, with hints of cinnamon and crunchy cacao nibs.

Mint Chocolate Chip: So dense and chewy, exactly how I like them! Perfect balance, not too sweet. I have not tried them in the fridge yet, but don't put them in the freezer-- they'll be rock hard! (They will thaw, of course.)

In my opinion, the first two (coconut and raspberry coconut) are more suitable for dessert or sweet snack, and the other two (almond crunch and chocolate mint) are my on the go meal replacement/complement. I imagine my kids would abscond with and happily devour any of these, but I don't plan on sharing too many. 😊

The ingredients seem great in comparison to other bars. Good amounts of protein and fiber. I have no issues with sugar alcohols, so no problems there.

I'm glad I stumbled on these at the store to try, which of course you could do if you're hesitant about trying a whole box. I love them all and they are my favorite protein bar.

1: Chocolate Raspberry Coconut on top, Chocolate Almond Crunch on bottom.
2: Mint Chocolate Chip

I serve it up in individual zipper bags for my daily breakfast, and add to it a tablespoon of crushed almonds to balance the protein and carbs better. If it had more fiber in it, and less sweetener (like the 7-grain Kashi), the net carbs would be lower. (My goal is to eat 25 g of protein for every 45 net carbs I ingest.) The flavor is good. I enjoy it with raisins and dried cranberries added, or alone with the almonds. I've lost 5 pounds in the first two weeks of focusing on proteins and carbs, and I know this was at least a small part of that process!

title: Doesn't pack much of a flavoring punch, tastes somewhat sweet, and it's not just shiitake mushrooms
text:
I love umami seasonings, so I decided to try this powder to compare with other umami products out there (such as Takii umami powder and Trader Joe's umami seasoning) that I've used in the past. A few of my observations:

-While tasting it by itself, it tasted a bit too light. The flavor profile is somewhat sweet (which was a surprise) and has a slight tanginess to it, probably due to the tomato and/or onions in the ingredients. I had to add a quite a bit more of it to my veggie stirfry to get that same level of umami as TJ's or Takii.
-The seasoning is very fine in consistency, though I find it too fine of a powder that can get bit messy (powdery and gets all over the place like flour). In comparison, TJ's umami seasoning was a bit more coarse and Takii was probably the easiest to handle since they were granules.
-The powder has more than just shiitake mushrooms, much like to TJ's umami seasoning, which has a ton of added ingredients. TJ's has the most additives (thyme, onions, mustard seed); this product has shiitake, salt, onion and tomato; Takii has just shiitake and salt. Out of the three I thought Takii had the most umami flavor with the fewest ingredients/additives (Trader Joe's umami seasoning is my least favorite by far of the three).

title: Hoosier Hills is the way to go....
text: Let's face it.  No cheese powder product is as healthy as we'd all like it to be.  The product's reason for living is convenience. However, if one is accustomed to using such products, one may be hard pressed to find a better product for the money. A side by side taste test with Kraft Mac&Cheese packets yields interesting results.  Our family, the five of us, preferred HHF's cheese to Kraft, 5 to zero.  The interesting thing is, when tasting just the cheeses, it's not even close!  Kraft's tastes bitter and chemical like.  Just a guess, but I'm bettin that Kraft's has an appreciable dose of 'flavor enhancers' which include MSG and the like.  HHF's tastes much more like a natural cheese.  Kraft's flavor when combined with macaroni, milk, and butter is hard to beat, but at what cumulative cost?  Who really knows.  HHF's requires about 1.5 times as much powder to compare to Krafts unless one adds a bit of salt, but I feel more confident that HHF's is not laden with potentially harmful chemicals, and it's cheaper to make your own.

title: Good flavor...Some tough parts
text:
I ordered this and the spicy from Buffalo Bills bills and this was definitely better than the spicy. This has a good peppery flavor and it's a lot of jerky. You will need scissors or a knife to cut pieces that you can eat. The slabs are like 7 X 10.

Like with the spicy jerky I'm not so sure this is the best quality meat. My package still has plenty of fat, gristle, and tough pieces of things you just cant chew up. I've tried lots of jerky and with good quality jerky I could eat a whole pound bag and never have the fat, gristle, and pieces I can't chew up like this.

Bottom line...This is better than the grocery store/gas station jerky and if I rated on just flavor I would give it 4 stars but the tough pieces that you can't chew takes away from the overall quality experience. Since I have had plenty of jerky that's not like that I know it can be done.

UPDATE...

Promptly after placing the review I received a call from Choo Choo R Snacks asking about my review. Based on my review the premium jerky was recommended and if I would like they would sound out 2lbs. If I didn't care for those I was offered a full refund on my purchase. That is great customer service! I'm happy to say that the premium jerky arrived today and is fantastic. It's on par with the best trade show jerky mentioned above that I have had. Thank again for turning a potential bad experience into a great one.

title: Tasty flavors, beware the soft textures and nature of the natural gum base!
text:
On a whim, I purchased Simply Gum's "Cleanse". I became enamored with the brand and splurged to try all the flavors. I was not disappointed. The ingredients are simple and tasty. The texture is softer than most chewing gums but for me that was a plus.

FLAVOR:
The flavors are well balanced in the Boost, Cleanse, and Revive flavors. The Ginger, Fennel, Peppermint, Spearmint, Coffee, Cinnamon, and Maple flavors are just as advertised. When you pop any of the varieties it into your mouth, there is a burst of flavor which fades gradually away over the course of a 20 minute chew. I'd say there is about 1/4 the flavor at the 30 minute mark as there was at the beginning.

TEXTURE/FRESHNESS:
The initial bite of the gum is quite hard, but the wax and chicle soon warm to a pleasantly soft chew. Some might say that it is too soft when compared to the wrigley's varieties. I'd say it has the toughness of a cheesecake. An odd comparison perhaps, but again a satisfyingly soft chew. The greatest irony is that the gum is too fresh. My supermarket pack had been sitting a while on the shelf. The more stale it is, the more 'tough' the gum is. I popped a spearmint into my mouth for a car ride. I could tell it was VERY fresh as it took very little time to soften. Within about 10 minutes or so, the gum had transformed in my mouth into a big, spearmint flavored loogie. Thank goodness they supply sheets of post-chew wrap.

BUBBLES
This is a CHEWING gum, not a bubble gum. The nature of the chicle base causes it to be very sticky when it gets outside of your mouth.

title: One of my favorite ginger shots/elixirs
text:
This is a nice ginger elixir with a simple ingredients list and good genuine flavor. It is just ginger, lemon, honey, and cardamom (all of it organic). It is also flexible in that it can be consumed straight up as a shot, with a little water to open up some of the flavors, or mixed into something (like a beverage or food dish).

The elixir comes in a glass bottle with a metal screw on lid. It is all well packed in bubble wrap, then plenty of packing paper, and then in a cardboard box, so it should easily make it through shipping safely (much better packed than most other glass containers I have gotten recently). Once opened, it needs to be refrigerated. If you plan to buy several and store a couple, I would suggest a dark place as the bottle is clear and you will want to protect the elixir from light.

The elixir is tasty, but does have that stronger ginger taste (like eating real ginger slices at a sushi restaurant). It has a nice bit to it combined with a zing of the lemon and the sweetness of the honey. Consuming it straight up will have the main ingredients overwhelming the cardamom, making it hard to taste, but if you add some water or mix it into something (like a drink), it cuts some of those core flavor profiles down and allows the cardamom to be more noticeable and present (although still not in your face and subtle).

I like this elixir and the core ingredients that it is made with. It tastes good and is good for you. When I have an upset stomach, I sometimes take something with ginger in it to help setting it down, and this elixir fits that need with a good balance of healthy ingredients. I like it so much right out of the bottle that I need to be more reserved and save some to try cooking with or mixing into other things. If you’re looking for a good ginger bite with some warm honey sweetness and some lemon punch, then I would recommend you try this elixir or possibly one of the other flavor variants.

title: Oats!
text:
First, as is always important, watch your prices--remember that ordering here may see price fluctuations far more often than your local store.

Second, the box is the same good-quality Quaker Oats that I've been eating for a long, long time. It's good--and a great ingredient. Storage-wise, there is a smidgen of challenge to house the larger box, but that's easily solved. Especially if you take the sealed bags out and just store the opened oats in an airtight container.

These are the "old-fashioned" oats, so it's a larger part of the oat than the "quick" ones. These work better in most recipes and have a fuller texture. The trade-off is that they do take longer to cook.

The extra-large amount meets the need of having oats on hand for a while!

title: My favorite faux coffee
text:
At one time I drank 1-2 pots of coffee a day. A few years ago my blood pressure was in the 140s, so my doctor said I needed to cut back on caffeine, salt, and alcohol. I had been drinking coffee for so long, and missed having a warm beverage in the morning, so I decided to find a substitute. Of all the ones I've tried, Dandy Blend is my favorite; I've been drinking it for a few years now. It goes well with cookies, toast, and chocolate.

It does not taste like coffee, nor do any of the coffee substitutes that I tried. I wanted a hot beverage that I could drink in the place of coffee, and for me, this one has stood the test of time. If you want coffee flavor, you will only get that from coffee. If you want a warm beverage to drink in its place, I recommend this one.

BTW, I check my blood pressure almost every morning and found alcohol raises it the most. YMMV.

I love 1/2 teaspoon of this in my coffee with a tiny amount of stevia. It is just right for my taste. I started with a tablespoon of cacao in my coffee and thought it was pretty good. But, as I tapered the amount down, I liked it better.

I'm using it for the pleasure of tasting a bit like a mocha latte and for health benefits. Studies indicate proven benefits fo heart, blood flow, and blood pressure. Newer research indicates the raw form has some prebiotic properties for the colon.

My body doesn't tolerate most of the prebiotic and probiotic supplements. So, I am working to find real food products that do what nature intended. I was ill for a long time and had a major tummy surgery. I'm doing better, but it involves a lot of trial and error. This Raw Organic Cacoa is good. I don't know yet if it is working as a prebiotic, but my tummy is happy with it.

title: 50% Sugar
text:
I couldn't figure out why my stir-fry tasted sweet, so I started checking ingredients labels and lo and behold... This Hoisin sauce is more than 50% sugar. The back of the jar lists 2 tablespoons of sauce as containing 1.4 tablespoons of added sugar. (18g)

Everyone has sugar in their kitchen. If you wanted several tablespoons of corn syrup/sugar in your food, you would add it. They're using it as filler to give you less product. Plus, it just tastes disgusting.

For reference, one tablespoon of granulated sugar is 12.5 grams, and one tablespoon of High Fructose Corn Syrup has 16g of sugar. Thus the 18g of added sugars is equal to 1.4T granulated sugar or 1.12T of HFCS

title: Excel-ent Is Right!
text:
A long time ago (early 90's) I first found these at Sam's Club. Then, it was no longer reasonable for me to continue membership, so I missed them for a lot of years. After that, I worked for a Personal Care Home and was able to get some again. That was 6 years ago. Now, finally, we meet again, and I can rest assured that I will always have descent mashed potatoes quickly at my fingertips.

I tried others when I didn't have Potato Pearls. They are not as good. Especially the ones that begin with I and end with oan. You can't have those as leftovers. They always turned out runny the second day, with only warming them up and not adding anything.

Now these, these Potato Pearls, they're the bee's knees of instant mashed potatoes. I hate calling them instant mashed potatoes, I feel like it cheapens them. They are just mashed potatoes. They are so good in flavor, texture, and ease of making them, I want to tell everybody. You can't go wrong with these. They're worth it.

October 28, 2012-I stopped using these for awhile and when I was ready to use them again I ordered a new carton. I was having a hard time getting a good batch made, and thought that the few poor reviews here, were right. I thought I might have to send them back. Then, I finally reread the directions, and here's what you need to know. It is absolutely necessary to pour the boiling water INTO the Potato Pearls when making small batches. Pouring the Potato Pearls into the boiling water is ONLY if you are making the whole carton (or bag). I know, it seems like it shouldn't make any difference, but it DOES! Trial and error proved it to me. I can't believe I had forgotten how to make them! They're so good.

title: I have used for years, love and recommend this product highly!
text:
This is as close to a perfect and super versatile seasoning as you can get!

I first came across this product about 5-6 years ago at Costco. They were demonstrating it with cheese & spinach ravioli drizzled with olive oil mixed with the product. Mahhhhvelous Flavor!!! Hooked & purchased!

I now use it as a seasoning flavor called for or experimented with on/in breads, pastas, veggies, all meats - roasted, baked or fried - fish, beans, lentils, sauces, salad dressings (try it mixed with powdered Ranch Dressing for a Ranch Italian salad dressing or on foods!) soups, stews, etc., etc., etc. The options are practically endless. You can just sprinkle on or mix with oil, butter or other products to make a spread, sauce, rub or whatever your imagination takes you to try it on.

However, sometimes there does need to be a stronger garlic or parmesan presence in the dish, so I just add more of whatever is needed, like you do in any kind of dish; you season it to your taste. You can usually figure out what to do if too much flavor, by adding more sauce, food, butter, oil or ? to soften it.

Experiment!!!! You'll find yourself using it in more dishes as you go along. Always start out with less, like you do with any new seasoning, then adding more while cooking until you find what works taste-wise for you - different dishes may need different amounts, too. Egg Dishes!!! Wonderful!

I was reading through the 1 & 2 star complaints and their not recognizing this as a seasoning/spread **mix** actually seems to be the problem, not the product. Also, addressing the complaints about receiving a powdered product instead of a 'spread'? The pictures show a powdered product, the picture of the side label states "mix with butter" At what point do you take responsibility for your own error?

Some were unhappy because there wasn't enough garlic or parmesan taste, others unhappy because there was too much! Taste is always a personal thing, right? Plus something that tasted one way one day might taste different another day in another type of dish, depending on a number of factors, too, so if not to your taste the first time, try again.

At least one complaint was over the fact there's silicon Dioxide, Micro Crystalline Cellulose used for anti-caking, plus the L-Glutamic Acid in the product but these are also part of the shelf stabilizing. The L-Glutamic Acid can be a very legitimate warning for some medical conditions relating to neurological, nervous, kidney or liver disorders. Investigate what or if any amount may be considered safe for you. It's toward the bottom of the ingredient list, so a small amount.

These and similar products are in many/most dried foods, but many preservatives were stated for years as not particularly good for anyone by health enthusiasts (for whom I am grateful as they brought to light a lot of products we now stay away from because of legitimate studies - trans-fats anyone?) My sister couldn't use anything with sulfur dioxide, a product used to preserve the color of dried fruit, as that truly isn't good for you if you have or may have a family tendency towards cancer, but not a problem for many others. However, with all the health concerns, aside from tests paid for by the product makers instead of independent testers, these 3 have been listed under the GRAS label as "Generally Recognized As Safe". Like anything else, even MSG - in light of recent studies, it's been found 'not guilty' of many issues - for most people they are safe when used moderately.

This product is shelf stable for at least a year, I had my first 18 oz for about 2 years as I got used to using it & it never got rancid or funny tasting, but I'm not recommending keeping it that long, it's just how it lasted for me in the way I stored it. Now I have to replace it much sooner as I'm using it in more and more dishes.

Wow! Sorry for the novelette! Do hope it helps though!

title: Folgers, I'm baaack!
text:
This coffee is so good! For years I've been mail-ordering expensive artisanal coffees. It was getting to be a bit ridiculous, cost-wise, so I thought I'd give Folgers a try again, thirty years later. I'm so glad I did. I like this "Gourmet Supreme" very much. The Classic Roast was fine, too, but maybe a little more bitter. The really mild one --"Simply Smooth"--is not very flavorful, IMO. These are the only three I've tried so far.

I use 68 grams of coffee per liter of water, which is just the perfect strength for me. The container is 680-something grams, so I get ten pots of coffee from a container. With the more expensive coffees I was buying, it was always 85 grams of coffee per liter of water (so four pots of coffee per 12-oz. bag). Not sure why I had to use so much more; maybe I was grinding those beans to the wrong size. I highly recommend Folgers, which is already ground to the correct size for my auto-drip coffee maker and is also fine for pour-over. Give it a try!

title: Not a fan of the new formula or flavors
text:
I really enjoyed this when I first found it. I have a bunch of unusual food allergies and need liquid calories and was so happy when I found OWYN. I wanted something organic but was satisfied that most of the ingredients were organic.

I was so happy when the turmeric and cookies and cream flavors were announced. I drink 1 or 2 a day and look forward to any variety. I just wanted to try 1 bottle, but the 4 pack wasn’t available. After many weeks I decided to trust my previous good experiences with OWYN and bought 12 packs of both.

I was very disappointed with the flavors of both. The turmeric is bland and has no flavor. The cookies and cream just tastes awful with a weird almost chemical like taste. I also had a weird reaction to it.

I’ve noticed that I’ve been having more problems with my allergies for a little while now and decided to take another look at the ingredients. I was disappointed to see that the ingredients have changed and ingredients that were organic now aren’t. I know myself and my allergies and something this slight can make a huge difference for me and this degree of sensitivity is total normal with my condition.

This might not seem like a major issue to most people. But when you’re me who’s dangerously close to being underweight and who can’t tolerate solid food well and needs liquid calories, it’s a major problem.

Before the formula change and new flavors this would’ve been a 5/5. Honestly it’s only a 1/5 now but my past good experiences with the original formula bump it up a little.

title: Death By Coffee might actually wake the dead.
text:
This is some of the best tasting coffee I've had. I only drink lattes because drip coffee is too acidic for me, but I immediately noticed the improvement in taste from the coffee I was drinking before. I spent $14-17 for a pound of my old stuff from a local roastery, so it's not a huge difference in price.
Normal coffee doesn't really do much for me. I can drink a few shots of espresso and go to sleep. The first time I had a double latte with Death by Coffee, I was going like the energizer bunny for 12 hours. Seriously. The effects have been less drastic since, but that's probably because I'm now further into my semester of law school and it saps all of my energy and will to live. Even so, if I have this stuff before bed, I will not be able to sleep for at least 6 hours. Made that mistake once. This coffee really seems to wake up my brain. If I drink this while I study, I focus better. Maybe it's psychosomatic, but I've never noticed this kind of correlation before and I almost always caffeinate while studying.

title: New taste combinations - Delightful
text:
The magic box of organic tea is unique in that it provides samples of twelve teas. Each are delicious, using combinations of organically grown herbs and spices. The teabags are sealed in individual wrappings and the tea bags themselves are the flow through design with strings and tabs attached making them quite easy to brew. The flavors are as follows:

I AM................................Sage, Ginger & Elderflower
IN THE MOOD................Hibiscus, Orange & Pepper
SANCTIFY..................... Ginger, Fennel & Cinnamon
LOVING.........................Green Tea, Cinnamon & Earl Grey
TALK TO ME..................Lavender, Licorice & Mint
DELIGHTED...................Ginger & Lemon
TOUCH THE GROUND...Honeybush, Aniseed & Sage
EMOTIONAL DETOX......Sweet Hibiscus & Mint
PURITY FLAME..............Sweet Choco & CHili
LIFE ON WINGS.............Fennel, Cardamom & Orange
JOYFUL SILENCE..........Apple & Lemon
HARMONY......................Chai Classic (no black tea)

Several of the flavors were familiar to me but there were some combinations that were new........ pleasing but new. In listing the ingredients, there were trace amounts of other spices and herbs such as cloves, tumeric root, lemon juice, lavender flowers, lemon grass, spearmint, coriander, blackberry leaf, nettle, rose petals, hops, orange peel, basil, fenugreek, yarrow flower, lemon verbena, raspberry leaves , etc. The one that I was really surprised about was the black pepper. Only one had more than a trace and you could definitely tell it was there.

These were all very interesting. I always use a spoonful of our wonderful local honey in my tea, but with these, I took several sips first so that I could experience the full flavor. The only one that I didn't really care for was In The Mood only because it had 5% black pepper and pepper really bothers my throat. But all the others were good. This is a nice wide variety of flavors to be enjoyed morning, noon or night.

I received this Magic Box in exchange for an honest review and honest is what I have been.

title: Interesting new class of performance beverage
text:
I'm always looking for new products to enhance performance, so I was very interested to try aquadopa and evaluate the effects. Aquadopa is a new class of drink unlike anything else on the market due to the inclusion of an extract from a plant called mucuna pruriens, a.k.a. velvet bean. This is combined with tyrosine, taurine, gingko biloba, and a small amount of caffeine. The idea behind the drink is that the amino acid L-dopa - found in abundance naturally in mucuna pruriens - is a chemical precursor to the neurotransmitter dopamine, which plays a vital role in motivation, focus, reward, cognitive function, and arousal. The other ingredients are meant to have a synergistic effect.

The drink itself comes in a small can of 8.4 ounces, and is non-carbonated. It has a very surprisingly pleasant and clean taste which is somewhat reminiscent of an iced cappuccino, but without the strong aftertaste of coffee. Interestingly, I was told that it left my breath with a fresh smell. The beverage is a clear liquid with a hint of caramel color. There are no artificial colors, preservatives, or sweeteners in the drink, which is important to most health conscious people. There is a small amount of sugar added for light sweetness to balance the herbal flavor from mucuna. I definitely wouldn't describe it as overly sweet. My first taste was a hesitant sip, and I found it to be very enjoyable. Definitely best served cold. I tried it both refrigerated and over ice, and either seemed very good. I liked the fact that you could taste the actual herb.

Let me first say that I went into this with a very skeptical mindset. So for my experiment I tried the drink after exercising, and on an empty stomach. I thought that although the conditions weren't strictly scientific, they would best allow me to evaluate the effects of aquadopa. At first I did not notice anything. I didn't notice any caffeine jitters after drinking aquadopa, and I definitely wouldn't classify this as an "energy drink" because the effects were very different. About 15-20 minutes after drinking a whole can I started to feel very motivated and began making a list of things I needed to get done that day. A companion who was with me later commented that he noticed that my conversation went from being very talkative and random to being more thoughtful, contemplative, and intense. It was an interesting experience because I had to do some statistics homework which involved complex mathematical calculations and I was amazed at how calm and focused I felt as I did the problems. I can't say exactly when the effect wore off, as I didn't notice any hard "crash" like I do with energy drinks or coffee. But I would say there was a gradual tapering and the extra boosted sense of focus and motivation lasted at least several hours. I also didn't feel wired or have trouble sleeping later, as I would have with coffee or energy drinks.

With a background in biochemistry, I evaluated the science behind the main ingredient. Mucuna pruriens has been used safely in traditional medicine in many parts of the world for thousands of years. It contains several compounds with known biochemically active properties including L-dopa, which is used in modern medicine to treat several conditions including Parkinson's disease, ADHD, and restless leg syndrome. I reached out to the developer of aquadopa, Dr. Andrew Hemmen, and verified his credentials as a board certified doctor of internal medicine. He said he had spent several years researching the brain science behind factors like drive, focus, and motivation, and realized that it may be possible to boost these factors with herbal supplements. For obvious reasons Dr. Hemmen mentioned disclaimers and pointed out that many elements combine to help an individual be successful, and no drink or herbal concoction could possibly claim to make someone into something they are not. The idea was to scientifically combine ingredients whose effects were well known and documented. The other ingredients I already mentioned, and they are more widely known so I won't comment on them.

Your experience may vary, but after trying one of these (available in Austin at Sprouts Farmers Market) I found out they just became available on Amazon and I ordered a case. For me, the effects matched the claims. I've repeated the experiment on myself and experienced similar effects.

As far as the price, Artisan Kettle is well worth to cost.

title: Don't buy 24 if you haven't tried this flavor before
text:
I'm a big fan of Chicken ramen for a quick meal or snack. I always add sriracha to my chicken ramen to add some extra dimension and heat so I thought the Sriracha Chicken flavor would be great for me. This product has none of the tasty, savory, salty flavors from the normal chicken version, and the "sriracha" flavor is really bad. It's somehow tangy and weakly hot, more like a very vinegar forward hot sauce. Granted, sriracha has vinegar, but it's nice and balanced - this spice packet is not balanced at all.

Taste is a very subjective thing, so while I really don't like this flavor, you might. But my recommendation with all Maruchan Ramen flavors is it to try to buy a single or a six pack at a local grocery store before committing to a 24pk on Amazon.

The whole point of prepackaged ramen is to be fast and convenient, but I wanted to add my favorite ramen upgrades! In almost every ramen I make, I add a splash of soy sauce and a squirt of sriracha. If I'm home, I'll always add about a teaspoon (eyeballed) of sesame oil, which really amps up the fragrance and taste. If I have the time or I'm feeling fancy, I'll quickly stir fry a few mushrooms and onions (scallions are best but I rarely have them) while the water heats and add that with a solid grind of black pepper.

Get a small bottle of sesame oil and start adding a drop of that and fresh ground pepper to your ramen and you'll be amazed!

title: Love the large crystals
text:
This is a perfect lemon salt for adding to sliced tomatoes or fruit. The large grains look good and taste good.

Like every other lemon salt I've tried, this stuff loves moisture, and could have a tendency to clump up. The fact that it's a small bottle is a plus, because I'll have used it all before the moisture that creeps in any time the bottle is opened has a chance to turn it into a solid lump.

I wish someone would put out a lemon salt that has a shaker top and maybe some of those dehumidifier packets in the bottom to help keep the stuff from attracting moisture! I use a finer-grained lemon salt with dried rice in the shaker for table use (the lemon flavor helps cut down on the amount of actual salt I get at the table).

text:
I've been looking for a decent instant coffee, and since I like Greek coffee, decided to give this a try. Long story short, it's not bad stuff -- but since I don't read Greek, it's taken a lot of experimentation with amounts to get the amounts right. I find that if I don't use enough of the instant granules, I get a thin acidic cup, so I personally use about two tablespoons per cup of hot water.

Remember that this is intended to taste like strong Greek coffee, not drip-brew, and is best taken with sugar, no cream. I normally take my coffee black, but this doesn't taste quite right to me without a little sugar.

I bought it to stretch out the rice that I had, since Seattle now has COVID-19. And it works beautifully for that purpose!

I cook it in a rice cooker, in a 1/3 ratio of barley, and 2/3 ratio of rice. The barley cooks up beautifully in the rice cooker on the regular setting, and it adds both a nutty taste and a chewy texture to the rice. It especially compliments Basmati rice. title: It's a Ch Ch Ch Ch Cherry Bomb
text:
First of all this was $9.98 when I bought it on Amazon in late Sept. By October it had more than doubled.... Halloween price-gouging anyone?
I was also super disappointed to open it up, pop a Milk Dud in my mouth, and taste.... CHERRY. The whole durn thing smells and tastes like cherry. I got two bags of this, and the Whoppers and Duds where about 4 to a bag. The Twizzlers had many open ones, just loose licorice floatin' around in there, so I had to throw those out.
So, I like regular old Twizzlers, but this whole bag is infected with cherry, and smells and tastes like cough syrup.
Considering I live in a development in a place where the rural kids come on the back of trucks, and I literally give out over 500 pieces of candy, and the kids don't seem to give a hoot what it is, I guess this was okay. But I think the whole thing was poor quality, and I did not like thinking of the kids trying to eat cherry-flavored Whoppers and Milk Duds. Yuck!
Also, definitely cheaper to buy the candy here than the dollar store, provided you get here before the October mark-up, which is just robbery.
Also bought this:http://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B005K6ZLSK?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o05_s00

title: One of the Finest Earl Grey Teas!
text: Like most other Earl Grey enthusiasts, I'm very fussy about my blend. I have gone through many brands, always disappointed at the lack of flavor or the artificial taste bearing little resemblance to the blend. Of course Earl Grey flavor is a matter of personal choice and, to me, Edinburgh Tea's blend is one of the finest out there, delivering a fresh, distinct yet mellow flavor that neither overwhelms nor under-delivers. The base tea is  delightfully smooth, well suited to delivering the lightly sweet natural essence of bergamot orange that characterizes Earl Grey. I have since tried other Edinburgh Tea blends, and they are also of good quality, making this my go-to choice for tea. The brand is not easy to find; I'm happy to have discovered it on Amazon! I hope more tea lovers will now be exposed to this wonderful tea company and find its teas to be as delicious as I do.

title: I'll definitely be buying another box!
text:
I have been wanting to try Matcha tea for a while now and I feel really good about choosing the Magus Brand.

I like how the packaging of the Matcha Sticks is very clean and modern. On the back of the box they offer both the Traditional and the the To-Go preparation methods as well as detailed information on the ingredients, flavor notes, preservation etc... I didn't know a lot about Matcha before I tried it so having the info in hand was helpful. One thing I really like about this brand is that they offer the pre-measured sticks. It takes the hassle out of measuring and it makes sure you correctly use the right amount. I'm also able to just throw it in my bag and go.

I chose to try the Traditional method (hot) for preparing it the first time . It was certainly more time consuming but I liked the Matcha Tea better this way. The next day I chose the To-Go method (cold) for preparation. It doesn't taste as good cold but I like the easy, pour and go. I know that regardless of the brand you purchase; Matcha doesn't taste all that great when you drink it plain. That said...I can drink this cold and actually enjoy it.

title: Great for cleaning/using as part of natural, homemade dishwasher soap
text:
Use this for my homemade dishwasher soap. I use:
1 C. Borax
1 C. Washing soda
1/2 C. Coarse Kosher salt
Mix together and use 1 or 1 1/2 T. Per load
PLUS add 1/2 tsp. Citric acid/load
Use white vinegar as my rinse aid.
I have hard water and no water filter and this still works great for me and is natural and economical. I tried it without the citric acid and my dishes were all coated with a cloudy film. But with it, they are shiny and clean. (I do also first rinse off all the food from my dishes before putting in dishwasher.) Amazing stuff! A little goes a long way. I still have a few water spots on my glasses from the hard water, but get that on my hand washed dishes too, just a little less when I wash by hand.

title: Should have read more reviews before I ordered
text:
I love thai tea, get it from restaurants whenever I see they carry it (most sushi/asian places will have it around here, not just 'Thai' restaurants). I'd been getting these tea bags from walmart locally, and drinking it every day for the last few weeks, but thought this looked like a better deal and less hassle. I should've known better.

Most of the 1 star reviews really nailed it. This doesn't taste like thai tea. Period. It tastes like someone tried to recreate the flavor from memory after drinking it a few times, with artificial flavors or something. Their description mentions alot of flavors that aren't even really the main ones in true thai tea. Tamarind and Star Anise are among two of the prominent flavors (from what I'm told) not 'vanilla, cacao and caramel'.

I promise I used enough milk, I was constantly adding more to desperately try to get the flavor right. Until I'd used almost half a gallon of milk and it was almost 2/3rds milk and only 1/3rd concentrate. Was a little more palatable at that point, but still not right and the flavor started to make me a little nauseous. I eventually gave up and just threw them all out the same day it arrived.

Luckily, I found the same brand of tea bags, that I'd been using, on here and ordered a few boxes of those. Some of the worst reviews for THAT one just say the flavor is a little 'weak', but it's fine to me. THIS one just didn't taste good.

title: Runny and Weak are NOT words usually associated with Texas.
text:
Meh. I like chili but I'm pretty picky about the flavor. This one did not impress me.

The container is odd because while it's microwavable it says to remove the lid and cover with plastic wrap. I didn't happen to have any of that in my desk drawer here at work, so I used a paper towel instead. Not sure why they didn't just provide the lid with the holes in it like every other microwavable bowl food does but whatever.

There was an odd, not chili, smell as it was heating up. It smelled more like canned ravioli than chili. And don't let "Texas Style" confuse you.. I thought there'd be a little spice to it.. But I've gotten more spice from cans of Hormel chili than this stuff. It was nice and chunky so it was at least filling, but the consistency was way too thin to be called chili. It was really more of a slighly chili-flavored soup. Even after I attempted to drain some of the liquid out, it was still too runny to eat at my desk without dripping it all over the place.

Don't think I'll be buying this again.

More than half of the packages have broken cookies, and on top of that, they taste stale.  Total fail all around.  So, no more Walkers for us. title: Moldy jerky again.
text:
I love this flavor and have purchased it many times in the past. I almost always buy the 16 oz bag since it's a pretty good deal.

My most recent purchase had several moldy pieces inside when I first opened the bag. Since this version tends to be a bit more moist than the others, I've had problems in the past with moldy jerky. Sometimes it appears a day or so after opening the package, but twice now the entire bag had to be thrown out because of mold in the bag when it was first opened. Jack Links is the only brand of beef jerky I've seen that says it has to be refrigerated after opening, which I do since it takes almost a week to eat an entire bag.

I contacted Jack Links customer service on their web page and left the details about the latest moldy bag of jerky. I received a letter a few days ago with the usual blah, blah, blah, but was most annoying is the coupon for up to $8.00 on a bag of jerky not to exceed a few ounces in size. I don't consider that to be an adequate response for a spoiled one pound bag.

Needless to say, I'm underwhelmed with their idea of customer service. The tendency to mold and their attitude toward loyal customers means that I'll steer clear of them in the future.

title: Well Insulated, Holds Heat In, Ergonomic No Spill Design
text:
I’m not a big fan of matcha tea but I’m a big fan of this handy tea brewer mug. It holds a lot of liquid, I’d guess about sixteen ounces. The way it works is you heat the water to a boil, our it into the container, add the strainer where you can put a tea bag (it comes with six Lipton matcha bags) or loose tea, and then close it snugly with the twist on top. It seals very well. You probably don’t need to take unnecessary risk of spills but when I shook it and turned it upside down and on it’s side there were no leaks.

Because of the long then shape the container fits in many sizes of car cup holders and it’s insulated enough that while it keeps your beverage hot for a long time you won’t feel any heat on the outside of either the cup or it’s lid. It’s well,balanced and doesn’t tip over easily.

The packaging was interesting because there was a sticker that was put over the instructions, which made me question if it was a misprint or if the instructions were changed for some reason. I liked the variety of flavors, and I loved the amount of protein in them. I didn't think that the portion size was very good. It barely even filled up the container it came in. I made it according to the instructions on the container both ways (overnight and in the microwave) and I didn't have much luck with how it turned out. Maybe I added too much alternative milk to it or maybe I needed to change up the instructions and find a way that worked better for me, but it the oats were almost always too mushy and soft. I think I would rather buy the ingredients separately and make my own amount of overnight oats because it would probably be cheaper. Not a bad quick and easy breakfast, but I didn't feel that the quality was there for the price that it cost.

This is the only coffee I enjoy when brewing an iced coffee, as the thickness also holds together creamer well without separating. The 96 pack is also priced at a very reasonable amount. Coming from a large family, there is about four or five of us that drink coffee, and before the 96 pack, we were running out of coffee all of the time. It simply isn't reasonable to buy the 30 pack version of this from the store once a week from the store, as it gets very expensive. Now, a 96 pack lasts about three weeks before we have to order more. It is priced just $10 higher than it would normally cost a 30 pack at the store, so this is quite a savings for us! I highly recommend this coffee to anyone, especially my iced coffee drinkers out there.

title: don't care for flavor or amount of liquid
text:
An organic/natural energy drink. It provides the equivalent of 1-2 cups of coffee. It has a nice color. But the flavor is flat and tinny, 16oz is a lot of liquid for an energy drink, and 27g of added sugar is just silly.

Sixteen ounces of meh-flavored liquid is a lot. There's a reason the competition are mostly intensely-flavored, small portions (small cans or shots). This much liquid also makes it harder to mix, for those of you using this in a bar setting. I'm not drinking an energy drink to make sure I reach my hydration goals.

I'm not sure why there's so much sugar added, either. Considering the natural, premium-priced organic ingredients, stevia would have been a natural fit, or better yet, a more tart flavor profile with less sweetener.

It may have just been my shipment, but all of my cans arrived with various degrees of small dents in them. At the size of this 8-pack, the cans either need to be sturdier, or be better packaged.

I like what Hiball is trying to do here, with natural ingredients instead of the secret/synthetic components of many energy drinks. But they fall flat. A better flavor, in a smaller volume, and figuring out how to provide balance without adding a lot of sugar would go a long way towards a better product. I'm going to stick to Redbull instead. As it is, Not Recommended.

text:
While I must say that this is the best cherry product I've tasted in concentrate or juice form, something went wrong along the way post order. The reason for my 3-star review is that one of the jugs arrived cracked with about one-quarter of the concentrate having leaked out. Given the cost of this product, that loss amounts to about $10.00. title: Great Flour - Some Advice / Tips
text: This is a great deal on almond flour - almonds are harder to harvest so they tend to be more expensive. This flour blends nicely into baked goods, thanks to being blanched and finely ground, and it gives them a lighter, more tender texture. A great way to cut down/replace some of the fat in your baked goods is to incorporate almond flour in the recipe, which does add fat but it also adds fiber, vitamins, & minerals. Beware though, a lot of keto recipes use a ton of almond flour, making them delicious but also very calorically dense. Many people are fooled into thinking almond flour baked goods are going to help their weight loss efforts, which they can as long as you're still in a caloric deficit at the end of the day. A tip if you're replacing regular flour with almond flour - you have to increase the binding agent (usually egg, but you can also use flax seed, chia seed, or a gum) and you may have to adjust the liquid.

It isn't bitter or too sweet, it's almost unflavored so it can be used in so many every day foods you prepare without losing the taste of the dish or food (my favorite is Ghee on banana bread).
The consistency is a great balance so you don't have a bit that is lumpy and one that isn't - its like gravy - you have to know your process to make a smoothly consistent Ghee which Veda has done. It makes it a lot easier to cook, bake or use as is on foods you'd use butter or oils, replacing them with a full healthy food such as Veda Ghee.
So far the first jar is going fast since it's replaces too many other things in the kitchen I use Ghee for now instead of finding the right oil or butter mixture because Ghee takes the place of that and is a lot easier to use.
Very pleased with Veda Ghee, it's not often you get Ghee made properly but Veda has it down properly.

title: Gritty and wormy but delicious with some cleaning
text:
Absolutely delicious mushrooms. You can smell them even through the plastic packaging. They make the most wonderful broth for soup and for adding to kapusta and pierogi at a much better price than anywhere else. This is the second time I have purchased these and they are very sandy and dirty. That being said, if you take the time to clean them they come out 100% grit and worm free. I soak mine in scalding water overnight then carefully remove the mushrooms and place in another bowl. Reserve the soaking liquid and strain through a coffee filter or paper towels- this is very important to remove the grit. Clean the mushrooms and pot. Simmer in fresh water (this also produces a delicious secondary broth). Once a simmer is reached, just remove the mushrooms with a slotted spoon and once again strain the liquid through a coffee filter or paper towels and reuse as simmering water. Repeat this a few times until they are grit and worm free (about 5 times). The worms all come loose after the second simmer and any bad mushrooms dissolve a and get strained. It does take some time to clean and prepare them but for the price? Outstanding. I understand why the reviews are low but if you are making a broth or using in sauerkraut it is wonderful.

Second picture is the amount of grit and worms that come loose after just one soak.

title: Delicious, enjoyable snack, but watch the nutritional data
text:
Suffice it to say that I am one of those middle-aged men who, when faced with the absence of snacks in the house, could eat a whole bag of walnuts with which my wife had intended to bake cookies, and then try to convince her that she forgot to add the bag to the shopping cart. When I saw this Planters snack, I thought I'd never have to do that to her again.

These bars are a really savory combination of sweet and salty; a good blance of the two, and the same holds true with its texture; a satisfying mixture of crisp and chewy. Nut lovers will certainly enjoy these bars, although I thought the size of each bar was actually pretty disappointing (I see that someone added a picture of the bar as compared to a dollar bill at the top of this screen... a brilliant idea!). The bar is actually smaller than your usual breakfast granola bar, but then again if something contains nuts as expensive as cashews, I suppose it's to be expected.

The only thing that concerned me was the nutritional information. For a 1.62 ounce bar, 220 calaries and 12 grams of fat is pretty steep (this coming from a guy who covers up his peanut habit to his wife over baking walnuts).

In short, both my wife and I really enjoyed these bars, and would certainly buy them again, however we both look at them as a special treat and not a daily snack, something that will knock off hunger the way the Snickers bar is so marketed.
