After about four to six weeks all bags had worms and live flour beetles in them, some had chewed through the bags. I have bought a lot of King Arthur flour types from Amazon but this is the first time I have had this problem. The first order was delivered on April 16, 2021 and the next two orders were delivered on April 21, 2021. Total of 18 bags each 5 pounds, that is 90 pounds of bad flour. I had three other types of flour including rye, white, durum stored in the same pantry but none had any issues and some have been stored for almost a year. title: Best Kefir Grains with Amazing Customer Service
text: I ordered my first batch about a year ago and everything was great. A huge storm ripped through the midwest in 2020 and knocked out my power for a while and my constant brew got too hot and everything didn't taste right after that. I ordered another batch and somehow the USPS ended up sending it all over the country. Usually, everything is shipped right away and I get it after 2-3 days. After about 5 days and still no package, I wrote to Florida Sun Kefir to ask if they had any recommendations on what I should do to make sure the grains activated correctly after sitting in shipping for a little too long. They immediately sent me an unexpected replacement (that came in 2 days) which is now thriving. I'm a customer of theirs for life. Great products and great customer service. I also tried their dehydrated grains and those worked well but took longer to establish. I prefer the live grains because after the first one or two batches to activate the grains they are good to go. I get great carbonation even in my first ferment with an open (coffee filter covered) container, and even better in my second ferment with flip-top bottles flavored with fruit juice. I use a 5:1 kefir to juice ratio and it has worked really well so far. It's helped my family stop drinking soda and has drastically improved our bowel/gut health.

title: A Sweet and Refreshing Source of Caffeine from Super ENRGY; It Will Perk You UP!!!
text:
When Dad was ill in the hospital, I didn't have time to brew a much-needed cup of caffeine in the form of coffee or tea. Fortunately, a twelve-ounce can of Super ENRGY Healthy Energy Drink perked me up in the same manner that two cups of coffee would. It definitely gave me the energy to face another day at the hospital. I like that it was sweetened with monk fruit and stevia extract. They are all-natural sweeteners that won't cause cancer like sucralose and aspartame. I like that the twelve-ounce can only has twenty calories. Each can has about the same caffeine as two cups of coffee. Underneath the can, there is a best by date of 02 FEB 2024, which is a most excellent date.

The Mango Peachpop has real mango and peach juice. The taste could have been improved. Perhaps more mango and peach juice could've been added. The price is a bit high for me. At the time of this review, the price is $31.99 for a twelve pack. That is about $2.67 per can. I would prefer it if the price were about $2.25 per can. The twelve pack arrived nearly shrink-wrapped in its entirety. None of my cans were missing or damaged. I am thankful for this. Furthermore, this product is distributed by Kitu Life Inc. of Austin, Texas.

Overall, I would recommend the Super ENRGY Healthy Energy Drink, Mango Peachpop, to those who like fruity energy drinks. However, I would warn them that it is sweetened with monk fruit and stevia extract because not everyone likes these sweeteners as much as I do.

This variety set of coffee is a lot of coffee! The box has 5 Illy's 8.8oz cans of whole bean coffee that could probably last you most of the year depending on how much coffee you make. I did receive the pictured Arabica Selection coffees. This Illy's selection has more flavors like India and Nicaragua, but those are not in this variety set. Dates are stamped on the bottom of each can. One date I think is the date the beans were canned and the other date is its Best Before date. It does not indicate what these dates are exactly so this is just my guess. Each can's date is different from each other too. The oldest can has the date of 3/22/2022 which is nearly a year ago but its Best By date is 3/2024 so it has a 2 year shelf life. The can with the most recent date is in 9/2022. I got this set in 1/2023 so I got about at least a year which is enough time. I've not tried them all yet, but so far the coffee is delicious!!

At this moment its priced at $64.99 so that makes each can $12.99 each. If you buy them individually they go for $14.99 so you will be saving $9.96! This set is packaged in a 5-sided box that fits all 5 cans and is wrapped in plastic. The box is pretty simple and thin, but it would make gift wrapping it pretty easy so this would make a great gift. Highly recommend this!!

title: Can be used as a spreadable nut butter too!
text:
I was really surprised how much water to cashew milk concentrate I should use to make a creamy nut milk similar to those you can find at the store! Actually most of the nutmilks I've seen at my grocery store are almond or maybe oak, so to find a convenient way to enjoy cashew milk was a really nice surprise.

Since the only ingredient is cashew, there are no gums or emulsifiers that a commercial nut milk will have. That's better for the body, but also means the particles and the fats will separate from the water soon after you blend it up. Just shake or stir it a bit before you sip and it'll be wonderful.

It arrives well padded by styrofoam and tightly packed in cardboard so you don't need to worry the glass jar will be damaged. Even better, this nut butter doesn't need to be refrigerated, which makes it that much easier to scoop just the right amount each time (my fridge has a tendency to freeze things almost rock solid...)

title: Huge surprise
text:
Color me truly surprised that I like this stuff as much as I do. I'm not a big peanut butter fan to start with, but I love chocolate. Bumping up the protein? A plus, but adding whey protein sounded a bit like adding something healthy to something unhealthy and ruining both.

Not so. This is a super-tasty, not too sweet chocolate peanut butter that I feel kind of good about. It's definitely got what we call "torr" around here, a Norwegian word that means catch-in-the-throat-dry, so eating it out of the jar is not a good idea. Eating it without something to drink, not a good idea. But eating it? Good idea. It's got a nice lot of protein and fiber, less sugar than I'd have expected, and is beautifully spreadable. It does say that there might be oil separation, but so far I haven't seen any sign of it. It also apparently doesn't need refrigeration after opening, at least according to my reading of the label.

Why it's called "chocolate chip" I don't know because I can't find any chips. This is just creamy (though slightly gritty, I admit) chocolate peanut butter. And if that's your jam, you may well enjoy this.

title: Authentic chai masala
text: This is the real deal...we stayed with friends in India for almost a month and my daughter lived there for a semester teaching English, and this is what they use to make what we would call “chai tea.” “Chai” actually means tea,  so when we say “chai tea,” we are really saying tea tea. “Masala” is the word for spice. So the correct term is “chai masala”, which means spiced tea. In the area of India we stayed, they use Taj Mahal tea and Everest chai masala to make their spiced tea, and then they add milk and sugar to make what we would call a chai latte. The first time I visited India I brought back both the tea and the spice so I could make chai masala at home. I used it very sparingly, thinking I wouldn’t be able to get it until the next time I went to India. But I stumbled across it on Amazon, so now I can use it whenever I want! I recommend this for an authentic Indian chai masala.

title: WARNING - These noodles are addictive!
text:
I bought the Seafood Noodle soup because of a review in the Serious Eats newsletter.

I'll cut to the chase - this is the best instant ramen noodles meal I've ever had. Bar none. Period. Rich, filling, overflowing with flavor. Trust me, I could go on with the superlatives.

Note: the instructions call for filling the cup with water up to the indented line. I have changed that to a third of the way between the indented line and the rim. I also added to the cooked noodle soup the juice of 1/2 lime, which adds a bit of tartness that I like (lemon doesn't work as well, but that's probably a matter of personal taste).

These end up being about 3 times the cost of the noodle soups you can buy at your grocery store. They're much more than 3 times the soup.

As my title says, these are addictive. You have been warned.
Save money, buy in bulk

title: Ruined by rocks disguised as raisins
text:
I bought 5 boxes of this cereal from the grocery store. Ever since Kellogg’s special k protein cereal was ruined with its new formula I’ve been on a seemingly futile quest to find a healthy high protein cereal. When I saw this cereal in Publix I though I struck gold. It had all the right elements, good taste, high fiber, had go protein. The box even felt heavy, like you’re getting some bang for your money (unlike that nonsense hippie Kashi cereal full of puffs of yuck).

Unfortunately this cereal has a fatal flaw that just ruined the entire cereal and I’m baffled at the sheer stupidity behind this decision. Do you like raisins? How do you like them? Do you prefer them as you would expect to find them from like in those little boxes you had as a kid with raisins in them? Or, would you like your raisins to be placed out in the sun for weeks until they are dried rock hard husks of what a raisin should be? My friends if you prefer the latter, then THIS is the cereal for you!

I don’t know what genius green lit this cereal, but I would like to watch then eat just a spoonful of these dried-out husks of raisins, with s challenge that they must chew and swallow the raisins in under 30 seconds or be punished in some creative manner. (Rubs hands deviously). It’s just frustrating, I’m a personal trainer and older than most of my competition. I’ve studied fitness and nutrition greatly. I KNOW that having a high protein meal prior to bed is required for optimal muscle growth. However in an attempt to keep my meat consumption low, I’d prefer having s high protein plant based snack before bed. Basic Oatmeal would be obvious but that’s my morning go-to-breakfast every day. It simply should NOT be this difficult to find a quality high protein cereal.

title: Huge kernels, Great taste!
text: So, I'm Lithuanian and Kasha is our main staple. I know some Lith's who can't live 2 days without. This product may be a bit pricey & is avalable for much cheaper at my grocers... BUT.... The kernels in this Organic Buckwheat are huge!! I really Love it! Beautiful.  Even though they are toasted, making it easier to cook, I crack a raw egg, soak the kernels in the measuring cup, keeping it simple since an 16.9 oz. plastic water bottle measures about 2 cups, for 15 minutes or so, toss the soaked kernels & extra egg in a hot pan and after the kernels are dryed of egg I put the cup of Kash/egg in 2 cups of boiling water w/ one tbl spoon, of butter some salt.... cover, turn down to simmer into the plump kernels, making a healthy sustainable staple to anyone's meal. 😚👌💋  Fabulous! I love it alone, with a roast duck, a new treat for Thanksgiving, Christmas (of course)anything, anytime... except Sushi, maybe.. haven't tried that. But if you have Central or Eastern European ancestry, this grain will make you feel great!  Valgysime! 🤲🌾

title: I was hit with the most amazing aroma. I immediately looked for my coffee grinder ...
text:
Let me start by giving you my first impression of coffee beans aging in rum/whiskey barrels. I was not a fan. HOWEVER, somehow this ingenious combination makes the most Aromatic, Sophisticated, Smooth and YUMMY cup of coffee. When I opened the bag, I was hit with the most amazing aroma. I immediately looked for my coffee grinder and grounded up a batch. After the percolator finished its job, I served a cup with a hint of sugar and cream. The first sip to the last one was unbelievable. I couldn't tell you right off the bat all the flavors I was tasting because I drank it so fast. All I knew was that the flavors were well balanced, delicious and I knew I was drinking a really well crafted coffee. Caramel, molasses, vanilla with a slight hint of rum were the flavors I tasted on my second cup ,when I slowed down. Absolutely delicious combination.

If your regular go-to coffee is starting to taste blah or if you're looking for a new coffee experience, seriously TRY Coopers Cask Coffee. I plan on trying the other flavors as well, although it will be hard to pull me away from the Thomas Tew Rum Barrel!!

title: Delicious and Nutritious.
text:
I have eight children, and chocolate is my go-to anti-stress remedy. I really don't need any convincing to consume mass quantities of the stuff, so when I was offered the chance to review this product, I jumped at the chance. My package arrived as one solid chunk of cocoa butter, not wafers, but I blame the summer heat, and delivery service, not the manufacturer for this. It's still totally usable. Cocoa butter is a solid at room temperature, but has a low melting point. I lived in Germany for a few years, and toured a magnificent chocolate factory in Belgium. American "chocolates" have been forever ruined for me. The main difference is that Real untempered chocolates melt in your mouth, and if you aren't fast, on your hands as well. In the U.S. wax is added to chocolate to keep it from melting as easily, and as a filler. Eww. This product is not deodorized, which means that it has a nice, pleasantly strong cocoa smell. The color is a nice ivory. I rubbed a bit on my palm, and it melted and absorbed quickly, leaving my hand soft, yet not greasy. Making homemade chocolates with real, unrefined, raw cocoa butter is healthy, as well as delicious. Cocoa butter is a good fat, and contains wonderful antioxidants, and is not only edible, but can also be used topically. Raw Organic included a recipe for homemade chocolate, as well as one for homemade body butter. Cocoa butter had a shelf life of two to five years, if you don't actually eat it all right away.
Dr Axe says, "Cocoa beans are seeds from Theobroma cacao L. plant, a member of the Sterculiaceae plant family. These beans are used to make one of the most important and widespread functional foods in human history: chocolate. Cocoa butter is the fat source used to make chocolate. Cocoa butter is great for naturally healing dry, sensitive skin. Real cocoa butter is completely edible, plus it’s also used very often in skin lotions, lip glosses, chapsticks and other beauty ointments. Cocoa butter is a healthy fat, mostly saturated just like coconut oil. Cocoa butter benefits include: preventing skin dryness and peeling; healing chapped lips; fighting signs of aging; soothing burns, rashes and infections; treating mouth sores; working as a shaving cream; improving heart health; and raising immunity."
I heartily recommend this product.

title: So Convenient - BEST Vietnamese 3in1 Coffee Ever Made!
text:
Very good flavor. Easy to use. Easy to carry. Cost effective.

This is NOT Instant coffee as you know it. The coffee in here is pulverized coffee beans mixed with creamer and sugar. It is made in an instant but the coffee it-self is not freeze-dried or brewed, then dried. It is close to a French Press with coffee richness...the cream and sugar are an added bonus. This is my first time trying it and I've had 2 cups already, one for breakfast and one in the afternoon. I can feel the caffeine and will probably be up all night since I'm sensitive to it...but it tastes great. I love coffee flavored 'anything'. Dissolves instantly in boiling water. I just stir it with a straw and sip through the straw so the coffee doesn't stain my teeth. I used about 8 oz water to one packet for the second cup and about 6 oz for the first cup. Both were delicious. Will buy again.

*** Oh No! I did not just make iced coffee with this --- yes I did; it's AWESOME! I don't even add hot water, just pour cold water over ice in a travel mug (mine is 24oz Contigo) and add a spoon of sweetened condensed milk, add your coffee packet and shake. I like mine lite and weak so I can guzzle it down all day long in this heat-wave we are in. Use 2 packs for a stronger coffee. I LOVE this stuff! '

*Just ordered another 100 pack so I don't run out. I would hate to be without this. So easy, so convenient.

My husband is doing the Paleo diet that does not allow soy based products but he loves Soy Sauce. Luckily, we discovered this product! Here is a quick breakdown:
1. It tastes SO similar to soy sauce, I would have to argue that if you did a blind taste test, no one would be able to tell the difference!
2. Even though it has a much less sodium content- it still tastes just as salty!
3. It does not taste like coconut at all
4. I mixed it with wasabi for sushi I was eating and it tasted exactly like the real thing!
5. I also have cooked with it and again, can't tell the difference

I was pretty skeptical to order this but I am so glad we did. I don't think I will ever go back to normal soy sauce, I probably prefer this one!

When made with milk, tastes very much like hot chocolate with coffee notes. The coffee flavor comes through towards the end of the flavor, and adds a nice element to the semi-sweet chocolate flavor. The color comes through like a nice hot chocolate with notable bits floating in the latte.

Latte texture is very smooth, not grainy at all. There was a bit of particulates towards the bottom of the cup, but it didn’t ruin the flavor or sensation while drinking.

When made with milk, it’s very delicious and I am grateful that it’s not overly sweet either!

I decided to make another cup, but this time with water. The color and flavor profile are different when compared against making it with milk. The flavor is definitely more bitter, coffee like. The coffee flavor definitely comes through stronger this way. Color is also very dark, a dark brown hue.

It has marketing that states it’s vegan friendly, but also says it may contain milk due to processing? Bit strange to say it’s vegan friendly if it may contain milk.

title: The Spice is Right
text:
My morning mocha will never be the same again. Just two spoonfuls of this lightly spiced dark chocolate completely transform it from routine to revelatory. The blend of cinnamon, anise, citrus, pepper, and nutmeg is subtle, well-balanced, yet powerfully aromatic. It's like a little taste of the holidays, any day! It's very finely ground so it's a snap to incorporate. I just add it to the bottom of my mug before pulling a shot of espresso, and the heat of that melts it instantly. There's just enough sweetness that I don't need to add any extra sugar, but I don't like my mochas particularly sweet, so your mileage may vary. This is just perfect as is, with a tiny splash of almond milk to lighten the brew.

The list of ingredients is short and sweet; all real foods you'd find in any pantry. It's "accidentally" vegan and dairy-free (kosher), too!

If I can ever spare enough to bake with, I seriously want to play around with making some easy fudge... But I can barely keep this around the kitchen. I need to buy it in bulk!

This post was sponsored by AMERICAN HERITAGE® Chocolate as part of an E-Commerce Review Program. I received this product to facilitate my review, all opinions are my own.

title: Incredibly delicious!
text:
Yes it's bright green, yes it is full of sugar, but by gum is this mint syrup delicious! Like several other reviewers, I grew up in Europe where this can be considered a fairly common drink. Most cafés in France, Belgium and even Italy will carry a mint syrup, and no, they don't use it in coffee! Add a dash (or four) to cold water (flat or sparkling) and you have created what is easily one of the most refreshing drinks imaginable. The mint tastes is not overly sugary, making it excellent as a cocktail mixer/modifier (alcoholic or virgin). Use Teisseire mint syrup to add a punch in flavor and presentation!

I highly recommend that you give this sirop de menthe a try!!

title: Not so Convenient as All That
text: Wickedly Prime Lentil Pasta Meal, Broccoli Cheddar, Gluten Free, 10.1-ounces (Pack of 4), by Wickedly Prime, an Amazon brand. Well, I’m a little confused about this product, which is, I suppose, meant to be a convenient enrichment of ordinary mac ‘n’ cheese. To begin with, I have always understood that packages were to list foods that were their largest ingredient first, then down to lesser ingredients. But this package lists broccoli first, and I’m telling you, there aint nothing but a few wisps of broccoli to be found in here. Then it lists cheddar, which is contained in just a small bag inside.  And then it lists lentil rotini – pasta—that fills the box.  The product requires stovetop cooking, in an era when I thought the microwave reigned supreme for convenience. Then it asks for milk and butter.  Now, I consider myself a fairly ordinary, traditional sort of person in a fairly ordinary, traditional home, but it’s been years since dairy milk or butter were in my fridge. Strictly Almond Milk Vanilla, Reduced Sugar, and ICBINB Lite. You can bet I wasn’t going to buy dairy milk or butter just to try this product.  So, I used what I had.  And it tasted blandly OK. Well, the directions were easy enough to follow, and it was done in less than 15 minutes, as the package boasts, come to that. And the finished product was edible.  But I gave my three remaining boxes to an appeal for food for needy schoolchildren.

title: My Favorite Beverage When I'm Lucky
text:
Raspberry iced tea is my favorite beverage, and Sweet Leaf is my favorite raspberry iced tea. I find it better than Snapple brand raspberry tea, which is a bit flat and tends to have too much leaf residue on the bottom, leading to bitterness and uneven taste, and almost all restaurant teas, which tend to use the wrong tea as the base, darjeeling and random shots of raspberry syrup do not a great iced tea make.

Unfortunately, the taste of this tea varies wildly, from delicious to sort of OK. Getting it in glass bottles seems to help, but it is very much hit or miss.

This tea, as its name suggests, is sweet. My wife thinks it's too sweet, and many will share that opinion, but it is much less sweet than the saturated sugar solution McDonald's sells as sweet tea. Just as ice cream needs to be extra sweet to make up for the numbing of the tongue with cold, ice cold iced tea needs much more sugar than hot tea ever would. Given this, this tea is best served right out of the refrigerator or over chipped ice, a room temperature beverage it is not.

They do not specify which tea they use other than a black tea. Whatever it is, it's quite mild.

According to the Sweet Leaf website, the lack of preservatives make it best to consume within a week of opening even if refrigerated. This might also explain the taste variance. I have no phobia's against FDA approved preservatives, and I wish they would add them if it made the experience uniformly good.

The other Sweet Leaf teas are pretty good, especially the [[ASIN:B001RBZ6MI honey mint tea]], but this is my go to beverage.

title: Like orange soda - but with a big boost of caffeine!
text:
My husband works insane 16-hour shifts and I've been ordering a bunch of different "natural" energy drinks for him to sample lately - to keep him awake and on his toes without me worrying about him overdoing it on the usual (awful) energy drinks he picks up at the gas station on the way in to work. Of the several different brands and types I've ordered lately, THESE are the ones he keeps reaching for!

I ordered the "Poppin Orange" flavor and it's carbonated and has a light orange soda taste. It does have a little bit of that green tea extract aftertaste that I can't really describe...almost metallic. It's sweetened with a blend of erythritol, stevia, & monk fruit - usually stevia has a bitter aftertaste to me and monk fruit is too sweet, but I don't detect any bitterness in this and the sweetness is just fine.

In addition to the caffeine (160mg per can), these contain 110% of your daily value of each vitamin B12 AND vitamin C, 25% of your daily value of zinc, and 10% of your daily value of potassium. So they're still just a high-caffeine energy drink, but a little added extra nutrition. I feel much better about my husband drinking these than the big name-brand energy drinks!

title: Good quality; reasonable price
text:
Parmesan is one of the handful of things I make sure to have on hand at all time. And Reggiano is, of course, the "real deal." All in all, my favorite of all cheeses.

I've ordered from this vendor several times. The cheese comes packed in a padded and insulated bag and has always arrived in perfect condition.

On past orders, I'd receive one big chunk sometimes with an extra smaller piece to get the weight right. I've always received a few ounces over the nominal 5 pounds.

For past orders, it looked like the cheese had been sliced "in house" from a Parmesan "wheel" and had been vacuum packed. This time I got several smaller pieces, individually vacuum packed. There are three pieces in total, each a bit over 1 1/2 pounds. As usual, the total weight is a few ounces over 5 pounds. The pieces have the amount of rind you would expect. If you cut a whole wheel of Parmesan in half across the "equator" and then cut wedges from the center of the wheel to the outside, this is what you would get.

When I've received the larger independently packed piece, I'd immediately cut the Parmesan into smaller pieces and vacuum pack them separately, so the separately packaged pieces in this shipment are actually more convenient for me.

The authenticity of the cheese is evident both from the printing on the rind, the dense slightly crystalline texture, and the delicious taste.

title: These have been an easy way to add fiber to my diet, and they have more flavor than other chia seeds I've tried
text:
I've only tried chia seeds from the bulk food section of my local store, and those were like eating crunch with no flavor at all. So I was a little surprised when I tasted these and they actually had a little flavor--very mild, of course, but it makes me wonder just how old and stale those bulk bin chia seeds were. These seem to be very fresh by comparison.

They're organic, too, which is not usually a very high priority for me. But chia seeds can't really be washed, so I'm a bit more concerned with the source of my chia seeds. The freshness and the organic label are enough to make me dump my old source and switch to these from now on.

I don't have a lot of different uses for chia seeds yet, but they're so easy to use it hasn't been a problem. I soak them in water for a few minutes and then mix them into cottage cheese or yogurt, or spoon them over a salad. If I'm really lazy I soak them in water and just drink the water. It's a fairly bland drink but a great source of fiber. And as a regular laxative user, adding a nightly dose of chia fiber has made my mornings a bit easier, too.

Since I had some popped amaranth on hand (doesn't everybody? But I tried it for Thanksgiving and it replaced bread crumbs nicely) I mixed peanut butter and some honey, then rolled that into balls and coated them with equal parts popped amaranth and chia seeds. A couple of those make an amazing (if messy) afternoon snack, with a serious dose of protein to keep me awake until dinner.

I also cook quinoa with a little extra water, and when it's done I mix in a tablespoon or so of chia seeds and let it stand for a few minutes. I might serve that hot, with black beans and spices, or chill and add some chopped veggies and dressing. Now that I think about it, the quinoa and chia would also work for breakfast instead of oatmeal. That takes care of tomorrow's breakfast...

I'm finding that chia seeds are an easy to use source of protein and fiber. These seeds are the freshest ones that I've found, and they're organic. They're also significantly less expensive than the ones I've found locally, which may be why my local source has stale seeds. I received a sample of these to review, but I'll be buying more in the future.

title: Alert! No longer the Good Earth you remember
text:
I've been drinking and evangelizing Good Earth for probably close to 20 years, and have turned a lot of people on to it. A lot of "natural" brands emerged over the last 20-30 years, and most felt like they were sort of greenwashing exercises. Good Earth was a product and company that I actually loved and trusted. The original herbal Good Earth tea is sort of irreplaceable as a sweet, caffeine free natural beverage. Two hours ago, I would have given it a 5-star rating based on the box that's in my cupboard.

But I just got back from the store, where I discovered that in addition to changing the package (sad but no big deal), they've changed the recipe to include artificial flavorings. I'm absolutely flabbergasted that they have decided to throw away decades of customer trust this way. Artificial flavors in Good Earth tea! I want to die, just so I can roll over in my own grave.

Is the tea still tasty? I expect so, though when you throw chemical flavorings into the mix, my beverage options just got about a thousand times broader, and I don't think I'll ever find out. Are artificial flavors really that bad? Again, maybe not, and when I'm lazy I'm sure I consume a lot of them. But that makes the loss of a really great natural product that much harder to take.

If it were any other product or brand, I wouldn't give it a second thought. But as I said, Good Earth was special. Almost sacred, as I could do a little relaxation ritual during my day that centered around it. Now it feels like that tiny but precious sacred trust has been broken, and I feel curiously hurt by it.

It's hard not to feel like they've turned their back on the natural ethos that the original core customer base embraces, and corrupted the name Good Earth irreparably. They certainly have for me.

text:
This is quick to prepare and delicious on a variety of foods ~ mashed potato ~
meatloaf ~ meatballs ~ roast beef ~ chicken and pork.
This is also a convenient flavoring to add to many recipes ~ stews and flavoring in a pot roast.

This 21 oz bottle is a very nice large size to have on hand.
And much more economical then the packets that are under one oz & make one cup.

Directions are included on the bottle ~ lift white arrow at left-hand bottom corner of back label.
Directions for ~ 2 cups ~ 1 quart ~ 1 gallon ~ but make any amount going up or down from those amounts.

Heat water to a boil ~ turn off heat ~ whisk in gravy mix ~ stir for 30 to 60 seconds ~ Done!

I've found Caffe' Borbone so good, I gave away a half case of Lucaffe Arabica I had on hand to a neighbor.

I just ordered a dedicated ESE machine, a Spinell Lolita for my small office. Thank you for turning hunting for fresh and tasty ESE pods into drinking them courtesy of Caffe' Borbone. text:
I flew 1st on a plane a little over 3 years ago, and I was given a package of these cookies. I don't know what the folks in coach got, but it couldn't have been as delicious as these things. My kid got air sick and threw up, but these were so good that I kept on eating them, even after witnessing the vile pile that my child ejected from her mouth into a bag, while sitting right next to me. And I don't have a very strong stomach lol. I've been on the hunt for them ever since, and I finally just ordered some.
They're every bit as good as I remembered. They're not soft, but they're not hard. They're *delightfully* chewy, I guess. There are several chewy pieces of spicy, candied ginger in the sweet biscuit; they're slam full of candied ginger. Spicy, but also sweet. My favorite cookie ever, and I'm a big fan of cookies, in general. I'm presently trying to hold myself back from sitting down and eating an entire container of them. Best cookies EVER.

title: Great!
text:
Received my grains 2 days ago. I immediately started them in. I disolved my organic whole cane sugar and maple syrup in about 1/3 cup of boiling hot water. Then I added cold water to fill the jar. Once I added the cold water the entire misture was luke warm. Then I added the grains. In preparation I used boiling hot water to rinse down everything I used to make sure it was clean.

After about 42 hours I strained the water and started the process again. The grains about doubled in size/quantity appearance.The resulting Kefir Water tasted like apple cider. I am putting the rest into the fridge with the top closed to see what I get in a couple more days. If the grains grow like they did this first time around then I will be ready to try my first recipe :-)

Tip: My kitchen gets somewhat cold so I set the jar on the back of my stove above a burner and kept the burner on a low heat which kept the jar from getting too cold. I kept my jar of coconut oil right next to it because coconut oil liquifies at about 77 degrees. This let me know about how my kefir was doing. The first day growth was slow because it was cold. The second day it doubled when I figured this out. Temperature really matters.

title: FAKE NUTRITION LABEL, MORE CALORIES THAN NORMAL PB

I received it, and was surprised by the taste, but more so by the low fat, sugar, and calorie content. As it turns out, loved it so much started eating it out of the jar, using about 4 tbsp per day. After opening the third bottle of this product, something told me to research it, because it was simply too good to be true. And guess what: it was too good to be true. In fact, they have a higher calorie AND fat content than regular peanut butter. This is NOT 28 CALORIES PER 2 TBSP, it is 200 CALORIES PER TABLESPOON.  I could not believe my eyes, until the scale showed I had gained 5 lbs in three weeks, considering I am a VERY clean eater, and my weight had not gone up or down for a very long time. I hope this information helps anyone here before buying it, because for me, If I could sue, I would sure as hell do.

text: My house guest bought this bundle for me knowing how much I enjoy flavored coffee. I was super excited when the capsules arrived.  Regrettably, these are not what I expected.  The coffee is so acrid and bitter it is almost undrinkable. I have tried each one and none of them are very palatable or pleasurable to drink. I would like to clarify that I always imbibe my espresso in very small espresso/demitasse cups which only hold about 3oz. Therefore, I'm accustomed to a strong, intense brew. title: It won’t get stuck in your teeth and 3 cups is only 140 cal
text:
Though I generally review entertainment products on Amazon I do occasionally review food products and in September – at the Natural Foods East trade show in Philadelphia – the company had a booth and I tasted a sample. I liked it and got a few of the varieties of this product. This “flavor” was my favorite.

I LOVE popcorn because it’s filling and low in calories (well, lower) But I find more and more bagged popcorn has either unpopped kernels, which I have to remove from my mouth, or they stick between my teeth. Well this brand has solved that problem by removing the “hull” or “skin”. So the pieces are soft (like a cloud). A 3 cup (!) serving has only 140 calories. That’s the good news. This variety is also gluten free, nut free, and kosher. It is however not Vegan. (but 3 of their other flavors are actually Vegan) Nor dairy fee because of “shared equipment”

The ingredients are pretty simple: corn, sunflower oil, cane sugar and salt The oil means 6g of fat (no trans fat) and 7g of sugar – 14% of DV. The sodium on this one is low at just 8mg (3% of DV) While popcorn can be a good source of fiber – the hull-less corm has none.

But it is tasty! It’s apparently a family run business. The shelf life is also good. I received it in November 2021 and “Best by” date is August 2022.

As I said, I tried a few varieties and this was my favorite when it comes to taste.

Steve Ramm

title: Effective yeast, slightly strong flavor, great price.
text:
TL;DR: This yeast works great, rises fast, has a great price for the amount you receive.

For others:
I have tons of food allergies which stops me from buying most store bought food, packaged food, and restaurants. We bake all of our own bread, cakes, and anything else. When ever we use yeast for baking, we use this kind. The yeast rises quickly with our local clover honey and the right temperature warm water. It typically doubles in 5-10 minutes, often spilling if we don't watch it carefully. The taste can be strong, but we found by using about 1/4 less than any particular recipe asks for and instead giving it more time to rise, we reduce the yeasty flavor. The last good thing about this product is that you get a lot of yeast for the price - those $7 jars at the supermarket equal about a sixteenth amount of this package for a fraction of the cost. This is the cheapest I have found yeast for in my area, including warehouse stores and discount grocers.

title: Gluten free kind of sucks but Bob's 1- to- 1 is making it better
text:
I really like to cook and bake so when the GI doc said that I was intolerant and he didn't just mean that I hate stupid people I got very concerned. I have had "stomach" problems for years and going gluten free has made a significant difference in how I feel but can be a real pan in the rear if you enjoy a healthy dose of browns and grays in your diet.

I tried multiple flour substitutes but had uncomfortable reactions to many of them and had read many favorable reviews about Bob's 1 to 1. I cant say that I like all of Bob' s gluten free stuff but the 1 to 1 flour and muffin mixes turn out some pretty good stuff. Even my kids like my biscuits when I use this flour. We have also made cookies which we scarfed down too fast to get pictures of.

We have plans to make some banana bread which I will post pictures of when done. I haven't tried using it to flour and fry anything but I am sure it would work really well. Maybe there is gravy in my future, maybe not but it's an option. Stay away from this kind of flour if you are going to make pizza dough and with find a good 00 flour substitute.

I steep 3 heaping teaspoons in 12-ish ounces of water in a French Press pot for 6 minutes and then pour into a mug and add coconut milk. It is delicious! Or, I've made the base as described, but then pour into a blender and make a Bulletproof style drink out of it by adding 1 1/2 TB grass fed butter and 1 1/2 TB coconut oil and blend it up. Delicious! I'll definitely be purchasing more!!

title: Happy Belly Indeed!
text:
My mother HATED shredded wheat – all varieties. So, I didn’t get to experience it when I was growing up.

Even the frosted variety was off-limits.

Seeing these on the VINE program, I thought “nothing ventured, nothing gained”. And, I got them.

The box probably should’ve gone in a shipping box and not a poly bag. So, when they arrived, the box was a bit smashed.

I opened the box and bag to check them, and decided to grab a few squares.

I was surprised! Even without milk, they were sweet and tasty. Definitely not “dry” and I couldn’t see what was so bad about them.

I offered a square to my mom who, despite her past experiences, tried it. She was amazed. She really was.

As I can’t eat cereal with any kind of milk (soy, diary, definitely not nut due to allergies), I actually decided to snack on these “dry”. They were, for me, a bit habit forming.

With regard to the milk, I’m waiting on my mom to gather up the courage to try them that way.

For the price and brand – I’m VERY pleased. And, it’s even better that I can save 5% on Subscribe and Save bringing this to less than $3 per box.

If you are cutting back on sugar, then simply substitute Splenda for the sugar, and substitute artiificially flavored lemonade drink mix. A bit of lemon juice will work just as well. I know you'll love it!

It Tastes like the Russian tea that we made when we were children and brings back fond memories!!!

title: Welllean Rice - Read my review to know why you must buy this OR just save time, buy it immediately!
text:
This is SOOO good... I made egg fried rice with shrimp, the flavor was unbelievable. Its even better then the real white rice. The final texture of the cooked fried rice dish reminds me of beaten rice - used in some Indian dishes, which makes the rice a bit chewy...for the lack of better term. Since this is almost 0 calories, I can add more meats, olive oil (or coconut oil) and/or nuts and not worry about make it too calorie dense. Since then I have tried several side dishes and everyone of them exceeded my expectation. the best part is no need to spend time cooking rice. Also the product can handle heavy mixing and stirring and still remain fluffy unlike real white rice.
I also mixed other cooked grains/cooked dry peas (like green chick peas, black eyed peas) and it turned out great. I can eat so much more and still stay within the meal calorie goal. (I use myfitnesspal to track).

Initially, I just got this to balance out the calories during the Christmas holiday season but my order was delayed by 2 weeks (out of stock) and the seller immediately apologized when I contacted them and refunded me as a good will gesture. My packet still arrived on Dec 27th instead of 14th. It was worth the wait. I am customer for life and I have subscribed for auto deliveries now.

The only thing I hope they would change - the price is higher than most other brands (but this still is the best tasting and texture, I have tried them all I would continue to buy these.) It is double packed with 2 really high quality packaging. I hope they find a way to reduce the packaging per oz of the product and offer a bulk price for a larger quantity inside each packet. I am sure lot more people would try this if they reduced the price. Either ways, I am sold and I plan on making this a part of my must have pantry items.

title: I like salt. I expect jerky to be on the ...
text:
I like salt. I expect jerky to be on the salty side. However, some of these were so salty I found them to be inedible, at least for me.
The best flavor was the Carolina BBQ (430mg per 1 oz), second the Maple Bacon (480 mg per 1 oz), Smoked Chipotle (500 mg per 1 oz), Siracha Maple (530 mg per 1 oz) and my least favorite Smoked Black Pepper (500 mg per 1 oz). I really wanted to love them all.
The Black Pepper tasted like mostly salt little pepper. Even though the Siracha has more salt, it was a little better than the pepper because the salt was balanced a bit more with the maple sweetness, plus the bonus of the hot pepper kick at the end.
If I were to see this product in my local natural grocers or co-op, I would only purchase the BBQ maybe the Bacon. I might try ordering some of their limited edition flavors at their website if I can find out the salt content. Otherwise, I won't be ordering this 5 flavor variety pack again.

You don't want to eat them whole: they are designed to go through digestive tract intact, that's how they spread in the nature. Invest in a grinder, or use my newly discovered technique: soak them in water, then when they (very quickly) go soft, add some honey and maybe milk. Yum!

I never had the patience to soak these for long enough for them to sprout just a bit in large quantities and thus become superfood (though they are pretty close to superfood as they are), going to try that.

title: Great Tasting Coffee. Awesome aroma and crema.
text: I have been buying SpressoLuxe coffee for a while. The quality of the coffee is excellent. It tastes as the real Italian Espresso. I don't understand why other reviews call this coffee weak or bad. The acidity of the coffee is lower than Nespresso because Nespresso uses 5% to 10% instant coffee in their capsules (Nestle owns Nespresso but also Nescafe, get it?). That's why their capsules produce a thicker and whiter crema that is always the same no matter which flavor you try. It's artificially produced. Spresso Luxe is 100% artisan coffee and it doesn't produce the bitterness sometimes associated with Nespresso which most customers are already used to.  The crema is bolder and darker as a result of a perfect extraction. It's even more affordable. There are some compatibility issues with the latest Nespresso Machine models but it's advertised in their website and also here on Amazon. Read the descriptions! It works well with my Citiz at home, in my girlfriend's U machine and in the DeLonghi Lattissima at work. I gave this as a present to a friend that has a brand new, 2014 Pixie and he had trouble using them. They did not perforate. I called the number on the box and they confirmed the compatibility issues they advertize on their website and on Amazon and they said they are working on the new capsule that will be 100% compatible. Overall this is a great product, more affordable than Nespresso and of excellent taste and quality.

title: Intriguing new confection
text:
This is something totally new to me. I've tried all the other creamy spreads, like Nutella and the Hershey's spreads, but this is something quite different. For one thing, it's kinda chunky and thick - it really is a sort of batter. The flavor is pretty good, and it IS spreadable, so it's appropriate for a durable cracker or a piece of toast and if you're decadent enough, I guess it would make a darn tasty sandwich. Eating it right out of the jar is more my style; and then there's always a 90-second Mug Cake:

2 tbsp. of butter
2 tbsp. of cookie butter (spread)
1 tsp vanilla (I get a little liberal with vanilla)
1 egg
2 tbsps. sugar
4 tbsps. flour
pinch of salt
1/4 tsp baking powder
90 seconds in the microwave

I tried this last night, and it does make up to a passable little cake. It was a little dry - you can fudge with the ingredients a little to try to remedy that - but it was certainly edible.

I thought I was going to be much more impressed with the chocolate variety than I was, but I ended up being very happy with the speculoos and graham flavors. I'm sure all of them could be used as an ingredient in whatever you want to take a stab at in the baking line.

title: Great chocolate but DON'T ORDER IN SUMMER
text:
We are chocoholics and we always have Dove Dark Chocolate Promises in the house. They are the best. Amazon delivery of them, not so much. I was wary of ordering chocolate in the summer, but decided to try it since they are shipped with "cool packs." I have ordered these many times in the past and they always arrive within 1-2 days, so I figured there was a good chance the cool pack would actually work. So I was surprised that the projected delivery date was 7 days out! Optimistically I thought that still meant it wouldn't ship until 1-2 days before delivery, but...no. The day after I ordered, I got the "shipped" notification, with the original delivery date (now 6 days out). It actually ended up arriving 2 days early, but of course it was in transit for 4 days, so when I measured the temperature of the "cool" pack immediately after bringing it into the house, it was at 90 degrees -- the melting temperature of chocolate. It didn't even sit in the sun, I took it right out of the driver's hands.

I put it all in the fridge and it firmed back up without deforming too much or "blooming" (getting the white stuff you can see after chocolate melts and resolidifies), so I kept it since I hate waste. Still tastes good but the consistency is a little off.

Bottom line: cool packs don't do a darn bit of good if the product is in transit more than 1-2 days, so if you must order chocolate in the summer, make sure it will be delivered quickly.

title: The IC website recommended Puroast so I decided to give it a try
text:
I have Interstitial Cystitis (IC) and the acid in coffee is a no-no. I am a big coffee drinker and just could not give up my morning "hug" coffee! The IC website recommended Puroast so I decided to give it a try. I have to say I was pleasantly surprised at just how good it was. The first few sips was different because I was used to my other brand of coffee, but once I got used to the difference I loved it. And being able to order Mocha Java which is my favorite flavor was icing on the cake! There was no bitter taste at all. I ground up a few days worth of beans and store it in my pantry. The coffee is fresh every morning this way. I did find that I needed to use just a little more grounds than normal to get the strength I was used to. The coffee does not seem to cause me any problems with my IC. So glad I don't have to give up my coffee!

I would recommend this coffee to anyone who has problems with the acid in the coffee.

title: Community Coffee, 16-Ounce Bags, Dark Roast
text:
Community Coffee is the coffee of Louisiana. We have a heritage of enjoying rich, full bodied coffee. No other coffee meets these requirements as well as Community. The 16-Ounce vacuum bag is becoming hard to find and more expensive. Community, like most other brands, has switched to smaller 12-ounce and larger 32-ounce loose packed (not vacuum) bags in the past year. The new bags do not maintain the fresheness we have come to expect from the vacuum pouch. Further, it is typically priced at a higher price per ounce. Preordering through Amazon to receive the 10 pound bale on a regularly scheduled (1-6 months, your choice) basis has proven to be a system that works well for me at a lower price and delivered to my door.
Today is Thursday, July 11, 3013. I was contacted earlier this month by Amazon.com and informed that they could not honor my subscription for Community Dark Roast coffee. I agreed to allow the shipment to be pushed back until August, 2013 (next Month). Now, I see that the coffee is not available and have agreed to be contacted when it does become available, if it becomes available through Amazon.com, again. So, I'll wait until August and see if Amazon.com can/will honor the subscription.

title: Great tea at a great price.
text:
I drink a lot of tea and have used Taylors of Harrogate Yorkshire Red for years. I bought the sachets in the past but recently learned that loose leaf tea taste better than the sachets so I switched. I'm glad I did because there is a definite difference in the flavor of the tea. At first I thought it was just because it was something new but the flavor has remained consistently better over time.

I bought the Kilo Bag, 35.27 Ounce and used way to much at first. I used two heaping table spoons of it the first time I made it and it was very bitter and strong tasting. After doing a little research I learned to make it using 1/2 table spoon in a 18 oz cup and this was much much better. I didn't realize it takes less to make a really good cup of tea. This bag of tea will last a long time. I placed the tea in a glass jar with a tight sealing lid. So far the flavor remains constantly good.

I'm not a tea snob just a regular guy who likes a good cup of tea. I felt if I told you of my experience you might not make the same mistake I made and be able to enjoy a good cup of tea right from the start. I don't add sugar or milk to my tea but drink it without any additives.

Taylors of Harrogate Yorkshire Red Loose Leaf tea is a very flavorful tea and I really enjoy it. I hope you do as well.

title: If coffee were beer...
text:
I started out with the Breakfast Blend because I prefer a lighter roast in the morning. It went so fast, I soon had to order more, and decided the awesomeness warranted getting the variety box. I figured I'd give the flavored ones to the neighbors, but I was astounded to find that those were also awesome, so now I'm back for both a flavored variety pack - words I thought I would never say - and the unflavored stuff, too. I had to get a bigger pod-organizer because between me and the neighbors, I'm up to about an 80-pod/month habit.

If coffee were beer...:

If you're looking for "slap-in-the-face" blend (do you drink the extra-hopped, uber-IPA beers that are happening now?), this coffee is probably not going to cut it for you. Actually, if this is you, you might have a better time of it if you ditch the coffee robot and go back to a regular coffee pot because you can pack that filter full of however much you want and get mud every time. I don't know how to make Turkish coffee, but I hear that's excellent for "slap-in-the-face" afficionados.

If you insist on a "coffee experience," these are the pods you are looking for. These are bright, complex, well-balanced coffees for people who want to -taste- the coffee. Remember when craft beer / microbrew was balanced (back before the great hop wars)? Into copper, red, and/or brown ales? This is the extra good stuff.

title: They've changed the product - it's not good like it used to be!
text:
Killer Dave's used to be the best bread ever ... and I should know, I've been grinding my wheat fresh and baking homemade bread for over 40 years with sunflower, flax and pumpkin seeds. When I discovered Killer Dave's bread, 3-4 years ago, I stopped baking my fresh bread because Killer Dave's was the same high quality - fresh ingredients and real fresh ground wheat - and even though it's expensive, it's cheaper than firing up my oven and baking my own bread at home.

I worried when I heard that the company had been sold a couple years ago --- but the quality seemed to still be there so I have continued buying it (a couple loaves a week).

But now, it seems that they have finally decided to cut corners. The last couple of loaves I've purchased have been dry and awful. They don't taste like real whole wheat any longer .. and the bread is more like your typical grocery store bread that says 100% whole wheat but really isn't (like they add the bran and vitamins back in to old, refined flour and then say it is whole again).

They didn't drop the price any - it's still expensive -- but now it's a few steps down from Orowheat and the other "premium" grocery store brands. It's a sad, sad day :( ... but I guess I will take the time to go back to baking my own bread at home again.

title: Fabulous Product at a Not-Fabulous Price
text:
This is absolutely the best non-artifical, non-sugar sweetening substance I've found. The taste is easy to get used to--I'd call it Very Nearly Just Like Sugar. No bitter taste or unpleasant, lingering after-taste. I'd make this my default, always-in-the-cupboard sweetener in a heartbeat were it not for some drawbacks.

Practice first. In my experience, it's not quite as sweet as sugar if you're comparing equal quantities. I have found it takes 1 1/2 to 2 times as much Just Like Sugar for certain uses.

If you transfer the sweetener to another container, be prepared for a "dust cloud" ... more than you get with cane sugar. It smells delightful, but if you have breathing problems this could affect, you might want to get someone to help or cover your nose/mouth.

Also, if you are using it for beverages, it dissolves most easily in hot drinks, so make sure the hot beverage is ready to drink before you add the sweetener. If you're adding it to cold fluids, the sweetener clumps and is resistant to dissolving (rather like packaged hot cocoa), though you'll get it mixed in eventually. As for cooking/baking ... no troubles.

The biggest drawback with this product is the price. One pound (in this container) will cost about $27. One pound of Just Like Sugar in a one pound bag, on Amazon, will cost $20.25. One pound of Domino Pure Cane Sugar, on Amazon, will cost about $2.00. I can't break it down by pound, because it's sold by packet, but a 500-packet case of Sweet & Low, on Amazon, will cost about $10.00. So, Just Like Sugar is way out of my budgetary league.

I have a hard time believing manufacturing chicory-root-sweetener is that expensive. Maybe it is, but I suspect the price reflects how the product suits the current dietary climate. Such a pity, because this truly is the best stuff out there, and I think by now I've tried them all. But four stars anyway, because I'd definitely live with the product's other idiosyncrasies if it just didn't cost so much. That said, if money isn't an issue for you, Just Like Sugar is the way to go.

title: Great Taste
text: My vegan cousin turned me onto these Lupini beans. We are of Italian descent and she remembers our grandfather eating lupini beans by the handful. I am on a low carb diet, I have been for years and years, so I was super excited to hear about this snack from her. I immediately ordered them and got within two days. I will say that they are tasty, especially the rosemary & garlic. Also, they are so easy to eat the entire package. Luckily they have zero net carbs, lots of protein, and of course it is an added benefit that they are plant-based. The only downside for me is they are a bit slimy. The item is exactly as advertised, so there is no ding in the description of the product. It is just, I have to kind of gear myself up to eat them because they are a bit slimy. Actually they are not slimy, they are just moist, if that makes sense. Two thumbs up to the company that makes this product, as it is a small family business, and I love to support that. Although, the price point is a bit high, but honestly, I am only buying them for myself, and when you give up so much to be on a low carb diet, I feel a bit entitled to splurge a little and get this product. All and all, I would recommend. I just do not know if I could eat them everyday!

My best guess is that they buy or store the seed in bulk, in those strong paper bags like dog food comes in. title: Didn’t care for these grits
text:
I love to make both cheese grits and polenta, and prefer my grits to be “small batch” (or close), medium to coarse size, stone ground, and YELLOW (which have much more flavor than the white varieties). There are several smaller mills in the South that consistently produce the grits I like, and I buy from them exclusively. But when two of my go-to brands weren’t available the last time I needed to order more, I decided to try these. I wasn’t impressed, especially since these came from a small family mill in NC, which should be a reliable source for good grits. These were much smaller than I like my grits, which affects both cooking time and the texture of the cooked product, especially polenta. I could’ve overlooked the size if their other qualities were good, but they weren’t. These were essentially tasteless (and what taste they did have seemed stale), the cooking instructions on the package were poorly written and inaccurate, and they did NOT cook up creamy like properly ground yellow corn grits grits should. {** I’ve since noticed that the Carolina Grits Company is only a mill, and their corn comes from a variety of sources, which probably explains their inferior quality.} I’ve only made one batch to date, and IDK how I’m going to use up the rest (I bought two 1 lb. packages). Of the products sold here on Amazon, I much prefer - and would highly recommend - either Professor Torbert’s Orange Corn Grits - which cook up and look like yellow grits -
(https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07MBCXM9X/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=) or Palmetto Farms YELLOW stone ground grits (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B009HGBF2A/ref=sspa_dk_detail_9?psc=1&pd_rd_i=B009HGBF2A&pd_rd_w=AO227&pf_rd_p=7d37a48b-2b1a-4373-8c1a-bdcc5da66be9&pd_rd_wg=fY6Xk&pf_rd_r=9WS03VCDN2BZRMKGPHDH&pd_rd_r=b4616487-6c6c-4a8f-98e8-704bc00c9ddb&spLa=ZW5jcnlwdGVkUXVhbGlmaWVyPUEzQ05FV0hRRU5NRjRTJmVuY3J5cHRlZElkPUEwMzQ1MzY5MkNaUExQQzVITjRTTSZlbmNyeXB0ZWRBZElkPUEwMjc2MTE1MllaQllXMTdCTFlMJndpZGdldE5hbWU9c3BfZGV0YWlsJmFjdGlvbj1jbGlja1JlZGlyZWN0JmRvTm90TG9nQ2xpY2s9dHJ1ZQ==). title: okay but not as healthy as it appears
text:
I am always looking for healthier, whole grain versions of foods I enjoy. Unfortunately, these Peacock brand noodles are yet another food masquerading as healthy. The product title in big letters on the front says "Brown Rice Vermicelli", making the consumer think "this is made with brown rice, so it should be a healthy choice". But the first indication that it is not is when looking at the fiber content on the nutrition facts - only 0.6g per 2oz serving. Then onto the ingredients list to see why so low... contains brown rice, sago starch and water. The sago starch comes from palms and must not have much (if any) fiber.

The Annie Chun's Maifun Brown Rice Noodles (sold on Amazon and in my local healthy grocer) has become one of my staples and is my frame of reference when comparing to the Peacock brand. The Annie Chun's product is made with 100% whole grain, with ingredients brown rice flour and water. Per 2oz serving, it has 4g fiber and pretty much the same calories and other nutrients as the Peacock brand.

If you do try this Peacock brand noodles and have not used rice noodles before, you will need to seek guidance elsewhere on preparation. As others have pointed out, the Peacock package gives almost no directions on how to prepare the product, aside from a brief mention in the recipes (in the header text it does say that they are "easy-to-cook" but does not say how). It also contains a very strange recipe for rice noodles: Aglio Olio style - this is an Italian recipe for noodles with olive oil/garlic/sprinkled with grated cheese that I think would not be very tasty. The second recipe appears to be for a soup with veggie strips. Neither recipe gives amounts or much direction. In comparison, the Annie Chun's package gives clear, specific directions on rice noodle preparation and two recipes.

I use rice noodles = maifun = rice sticks = sometimes called vermicelli for making the Vietnamese salad "bun tofu", to serve with stir-fried veggies or in lettuce rolls. They can also be used in spring rolls/egg rolls. When cooking with thin rice noodles, be careful not to oversoak/overcook/overmix or they tend to disintegrate. Asian rice noodle vermicelli (maifun) are not the same as Italian vermicelli and are not readily interchangeable. If making an Italian recipe, the best results would be expected from Italian pasta and not maifun.

A few final notes... Both Peacock and Annie Chun's brown rice noodles are gluten free. The Peacock is made in Singapore and the Annie Chun's in Thailand. The Peacock noodles do taste fine (kind of bland), but so do the Annie Chun's. At this time, they are both approximately the same price. Peacock come in an plastic bag with some noodle crushage upon shipping; Annie Chun's are perfect upon removal from their cellophane bag in a box. Overall, I highly recommend the Annie Chun's Maifun as a healthier option over the Peacock brand. On a related note, the Annie Chun's soba and brown rice pad thai noodles are also excellent.

Rating for this product: 2.5 stars rounded down to 2 stars.

text:

title: Convenient and great in recipes
text:
When the pandemic made milk in stores unavailable, I couldn't find lactose free milk, and I am not only lactose intolerant but I've discovered that lactose free milk lasts longer once opened. We had discovered Natrel milk here at Amazon when we were looking for shelf stable milk, and after an order of regular milk, they got Natrel Lactose Free 1% Milk in stock.

Natrel and any other shelf stable milk doesn't taste exactly like the cold milk you get in the dairy section, but this Lactose Free 1% comes as close as I've tasted so far. It works well in recipes (I've used it in bread, brownies and cake), is fine in protein drinks, and isn't bad when you just want a glass of cold milk - not quite as good as my favorites, but it's not bad at all.

Yes, it's pricier than buying cold milk at the store, but so are most of the shelf stable milks, and some of the others have a weird, bitter taste - this one doesn't have that. I like it better than powdered milk mixed into cold water. And you can't beat the convenience - when you're running low on milk, just get a warm carton out of the box and stick it in the fridge. Our local store still has only a little lactose-free low fat, so I'm so glad we can get the Natrel so we don't have to do without milk.

title: Espresso is fine, packaging is terrible and inconvenient.
text: I usually buy Lavazza Gran Crema pods for my espresso maker at home.  This was the first time I've strayed from that brand.  I won't be buying the Caffe Borbone again.  I found the espresso itself to be fine.  Howver, I have had continual trouble with the packaging.  More than 50% of the packets have the espresso pod 'trapped' into the seams of the packet.  I cut open the top and attempt to remove the pod and it is stuck.  The first time or so I tugged and the paper ripped and loose espresso was all over.  Now, I have to exercise care when opening and cut all around the perimeter of the package in order to get the pod out.  Depending on where the pod is attached to the packet, you may not be able to save it and the paper tears anyhow.  Way too time consuming and inconvenient.  In the past 2 days alone, out of 8 pods opened, one had already torn apart prior to my opening the package and got tossed.  5 of the others were trapped in seams of the packet.  Out of more than 500 packets of Lavazza, I've never had this happen.  So for convenience and trust factors more than anything else, I'm going back to Lavazza.

title: Yes.
text:
I bought this cereal immediately after learning of it's brand new existence on John Oliver. This cereal tastes like candy. When I first opened it I was imagining something closer to hundreds of small twinkies, soft with a creamy filling. This cereal is not like that. It's more like crunchy sugar cubes shaped vaguely like twinkies. While there is no filling, the cereal is coated in something that tastes kinda like cream (I'm betting this is also sugar).

I've had this for breakfast twice now. First time I poured the milk and immediately ate it. It was good but it's so crunchy that it hurt my mouth. Second time I let it soak in milk for 10 minutes before trying to eat it, in the hopes of softening them up and getting them closer to a soft Twinkie texture. However, after 10 minutes the cereal was still just as crunchy as freshly poured, and my mouth still hurt afterward and my milk was warm.

10/10 would buy again.

title: Very enjoyable! Takes a bit of trial and error to get just right!
text: I love the flavor of this Jasmine Green Tea from MEIRRY Premium Teas. One of my all time favorite teas, I typically use a bagged jasmine green tea from Bromley, and this brand had a similar flavor profile. This MEIRRY tea arrives in an adorable lime green tin that you can certainly reuse as a pencil cup, bud vase or little pot for a succulent and it had an expiration date 2 years into the future! Because it is a loose tea with large leaves and flower buds, it is difficult to judge the tea to water ratio. The label directions suggest 1oz of tea to 10oz of water, but if you do not have a scale handy, trying to judge 1oz of tea is quite challenging! The first pot I made was way too strong, then way too weak, but just like Goldilocks, the third pot was just right! I appreciate seeing the whole leaves and flower buds in the tea, but they do swell quite a bit which makes cleaning your tea pot kinda difficult, but I think the flavor of this jasmine green tea was well worth any additional effort! All in all, this MEIRRY jasmine green tea makes a decent cuppa and would make an adorable gift packaged with a tea towel, some biscuits, maybe a jar of local honey and you'd have a unique and thoughtful gift any tea lover would appreciate!

The label came off so cannot determine the Best By date but these seem to be fresh enough considering that the preparation process requires first cooking and then drying these seeds.

Received in a relatively thin resealable plastic bag.

The peppercorns were almost uniform in the black color. Sometimes there can be some variation.

Please note that black pepper is made from unripened berries. White pepper uses a similar process but comes from ripened berries.

I prefer more pepper than most and found this pepper to have a very pleasant fragrance and taste with a slightly lower kick than some others but very flavorful as pepper goes.

title: Good beans
text: I used these beans for Cornell bread. I took a small portion of beans and put them in water just to see how dirty they were. I swished them around and the water stayed quite clear. The beans were very clean already so I didn't bother to wash any of the other beans. I sorted through the beans and picked out a few less than perfect beans, but there were very few bad and unsightly beans. I ground the dry beans in my Wondermill. The flour was very nice and I baked it in my bread. The Cornell bread was excellent. I used Bob's Red Mill soy flour in the past, but it's hard to find right now and I think soy flour really isn't going to be fresh very long due to its high fat content. Also, this is a way cheaper way to get soy flour compared to buying it already ground. So this is fresh flour and I will store it in my freezer and use it up in a few weeks. I highly recommend it if you bake Cornell bread.

title: Best honey-filled hard candies I've tasted!
text: I decided to try these Cedrinca candies mainly because they are eligible for free shipping (many of the "gourmet" products are not).  They are REALLY GREAT, and have the most intense honey flavor of any filled or unfilled honey candies that I have tasted.  The filling consists of quite a dollop of honey, so the candies are fairly large, and for a hard candy addict like myself, it's not practical to suck on them when I'm trying to carry on a conversation, or just have a hard candy discreetly in public.  For those situations I would recommend the Go Naturally honey candies, which are much smaller, and also eligible for free shipping.  In fact, the Cedrinca honey candies are so addictive that I keep them in an inconvenient drawer, so that I have time to think "do I really need another one?" before getting them out. On the downside, in addition to sugar and honey, the Cedrinca candies do contain "glucose syrup," which according to Wikipedia is the same as corn syrup (I don't know if it's high-fructose corn syrup or not).  The Go Naturally products contain just "Organic Evaporated Cane Juice, Organic Brown Rice Syrup, & Organic Honey" - so they might be more suitable for people who are trying to avoid corn syrup.

title: An Outstanding All Purpose Seasoning!!I
text:
I have been using Magic Dust for about a year, after reading Mike Mills' book, "Peace, Love & Barbeque". Mike is, of course, the proprietor of the 17th Street Bar & Grill and the developer of the formula for Magic Dust. Mike claims that this stuff works on everything but ice cream, and he's not far off the mark. I wouldn't use it on anything in the dessert category, but I have used it on just about everything else, including veggies, soup and even scrambled eggs! Needless to say, it is great on meat, poultry and fish, whether grilled, barbequed or done in the oven.

Shortly after getting it, I noticed that the level was dropping faster than I was using it. Turns out the the SO, who initially turned up her nose at "that barbeque stuff" had developed her own addiction to it. Mills offers this stuff in one pound bags from the 17th Street Bar & Grill site, and that's the way to buy it. As Mike says in his book, "It keeps indefinately but it won't last long!"

title: If you love spicy food you'll be hooked.
text: OMG!! SO spicy and yummy! So let me tell you a little bit about myself. I'm a spicy food ADDICT. Borderline obsessed. As an Asian, I was desensitized to spicy food at a very early age. You're talking to a girl who literally used to eat spicy pepper paste and butter sandwiches for breakfast as a child (it sounds gross but it's yummy I promise). I loved spicy food so much, even at the age of roughly 7, that sometimes I'd just eat Asian hot pepper sauce out of the jar. Anyway, these are SUPER hot but in a way that's still enjoyable. The "pain" is a good kind of pain. Your nose will run. Your eyes will water. But you'll still be slurping down more noodles. The taste of these can best be described as very similar to Shin Ramyun except without the watery broth, much MUCH hotter, and slightly sweet. The noodles themselves are also way better. They are excellent and unlike ramen I've tried before. They're nice and firm and chewy, not soggy and mushy like many other ramen. They also hold well as leftovers/reheated. I got a single pack at H Mart because I wanted to try it for the first time. I'm totally hooked now! I can't believe I just ate the whole pack.  I almost never eat all of the ramen I make. I guess that's a negative about these. You won't be able to control yourself. You'll eat the whole pack and then feel guilty like I do now! Lol

title: tried both kinds, not exactly impressed
text:
UPDATE:

-1 star, down from 3.

I ordered the hot & spicy version this time. it's definitely a bit hot but not too hot. the problem is that there is too much spice (as compared to the plain asparagus one, which is very underspiced) -- there is absolutely no asparagus taste or aroma. I could not taste the bell pepper anywhere either, nor the garlic. the overall taste is purely red chilis, everything else gets lost. even the whole garlic clove itself tasted of mostly chili pepper, barely of garlic.

I would almost give 1 star instead of 2, except both versions have that wonderful perfect crisp crunchiness.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

opened the first jar today, and got some good asparagus aroma.

wow-crispy! this is the kind of delicate crunchiness you aspire to, when blanching fresh asparagus.

almost all of the spears are closer to baby-size, and even the few larger ones still have such a great texture!

but

sadly, the sugar + white-vinegar ends up being the true bland overpowering flavor here. (and some mild mustard-seed/mustard-leaf flavor. and I can't even taste the garlic... but I do have a serious temptation to eat the garlic clove at the bottom of the jar...)

I wish I'd tried the spicy version instead. but this is ok, it will definitely get eaten. and, again, it is crispy in the best way.

I maybe had the wrong expectation - I was looking for a sort of side condiment to rice/noodle dishes. this however would definitely make a great cocktail addition, as other reviewers have mentioned. or on a cheese/crudite plate.

title: Hoosier's seems better for the same price as low-fat
text:
Just ordered my third pound of Hoosier's, very pleased with it. Some people recommend putting a spoonful into biscuits, cakes, bread, etc to improve texture and I've found Hoosiers very good for that.

I've been getting Milkman low fat dried milk as well, thinking it was probably cheaper than dried whole milk. But now I've started some price comparison and Hoosier and Peak* seem to be about $12 per pound for their milk powder. I haven't seen a figure for MM by the pound, but their 'Shipping Weight' for box and envelopes and all was 3.2 pounds. Estimating the actual milk powder as 2 pounds, MM's price for one pound would also be about $12.

* Peak was actually more expensive, $12 for .8 of a pound.

If I've got the math wrong, please someone correct me!

Anyway, Hoosier's is better, as you'd expect from whole milk.

title: Just ok MEDIUM, not HOT pepper sauce
text:
When I first opened this sauce, I did as I always do with a "new" hot sauce - put a drop on my finger and licked it off. Nothing. No hotter than Frank's or Tabasco. I left it out on the counter for a few hours, and this time I thought "maybe I didn't shake it up enough, or at all." Gave it another shot , and this time after vigorous shaking there was definitely a stronger spiciness. Having it at room temperature helped also; right out of the fridge the heat is usually going to be muted so let your hot sauce warm up and breathe a little bit. I've tried it in chicken soup and with pork, and the light lime character combined with the fruity habanero flavor works nicely. It's certainly got a decent flavor overall and I'm not unhappy to have this as an option in my rotating cupboard of hot sauces.

But it's far from a "widow maker". Hot sauce manufacturers should know by now that if you're going to trump up your product as supremely spicy, you'd better deliver, and this doesn't on that front. Sure, for people like my mom who can't handle the heat at all, this would be like drinking fire; but if you're the kind of person who loves turning up the heat and are attracted to the hottest-of-the-hot, I'm afraid this doesn't deliver, so overall I have to give this a mixed rating. Truth in advertising is important!

title: Hooked For Life!
text: I've been trying to cut back on my sugar intake & I'm the kind of person who likes some coffee with my creamer... so I was very skeptical to try these. After reading a lot of reviews online, it was obvious that most people just used a few pumps in their coffee, but I just couldn't find the flavor when I tried it like that. So I poured some cold brew coffee over ice & added a bit of almond milk. In a separate jar, I added a little bit of half & half & 2-3 pumps of the skinny syrup, then blended them together with my handheld frother. Then I poured that into my coffee & it was SO GOOD.... Finally my taste buds & my waistline have agreed on something!!! If you are hesitant, don't be! The flavor is there, you just have to work with it to find out what works for you :)

title: Cucumber...so sad
text: I used to be able to purchase this water at Henry's and Whole Foods many, many years ago.  Then it disappeared.  I was super excited when I saw the cucumber flavor available on Amazon!  I read the reviews mentioning a "funny" taste about some of the flavors, but loved this cucumber water so much, I ordered it hoping for the best.  I chilled one bottle to perfection and was anticipating the delicious, cool cucumbery goodness.  Nope.  There is a rancid taste and smell. Rancid, like oil that has gone off. I could barely taste the cucumber through the rancid flavor.  I didn't finish the bottle.  I went to the returns option on my Amazon account to return the case, because that's what one does with items that have clearly gone bad or are not what one wished for when ordering.  Unfortunately, this item is not eligible for return. What?! I haven't scrolled through every single review to see if/how anyone else has been able to return their "funny" tasting water for a refund, but I'd sure like to be able to get my money back.  Oh, the water is dated June 7, 2013.  So bummed this didn't work out, and so unhappy there doesn't seem to be a way to return the water so the company can taste and smell for themselves how rancid and yucky this case is. Sad. Face.
