title: Just pasta. People won't know it's gluten free unless you tell them!
text:
My husband and I aren't sensitive to gluten, but we like to mix it up so that our diets aren't so entirely dependent on wheat. So we are very familiar with regular wheat pasta. This yellow pea rotini LOOKS like normal rotini. It takes a bit longer to cook, but the texture once it's fully cooked is the closest to regular pasta of any gluten-free pasta we've tried so far!

You can taste a bit of that earthy, starchy, legume taste from the peas - but once you load it up with sauce and toppings I don't think the average person would know it was gluten free unless you told them.

Currently, as case of 6 boxes of this rotini is priced at $34.99 - so over $5.80 a box, making it rather expensive pasta. If you're gluten-sensitive and craving that real pasta experience though, this is a treat!

title: Unique, delicious, & healthy way to snack
text:
I have a weakness for chip-like snack foods, and Brad's Strawberry Beet Kale Chips are my absolute favorite (followed closely by Brad's Original Kale Chips). The flavor is hard to describe - it's not like anything I've ever tasted. Not overly sweet, but more sweet than salty. I would never know the sweetness is from beets if it didn't say as much on the package. Overall, these chips are just a really creative flavor idea that's well executed.

Pros:
-Unique combination of kale and beets that you cannot reproduce at home
-Not overly salty like most kale chips
-No strange ingredients or additives like most diet foods, so safe for sensitive stomachs
-No fake strawberry flavor
-About half as many calories as many other kale chips such as Rhythm
-Super healthy(!!)
-Quality control seems to be top-notch - I've ordered a LOT of these from numerous sources, and the chips inside are always fresh

Cons:
-Get stuck in your teeth in a big way (although that's true of all kale chips I've tried)
-Expensive
-Hard to find in stores

title: Rum Punch Anyone?
text:
I sampled many...too many pineapple juices and this one was the BEST main ingredient for my rum punch recipe. It was smooth, consistent and the right amount of sweet so as to not have to add additional sugar. The longer rum punch sits in your fridge the more integrated the flavors become. (Think "nectar of the gods") This is one more reason why this particular brand is an excellent choice for mixed cocktails. It allows other flavors in to mingle with it. Here's my gallon size recipe for rum punch in case you want to try it.

Add to the gallon mason jar the following:
Finely grate 1/2 of a whole nutmeg into the jar before you add wet ingredients.
5 quick dashes of Angostura Bitters
1 lime, juiced (I love to add the pulp, mashed)
1 32oz jar of Knudsen's organic pineapple juice
8oz organic orange juice with pulp (make sure this is sweet and not tart)
1/2 cup red cherries with juice (Trader Joe's dark cherries from Germany are excellent)
Fill to the very top with Kirkland brand Spiced Rum* (or golden rum)
Store in the fridge, shake the jar before you serve it on ice. Be sure to grate extra nutmeg on top when serving.

* Kirkland buys their rum from St. Croix distillery. It's good quality rum and the perfect sweetness for this mixed drink. Don't let the spice in the title fool you. It's no ordinary spiced rum. It has a lovely vanilla flavor with some nebulous spice hints that do not overpower.

If you don't have a gallon size mason jar, mix everything in a large pot and store it in multiple jars. Makes an excellent gift! If you do it this way, you can "taste as you go" and adjust it accordingly. The above recipe fits exactly a 1 gal jar.

FWIW, I have never sipped this pineapple juice by itself. My kids do and love it. I have to hide it for my punch recipe so they don't see it and ask for it. LOL

Cheers!

title: Nut free and safe for kids & crazy deliciousness!
text:
I used to eat peanut butter everyday. It was my sweet and salty pleasure. A teaspoon here or there - was all I needed to start the day or finish the night. Then we had kids and our guys had severe nut allergies. All of a sudden no more peanut butter. I’ve tried to replace it with the various products on the market and nothing compares.

Then a friend of mine told me about these chickpea butters by fieldtrip! I’ve never done a product review (can you tell by how long this is) but this stuff is absolutely delicious. This field trip company goes from making jerky to various salty and sweet spreads! I don’t know who these guys are but if they were running for president and we could have these types of options in all our schools - I’d vote for them! Thanks for the innovation and the delicious spreads.

I’ve use the chickpea butter on good old white bread for my son and he loves it. We’ve put it in our protein shakes and on top of ice cream sundaes- just the other day I topped of a parfait with it. Let’s go and get some more flavors - this is amazing!!! Thanks you fieldtrip! You all are a laboratory of innovation doing the food gods work!

title: Exploding K-Cups -- SOLVED -  Now Bad Taste
text:
Last Update....June 2, 2022. I bought some more directly from Mauds hoping it would be better but still a stale bad taste. I have thrown over100 k cups away. I wrote to Mauds but nothing more than a nothing type response. I am happy to say that I have tried Angelinos k cups and exceptionally happy. No more exploding cups and stale bad taste

UPDATE.....March 8, 2022. I was so glad the exploding cups seems to be solved. However, the recent purchase was bad coffee as it tasted stale and not drinkable. I have purchased 15 boxes and this one was bad. I BB wrote to Maids and got back a standard reply of we will look into it. I am left with an almost full box of 100 that I can not use.

UPDATE....I am happy to write that it seems like Maud's has fixed the problem. I have not had an exploding one in the last two orders of these k-cups.

Like others, I have encountered exploding Maud’s K-Cups and sending hot water and grounds all over the machine. This typically happens when the coffee is almost done brewing. It is a real pain to clean up the machine after this happens. I have not encountered this problem with any other brand K-Cups but these Maud’s Half-Caf K-Cups do it about one in 15-20 K-Cups.

After reading on the web, other people report the same issue with the Maud’s K-Cups. People have theorized that the causes for these were -
• Pressurized K-Cup with bulging lid
• High Altitude usage
• Poorly sealed top foil
• Dirty needles

I got disgusted with this and decided to try to figure out what was going on with them. In my case, the tops were not budged and the foil on top was securely on the cup. The K-Cup would start to make a cup of coffee and then almost at the end would flash a high pressure text on the screen. When opened the machine, the coffee and grounds would start streaming out the top of the pod.

So how does a K-Cup work? The inside has a filter in it which holds the coffee. The top needle punctures the foil and maintains a tight seal with the foil top. The hot water is forced through the coffee and thru the filter where goes out thru the bottom needle to your cup.

I collected a couple of Maud’s K-Cups which had exploded and carefully cut the bottom off of the cup and also removed the foil top. The top foil was securely fastened and not the source of the problem. In both cases, the filter paper in the Maud’s had a slight tear in it right in the middle. This is where the filter paper would have contacted the domed area at the bottom during brewing. The area under the filter had coffee grounds between the filter paper and the bottom plastic. It would appear that during brewing, the coffee expands and pushes the filter paper against the domed area and tears. This allows coffee grounds to get below the filter and clog the needle that punctures the bottom of the cup. All of this results in high pressure in the k-cup and grounds coming back out the top when the machine is opened up. It also could cause the foil top to come loose from the cup.

I do not know if the tear in the filter paper is due to its properties or handling of it. It may also be that some K-Cups are filled with more coffee and put more pressure on the bottom of the filter paper.
I have attached two pictures. This first shows the inside of the cup of a cup that exploded. You can see the tear in the filter paper. The second shows the bottom of the cup with the plastic cut off. You can see the tear in the filter paper and that coffee grounds have gotten below the filter paper to clog the needle.
Unfortunately, cleaning the machine, the needles or anything else is not going to prevent this tearing of the filter paper.

I have notified Maud’s and think that I have finally gotten their attention. It is a potential safety hazard as the hot coffee comes back out the top of the KL-Cup.

I have gone to using one the reusable K-Cups and filling it with the Maud’s Half-Caf coffee. It tastes the same and no exploding K-Cups.

title: DISGUSTING AFTERTASTE! AVOID AT ALL COSTS!
text:
I have desperately been trying to find a replacement for Cherry Fruit Roll-Ups for years. I have no idea why they stopped making them, but I haven't seen any since the early 90's. So I try cherry flavored fruit leather whenever I find them. I ordered these thinking they'd be worth a try. Too bad I don't have a time machine and could go back to stop myself from buying this nasty crap.

The aftertaste is horrifying. I don't know what it was, but my money is on the sulfur that is in this, for some damn reason. Why you would ever need sulfur in food, supposedly as a color stabilizer, I can't fathom a reason. But then I'm not a food scientist, so what do I know? I just know that Fruit Roll Up and Stretch Island don't feel the need for that crap.

I really should have looked at the reviews, the fact that at least 2 separate people had maggots in their orders really should have told me something.

I don't know if this trash went bad, but with how disgusting it was, I think it never was good.

Stay the hell away from this horrible tasting crap.

title: Took a chance, now I regret it
text:
I've been looking for a loose leaf 1 lb Earl Grey that tastes like Harney & Sons, but without their price. Tried the Numi Aged Earl Grey, and that wasn't anything like Harney, but it is drinkable. This stuff from Davidson's isn't even that. I literally can not tolerate it unless I cut it with something else (usually fresh spearmint or tulsi), and then I ask myself why would I even bother drinking it. Well, the same reason I didn't buy Harney in the first place - I'm cheap!

Opening the bag, I wasn't too alarmed that there were no light floral fragrances. The first sip, however, had me thinking that someone had washed out my cup with Windex. And the second sip. So I'm thinking that maybe I've fouled my mouth somehow and I'm not tasting right. I asked someone else to take a sip - the expression on her face was enough, though she didn't go immediately to Windex until I suggested it. This Davidson's is making its way to the trash today. I would compost it or use it as mulch for my rhodos, but since I'm not sure if the factory had a chemical accident while producing this, I'd rather not poison anything else.

title: Versatile replacement but use less
text: Hope and Harvest Cassava flour works as a decent replacement for all purpose and wheat flour. It is well refined and very white. It doesn't have any strong smells and smells almost like all-purpose flour, with about the same consistency. I looked up a few recipes for it and all of them recommend using less cassava flour than all-purpose as a replacement. It felt mostly the same when using it to make banana bread, and the results were nice and moist with a brown crust. Nutritionally, it is a bit different than other flours although wheat flours also tend to be low in similar values. It has no significant amount of protein, sodium, cholesterol, or fat but a very large amount of carbs. The main difference with wheat is the lack of protein as well as differences in minor nutrients. Overall, it's a decent wheat and grain flour replacement in terms of results but remember to adjust the quantity used. One annoying thing is while the bag looks good and is a durable plastic, the zip lock seal is terrible. It won't zip plus parts of the zip lock are not attached to the bag, so gaps are inevitable. I just fold the top and binder clip it, but I would probably relocate it to a different container in the future.

title: This coconut flour is a great source of dietary fiber!
text: I used to buy organic coconut fiber to add to smoothies as a source of dietary fiber, but it became unavailable.  The manufacturer suggested I substitute coconut flour, which is really the same thing but more finely ground. This is the fiber left over from coconut after most of the oil is removed, and it is an outstanding low carbohydrate source of dietary fiber.  It absorbs a great deal of water, which is excellent for elimination.  The coconut fiber cured my 87 year old mother's problems with constipation after years of trying other remedies that didn't work.  I've tried other finer ground coconut flours in smoothies or mixed with yogurt, but none were as palatable as Let's Do Organic because they were too finely ground and over-thickened the mixture.  This brand also has the best coconut taste of any I've tried, and it is excellent in my low carb, high fiber and protein pancake recipe. It also makes an excellent low carb, high fiber coating for fried or sauteed seafood, especially when mixed with rice protein powder. More people should be aware of the health benefits of coconut fiber.  I'm sending a six pack of this to my mother.  Since the other coconut fiber is no longer available, I'm sure she'll be relieved!  lol!!

I've been vegetarian so long that I don't know what a beef burger is supposed to taste like, so I served some of these to meat eaters and asked their opinion. They agreed that they wouldn't have guessed it wasn't meat if they hadn't been told before trying it. "I wouldn't send it back at a restaurant" is waaay better than other kinds of meat substitutes would get, especially since I'm no expert at cooking burgers (yet)!

For the record, I've also tested out Impossible Burger in the same way, and it got the same response. They're extremely similar products. text:
I love these daifuku! Although I have never had fresh daifuku, so I don't have much to compare it to (just other store-bought brands I have tried on amazon). I really like this particular brand/flavor and have ordered it from multiple sellers; this seller has the most reasonable price.

For anyone who hasn't had daifuku, it is a sweet dessert made of mocchi (very soft, kinda gummy/gelatinish rice gluten) with a sweet filling. This particular product has strawberry flavored mocchi with a sweet strawberry filling.
Just FYI, it doesn't taste like real strawberries but rather artificial strawberry flavoring (like strawberry candy or jello) which I actually like.
I love this daifuku; its unique texture (we really don't have anything like it in the US), makes it a fun treat to try and something interesting to share with friends/family.

text:
I feel that I'm being generous with two stars, which I've given for the attempt at including somewhat nutritious ingredients, which are wheat pasta and quinoa. I feel that the balance of these is outweighed by the high salt content and the high fat from the 4 tablespoons of butter that you add. This is comparable "nutritional value" to your standard packaged mac and cheese, with even higher fat than some, less nutrition in some cases, and certainly less appeal and flavor, in my opinion. My regular store brand shells and cheese has 12 grams of protein per cup of prepared, compared to the 9 grams in Tiny Hero's serving.

What I ended up doing was mixing some vegetables with the remaining amount of maq and cheese to cut the greasiness of all that butter, and to add some flavor. That was more appealing to me, though it still wasn't going to be a fave dish.

I really can't recommend this and will try to donate the rest of my order. I hate to waste food but this is not my cup of tea. My husband tried it too but wouldn't eat it after one taste, so I know it's not just me.

title: A nice French onion flavored salt
text:
This is more like a French onion flavored salt than French onion seasoning. I tasted this Gustus Vitae French Onion Seasoning on its own, and it tasted like a nice combo of salt and French onion flavor. It's not good for making dips, though. I tried using a third of what my recipe called for (it called for onion soup mix), and while the onion taste was mild, it was a little too salty. I'll need to find another use for it, probably as a rub on a pork loin or something.

ETA: We used this as a rub on a beef roast and it was absolutely delicious. A new family favorite. We rubbed the beef with the french onion spice, let it sit for two hours at room temperature, and then roasted the beef in the oven. Scrumptious!

Overall, if you're looking for a French onion salt, this has a great flavor.

title: Deceptive Advertising - it's not Harissa
text: It's not Harissa.  However much the vendor and "buyers" claim that it is the best ever, it can't be the best because it isn't Harissa.  I purchased a jar of this at a local Bristol Farms and was disappointed.  It is not that it is a bad tasting product per se, although it is hardly exceptional. Real Harissa, whether made in Morocco, Tunisia, or even France is a smooth pepper paste, the consistency of mustard, with caraway and coriander in addition to peppers, salt, garlic.  It has a distinctive taste unlike another "pepper sauce" which is attributable to the caraway and coriander.  I wish that manufacturers had the ethics to label their product accurately and I wish that vendors did the same. This is a bit like a company labeling their mustard "Dijon" only to find that it is a bright yellow, vinegary, mustard ala Kraft Foods.

title: My Favorite Larabar Flavor!  Whole30 Approved!
text:
I first started buying Larabars when I did Whole30 back in January. These are really one of the only approved bars you can eat on Whole30 as the ingedients are simply dates, coconut, almonds, cashews, and coconut oil. If you've never tasted a date, they are very sweet and have an almost caramel quality to them. This bar is simply macerated dates and nuts pressed into a bar and the coconut oil gives it a nice coconut taste. Yes, these are sweet, and no, they are not sugar free. There is no ADDED sugar, but dates have plenty of sugar in them. They are also not low in calories -- they pack in over 200 calories, but, they are great for a midday snack on a day you know you may not be getting meals in, and I love them before a good workout. It could also be a candy bar replacement if you are a fiend for the things. The Coconut Cream Pie is my favorite. It's sweet, chewy, and I LOVE the coconut flavor.

If you're looking for a whole food product with simple ingredients, these are the bars for you. They come in lots of flavors, and I've reviewed each flavor separately.

title: Unimpressed
text:
I wasn't sure what to expect with these pecans, as I generally get them locally or from Trader Joe's. I am a grain-free baker, and I use pecans as a flour base in many things. Pecan flour is difficult to find, pricey when I do, and not smoothly milled from whole or halved pecans on home equipment. I wanted to try these as a possibility for easier flour milling, and direct inclusion into grain-free wedding cookies, etc.
When I opened the bag just to taste them, I got shell, right away. In all the time I've bought local shelled pecans (which is years), and from Trader Joe's, I've never gotten shell. That's a major strike for me, as the shell is a detriment to teeth, and it tastes bitter. I'd be really bummed for someone to get shell in their baked goods from me.
When I poured the pecan bits out to measure, sure enough, there was shell on top. You can see it as the dark flecks in image, below. From that experience alone, I won't use these pean pieces.
Regarding the product's flavor and texture, they were flat and dry. With pecans, I expect a mild sweet flavor with a nutty background. These taste like bitter cardboard. They aren't particularly flavorful at all, and I couldn't get past the bitter shell to find the nuttiness. They are a dry texture, no softness or tenderness about them.
Also, as I bake with awareness to various allergens, intolerances, and sensitivities, these are processed on equipment with various other nuts. There's no quality control in that regard, and exposure to other nuts is a high possibility. People with nut allergies may have complications with these pecans.
In all, I won't buy these pecan pieces, again.I wasn't happy with the shell, though even if that hadn't happened, the taste and texture of the pecan was not there.

The kola flavor is similar to if you were dump a can of diet Pepsi in a jug of water then add the stevia aftertaste (strong aftertaste).

Mango ginger is less horrific. Doesn't taste like mango or ginger to me but more like an orange seltzer water plus stevia aftertaste. Still not great but ok.

Grapefruit is by far the best flavor. Tastes like grapefruit sparkling water. The stevia aftertaste is highly outweighed by the grapefruit flavor. I could actually say I enjoyed that one a bit.

Caffeine from V8 energy doesn't cause anxiety for me the way soda and coffee do. This feels more like a soda level anxiety.

title: healthy herbal rooibos tea with added bits of herbs & fruit. Tasty selection. Love "Red" tea
text:
Subtle, delicate, cozy. Naturally sweet. Hot teas to curl up with on the couch and a book, or make it iced and sit outside to enjoy the sunset. These Carmien teas have a fresh, natural, pleasing taste. I have them in the variety pack that includes Tropical Burst, Floral Berry, and Citrus Chai. This pack uses RED Rooibos tea and other herbs and spices to create the flavor. (the other variety pack uses Green rooibos).

Rooibos tea is native to South Africa, where this product is from. Naturally decaffeinated, lightly naturally sweet, smooth, delicate, red. I have been drinking Rooibos for over 20 years, before it became readily available in the US. A friend of mine would travel to Africa, and always brings me back this lovely red tea. It is the tea that made me open to drinking tea on a regular basis- just a gentle, nourishing flavor. And so I have for many years, and I loved seeing it become readily available.

I am not normally into fruity or floral, but it works here. I think I like it best iced. I am a big fan of Chai, especially Chai rooibos, and this has the addition of some citrus bits. It is lovely. The hint of orange just goes so well with Chai. Has a bit of a holiday vibe to it.

This makes for a nice sampler. I think it would make a nice addition to a tea lovers gift basket.
I would consider this brand again, especially if I could choose one flavor at a time (I'll go through the Chai quicker than the other two).

text:
I'm sorry I wasted my time and killed a tree in ordering a box of these unpalatable Keto bars. It's made by a company called Hungry Buddha but Starving Buddha might be a more appropriate name because I would rather starve than eat anything like this again. I thought other reviewers were exaggerating when they said it tasted like acetone nail remover and paint thinner. I chuckled, thinking that anything advertised as cocoa and coconut couldn't possibly be THAT bad. Famous last words...

Alas, all the bad reviews are true. You bite into it, expecting something resembling a Mounds bar, and immediately a burning chemical vapor bursts from the bar and rises to the roof of your mouth. Cocoa? Coconut? What a joke! You taste neither. It's as if you fell into a sewer, swallowed a mouthful of polluted water and your gag reflex kicks in. I had to gargle with mouthwash just to get the taste out.

What a waste of plastic wrap, cardboard box and time. Did no one at this company actually taste these bars? Were their tastebuds deadened by COVID-19? I feel bad dumping out edibles at a time of food insecurity, but this box is truly NOT edible and I wouldn't put a starving homeless person a taste of something like this.

I can honestly say this is the worst-tasting product I've had since I started ordering snacks from Amazon.

title: For gluten intolerant and highest nutrition, shop carefully
text: I love farro and the Roland Pearled Farro is very good. I have bought it many times. But know what you are buying. There are 3 forms of farro. Pearled farro is faster cooking, but it is like the "white rice" of farro. It is a hybridized form of the grain that has been processed, stripping out most of the nutritional value. Tasty and quick, but not as healthy. There is a semi-pearled form of farro commonly referred to as Spelt (also called emmer farro). Less of the nutrients are stripped away in processing, but it is also a hybridized form of the grain. For the real ancient grain, not processed, not hybridized, search Amazon for Einkorn (also called Farro Piccolo). These are the original farro wheatberries. For people wanting to reduce gluten, and for those looking for the highest nutritional benefit of farro, the Einkorn version is the best. Yes, the Roland pearled farro is excellent. It is very flavorful and easy to prepare. But nutritionally, pearled farro is the bottom of the list of types of farro.

title: Interesting oil. Herbal, aromatic and peppery. Clean and fresh. 2% Thymoquinone
text:
Thymoquinone is a small molecule that is isolated from the plant Nigella sativa, which is also known as black cumin. Because this molecule is small and relatively flat, it binds rather promiscuously to proteins in the body, so it's not surprising that correlation with ingestion of thymoquinone has been linked with various effects. In particular, there is literature supporting the use of this molecule for analgesic, anticancer, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic purposes. You'll need to decide for yourself whether it's useful for those purposes, and for yourself.

But in any event, there has been increasing interest in the oil obtained from black cumin seeds. The oil can both be consumed orally and used on the skin. I tested this for flavor, dipping bread in it.

The flavor is very strongly herbal, peppery, and aromatic. There are also bitter notes. This certainly won't be the choice of most people looking for another versatile table oil (e.g. olive oil). I think you'd want to be pretty sold on the health benefits. But if you are intent on using this oil, the flavor is pronounced but pleasant. Note that this can also be used as cooking oil, and that's not uncommon with Indian food.

title: Superb Afghan Saffron
text:
I am so happy with this purchase of Saffron. Each little thread is in perfect condition. I did not know the difference between good saffron and excellent. I now realize the difference.

This seller is spot on with the description of this Saffron. I purchased three separate small tins . I had decided to purchase one for myself and the other two will be gifts for my Persian girlfriends.

Saffron was completely unknown to me 10 years ago until I was working with my beautiful friend on a game show and we brought in our lunches daily to save time running back and forth from the crew tent . My friend always had this beautiful golden tea and I finally asked her what it was because it looked like apple juice. The next day she brought me my own container of this liquid gold. I am now obsessed with the subtle flavor of this as my daily tea.

I was also taught how to infuse dishes such as rice with Barberries and Saffron. This is a beautiful dish and it smells sooooo good and I found that I make this often.

The difference with this saffron from this seller is amazing . I can use less saffron threads and get that same sparkling color and the fragrance is well bodied. My journey with Saffron has been love at first sight and now I have found the most fresh, most color and flavorful saffron on Amazon. I don’t have to have people send me the rich and well priced Saffron from Glendale, California. I now know exactly where to purchase my personal indulgence in this incredible herb. ( I don’t know if it’s a herb or spice)

Less is more with this particular seller’s Afghan Saffron. I do not care at all for Spanish saffron because of the difference in flavor and fragrance. However, if I were to try Spanish Saffron again, I would definitely purchase from this seller again since they absolutely do know their products.

The tin that it came in is extra nice as well! It has a screw on top which is perfect for my purse when I want to add saffron to my hot tea at work.

I am hooked! In. Very good way.

title: Organic Virgin coconut oil, without the coconut taste
text: So I have been hearing all the rage over coconut oil. and how it's a healthy fat.  So I decided to try it.  Now I like coconut on some things, but to have something battered in coconut like coconut shrimp where you can really taste the coconut I don't care for.  So yes for this reason I was a bit skeptical about my food having a strong coconut taste.  Well, I have tried it, and no you do not have your food all tasting like coconut!  I've used it to saute vegetables and also for main dishes.  I made a mexican dish called arroz con pollo, which is chicken and rice.  I used the coconut oil to fry my rice, which it browned up the same as if I was using my normal olive oil.  Now while I am cooking with the coconut oil, it does smell like strong coconut.  After serving the dish I was expecting either my husband or the kids to say "why does it taste different" or "Did you put coconut in there?"  But they never said anything about it tasting like coconut!  After dinner I asked my husband if he didn't notice anything different!  He said no, that the food was good.  The coconut oil itself was easy to use.  It reminds me of shortening but not so solid.  More like a soft solid.  You just scoop a little out and put in heated pan.  Coconut oil isn't just for cooking either.  It can also be used on hair and skin, making both softer.  I myself will mainly be using this coconut oil for cooking and using in recipes.  This is a twin pack so you could use one just for cooking and the other for experimenting with, if you want to try it for on your hair and skin.  The coconut oil is easy to use for cooking and you would use it like you do any other oil.  I normally use olive oil but this one is good too and it's also organic.  I will definitely be looking into buying some more when I run out.  I did receive this item in exchange for my honest unbiased review.

title: Important source of antioxidants.
text:
This herbal, caffeine free red tea (fermented to give it a rusty color) is from a South African rooibos plant, Aspalathus linearis in the legume family. The flavonoid aspalathin is found in rooibos, and has a companion phenolic antioxidant, nothofagin. Red tea is credited with antimutagenic and antioxidant properties. The rooibos plant also contains the antioxidants quercetin and luteolin. It was discovered during ethnobotanical studies of local users after explorers used it instead of the traditional teas from Camellia sinensis. Green rooibos tea (unfermented, available from Davidson's) is also a source of the antioxidant flavonoid aspalathin. Brewing instructions are on the package.

At the end of this review are papers you might like to read if interested in the topical and health benefits of these South Aftrican teas.

These teas go well with spearmint and peppermint teas. I like them just plain, with the flavor from Davidson's or Ridgways not with the "dusty aftertaste" some sources describe. I use the bulk form at home and make it up in gift containers as a house present for my friends who like tea.

Ridgways Tea has the red rooibos in convenient bags.

Rooibos is a native of the delicate fynbos ecosystem of South Africa and seems to resist efforts to grow it elsewhere. A close relative of rooibos from the South Aftrican region is honeybush (Cyclopia), another member of the legume family with antioxidant properties. Several species of honeybush are also used for herbal teas. Davidson's also has honeybush tea in bulk.

title: I have to say that although the waffle mix was really good the first day
text:
Purchased this waffle mix for the first time for a big family reunion where we were feeding an army! We made up all three cans and had a small bowl of waffle mix left over. I have to say that although the waffle mix was really good the first day, I had one waffle the next day from the bowl that sat overnight and it was amazing!! The batter had discolored so slightly on the top, but don't let this scare you. It was perfect!!! Be sure to cover tightly in Saran wrap. Seriously, I will always let it sit overnight. We also used 5 oz. whole milk in place of the 5 oz. water and added 1/2 t. vanilla per 1 cup of waffle mix. Make my homemade "Buttermilk syrup" to pour on the top and prepare for one amazing breakfast!!!

"Buttermilk Syrup"

1 1/2 Cups white sugar
3/4 Cup buttermilk
1/2 Cup butter
2 Tbsp corn syrup
1 tsp baking soda
2 tsp vanilla extract

Directions:
1. In a saucepan, stir together the sugar, buttermilk, butter, corn syrup, and baking soda. Bring to a boil, and cook for 5-7 minutes. Remove from the heat, and stir in the vanilla.

title: Love thos coffee
text:
If you're a McDonald's coffee lover, you owe it to yourself to try McCafe k cups. These little pods of liquid gold are the perfect solution for a quick and delicious cup of coffee at home.

What sets them apart from other brands is the quality of the coffee itself. It's rich, smooth, and flavorful, with just the right balance of boldness and smoothness. I'm a bit of a coffee snob, but I was pleasantly surprised by the taste and aroma of this coffee.

The convenience of k cups is also a big plus. They're so easy to use, just pop them into your Keurig machine, and you have a fresh cup of coffee in no time. It's perfect for those busy mornings when you're running late or just don't have time to brew a whole pot of coffee.

One thing to note is that the k cups are not the most environmentally friendly option. They are single-use and end up contributing to the waste stream. However, the pods are recyclable, so if you're conscious about your environmental impact, you can make an effort to recycle them properly.

Overall, I highly recommend these k cups for anyone looking for a delicious and convenient cup of coffee. The quality of the coffee alone makes it worth the purchase, and the convenience is just the cherry on top. Five stars all the way!

title: Tastes just like the movie theater only fresher
text:
I got one of those small movie theater like poppers for a gift and the popcorn it came with was good and while it had a recipe book it just was missing something so I came across these packs and the popcorn comes out perfect.

The best thing about it is with the small size it makes just the right amount of popcorn, they say the 2.5 Ounce packs are good for 2 servings, but I find it works quite well for 3 for my family. The popcorn is amazing right out of the popper, you don't know what you are missing with movie theater popcorn that sits for 5-10 minutes before you get it if you haven't tried it right out of the popper.

The biggest key to making this in my popper for me is to shake up the packet so the seasoning is evenly distributed in the popcorn and to make sure to kneed the oil side if it has been stored cool enough for it to start to solidify. I haven't found that storage in cold temperatures affect the outcome at all. The instructions with my popper say to warm it first, but I just cut the corners off both sides of the pack with scissors and then turn on the popper and then squeeze in the oil and let it run until it is liquid then dump in all the popcorn and seasoning and it comes out perfect every time.

title: The best of some bad substitutes
text:
Erythritol is not quite as chemical-tasting as stevia, but still....yech. I tried using it in coffee instead of sugar. Little by little I tried substituting this for sugar, knowing that it's not quite as sweet (i.e. you need more) and substituting accordingly. This still has that chemical/metallic taste that other artificial sweeteners and sugar substitutes have, but it's not quite as bad. However, I started using less and less of this every day, and the net result was that the coffee tasted best with none of this in it - I now use half the sugar as before and tough it out, cringing at the thought at ever having to try this stuff again.
In its defense, Anthony's seemed to do a good job - it was pure white, and there were no chunks or unpleasant surprises (sans the overall taste), and it's made in the USA, so if you can stomach this sweetener, this seems like a good choice.

It wasn’t because it’s overwhelmingly spicy, either- I had zero problem handling the spice. My tongue didn’t burn, and I didn’t feel any pain at all. I just felt like I walked into the dustiest room ever…. My eyes watered and my husband actually checked on me because I was sneezing so aggressively. I tried to use tons of fat (oil and butter) to see if the seasoning would stick better and not be so abrasive (I felt like I was inhaling smelling salts?!), but to no avail…. I don’t know if too many others experience this, but WHEW. The butter and white cheddar are my two favorite flavors, and I’d highly recommend them to anyone. I’d say steer clear of sriracha.

title: Great plant based burgers when cooked properly
text:
These burgers are great when cooked properly. I have experimented cooking them several different ways (starting with the directions on the box). My preferred cooking method is to heat them on high in the microwave for 30 seconds on each side then cook them on the stovetop in a non-stick frying pan (no oil).

The microwave gets them moist at the cost of making them too soft, so finishing them on the stovetop firms up the outsides to get the best of both worlds (moist but not prone to falling apart).

Note that these may have a spice kick for you. I am extremely tolerant of spicy foods so they are not that spicy to me usually. That said, it seems like their spice level varies from patty to patty so be aware of this.

title: Great starter tea with rich, open flavor
text:
When I first received this package, I was pleased to note the tea is packaged in a thick foil bag to keep out moisture and heat. I live in Arizona, so anything that keeps my tea airtight and flavorful is a huge plus. Unfortunately, I also noted that there are no brewing instructions on the bag. While I understand that some brewing instructions are more guidelines than actual rules--such as the amount of tea used, if you happen to like your tea quite strong or very weak--it's incredibly important to know brew temperature and have an idea what the "ideal" amount of tea used should be. The bag also doesn't give any hints other than that this is a black tea, and says that for further information I should visit the website.

I decided to take my best guess when I opened the bag and checked the cut of the leaves, so onward to tearing open the bag! It comes with a resealable zip-lock, so scissors might be wiser than my "just rip it, that's what the tab is for" philosophy, but the sealed part seemed more than ample for tearing without a pair of scissors on hand, and this proved to be true--tearing open the bag didn't interfere with the zip-lock in any way. I took a deep smell of the tea for a guess of how to brew it. My first impression was very strongly one of roasted pumpkin, and the cut of the leaves is open and long instead of small, so I decided to follow the brewing instructions for houjicha (4-5 min at 180 degrees).

A few minutes later, I pulled out my steeper and took a sip. The initial flavor was one of plain black tea, but it almost immediately opened up into the sweetness the listing describes. Given a moment to sit, the flavor was much fuller and less astringent than a "regular" black tea, and lacked the bitter aftertaste that unfortunately accompanies so many black teas. (This was a huge plus; one reason I avoid plain black teas is the bitterness.) After tasting the flavor plain, I added some sugar, and found that it brought out the natural sweetness of the tea quite well. Adding the sugar gave the tea a fuller dimension, and created some interesting and flavorful after-notes that were pretty awesome. Finally I added some milk, and my only complaint is that black tea contains caffeine and I can't drink this before bed every night. Adding milk created a delicious evening beverage with multilayered flavor, and made me want a second cup. Highly important to me, perhaps irrelevant to other people: the milk also let the color of the tea come out more clearly (black tea in a black cup isn't exactly striking), and showed it to be strong and of a quality cut. I can't abide black teas that look "thin" or "watery" when milk is added because they're almost always weak or stale-tasting, and the yunnan gongfu with milk is a beautiful thick rich ruddy color. Aesthetically pleasing, flavorfully excellent.

I saved the tea in the steeper while I enjoyed the first cup, then went back to see how it brewed up on a re-brew. The answer is "much weaker, and with a different flavor." HOWEVER, I didn't feel this was an issue--the second cup had a different flavor, was better without milk instead of with it, and was almost like getting an entirely different kind of tea for a single price. As a bedtime nightcap, it was ideal; I can also see the re-brew being great for kids who think they like tea, but aren't really ready for brews more complicated than Lipton and chamomile yet.

Overall impression: delicious tea, and a great starter for people who want to begin exploring teas but don't want to dive headfirst into stuff that tastes absolutely nothing like the tea they find at the grocery store. I strongly recommend the brewing directions above, as the package provided none. If I could change one thing about the product, this would be it--teas are variable, and knowing the instructions for an optimum cup are important.

DISCLAIMER: In accordance with Amazon.com policy, I fully disclose that I received this product at a reduced cost in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. I stand behind this review as being truthful and based on my real experience with the product.

title: a syrup, not a paste
text:
When this arrived, the seal had been broken and some of it had leaked out all over the jar and the inside of the package. The jar was almost full, so not much leaked out and, since it doesn't need to be refrigerated after opening, I assumed it was still save to eat once I washed off the outside thoroughly. However, it definitely needs a better external and definitely an internal seal for safety purposes.

I was stunned that this was so thin as it is described as a "paste". It is definitely vanilla syrup with real specks of vanilla suspended in a sugar syrup. It works well for ice cream, cake, or stirred into drinks, but it doesn't work the same as vanilla paste which is used for baking as it doesn't have the same consistency or intense vanilla flavor of traditional vanilla paste. This is more of a dessert topping than a paste which is fine, but it was not what I was expecting at all based on the description.

The flavor of this is good. The vanilla comes through authentically and it isn't too sweet (though it is a thin sugar syrup so it adds plenty of sweetness). It also adds a nice look to desserts that it is spooned on top of.

title: Highly Satisfying Taste
text:
I have a strange palate, perhaps. I actually do enjoy plain coffee and earthy, even bitter flavors. This is definitely not bitter tasting to me at all. It’s made from mushrooms so yeah, it does have a mild earthy taste.

What I love the most is the coffee flavor. It’s actually pretty darn good for instant coffee!! I usually loathe instant but will drink it anyway if that’s all I have. But this is something that I genuinely look forward to drinking in the morning.

It’s so fast and easy to make. I does settle in the bottom of the cup when I make too much, but that’s not a problem. I just add more water and finish it off. I enjoy the hint of mushroom flavor, which is barely there in my opinion.

My only real complaint is the amount you get for the cost. I wish there was just more for the money. I’m almost out now, and I simply won’t be able to buy more. I’m really going to miss this!!!

If cost is not a factor then I would recommend this. I really do feel great after drinking this in the morning. It’s just a nice uplifting feeling that lasts for hours. I’m beginning to love these mushrooms!

title: I thoroughly enjoyed the MRE I received
text:
I thoroughly enjoyed the MRE I received, Menu 5 - Chicken with Tomatoes and Feta Cheese. Also contained in the pack was a pack of vegetable-flavored crackers with some jalapeno cheese spread, dried cranberries ("cranberries, osmotic"), a bag of M&Ms, chocolate flavor First Strike energy bar, a pack of grape flavored generic Gatorade electrolyte drink mix, and an accessory pack that included some drinkable instant coffee (I'm not a coffee drinker, but I could drink it with the supplied creamer and sugar -- coffee enthusiasts will undoubtedly be disappointed, of course).

The Chicken main course was excellent -- very flavorful and the chicken was quite tender. The crackers and cheese spread were decent, not great but perfectly edible. The M&Ms and dried cranberries were fresh, as was expected. The grape generic Gatorade was pretty good -- not as good as real Gatorade, but better than Koolaid or Powerade.

Overall I'm very pleased. I hope all of the other menus are as good as this one. I'm definitely planning on buying a few more to keep around for emergencies or camping/etc.

title: OMG...lifesaver!
text:
Our 6th baby. Never had severe nausea before, but this time...wow! Went to the doctor and got a prescription, but needed something less potent for the work hours. Ordered this candy and some honey/tea crystal because of the reviews.

This candy saved our lives. It works! It's a little bit of an odd flavor, but not too bad. There has even been a period where my wife could not eat anything sweet, but she could still eat this candy. Anytime you feel bad, just start sucking on one of these things, and the nausea will go away. You may have to go through 4-6 of them before the nausea is completely gone, but it sure beats the heck out of puking! Go ahead and order the full 3LB bag, because you never know how long the nausea will last, and the candy is a better deal this way.

(The honey/tea crystals are just gross, and I had to throw them ALL away! I even tried just chewing on them--it tasted like jalapeno flavored Pop Rocks--yuck! Do not buy the honey/tea crystals!)

title: Good cup of coffee at a good price and ignor the eco-angle
text: It's a GOOD cup of coffee at a good price. I am little concerned about organic versus non-organic; I just want a good product and organic is of little concern. I don't care if it was produced in the rainy-est  part of any rainforest or in the backyard of a crack house in a Detroit slum. Nor do I care if any family, coffee grower or company makes or is guaranteed a profit. The market will determine whether the product is worthy of a profit. I do not buy the "sizzle"; I buy the steak....and this is a good cup of coffee, without regard to where or how it's produced. The pod is different than the usual type and I expect its construction makes better use of the ground coffee it contains, and I assume that this maker is not being forced to pay a royalty to whomever holds the million dollar pod patent (which means the consumer pays for it....there is nothing free...the consumer pays for everything directly or indirectly). As some earlier reviews have commented there are more grounds remaining in the cup bottom, and I believe that should be expected. The only culture I've ever noted that likes to gulp the last teaspoon of coffee seems to be Americans who traditionally chug the last few drop like downing a jigger of whiskey. Leaving a few grounds in the cup seems to be the norm and not the exception. There were reviews about expiration dates being too short; my product had an expiration date of exactly one year from the day I received the product. My city does not allow any food stuffs mixed with recyclables, so the effort and cost  to make the pod recyclable is lost. BOTTOMLINE: A good cup of coffee at a good price and I've already ordered another variety

title: Result is not what they claim
text: Let me start by saying that I exclusively pump for my baby due issues with breastfeeding.  I have pumped since my baby was 4 days old.  I have established my supply over 13 weeks and I am currently pumping 33-35 oz per day.  At times my girls are superstars and I am able to pump this amount effortlessly.  Other times I need to go through pumping “marathons” in order to meet this quota.  I purchased these cookies to help through these “marathon” times but I have seen no results.  I have consumed them twice per day for 1 week (which gets super expensive) and have seen no results or increase in my supply.  The results seen in these reviews maybe deceiving and I fuentes by other factors, such as pumping frequency and length.  My advice, save the calories, drink plenty of fluids, power pump, invest/rent hospital grade pump, etc..

text: This review is for Tolerant Organic Kids Green Lentil Safari Pasta, 8 Ounce Box (Case of 6), Single Ingredient Plant-Based Protein Pasta, Vegan Pasta, Gluten Free Pasta, School Safe, Low Glycemic Index Pasta. This pasta is made with only one ingredient which is organic green lentil flour. It is nice that there aren't a bunch of random things in here and this is healthy. We aren't really sure if we like it though. If you are used to regular pasta, this will taste a little strange to you but it is easy to cover to flavor a little by adding sauce or topping it with different meats and veggies. The biggest issue we seem to have with this is the texture. The texture is different than normal pasta but it is fine when it is fresh and hot. If you let it sit for any amount of time, it seems to get dry, crumbly and chalky. I think it is worth it to try and see if you and your kids will eat it. I also don't recommend keeping any leftovers and putting it in the fridge because the texture becomes strange and you won't want to eat it.

title: Good for those without Local Fresh Options
text:
For the price and the fact that these are processed, these taro pastries are pretty good. But they don’t stand up to the ones I get from the bakery. Like the bakery ones that cost $2.75 each at my locale, these manufactured ones ($12.69/6=$2.12 each) have that good flakiness to them and soft filling. They’re both mildly sweet, but these ones are faintly sweeter with a pinch of more salt than I prefer. I also don’t detect as much of a taro flavor, fragrance, or texture in these as I do in the fresh ones, but that’s not to say that the taro flavor is absent. By texture, I mean that the consistency in these ones is closer to a red bean paste than to a potato; it’s not as smooth or creamy.

If I didn’t live near a bakery that sells fresh taro pastries, I would get these again. Maybe then they would satisfy my taste for taro. As of now, I think I’ll continue to pay the extra 63¢ at my bakery.

The batch I received was made on 12/11/2020 with an expiry date of 4/11/2021.

title: It has a good hotness to it and an intense cinnamon flavor but ...
text:
This cinnamon is richly flavored and has a "hot" snap to it which is very pleasant in baked goods. I have been using Saigon cinnamon in my cafe for the last 17 years and have learned not all Saigon cinnamon is the same. Some varieties stating early harvest and roasted are much more flavorful with dark overtones and a smoky finish. Other varieties have a flavor that is mild and has little of the hot snap that premium Saigon cinnamon is famous for. Kirkland brand Saigon cinnamon falls somewhere in the middle. It has a good hotness to it and an intense cinnamon flavor but not as complex as premiums selling up to four times what this costs. A great value for the dollar, I'm sure you will be pleased.
Something I have noticed on many reviews here is the warning than this will cause liver damage. That warning looks like it comes from well meaning but unread people that don't follow information to its source. The Drs in Mississippi that performed this study stated that a "small percentage" of the test subjects were affected by liver damage with "very high doses" of Saigon cinnamon. Reading further I discovered that this was only in rats with no human correlating data.
Conclusion from most health expertise to use less than a fluid ounce per day and you should be safe, even most individuals who may be susceptible to liver damage. By the way, the compound in cinnamon that causes liver damage is the same in Coumadin or Warfarin branded blood thinners.

title: Nice product
text:
Our family has been gluten free for 5 years and this is definitely one of the better tasting products.

The one negative, for which I dropped 1 star is the package size. It seems if you go to the store locally most spaghetti packages are 16 ounces, but I've found if it is labeled organic they drop it down to 12 ounces; my guess is to keep the product at a price point similar to the non-organic ones. We have a family of 5 and this just isn't enough, 16 ounces works good, but 12 is not enough.

I've noticed these sort of packaging tricks with many products lately, makes it a bit harder for a consumer to compare apples to apples. For me I'd rather have paid more for a standard size package than have to use a partial box to make up the difference. For a smaller family this may not matter, but for anyone used to a standard package size the difference will be noticeable.

There is a limit to how much cadmium can be found in chocolate too depending on what country you'r in. Bottom line to chocolate lovers like myself- enjoy sparingly :) P.S California has some pretty tight restrictions on a lot of things and require lots of warnings in regards to chemicals/ so its common to see these warning on anything from food to furniture.

title: Not a short cut, not authentic...
text:
This isn't horrible but it isn't delicious. I bought it because everyone else in the household disdians Thai food. I figured I'd buy it and make enough food for myself for 2 meals. I bought some vegetables to include because most ready made dishes/sauces don't ever seem to have enough. I usually have international type pantry items and basic groceries on hand and it really helped once I slow stewed the veges I dropped in with the chicken thighs in the sauce. I had to add lime zest, lemongrass, ginger, cilantro, the lime's juice, a can of coconut milk, fish sauce, soy sauce as well as some spices to give the dish life.
Now if you've never made this dish or tasted an authentic Thai Green Curry before you may like it. It is so mild that my Mother liked it when she made a packet for herself strictly to the directions on the back. She has a palate that can't stand hot or robust spicing. Now I'm not saying this product is inedible. It's just that it's not a base, it's not a shortcut nor is it a full sauce. It would be better to just buy the Thai Green Curry paste you'd get in an Oriental grocery store and make your own.

title: Perfect for secret batching! :)))
text:
I've made several batches of almond paste (1 cup almond flour, 3/4 c. [organic] powdered sugar, 1 tsp. vanilla, one egg substitute and a tbsp water all mashed together - easy!)
as well as biskvi bottoms (baked the almond paste into white knucklingly delicious chewy cookies) and used it in vegan cakes. Oh, oh, oh so good!!
(But it's not like I've made tiny, personal batches of marzipan late every single night after I've made everyone else go to bed..just me, the TV and the marzipan..Not!)

PROS:
- Dry and easy to scoop out
- Bakes beautifully
- Tastes great with a subtler almond flavor than expected
- Not so finely ground that you can confuse it with "regular" flour; still has a crunchy/chewy quality

CON - and this is only a packaging, not a product, con:
- The reclosable zipper broke after opening twice. (I ended up using a bag clip).

To be on the safe side I keep this in the fridge, away from bugs with and bad intentions (of course excluding silverfish and ladybugs, which would never have anything but perfectly lovely intentions, I'm sure), from small, grasping and somehow always sticky hands, as well as away from paws and long, drooly tongues, which are amazingly adept at reaching into yummy smelling pantry corners.

title: Mediocre bean quality. Over roasted; especially for a Colombian, which is not my personal "cup of tea" (pun intended).
text:
I like different coffees for different reasons. I believe that Colombian coffee is supposed to be a "mild, well-balanced" coffee. I'll be the first to admit that I'm a bit of a coffee snob though I prefer to use the term "connoisseur" but there's a lot to be said for humility so I'll just keep it at snob :-).

This coffee lacks two attributes that cause this it to be less than terrific. Admittedly; one of them is a personal preference while the other is absolutely objective and measurable. On a personal level, I prefer my beans to not be roasted as long (not as dark and oily) as these beans are roasted; particularly for a coffee that should be mild. This over roasting; analagous to the degree of roasting by the very large and well-known Seattle-based coffee company with the green & white logo, in my opinion, gives it a bitter taste as opposed to a smooth one. This may be okay for a French Roast but not a Colombian lover.

The second, objective and measurable feature about these beans is that while they may be Arabica, they are smaller and thus of a lower grade of coffee bean than the brand of Colombian I've been drinking and will go back to drinking now that I've tried this. At best, these beans would be graded AA and while I didn't measure them I don't believe they're even an AA grade. AA is a coffee grading term that refers to a specific, larger than normal, bean size. Kenya AA coffee beans, for example, pass through Grade 18 (18/64" diameter) sieve perforations, but are too large to pass through Grade 16 (16/64" diameter) sieve perforations. AA+ refers to coffee beans AA or larger. The term AA is used as a coffee quality "grade" due to the general correlation (with many exceptions) between coffee bean size and coffee flavor. If a side by side taste test were done and all other things being equal, even a non-discerning palette will easily taste a difference between an AA and an AA+ grade of bean.

Unfortunately, you won't find the best Colombian coffee here at Amazon. For a real Colombian taste treat try the Colombian Supremo (the biggest and best grade of Colombian beans) from a company whose initials are GJ's (Amazon's policy not to give out competitors' names in reviews). Expect to pay about $14/pound but better is almost always going to cost more; though there is a great Kenya AA (Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf Kenya AA) (CBTL) available for a good price, at least at the time of this writing, currently here at Amazon. I just paid $8.04/pound here at Amazon which is an amazingly good price for that coffee. It costs almost double that if bought directly from CBTL.

title: What a shame
text:
After trying this coconut milk from the local store a couple years ago, I decided to buy future cans through Amazon - resulting in a moderate savings. I chose it because it was tasty, high quality, and BPA free. I had gone through about 2-3 boxes; no complaints.

Then they shipped me an order that was manufactured in Sri Lanka, not Thailand as the others were. Apparently this is due to a shortage. That would be fine if the taste was the same, but are you kidding me with this quality control!? The taste and texture are horrible. It's like they added powdered and freeze dried coconut milk to dirty water. It completely ruined the smoothie I added it to.

I now will be throwing away 11.5 cans of this stuff, as I didn't get to it before the return window. I don't know what the risk of getting another case from Sri Lanka is, but I'm not taking a chance. I'll be buying Native Forest from the local store from now on. (And checking EVERY SINGLE CAN to make sure it's from Thailand.)

People need to keep that in mind when weighing a healthier snack item like this against some unhealthy junk food snack that contains a bunch of chemicals and sugar. Whenever I'm able to go out backpacking someday, I'm definitely have a bunch of these snack bars in various flavors in my pack. text: The two jars with this Gefilte Fish were packed extremely carefully (probably at the Manischewitz factory). The "Best By" date on the jars was somewhere in October of 2024 (and I received the jars in March of 2022). The taste of the fish was okay, and the taste of the broth was better than okay. The broth was not jelled, by the way, just liquid. I cannot compare the taste of this Gefilte Fish with the tastes of other Gefilte Fishes available on Amazon; it was probably about three or four years since I ate any of them. P.S. All these Gefilte Fishes which are sold in jars should be called, I think, "Nongefilted" Gefilte Fish, because the Gefilte Fish is a stuffed fish, and in jars we receive only the stuffing (and the broth). It was a lifetime ago when I ate the real Gefilte Fish, made by my grandmother. She boiled fish (carp usually) that long that even the bones of the fish were eatable after that boiling. And fish was stuffed, inside the skin of carp, and it was eaten with the horseredish with beets. I have no idea whether the real Gefilte Fish, the stuffed one, is made and sold today... Maybe in some restaurants?

The benefits of these powdered binders, thickeners, and emulsion stabilizers cannot be overstated. They help to make the final product of homemade recipes such as my frappuccino, flavored infused syrups, and other concoctions, look and act as they should. This Xanthan Gum, for instance, helps to bind ingredients together in a blended drink that would normally separate without constantly being stirred. It only takes a tiny amount blended into a recipe to work. The 15 oz. package I bought will last me quite a long time.

title: These jars are packed with heat!
text:
This is almost a five level heat factor hot sauce. Almost. It's about 4 1/2. So, it's high and wow, it has some flavor and heat packed into this bottle. I've actually never even heard of the scotch bonnet pepper - I must be living under a rock. I'm familiar with the jalapeno pepper but the heat factor compared to the Scotch Bonnet pepper makes jalapeno peppers look weak! The scotch bonnet pepper is anywhere 12 to 140 times hotter than the jalapeno pepper. The scotch bonnet pepper is closely related to the habanero pepper so if you are familiar with that pepper, take note.

One thing I noticed about this hot sauce and the scotch bonnet flavor is that it is a sweet-hot flavor all mixed into one. Yes, it's spicy but it also has some sweet mixed in. It's a very slight sweet taste - very mild - just a hint of it - almost like an apple and a cherry. It's very distinct and it is something that I have found to enjoy while using this hot sauce. Because of the heat factor, I haven't used this a lot. It will burn your mouth and throat for a good 1-2 minutes after swallowing. It had me almost in tears - forehead sweating! I wouldn't recommend using this for chips and hot sauce but a tad here on perhaps a fajita, potatoes to spice 'em up, or a special Caribbean recipe is sure to impress your taste buds. This is PURE heat packed into a bottle. I have thoroughly enjoyed the unique level of heat and the sweetness that make my taste buds scream for more - but only a little bit more at a time, hah! This does have to be stored in the fridge after opening to maintain freshness. Oh, and two bottles! Keep one for yourself and give the other to a person who loves the heat. I actually gave one bottle to my dad who is a lover of the Texas Pete hot sauce. We'll see how he feels about this one!

DISCLAIMER: I received this hot sauce at a discounted price or for free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: Surprisingly good Assam tippy tea. I'm impressed. Here are some tips for getting the best flavor.
text:
I'm a little obsessed with good tea. I thought I'd order this to take with me on a business trip, so I could enjoy loose leaf tea on the road, and not place my more expensive stash at risk while I travel.

Well, I have to say I'm VERY impressed! I was expecting mediocre, okay, pleasant tea. This is actually very good stuff.

I mixed this tea with the Ahmad Ceylon Earl Grey to add some flavor. I used one teaspoon of Earl Grey, two teaspoons of the Kalami Assam, placing the Earl Grey on top of the unflavored Assam to balance out the extraction. I also added two teaspoons of Xilitol (healthy sugar substitute) to the pot.

I used a standard teapot with a contact infuser, boiling 0.75 liters of water, waiting ten seconds, then pouring the water into the infuser. I set the timer to 3:00 minutes. After 3:00 minutes, I removed the tea leaves, stirred the pot, covered it, and began pouring.

The flavor was very good, well-balanced, and not bitter. after the third cup, the flavor actually improved (this tasted better when it cooled off a bit, not too hot). I enjoyed every sip, and finished the whole pot within 40 minutes.

Here are a couple of additional tips, after some experimenting:

1. My ideal brewing time for this tea is 3 minutes. 4 minutes can work if you like a stronger, more astringent brew. After 4 minutes the tea quickly became bitter. 3 minutes seems idea.

2. Count to ten (ten seconds) after boiling the water before pouring it over the tea leaves. Otherwise you might burn your tea and ruin the flavor. This tea blend has many broken leaves in it, which release a lot of tannic acid when burned. That's what leads to the bitter flavor.

3. If you hot brew this tea and then refrigerate it, the tea will become very cloudy and lose much of its fragrant flavor. Although I prefer iced tea, this tea is best served warm or hot.

4. This tea makes a decent cold brew. If you cold brew the tea, it will not become cloudy. I am mixing 1/3 Earl Grey, 2/3 Kalami Assam, 2 table spoons (6 teaspoons) in a 32 ounce Mason Jar, and then leaving it in the refrigerator for two days, with some sugar in the jar. The flavor is very smooth and uplifting, with no bitterness. The tea comes out clear (not cloudy) if you cold brew it. The flavor is different from a hot brew.

Hope that helps. I do recommend this as a budget tea. It will take me 6 months to get through this supply, if I use it to make two teapots per week.

title: (Mostly) like movie popcorn!
text:
I bought this product somewhere else, but will likely stock up on Amazon due to the better prices.

I've only tried the butter version, but can confidently say that it basically takes like movie theater popcorn! It's slightly lighter, but no less in terms of taste. If you're the type to slather the popcorn in the fake movie theater butter, then you'll likely notice a difference. The problem is that the butter only really covers the top layers of the popcorn anyway.

This tastes like a fluffier and taster version of the movie popcorn that's not slathered in butter. It's just better. It doesn't have a stale taste, and the butter flavor is evenly distributed among every popped kernel. There are some crushed kernels, but no more than you'd expect from most bagged popcorns.

Honestly, I've stopped using bagged microwave popcorn. There are no uncooked kernels or overcooked kernels. There's always just the right amount of butter and salt on each kernel to taste like this is straight from the theater (unless, like I mentioned you're a fan of drenching the top layers in fake butter). Overall, I can't recommend this product enough!

title: Servings Per Bottle = Greater Than One, Apparently
text:
This New England winter is brutal. The winds keep howling, the temps keep dropping and the snow is pounding us like we owe the clouds money. Every day I'm bundling up and shoveling four feet of something -- snow, ice, stranded hybrids, Kennedys -- and I'm done with it. I just wanted to find some way to warm up.

Also, to feel my toes again and have my [...] crawl back out of my rib cage. But I settled for trying to warm up.

I've always heard that if you warm up on the inside, then the outside will follow. So I bought this bottle of El Yucateco and saved it for the next inevitable snowstorm. When I was done shoveling and still shivering, I opened it up and slammed it down the hatch -- all eight ounces.

First, a few words about the taste: El Yucateco red has a nice tangy element, lingering through the forward habanero kick and beyond. The additional spices play well with the primary pepper, adding a savory depth that's more than just pure heat or capsaicin jolt. The tomato base and hearty thick texture promise a richness and complexity of flavor that is delivered quite nicely to the palate.

And now, a few words about the unrelenting napalm burn that traveled around my mouth, down my gullet and -- over the next twelve hours or so -- into, through, and out my intestines, scorching and defiling every square millimeter of delicate insides that it touched: [...]

Overall, I'd say this would make a very nice complement to a variety of Mexican or South American dishes, as well as grilled meats, starchy vegetables or as an extra kick to, say, garlicky green veggie side dishes. Also, it's unlikely that I'll be able to sit down without searing pain for at least a month. So 'use in moderation' is the take-home message, I suppose.

title: In one word: Awesome!
text: Nutiva's Organic White Chia Seeds are a fantastic, nutritious food you can add to most anything. The seeds are mostly tasteless so they won't adversely affect the food or drink they've been added to. This is my first experience with chia seeds and I could not be happier. Looking to find an egg replacement for recipes, and having had mixed results with flax seed which sometimes alters the taste, I set out to try the chia in as many different recipes as possible. The recipes ranged from cookies to muffins and cupcakes, breads to pancakes, and they've all turned out terrific; the seeds worked just as well as eggs and I feel better about it. In place of 1 egg, 1 tablespoon of chia seed with 2-3 tablespoons of water, soaked for 15-20 minutes, worked out best in my baking experience. They are also great in homemade granola bars, tossed into both cold and hot cereals, and in smoothies or juices. The versatility of the "superfood" the Aztecs and Mayans revered is amazing. The nutritional benefits, which are many, of chia seeds can be found by an internet search, but a some of them include: omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, protein, essential minerals, and rare antioxidants.  I'm sold and I highly recommend [[ASIN:B0054TWQMM Nutiva Organic White Chia Seeds, 14-Ounce, 2-Count Pouches]] without reservation. You can be sure I'll always have this stocked in my pantry.

title: Taste Delicious, but Beware of High Saturated Fat, Cholesterol, & Sodium
text:
[[VIDEOID:c7bcfcebf809a247c6a6d4e0d2a3310e]] Hello Everyone!

Thank you for watching or reading this review :)

Campbell's Go Soup's "Creamy Red Pepper with Smoked Gouda Taste" taste DELICIOUS. You will catch the different flavors of:

Tomato
Gouda (which tastes like smoked cheese in this soup)
Spices
Sweet Basil

If you love spices, cheese and tomato, you will love this soup.

HOWEVER, if you have ANY health issues (i.e. high blood pressure, cholesterol, on a low-fat diet, etc), this soup is NOT for you.

Why?

Because the nutrition guide is deceptive, it lists the soup for 2 servings but you WILL eat this in one setting. This soup will take 90% of your saturated fat, 40% of your cholesterol, and 66% of your sodium intakes for the entire day. Those numbers are crazy high, I was thirsty for water after I finish this video due to the very high salt content.

If the high numbers don't bother you, then you will LOVE this soup if you are a fan of tomatoes, or cheeses, or spices (I am a lover of all three) :)

title: These have been my most favorite packaged noodles by far for more than a decade
text:
Though I never bought this item from Amazon, these have been my most favorite packaged noodles by far for more than a decade, and today my taste buds feel vindicated after finding out that it's the number one best seller on Amazon. I have tried a few other noodles out of curiosity, always in the hope of discovering better or other great-tasting pre-packaged noodles, but have never found anything close to it. That said, I have not really tried out a large number of other varieties of noodles and I also came across The Ramen Rater website today and do plan to try out his all time best packages over the next few months .. but I digress.

While I like its extra-hot spicy taste, I usually add the following ingredients (sparingly, so as not to overwhelm its original taste): shrimp, green hot serrano chili peppers, button mushrooms, frozen peas, a few slices of chopped tomatoes, garlic, ginger, Chinese parsley (a k a coriander leaves or Cilantro) and last but not the least, my own secret ingredient - a few tablespoons of ready-made Tom Yum Paste which I buy from Asian grocery stores. Sometimes I also add lime juice and or lemon / lime zest at the end if I want a slightly sour taste. These ingredients, especially the Tom Yum paste even make far lesser noodles like [[ASIN:B003OB2DM0 Maruchan Instant Lunch, Hot and Spicy Shrimp, 2.25-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12)]] - which are sold by Walmart for about thirty cents per cup - taste almost (but not quite) as good.

title: Lucy Jo wherever you are, I love you
text: As someone that suffers from extreme GERD, I mean the kind that has put me in the hospital a few times, the kind that nearly killed me at least once, this coffee is heaven sent. I had been strictly cold brew for the acid reduction but now I can finally brew a hot pot of delicious coffee and I can absolutely 100% tell you, yes, it's much lower in acid that your typical Maxwell house. I have had a few of Jucy Jo's blends this one is my favorite. It's mildly sweet, a touch earthy, just a mild touch of bitterness on the back end, it's a smooth, easy to drink black, great with a touch of half and half and a single spoon of sugar to just brighten up the sweetness a bit, but sincerely, even if you don't typically drink coffee black, try this one, it's quite pleasant as a black cup of coffee and more than anything, it really does hold up to it's claim, it should not upset your stomach. Trust me, I have had motility exams and my stomach acid production is pretty much record setting, so I had to give up regular hot coffee for years in exchange for cold brew that killed just enough of the acid to make it drinkable for me. Lucy Jo has me enjoying hot coffee again. I love her wherever that beautiful acid killing coffee roasting lady is.

title: Keto family’s friend
text:
We are a family that is partly keto and those members of our family stick to it.

We’ve tried all different types of pork rinds - regular, BBQ, anything else you can possibly find. These are the best by far.

Why you ask?
1) Decent price - you can pick up an 8oz barrel for around $5 usually which is a way better deal than those small bags in the store for $3.50
2) They have very few of those bad looking ones that can taste questionable and if you find one in these it generally still tastes good.
3) You can tell they are fresh
4) the barrel has a lid - it sounds silly but we find they keep better than those bags with chip clips
5) for those keto folks - these definitely hit that crunch craving
6) I typically find larger pieces than in some of the other brands which I like

Cons:
- How to hide these from other people in family? they disappear so quickly...

title: Foodies Will LOVE It (Even Non-Foodies Like Me Can Use It to Dress Up Ordinary Meals to Seem Gourmet)
text:
PROS AT A GLANCE:
Definitely gourmet, flavorful, lower sodium than regular salt, high-quality, great information provided from the company about product, doesn't pull moisture from food, kosher product, can be dried for more traditional grinding and use (company provides information on how to do this)

CONS AT A GLANCE:
It's expensive "just for salt," but you get what you pay for, and this is definitely gourmet stuff. For foodies, this will be 100% worth the cost; for regular people who just want some cheap salt to toss onto something, the price and quantity will be a drawback.

FULL REVIEW:
To be honest, I hadn't really known what to expect from gourmet salt. I'm not exactly what I would call a "foodie," but regular salt can be a bit too much for me. This has a nice, subtle but effective flavor, and from what I can tell is much healthier than regular salt. It comes in a bag, which I'm not used to, and isn't fully dried, which I'm also not entirely used to. My idea of salt is normally whatever comes in the cheap pour-spout, but I'm pretty sure this salt has now turned me around in my earlier thinking that salt is salt is salt is salt...

A little goes a long way with this salt, and so far I've tried seasoning my dinner with it and adding it to popcorn. It has a lovely flavor that isn't quite as "in your face" as regular table salt, and I found both my dinners and my popcorn much more pleasant with this addition than with regular salt. Because it's not fully dried, it doesn't dry out your food, so you can have complimentary salt flavoring without turning your meal into a dry mess. I'm experimenting with adding it into different dishes and will hopefully be able to upload some photos and videos soon. For the time being, I wanted to hop on here and say that yes, I'm a believer. Thank goodness a little of this stuff goes a long way, because I will be coming back for more when I run out!

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review, and that is what I am providing. I will never shy away from listing negatives about products just because I received a discount; usually, I choose products that I am interested in trying already, and check out the reviews ahead of time to ensure it's something I will probably like, so many of my reviews are positive as a result of careful selection upfront, not because my positive reviews have been "bought." If there are any questions I haven't addressed, or if there's more information I could provide in the meantime, please feel free to comment and I'll update as soon as I can!
