title: Great for royal icing!
text:
I love decorating sugar cookies, but when my daughter was diagnosed with food allergies I knew I needed to change my recipes. This powder is exactly what I have been looking for to make royal icing. I had previously tried using aquafaba instead of meringue powder, but the icing didn’t harden as well and the colors seemed to run more easily. This meringue powder yields a nice icing consistency that dries relatively quickly, smoothly, and is quite comparable to regular royal icing. I was able to draw on the cookie with food marker after leaving them for about 5 hours, so it definitely “crusts” like normal royal icing. The taste is also very good. It’s a bit lemony, which hides the beany, earthy taste that comes with chickpea substitutes. I actually couldn’t resist eating the icing while I was making the cookies, so Id say it’s yummy. I used Sweet Ambs suggestions on how to make the frosting and overall I was very pleased with the results!

The one downside is the price. The suggested recipe calls for 45g of meringue powder with just 1lb of powdered sugar. That’s about twice the amount needed for an equivalent amount of sugar using typical meringue. A bag for $18 (+ shipping) is only going to give you about 10 dozen cookies worth of frosting.

Other than that would definitely recommend this product!

I bought this to use for stocking stuffer candy for Christmas, expecting to give the milk chocolates to my kids and wife and keeping the dark for myself, since I'm the only one who likes it. Well now I'm stuck with more than a hundred pieces of dark chocolate and just a few of the caramel type for each of them. It's Dove, so it's still delicious, but I'm pretty annoyed that the package failed this badly at such a basic thing as including all the types listed. So avoid this unless you like gambling and/or dark chocolate A LOT.

title: It's good with some issues.
text:
This review is for the coffee flavor. I'll start with the good. It tastes great. It tastes like a milk-shake made with coffee ice cream. I've had it chilled and at room temp. Chilled is better but if for whatever reason you need it on the go and can't keep it cold, it still tastes fine. The texture is good. Some protein shakes have a chalky texture or after taste which these do not. I could drink these daily without tiring of them and the fact that there are a few other flavor is a bonus. It's also nice that you do not need a separate bottle like with whey powder. You just bring the drink with you, pop the top, and enjoy. No mess or cleanup.

The following are not necessarily pros or cons just thing I think need to be said. These are not, IMO, diet or weight loss shakes. They have 330 calories. This is meant to replace a meal not add protein to one. Unlike a whey powder shake that will have around 100-150 calories almost all coming from protein (25 grams or so), these have 12 fat, 38 carbs, and only 16 grams of protein. This isn't a negative just something to be aware of. If you are looking to increase the protein content of a meal, this is the wrong product. If you are underweight or struggle to get enough calories in per day this is a perfect product.

The negative main negative here is the value. It's just very expensive compared to many of the alternatives. I suppose you are paying for the convenience. Personally, I would not use these daily due to the cost. I might keep a 6 pack for quite a while using them in the odd occasion that I need a full meal's worth of calories but don't have time to eat whole foods and for whatever reason cannot skip that particular meal. I was fortunate enough to get them for free for review but I do not think I will go back and order a pack with my own money. It just doesn't get there for me. If cost is not a consideration for you, and the product fits your needs, it really is a good product.

title: Great Margarita Mix!
text:
I’ve been trying to maintain a low carb lifestyle. Living in Texas, friends and family are always meeting up in one of our local Tex-Mex restaurants for Margaritas a few times a month. It makes me sad. It’s just not the same sitting there drinking a low carb beer. With this mix, I can have a Margarita! Obviously, it’s not quite the Top Shelf with fresh lime and Grand Marnier, but it sure tastes better than an ultralight beer.

I order a regular size glass of ice water, and a double shot of a midrange tequila. I take a few sips from the glass, then add the tequila and mix. Voila! I’m drinking a Margarita! And it isn’t a bit less tasty than your average house Margarita.

And these packets fit in my hand bag, readily available whenever I find myself swinging off a barstool in the local Tex-Mex spot!

title: Thank Frank
text:
Frank's Red Hot is the standard bearer of the hot sauce world. As I noted in my review of [[ASIN:B0002PSOJW Huy Fong, Sriracha Hot Chili Sauce, 17 Ounce Bottle]], Tobasco is yesterday's news. Frank's is just a far superior product. Tobasco is your grandfather's hot sauce, just because he Frankly didn't know better. Not the grandfather you liked, the a-hole one. I prefer Frank's along with Louisiana-based hot sauces like Crystal for my every day use. AND I DO USE IT EVERY DAY. I put hot sauce on everything, including but not limited to:
Rice
Meat
Fish
Pizza
Pasta
Boobs (just checking if you are still paying attention)
Ethnic foods
Chicken products - not limited to the wings
Assorted Poultry
Wild Game
Sandwiches
Mozz Sticks
Mexican food - especially Trader Joe's Tamales which are f'ing delicious. Don't hate the player.

For those of you in the recipe game. Here is the recipe for Buffalo Sauce for wings: 1 Bottle of Franks for 1 stick of Butter. Heat on low. Stir. Boom. Dunzo.

It doesn't have the most kick in the world, but I ain't hatin, it just tastes good.

In conclusion, thanks Frank, you did good.

title: Versatile, Ready Made Broth
text:
I enjoy using beef broth for a homemade version of French Onion soup and the chicken soup is great for adding more flavor to rice and other dishes. The soup makes a good foundation for many dishes - eaten alone, it's a little bland. You can find recipes online that use up the whole 32 ounces at once because once you open a carton, you have to put it in the fridge and I tend it to forget about it and end up wasting the rest. The large size is the only issue I have with it, as I don't have a large family and using up one huge container of broth in one go is not practical. What I ended up doing is using half of the carton for soup and then pouring the rest into an ice cube tray so that I have ready made broth cubes.

Lastly, this lot of four boxes was carefully packaged and didn't leak, unlike the previous box I had ordered from the company. So overall my experience this time around was OK.

title: This is one of many reasons why Coffee Bean beats Bux
text: After 20 years in LA I came to love going to the Coffee Bean. Their brews are smoother and richer and the powders they use in their lattes and blended drinks give way better flavor and depth than the clowing syrups used by Starbucks. Sadly, when we moved away we never found anything even close to CB quality and taste so we started to order the powders on here. The vanilla is the best I have ever tasted, their chocolate powder is lovely for coffee, hot cocoa or shakes and this white chocolate is surprisingly delicious. Yes, it has quite a lot of sugar in one serving and the canister goes quickly if you use it daily but if this is your only sugar splurge it's not bad really and the taste is just incredible. As I grew to love the Coffee Bean's line of extreme blended drinks, which are stronger, I now make mine at home with a coconut milk base, plenty of good instant, the powder and ice. Sometimes I brew a few shots of Lavazza espresso in my Bialetti and add powder and ice. My husband never cared for coffee until I started making these at home. Now he loves it almost more than I do. Honestly, if you are a coffee person and love a rich sweet flavor, hot or cold, this is the platinum standard in coffee ingredients. But I still wish they would open CB in the Midwest!

title: Nom Nom Nom
text:
I think this was the best purchase decision I made all year. When my kids were little I never let baked goods from the store in the house and every night ground flour to bake with but drifted away from that as they got older and flew the nest. After years of buying fairly adequate bread, crackers whatnot at the store I decided to go back to making my own. I bought a Wondermill Jr. hand mill and based on previous reveiws here I ordered this Great River Organic Milling Hard Red Spring Wheat.

The other reviewers were correct this is absolutely fabulous wheat. It has a very high gluten content and makes a very dark flavorful satisfying loaf.

I would especially recommend this to anyone new to bread-making. I don't think you can make a bad load with this some good yeast and a bit of elbow grease. I used the SAF Instant you can order buy the pound just like the big bakeries do. It's just plain good yeast.

The best thing about this wheat is you can make each loaf for less than a dollar =))

Oh...this wheat is not good for pie crusts pastry kind of things...the gluten content is too high and will make anything like that tough. This is to make glorious bread.

title: Open Bottles in Huge Box
text:
I ordered these ketchup bottles, some cereal, and some Pop-Tarts for my kids, even though there was already a 1 star review that said that the bottles were not sealed. I thought that maybe it was a one-time issue. A huge box arrived today with all 3 items in it, and the ketchup bottles had rattled around the box, smashing into everything else, and leaking all over the place.

I tried to wash off the bottles, but then began to wonder which bottle it was that had leaked. The answer? There is no way to tell, as there were NO seals on ANY of the bottles. They all arrived unsealed.

If you don't mind about having bottles with no seal, and choose to order them anyway, my advice is to only order the ketchup, and wait a few days before ordering any other foodstuffs. Otherwise, you, too, may find that the ketchup is all over, and that anything else you've bought has been hammered in its travels by the out of control ketchup.

It also didn't help that, by packaging all these things together, the box was so heavy that my son had to help me into the house with it.

title: Much More Than Just Hot
text:
I do not like sauces that:
- overwhelm the flavor of the food they are put on
- don't have their own distinct flavor
- are excessively salty (I'm looking at you Tabasco)
- are excessively vinegary (still looking at you Tabasco)

I do like sauces that:
- pack walloping heat
- have lots of flavor and character
- make my friends lose their composure

Scorpion Hot Sauce delivers on all counts. Balsamic vinegar, raisins, and soy sauce stack together to make a uniquely sweet base that goes a long way towards balancing what the ingredient label lists as "pepper extract". I'm guessing that "pepper extract" is just molecular capsaicin because this stuff is freaking HOT.

title: Make it taste even better!
text: My kids love their Macaroni & Cheese but one day all we had was a generic brand.  They didn't eat it all that well (Kraft really is the best) so I decided to try to make it a little better for them.  Follow the recipe on the box with a couple exceptions.  Put one slice of velveeta chees in while melting the butter (I melt the butter while the noodles are draining so as to melt the butter and velveeta faster) and add 1/3 cup milk.  What you'll have is a less expensive version of the really creamy macaroni and cheese that Kraft sells for a lot more money.  By adding extra milk and cheese they're even getting more calcium.  My kids love it when I throw in hot dogs and even peas so feel free to throw in other things since it's so cheesy (the extra cheesy sauce will take things like peas that kids don't normally eat and make them taste good).  Give it a try and see what you and/or your kids think!

title: A mixed bag
text:
First thing I encountered with this, was trying to figure out the mixing portions. So incredibly stupid that there's no mixing scoop provided in the bag. The instructions say to "first mix 1 scoop (20g) of powder with 1 tablespoon of water until there are no lumps. Then fill up with 1 cup (200ml) cold water and stir in." I even stirred through the bag to try and find the scoop. There's no scoop. Upon looking up the conversion of 20 grams of powder to tablespoons, cups, and teaspoons... There's no clear cut "scoop" to use. I settled upon 2 tablespoons and a third. Very frustrating.
Upon mixing it, I don't see a way to achieve "until there are no more lumps". Even after adding the cup of water, it's still very difficult to get it to completely blend into liquid without clumps. The second time I mixed this, I used a shaker bottle and it was a little easier. It does continue to separate and clump though.
Ultimately, I used this with my oatmeal and it was ok. It's not nearly as tasty as store bought oat milk. But it should yield a lot of liquid for my oatmeal. And it ultimately does work for that. One suggestion.... PROVIDE A SCOOP IN THE BAG.

title: The best way to spruce up pasta sauce!
text: This was a huge childhood favorite of mine, so I'm so happy I've rediscovered it! Back when I was a kid (25 years ago or so) this was called "Spicy Spaghetti Sauce" but I can see why they changed the name--it's not spicy-hot, just spicy as in "has a lot of spices". It really does wonders to zip up more plain spaghetti sauces! The only problem I've found with it is that when you get toward the end of the bottle it tastes more like salt than anything else because of how the spices settle--but hey, that's pretty normal. This size bottle lasts a while, too--before I bought this 2-bottle set I got a single bottle, and I believe it lasted me about six months--that might not sound that long, but I'm a pasta fiend, so I probably average something like 2-3 plates of spaghetti a week. If you want an easy way to have flavorful spaghetti sauce without making it from scratch or buying a fancier, expensive bottle of the stuff, this is the BEST way to do it! (And I've found that it's pretty good at adding a little zip to some of the less-spiced expensive jars, too!)

title: Nice gift package
text:
This package from Drive Coffee comes packed in a gift box. Opening the box up, you see a whole lot of tightly packed shredded paper type filling, with a post card on top that has some brewing tips and other info on it. Once nice touch, the card in the box has a "packed and verified by" box where someone hand wrote their name, which left a positive impression for me.

The box I got had a 12oz can of Le Mans single origin medium roast coffee, and the 20oz travel mug. The coffee I normally buy comes in bags with a valve on it that lets you squeeze out the excess air, and allows gas to escape, so a can is a little different. The can did have a bunch of paper residue on it from all the packing material. It also has a hand written "roasted on" date, and the one I got was approximately 1 month old at the time I received it. 1 month is about the best you will get not ordering direct from a roaster, so I am good with that.

The coffee is a good medium roast.

The travel mug is interesting. It comes in its own retail package. It says it is triple walled. It is a nice looking mug. The lid has a button you press down, and it clicks, which opens the drinking spout. Then you can press it again to seal it and close the drinking spout. The mug does come with care instructions, but I found myself looking at the inside of the lid wondering how on earth to clean it. There are a lot of parts, and it isn't immediately obvious how to disassemble it. This is the kind of lid where, once you use it for coffee, there are so many parts in the lid that will forever taste like coffee, so don't expect to use it for other drinks later without also tasting coffee.

Anyway, it's a nice little package.

First, a bit of reviewer background: I love all tea…black, white, green….the more fragrant and complex, the better, but I’m certainly no professional tea taster/reviewer.

So, if you’re looking for black tea, make sure this type of black tea is what you want or you might be disappointed. If you do like white or green tea, this tea will likely be enjoyed.

title: Its not just about the caffeine
text:
You're probably like me and entered into the search bar "high caffeine coffee" and upon looking at all the options, you go for the ones with the most amount of high reviews, read a few, and order accordingly. I have my staples, but I like the old saying goes, "You don't know what you don't know", so I'm constantly trying out new brands. So you look at Raven's brew and think 'ehhhh...only 800 review? I dunno..."

I'm on my 4th order at the time of this writing, giving me a pretty decent sample of quality reliability. I also am writing this review from the perspective of a consumer who has not only a obsessive love affair with coffee, but a high caffeine tolerance, for me to get that charged state, I typically have to consume twice as much as the average person.

Boy am I glad I gave this a try. While I confess what I was looking for was something to turbo charge my mental processes for those sluggish days where as a self employed person, I -NEED- to get stuff done, and given my high caffeine tolerance this takes more than standard coffee. The copy on Deadman's Reach suggested I definitely found what I was looking for, but to blunt about my expectations, I figured that it'd likely not taste all that great. I was so very -very- wrong.

Deadman's is a *great* tasting dark roast, but it does matter how you brew it. I possess an absurd number of ways to brew coffee and even espresso, but my favorite is pour over. Putting Deadman's through a ordinary coffee drip coffee maker or a Keurig (something I used to be a raving fan of) is like drinking fine wine from a sweaty cowboy boot. It becomes too acidic, loses a great deal of it's flavor depth, coming across more as char than coffee. But with a pour over or even a french press, the flavor is downright sultry, smooth and commanding of attention.

Worth noting: I don't drink this every day, I have my other go-to brand for daily use, Deadman's is a combination of need for the higher octane and committing to knocking down important goals AFTER I've had a meditative 20 minutes of intimate savoring of my Deadmans. I'm completely serious, the flavor grabs me and makes the cup something I focus on and savor while pondering what I have to prioritize and absolutely get done. Then, after the last sip...its -ON-!!

So does it give you a turbo boost? Let me put it this way, after a cup I get out my Batman cape and get busy. A 2nd cup? Tony Stark's got nothing on me. 3rd cup...sorry can't say, never had more than 2
But the real magic of Deadmans (IMO) is how you get that kind of kick with such sultry, rich flavor. (again method matters).

Value: Ok this isn't cheap, at $15 for 12 oz of beans it's totally understandable if you said to yourself "Pfft...too much." However this is a *definite* case of quality over quantity. You won't be drinking this all day, 1 cup for those days you're just dragging tail and you just know your usual morning caffeine fix is not going to cut it... 2 cups on your zombie days. So these 12 oz actually go further because you literally drink less of it, even if you're a religious coffee consumer like I am. This 12 oz bag lasts as long as my 2lb bags do, despite how great it tastes, I hit the Deadman's only 2-3x a week. Each occasion is an event for me, I don't drink this on auto-pilot, I savor the mug as I scheme to take over the world knowing when I'm at the bottom of the cup, it's go time.

And as mentioned above, on my 4th bag over a 5 month period. Each has been outstanding in freshness and flavor, the bloom is almost a mushroom cloud. The beans I've bought roast to order aren't any fresher, seriously...this is true coffee snob quality. Give it a try, you won't be disappointed.

I have found it cheaper in only one local grocery store, it is not easy to find in mainstream stores. It's imported from Germany and its currently the only instant coffee I'd recommend. Sometimes I add one or one and a half tablespoons to a large coffee mug and if I want it lighter well just add less. The flavor is strong and bold but not too bold in my opinion. title: Tasty, but use sparingly.
text:
This product is basically lemon flavored table salt. That being said, I love it. I use it often on veggies or in sauces to give it a more sour and savory flavor.

I'll sprinkle a little on my tongue from time to time to excite my pallets before a meal to better experience the flavors. It's a pallet pre-exciter.

A little sprinkle in a pint of beer is also nice and brings out flavor tones.

I'm also a fan of using this on sweet apple slices to zest them up a bit, but found that using it on tarter apples like a granny smith are a bit overwhelming on the sour side.

I would not recommend this for anyone with high blood pressure (hypertension) because they are not made with lemons. It's basically table salt coated in malic acid (the stuff they coat warhead candies in to make them super sour.)

Use moderatly.

You don't have to do that with gel coloring.

title: Good Flavor, Steep at Lower Temps
text: As with most teas the strength and taste can vary depending on steeping time and temperature.  I found the steeping at a low temperature (167F) kept the tea light with a grassy taste that is pleasant. title: Decent price, good product, but hard-to-access/store packaging
text:
Paragon's yellow corn for popping is a far better general product than is available for sale in most supermarkets or food stores. Buying this yellow corn through Amazon ensures a fair price and qualifies for free-delivery convenience, as this [or similar] bulk-sized product bought elsewhere would add a $12-20 shipping charge atop the cost of the popping corn itself.

Product arrives in a one heavy, sealed package that is difficult to handle and is non-resealable--and that should not be used for storage: best if this popping corn immediately is placed into 2- or 3-quart air-tight containers (to better facilitate handling and to better preserve taste/"pop-a-bility"). As long as the needed moisture level within the popping kernels is maintained, this product will render somewhat large and delicious popped kernels. Most Paragon kernels pop, but this factor also is dependent upon the oil used and conditions governing the popping. Using butter-flavored coconut oil for popping seems to produce the most delicious results, although popping these Paragon kernels in canola oil renders a light and delicate taste and ensures even more popped kernels.

Overall, Paragon bulk yellow corn is a reliable choice as a general/non-gouremt popping corn.

title: Rich, full-flavored black tea / wonderful aroma - The only tea I carry in my emergency to-go bag
text:
My wife and I discovered this flavor on a trip to Florida, and it instantly became my favorite. It rivals a really, REALLY great cup of coffee in my book. I recommend this variety to everyone I know that loves a good cup of tea.

I assume most tea drinkers enjoy a variety of tea, which we select for the specific circumstance? My wife and I usually have a dozen of our favorites on hand, but this is my go-to tea. It has certain earthiness, but despite it being strong, it's not overpowering. There's only the mildest hint of coconut, but it's presence is there as a counterbalance to the dark earthy tones. VERY well balanced flavor, and it's got an appealing broad spectrum of notes that come together to near perfection for a black tea. Nice pleasant aroma - not perfume-y like an Earl Grey, just a good complement to the flavor.

This is the ONLY tea I have in my emergency to-go bag, because - let's face it, when catastrophe strikes, who doesn't want to take a moment to calm down and gather their thoughts over a perfect cup of tea?

I can't find it locally, and even if I could local stores couldn't beat Amazon's pricing and convenience. Get it as a subscription and save even more.

title: Not a replacement, but more of an experience
text:
So I get it, the reviews, to why people are so surprised of the taste. I love these seeds!

1. Taste pallet - my kids loved it. Some adults don’t. Why? Because my kids don’t have an understanding of a specific western taste pallet yet. I grew up with Indian food, so I ate a lot of diverse flavors that tasted “earthy”. It really comes down to how diverse and adaptable a persons pallet is. Your pallet is adjustable, but first see my second point.

2. Expectations - This has a very earthy flavor. It has a strong organic taste. This is not a peanut. This is not a pistachio. This is not a “grown in California” nut. This is from a very different part of the world, it’s not a 1 for 1 replacement. It gets marketed as a replacement at times, but in my opinion, it should be marketed as a new flavor of nuts. Therefore, an adjustment in expectations of the taste need to be made. I highly recommend you make that adjustment before popping one in your mouth. You’ll be fine once you know “this is not a peanut”.

Final word. The nuts taste delicious to me. They aren’t the other 100 nuts I eat, but if I wanted that flavor of nut, I would eat that flavor of nut. I wouldn’t be picking this seed and comparing it to a pistachio.

text:
Got these lovelies in the tumeric flavor from Whole Foods. Only one annoying little thing. The are stuck to this long wax paper. I don’t know how to get just one out, but I’ll deal with it cause these really are da bomb if done correctly.

Okay here is what ya do to make yourself a delicious quick satisfying meal.

1. Very lightly grease a pan to quickly warm up two very thin wraps.
2. Pull out/wash small amounts of the organic Romain heart leaves, Romain baby leaves, broccoli sprouts, onion sprouts, (or whatever other sprouts you have), 3 pepperoncinis, and slice up a small organic avocado to fit on the wrap.
3. Put all ingredients on the lightly warm wrap except the pepperoncinis. Pull the end off the pepperoncinis and let the water from inside drip on the other ingredients on your wrap. Cut up the remaining pepperoncinis and toss on the top of the other ingredients on your wrap.
4. Pour yourself a GT’s Kombucha.
5. The important thing here is not that some of the toppings will fall out of the wrap (if you make wraps like me). The important thing is the heavenly taste of the wrap and ingredients. I have never had this exact combination of taste anywhere. The inspiration just came to me with buying this wrap and other items in my fridge. But the wrap makes this dining experience memorable because the taste of it is a little sweet married with the freshness of the salad and the heavenly contrast of the pepperoncinis. 😋

Try it and post a review of other combinations you like. Always looking for ideas because I hated Covid, but love not going out for every meal now. Love having control over what I put in my body. And when it’s tastier than what I find in restaurants, it’s a win!

title: Stan the Man Reviews:  French Toasted Oak Ships
text:
This is a rather small package but, since the pieces are rather small, they compact well and you get a fair amount I make fake bourbon and cognac out of vodka, white rum, and neutral grain spirits so I can't speak to how well these work with wine. I never did even like wines with an oak or woody taste.

I have bought white oaks chips, both the medium and heavy toast, in the past as well as Jack Danniel's Old No. 7 whiskey barrel chips which are sold primarily for barbecuing and smokers. I prefer the heavy toast and Jack Danniels mixed together for a bourbon taste.

These are my attempt to make something like brandy or cognac and I have still to decide on whether they work well or not.

A guy I knew once who made moonshine rum with the little Megahome distiller Amazon sells said he prefers white oak.

On reading up on cognace, I found out that French bradies are often also made with white oak.

Still, I give them five stars since they almost immediately colored the vodka I put them into. Oak chips and the Jack Daniels take a while to start and a few hours to a day or so to develop.

I would recommend these it they suit your particular purpose in wine making since I do believe they would work just fine for you. That is why I gave them vive stars since there is probably not much wrong with them for the purposes intended.

title: Haven't Tried It? You NEED To!
text:
Have you ever wondered if there was a healthy alternative to peanut butter? Well, you found one.

It comes powdered. You mix 2 Tablespoons of the mix to 1 Tablespoon of water ( I actually recommend a little less, to get a more peanut-butter consistency), and voila. You have peanut butter.

I can't stay away from the chocolate-infused one, it's so addictive. But you want to know the best part about this peanut butter? It's 45 calories.

45 calories of bliss.

Normal peanut butter - Jiff? Skippy? 180 - 200 calories for 2 Tablespoons, not to mention all the other stuff peanut butter has shoved into it.

PB2 offers you a healthy alternative, and it really does taste just like peanut butter! You won't feel bad about making celery with peanut butter on top of it anymore. And it's easy and portable to take with you, too. Normal peanut butter gets all goopy, and there's a potential for mess. Depending on how you pack PB2, you can just take the powder with you.

It's also the best thing to add to protein shakes and smoothies. Peanut butter flavoring, with little to no guilt over what you're eating.

Thank you, PB2, for making this. I'm so addicted, I just can't stay away from it!

I won't lie, it's a little spendy, but try it. I swear. You'll never go back to normal peanut butter ever again!

title: Amazing for blood pressure.
text:
Wow, this stuff is amazing. I've been struggling with blood pressure on and off for a while. I've been on a couple different meds and all caused nasty side effects (lisinopril had me coughing up blood!). I've been working with a holistic MD on more natural remedies but still strugglng. Then two weeks ago I was in an auto accident and got taken to the ER (severe right-side pains, but nothing broken, they suspect mainly just muscle damage). At the ER they took my BP and it was 200/100! They thought I would drop dead on the spot. By the time I was ready to be discharged it has "dropped" to 187/95 which still had them unhappy.

When I got home I began reading more about blood pressure remedies and somehow stumbled upon hibiscus tea. I decided to oder this bag. I had to wait for it a couple days of course, even with Prime, so in the meantime took a baseline BP reading at home - 180/95, depressingly close to the last hospital reading.

Anyway, the tea came. I have a small teapot that holds 2-3 cups of tea (depending on cup size) and I make a full pot with a rounded tbsp of the hibiscus. After 3-4 days I found my BP readings were now in the 156/86 to 153/80 range. Wow, big difference. Another week went by and now my readings are in the 135/75 to 127/69 range. I'm rather dumbfounded. I'm the sort of person for whom these "miracle" cures other people talk about usually do nothing at all. But in this case I can hardly believe the drop.

This is only two weeks' worth of data of course, so it's only 'so far so good". Will have to keep drinking the tea and see what happens down the road.

10/23/14: Just an update after four months. I love the taste of this tea and still drink a cup or two every day. My BP has continued to drop. I was on vacation in July without the tea and it shot back up to 167/98! Began the tea again when I got back home and it dropped in days to 138/86. The longer I stay on it religiously the more the numbers drop. Numbers for last few days were 115/69, 122/72, 119/70, 127/73. 125/74, 118/70.

So this is a win-win for me since I love the taste also - a bit on the tart side, rather like unsweetened cranberries. But I've never been able to stand sweet tea or coffee, so perfect for me.

title: OBSESSED except for horseradish
text:
So, I didn’t buy these off Amazon I buy them at my local Smiths. TL;DR at the end.

Peppercorn and Chipotle are to DIE for, I literally cannot eat a sammich anymore without one (or both) of them because it just falls flat. They are good alone, they are good together. Both have a twinge of heat that one would expect from eating a mouth full of peppercorns or eating a canned chipotle in adobo - some bite but it goes away fast. Mostly just a flavor explosion. Our dear friend who thinks bell peppers are “a bit spicy” can tolerate them with eyes watering, and also thinks they are great, for a point of reference.
Both are neither overly spicy or overly tangy. *chefs kiss* I love them. If I want more heat that’s easy I have like, ghost pepper sauce in the fridge it’s really not a big deal. The FLAVOR is what’s good here.

HOOOOWEVER the mustard one is stupid it’s just a regular Dijon mixed with Mayo, why would I pay twice the money for one quarter of a bottle of each condiment; nothing special happened there.

The horseradish is *awful.* If you are looking for that sharp, brilliant horseradish flavor turn around. You will experience it for about .1 seconds before you are overwhelmed with a sweet flavor that is reminiscent of miraclewhip with three times as much sugar. It’s sickeningly sweet, makes me feel like I put vanilla pudding on my sandwich and a dab of wasabi on top. -10 I hate it and I’m more than a little mad that I spent $6 (at the grocery store) for something that tastes like a freaking… nougat filling with horseradish in it. Super nasty. If you’ve had the bottled PF Chang dynamite sauce and found it too sweet, it’s like that but turn down any hint of flavor and replace it with sweet. Yuck yuck yuck.

TL:DR peppercorn and chipotle are AMAZE i cant sandwich without them now, the mustardy one is whatever tastes, like you thinned out Dijon with Mayo and the horseradish is horseshit. Bleck.

title: Good But Could Be Better
text:
The cheddar cheese in this definitely makes it tastier. The Amy's version without cheese is definitely beyond bland. I only dropped Amy's version with cheddar cheese one star, because I do like them and eat them at least once a week, but the organic tortilla they're wrapped in is a bit leathery. I suppose that's because the tortilla is gluten free, which seems to be the catchword these days, even though only a very small percentage of people are truly allergic to or incapable of absorbing gluten. That's Amy's thing, so I do know what I'm in for, but there has to be a way to improve the tortilla even without gluten.

Because I grew up in the Desert Southwest, I cut the burrito into mouth-size pieces and sprinkle a little chili flakes on them to bring them up a notch. You may not want to do this unless you're used to some approximation of real Mexican food.

I do like the convenience of being able to microwave them and I do eat them.

Nespresso's own intense espresso capsules are about as close as you could ask to come to this in a home capsule-based system. But as you know, they are quite experience (around 70 cents per coffee). So I've looked for something acceptable that's closer to half the cost. I gave Gimoka Intenso a try (drank 200+ of them), partly based on reading the quite decent reviews on amazon.it. Well, this stuff is really pretty poor. Even in a caffelatte, I can taste at once that I've made the drink with inferior espresso. In many ways closer to undrinkable hotel/church coffee than to proper espresso.

Well, I've found something better. No, not as good as Nespresso, but [[ASIN:B07KPVW5Q9 Cafe La Llave]], at an only slightly higher price point, is way more drinkable and espresso-like than Gimoka Intenso. Give it a try.

title: A coffee substitute that tastes like coffe, and with no chicory root added.
text:
I love this coffee substitute! I used to use Postum, but the ingredients bothered me (it has one gram of wheat bran fiber per serving, and insoluble fiber and I aren't exactly on friendly terms). But this has only barley and rye, with zero fiber, so it's working very well for me. I've been having a mug at each meal, in the afternoon, and at night, as well as in the morning on the very cold days we've just experienced, and I've had no digestive upset whatsoever. And as someone who has both IBS and IBD, that's saying a lot.

For anyone who has ragweed allergy, like I do, this will be a blessing and a half. Because a lot of the coffee substitutes around use chicory root, and it is in the same family as ragweed; some people have used chicory root, or inulin made from it (and most inulin is), and they've had anaphylactic shock from it. So this beverage would solve more than one problem for many of us.

Also, there are a lot more servings per container than are in Postum, for less cost. And it really does taste like coffee! I make mine weak, not quite a teaspoon to about 12 oz. of water. I have it with foods I used to have coffee with, and it's so close to coffee that I'm surprised anew each time I make a fresh mug.

title: Viva Labs Products are of the HIGHEST Quality
text:
I received a gift box of Viva Labs products from a buddy who's a BIG fan of their products and thought I needed to try them- bless her, I can see why. I am SO impressed with the quality all round, I must post reviews for everything but in the interest of time I'll combine them:

[[ASIN:B00MGW5UVY MCT OIL, 32-Ounces]]: First time I'd tried, or even heard of it. I'm a convert! a noticeable improvement in how I feel, my energy level. While some say it's not for frying, I use it for sauteing, frying things at a lower temperature- yummy. Also use it in place of olive oil or butter to make garlic and dipping bread, and grilled cheese sandwiches. Taste it- it tastes GREAT. I subsequently tried another brand and it had a slightly bitter whang- this is pure, light and lovely. No more nasty canola oil for me (and for fried foods that require higher temperatures I'm using refined coconut oil).

[[ASIN:B00OZYNGUS ORGANIC CHIA SEEDS- 2 LBS]]- Gosh, so many uses for these seeds- I love them anywhere sesame seeds are normally used (e.g., sprinkled on grilled cheese sandwiches before browning, in salads, on deviled eggs, a zillion uses). My birds love them too.

[[ASIN:B00MGW81YM ORGANIC RAW CACAO NIBS, 1 lb]]- These remind me of coffee beans, the kind you buy dusted with cocoa, but these aren't sweetened so I tried them rolled in coconut sugar and mixed into a kind of brittle I made with yacon syrup. Great that way, plan to experiment more to find uses that complement their delicate flavor. LOVE the crunch.

[[ASIN:B00P6TUO5G ORGANIC CACAO POWDER FROM CRIOLLO BEANS, 2lb Bag]]- this makes the BEST mocha espressos, indistinguishable from Starbucks' at a fraction of the price. I use a tablespoon of cacao powder to two tablespoons of espresso (for a jumbo cup- 16 oz). The best cocoa I've had, I use it instead of Hershey's now. I also make fabulous chocolate pudding, brownies, EVERYTHING chocolate with it.

[[ASIN:B00PWW3LQ6 PREMIUM HIMALAYAN ORGANIC GOJI BERRIES, 1lb bag]] - Tough to tell what makes one feel better and more energetic without being systematic about it. I try to be, but I couldn’t resist tearing into this gift box, like Christmas. I munch away on these, a small handful a day, at the same time I use the MCT oil (and everything else). All I know is I feel great. They're sweeter than cranberries, taste a bit like raspberries- yummy. Mix into salads too.

[[ASIN:B00JPJRQ7W ORGANIC QUINOA, 100% Royal Bolivian Whole Grain, 4 LB Bag]]- I moved from another state where I shopped at Raley's. There was a brand of quinoa sold by them that was great, but not available in Southern California. Subsequent brands I tried were either tasteless, puny or bitter. This quinoa is just as good, if not better- no rinsing needed- fluffy, nutty tasting, wonderful.

[[ASIN:B00FQKI3W6 HIGH POTENCY VITAMIN D3, 5000 IU, 360 Softgels]]: I take two daily and feel good, what can I say? Tiny, easy to swallow, with no burping/aftertaste.

[[ASIN:B00STSUPCS TRIPLE STRENGTH GLUCOSAMINE, CHONDROITIN AND MSM, 240 Capsules]] - This glucosamine-chondroitin-MSM combo is the first I've tried. I've lately been getting aches and pains, especially after overexerting myself. This not only assuages the pain but I swear boosts my muscle strength and overall stamina. I take two in the morning and two at night. I also have a knee that inexplicably “goes out” every week or two and that’s a rarity now. Fantastic.

There isn't a single item here I plan to be without, so when I run out I'll be re-ordering- plan to try other Viva Labs products as well. The quality of everything is absolutely superb. Highest recommendation!

title: Used them to make vanilla extract and will definitely be buying again.
text:
I bought these to make vanilla extract as gifts for Christmas. I had purchased some very pricey organic beans from my local co-op, only to get them home and discover that they were moldy, so I needed to return them and find a suitable substitute. I was in a bit of a bind time-wise, so I needed to buy some quickly so they would have enough time to flavor the vodka used as a base for the extract. These were a good price and the right amount, so I bought them.

I wouldn't go so far to say there are 4 types of beans. There are really only three at best, and there is a bit of overlap of two, so more like just two types of splits and whole beans. However, they were perfect for what I needed them for. Unlike the beans I bought locally, these beans were percetly preserved and ready to use.

I purchased bottles used for home-brew and put a bunch of beans/splits into each jar. I then filled with vodka and let them sit for a couple months, gently agitating them once a day. The end product was fabulous. I will be buying these vanilla beans again to make more vanilla for next Christmas.

title: Long-time lover of Cola.
text:
Before you buy Zevia, you should know two major things:
#1- If you've never had something sweetened with erythritol or xylitol, the flavor is going to be weird for you. It took me a little while to warm up to it, but now I don't mind it at all.
#2- Erythritol can mess up your stomach if you aren't careful. So, if you are new to it, take it slow. I would not recommend drinking more than one a day until you see how it effects you. Those reviews on sugar-free gummy bears are a good example of people not used to this type of sweetener... Just a friendly warning.

About 10 years ago, I made the switch from regular soda to Zevia in an effort to cut calories. I'd started the optimal eating "diet" (here's a book about it, if you're curious: https://www.amazon.com/Hotze-Optimal-Eating-Cookbook-Steven/dp/B000WHGPXW/ref=cm_cr_arp_d_product_top?ie=UTF8) so was trying to stick to sweeteners like Xylitol and Erythritol. While it definitely took some getting used to, I grew to really love a few of the Zevia flavors. It's kind of funny because I've always been a Dr. Pepper drinker and not a big Coke fan, but the Dr. Zevia is probably my third favorite (a little too cherry for me) and the Cola is my number one. I've tried nearly all of the flavors over the years and have listed below how I feel about each. Sorry, I'm not the best at describing flavors/scents.
-COLA: My personal favorite; a very light, refreshing cola flavor without the heavy sweetness of regular Coke, or the weird flavor or Diet Coke.
-DR. ZEVIA: This is obviously the DP copy. While it does taste similar to DP, it definitely has a much heavier cherry flavor, in my opinion. Honestly, I feel it can lean a little cough-syrup tasting sometimes. I'd still say this is my third favorite flavor.
-STRAWBERRY: This is definitely my second favorite, but it's hard to find at regular grocery stores. I think this has a great, lightly sweet (but still fairly artificial) strawberry flavor. Think Strawberry Fanta but lighter.
-GINGER ALE: I'm not a big drinker of regular ginger ale, so I didn't think I'd be a huge fan of this one either, but I actual like it. I'd say it tastes fairly similar to Canadian Dry, so no complaints here. I wouldn't purchase it on purpose, but if none of the first 3 flavors I listed were available, I'd pick this next. It's a good mixer for drinks.
-LEMON LIME TWIST: I'd say this one is fairly similar to Sprite or 7Up, thought I couldn't tell you which it's closer to. Pretty standard and tastes fairly good.
-MOUNTAIN ZEVIA: I've seen a few people complain about the flavor or this one, but I actually didn't mind it. I mean, it tastes almost nothing like Mountain Dew, but it isn't bad. I'd say it's pretty similar to the Lemon Lime flavor. Not bad, not great.
-BLACK CHERRY: Very artificial cherry, but I still like it better than the Cherry Cola flavor, as it's a bit lighter.
-ORANGE: I find that this one has a very artificial and much sharper orange flavor than I'd prefer, and I'd almost say it's more tangerine than orange. I'd say this is less sweet than the Strawberry flavor, but don't hold me to that. I bought a 24 pack of this flavor last year and I still haven't finished the second 6-pack, so I probably would't repurchase it.
-CHERRY COLA: I go back and forth on this flavor. When I first started drinking Zevia, I actually loved this flavor and drank it often. Then one day, I suddenly decided I was sick of it, similar to my feelings on Dr. Zevia. It just seemed like the artificial cherry flavor started to take over and it was all I could focus on while drinking it. I don't necessarily know if anything changed with the flavor or if I just started noticing it more. Either way, I'm accidentally given this flavor every-so-often when I do grocery pickup, as the can looks almost identical to the regular Cola flavor (just has some cherries on one spot), but I often leave them sitting in the garage and never drink them.
-CREAM SODA: Not a fan of this one. I find it to be a bit sharper than normal cream soda, not as smooth. I think this sort of flavor really benefits from sweetness, and this version doesn't have much. It has a weird aftertaste as well.
-CREAMY ROOT BEER: I usually enjoy root beer (Barq's is my preferred) but really did not like this one. I don't know why, it just doesn't really taste like normal root beer to me. It has a weird aftertaste.
-GINGER ROOT BEER: I really don't know why there are two root beers, but they're both terrible. This one has a much sharper flavor to it and I despise it.
-GRAPE: The absolute worst flavor, in my opinion. I almost spit this one out the first time I tried it and have never purchased it again. I normally like grape soda, so I was surprised. It just tastes very artificially grape and gross.

The only flavors I have not tried are the Caffeine-Free Cola (I want caffeine) and Grapefruit Citrus (not a grapefruit fan).

For those that are saying the reviews must be fake because the flavors are terrible...you have to understand that anything sweetened with Xylitol or Erythritol tastes a lot different than those with regular sugar.

Overall, I love Zevia and will continue to buy. By the way, they also have great customer service - I had some issues in the past with bad batches (they tasted waaaaaay off; batch numbers matched on bottom) and they sent me free replacements (more than I bought) and coupons.

title: Weight loss, energy boost, cat supplement
text:
EDIT: A stray kitten came to us with Eosinophilic Granulomas (rodent ulcers or rodent mouth) Took three vets until we found out what was wrong. It was after repeated outbreaks of the lip sores this autoimmune disease causes that I began using Kal yeast in lieu of prednisone and clindamycin. He has been symptom free since, except for one time (last week)when stress triggered it after he escaped outside and became panicked. But after a few days of eating the yeast (in his food), he cleared up - and faster than the medical treatments we used before. I use about 1 T. per 5.5 oz. can. The best part is that he prefers his food with Kal yeast.

First discovered this brand in 1978. Occasionally tried others, to my dismay. This one tastes great, I just grab a spoonful and enjoy eating it dry. Seems to give me an immediate lift that way, along with satisfying the type of "hunger" that drives me to eat high calorie snacks. Add it to my cats' canned food, too; we all like Kal Yeast Flakes!

Local stores charge almost as much for the smaller size, and other web sites charge a higher price or much higher shipping. Wonderful that I can get this through Amazon! Otherwise, I'd be huffing and puffing up the hill to the local store to pay more.

title: Cup bottoms are too thick or hard to puncture
text: I thought the coffee was just ok. Little bit sour. The big issue is that the cups are either extra thick or too strong in the bottom. The puncture needle in the bottom of my Keurig broke off after about 10 uses of these cups. Could it be coincidence? Sure, I ended up pulling the needle out since it was broke but still attached to the plastic. To continue using the machine while I get a new one, I would puncture the bottom of the cup and leave it during brewing and then remove again. It works very well this way with Starbucks kcups. It was very, very difficult to puncture the bottom of the half-caff in this review. That needle is sharp! And I’m not weak. Folks have complained about a low flow and it’s probably due to he needle puncture. May not affect all coffee makers. YMMV.

title: think of it as an alternative to whole chickpeas
text:
Nutrition profile is really good - high in protein and fiber.
The texture is nothing like regular pasta though - after cooked, the elbows do not hold their shape, and mush when stirred.
I recommend using this pasta as an alternative to whole chickpeas - the taste and texture work in e.g. a curry sauce or a minestrone soup. (I used it in a spicy curry tomato sauce and it was very good.)
I advise against using this product as an alternative to wheat pasta. The texture and taste are so different that it would be disappointing. Definitely it would be impossible to use in a dish that needs a lot of mixing. If you tried to make mac-and-cheese, you would end up with mush.

title: Raspberry flavor more subtle than I expected, not a bad vitamin/wellness drink
text:
I tried these out, as I'm always on the lookout for a low-ish calorie drink to calm my afternoon snacking urges. Something that's actually healthy and low-ish in calories? Even better.

These are 20 calories per can, so they qualify as low-ish calorie.

The flavor will remind you of raspberry juice but don't expect a very strong flavor. It's more a gamish of raspberry, a bit of the muskiness of monk fruit, some general citric essence, and a combination of sweeteners like erythritol. On the whole, it's pleasant, and I had no problem shooting down a chilled can. But it felt short of "great". More like "not bad, and healthy."

Which, honestly, is good enough. Docked a star because they are pretty pricy per can.

title: "Darn Good" Chili Kicked Up
text:
Bear Creek "Darn Good" Chili is some of the best chili I've ever had. It is quick and easy by just following the instructions on the back of the packet. My family enjoys chili just a little spicier and a little meatier so I've added a few items to kick the chili up another notch. So here it is....

(2) packs of Bear Creek "Darn Good" Chili Mix
(2) cans of Tomato Paste
(2) cans of Rotel Tomatoes
(2) Small Onions (Chopped)
(1) Bellpepper (Chopped)
(4) cloves of Garlic (Chopped)
(1.5) lbs. of Ground Beef or Ground Chuck
(2) lbs. of Smoked Sausage (Finely Chopped)
Hint of Cayenne Pepper (To your taste)
Hint of liquid smoke

In a large pot, add both chili mixes to boiling water (As directed), then add the tomato paste. Stir well and turn fire down to a medium heat. In a large sauce pan, brown your ground beef and chopped sausage, then add to your pot. In the same large sauce pan, saute chopped onion, bellpeppers, and garlic (10-15 min) and then add to your pot. Add the Rotel Tomatoes, turn heat down to a simmer and let cook about 30 minutes (Stirring occasionally). Add cayenne pepper to taste and a hint of Liquid Smoke and let simmer for about 30 more minutes (Still stirring). In this last few minutes while the chili is cooking, bake up your favorite cornbread (I like "Jiffy"). Gather your family and friends for a "Darn Good" Chili time.

Recipe is even better in a CrockPot.....And I don't know why I added the Liquid Smoke (But it worked)

Hope ya like it!!!

title: Less costly than manuka, but offers some similar benefits
text: This honey is cloudy, somewhat potent, and simultaneously sweet and a little bitter. The flavor may not be for everyone, but I enjoy the complexity. One of the main reasons we use honey in our household is to help with our son's occasional allergies that lead to throat inflammation and cough. He's 3, and we've spent some time figuring out what to give him to help alleviate his cough. Manuka honey was on constant rotation, but it's definitely pricey (even more than this in most cases). This honey has also done wonders to soothe his throat during a flare up. We give him a spoonful before bed and it allows him to get to sleep without coughing much if at all. We've also used this for regular honey applications such as sweetening teas and making marinades. It's a bit expensive for those uses (when I can get a pound of local raw honey for around $15 or so). Still, the quality and complex flavor are pretty impressive and enjoyable.

text:
I tried the Chocolate biscotti, and these are "okay". They're not unpleasant to eat, and I certainly wouldn't refuse them if they were offered to me, but I probably wouldn't buy them. What would make them better? Make them larger (more convenient for dipping) or give them more flavor. Or both.

As other reviewers have pointed out, they don't have much flavor to them. It's not that the flavor is unpleasant, it's that there's really just not much at all. So they're not really that appealing to just munch on. I don't need a blast of chocolate or sweetness, but I'd like more than what these provide.

With not much flavor to them you'd think that they'd be great for dipping, right? That would get some flavor into them. Well, they would be great for dipping, except they're rather small. They absorb liquid well, but because of their size the amount you can dip is also rather small. So you dip about half the biscuit into your favorite hot beverage (cocoa in my case), but don't get much to munch on.

title: Hi.  My name is cat and I'm a VAB-a-holic.
text:
It wasn't too long ago that I can recall my life before vanilla almond butter and the memory is hazy and hard to focus on now. A "friend" convinced me to try this product and at first I didn't think it was anything that would change my life as I was a consumer of other "butter" products like the peanut variety and had once even tried apple butter with no unusual effects.

Well, that was before I added this product to my diet. As soon as I took the first taste I knew I was sunk. I tried to convince myself I needed other products like crackers to spread it on but in no time I was eating it right out of the jar. I've ordered this product now 693 times and empty plastic little tublettes are scattered all over my home. My friends have tried to intervene and quite frankly, most of them now are also consumers and there are scarcely any of them that aren't using it prolifically.

I sometimes wait for the Amazon truck to pull up as I peer out of a darkened room of my home, salivating profusely like a Pavlovian dog when I see the delivery guy. I've managed to stop going out to meet him as he exits the vehicle as I know he knows what's in the box and it's embarrassing.

I hope one day to find a VAB-a-holics anonymous meeting but the truth is I'd be only fooling myself by telling myself I'd actually go. My former life is but a vague shadow of what it is now. If only I hadn't tried that first tasty bite. I know what you're thinking. "Oh, I'm only going to eat mine on pieces of sliced apples and other healthy delivery vehicles!". Muh ha ha. Good luck with that. You'll be eating it straight out of the jar like the rest of us soon enough.

Take my advice now while you can. Stay far away from the vanilla almond butter. While I can't say for sure, had I just stuck to regular almond butter or the laughably "similar" Jiff and Skippy products I think I'd be OK.

Signed,

cat, a mere husk of the man I once was, albeit surrounded by the hint of the enchanting, wafting vanilla and nutty aromas...

As mentioned all of the flavors are rather subtle - there an initial bite on the tongue that reminds me of citric acid powder (but none is listed on the ingredients), some toasted coconut flavor, there's briefly something that's definitely very mango like to me, but they all fade away rather quickly. There's some sweet but like the flavors it's not heavy. Subjective summary - ultimately it all gets lost when used as a topping in yogurt or ice cream.

At which point you're left with the texture, which is spongy. Not like a sponge cake, requires more tooth than that to get through it. Again, subjective, but that's a food texture I really don't enjoy.

title: Great Instant Coffee for Making My Frappes and Lattes Tastier and Healthier!
text:
This instant dark roast coffee from Molecule Immunity Coffee is great for making my gourmet coffee drinks such as frappes and lattes. I made ordinary hot coffee per the directions on the box; it tasted fine, but it didn't really knock my socks off. I also made iced coffee by using one-half cup of boiling water, adding a packet of instant coffee, stirring it briskly, and pouring it into a mug full of ice cubes. The iced coffee tasted good, especially since the temperatures are beginning to climb. However, I really enjoyed using the packets of instant coffee to make French Vanilla and Mocha Frappes and Lattes.

In order to make a cold Frappe, I simply crush eight ice cubes, add one cup of skim milk, and add one packet of instant dark roast coffee from Molecule Immunity Coffee. Then I blend it all together very well. If I want a French Vanilla Frappe, I add French vanilla syrup. If I want a Mocha Frappe, I add a packet of hot cocoa mix. Either way, you are going to create a delicious frappe that is more nutritious than other types of frappes.

If I want a hot mocha latte, I simply warm eight ounces of skim milk, add a packet of hot cocoa, add a packet of instant dark roast coffee from Molecule Immunity Coffee, and froth it all together. If I want a French Vanilla Latte, I do the same except I substitute French vanilla syrup for the hot cocoa mix. Either way, you will have created a latte that is delicious and more nutritious than ordinary lattes.

Each packet of instant coffee only has five calories. There are twenty packets in a box. The packets are very thick and protective of the coffee inside; having notches at the top, they are relatively easy to tear open. The twenty packets arrived inside a company cardboard box that had three round, transparent seals keeping it shut. Again, they were relatively easy to remove with my fingers in order to open the box. The coffee itself contains cherry extract. Cherries are rich in Vitamin C, fiber, and antioxidants. Cherries are healthy for you. The coffee also contain WELLMUNE, which is a natural yeast beta glucan that strengthens one's immune system.

If you enjoy making gourmet coffee drinks, then I suggest you purchase the instant dark roast coffee from Molecule Immunity Coffee. This coffee will wake you up in the mornings, it has immunity-boosting properties, and can be used for the foundation of making delicious gourmet coffee drinks such as frappes and lattes.

title: Green Fig: Somewhat Disappointing
text:
Having never had or even heard of green fig preserves we decided we had to try this. After all, we love fresh figs. I think the problem here is two-fold. First, perhaps it's because figs don't have as strong a taste as say raspberries, the result is a preserve with a somewhat vague taste.

The second issue is that it's overwhelmingly sweet. Here too, the fact that it is fig may play a role. Again, going back to raspberries or certainly oranges, they have a tartness to them which downplays or contrasts with the sugar. The figs here do little but seemingly amplify the sweetness so it tastes somewhat like you're eating mildly flavored sugar preserves.

It took two long weeks to arrive, and when it did, I knew from the moment that I saw the bag that something was wrong. This is not by Barry Farms, and it's an extra coarse sea salt from Wincrest Foods instead! Tiny crystals in a smaller bag (a completely different type and brand).

I contacted the seller immediately to make them aware of this issue (Wincrest Bulk Foods) and they never replied leaving me to my own devices for a remedy. Amazon thankfully issued a gift card in the amount of my order, but I am still without the correct order that I placed, and am now out of sea salt for my OXO Salt grinder. Be warned.....

Update:

I left honest seller feedback on what happened here, and ironically enough, the company in question (Wincrest Bulk Foods), who did not have the time to even get back to me on the fact that they sent me the wrong brand and product that I had paid for, suddenly made time to leave a response to my seller feedback, which was stunning. They stated that I was confused and never ordered salt, but some other God forsaken item, that I had never even heard of, let alone purchased! They out and out lied (that was a new low out here)! They were trying to divert what they did by making it appear as if I were some, confused, buyer, and they did nothing wrong! This is why I try soooo hard to buy from Amazon only when at all possible.

Since there was no way for me to reply to this outrageous lie under their feedback section, I immediately removed the feedback entirely as it was useless now, and contacted Amazon along with Wincrest Bulk Foods, showing each a screenshot of the lie that was just left out by them under my honest and accurate feedback, Additionally, I also sent a screenshot from my Amazon account showing exactly what I had ordered on that day, and it showed Barry Farm's Coarse Sea Salt by Barry Farm's! So this is how some of these companies deflect the truth under thier feedback section....interesting.

I finally receive an e-mail from Wincrest Bulkfoods admitting that it was an error on their part, and that they had confused my order with someone else's under their feedback section (ya think) and that they removed it (another lie, as I removed the whole thing after I got a screen shot of it first)! The representative apologized for the mess, and promised gift card or not, they were sending me the Barry Farm Coarse Sea Salt I had ordered, and had been waiting on now for nearly 6 weeks!

I thanked them for the gesture, and told them that I would await what I had ordered. It's been almost three weeks now (and they offered this AFTER my product review here, which had been posted days prior, so it's not like I can even rationalize this as a reason for them to lie and not come through yet again), but here I am still without what I ordered! I was told that I would receive my Barry Farm's Sea Salt in a week, and that was nearly three weeks ago. I have looked and looked and there are no other vendors as of this writing, who are selling this form of Barry Farm Sea Salt for grinders here at Amazon but these people. :(

To say that this company cannot be trusted would be an understatement! They give new meaning to outrageous and flaky! I will have to look around online, and get it somewhere else. Ridiculous!

P.S. I see other new reviews now to my left and right peppered in here and there with others stating that the same thing just happened to them with this company (Wincrest Bulk Foods). After looking through my Amazon account at all the other orders I have placed over the years for this wonderful product, I see that Wincrest Bulk Foods has never been the vendor before (no wonder, as I had never had any issues in ordering this before). title: Don't Forget the Fridge
text:
I like hibiscus tea and I like roobios tea, but the thought of them mixed together sounds horrible.
Always happy to be proven wrong!
In this delightful tea, the roobios definitely overpowers the hibiscus, but surprisingly, not in a bad way. You get the earthiness but then comes that lovely touch of floral, all tempered with a touch of lemongrass.
And can I say that I'm absolutely thrilled that it is unsweetened? No stevia, thank goodness. The delightful organic ingredients stand on their own. Rose hips, chamomile, lemongrass, nettle, and lavender. Each of these works for beautiful hair and strong nails, as well as having some wonderful other properties that can be helpful. Rose hips and hibiscus are both good for the heart, and nettle is good for breathing and clearing the lungs making sure you have lots of skin-loving oxygen in your body. And of course everyone knows the wonderful chill you get from chamomile and lavender.
And to top it all off, all of this goodness comes in a glass bottle. Glass. Easy to recycle, and no nasty plastic leaching into your beverage. I'll be reusing the bottles and filling with my homemade kombucha, talk about a win-win.

Just remember that it's recommended that you store these bottles in the refrigerator, even though they are shelf stable. That's actually a good rule to follow for any bottled tea. Keep them cool and away from light.
Cheers!

title: It pays to know who will fulfill one's order
text:
Our go-to mustard for the past decade or two has been Bornier Organic Wholegrain, ASIN B07JZ8SMKZ, which we purchased from Amazon most recently on June 1 of last year (2021). But, as our current 7.4 oz. jar of Bornier is nearly exhausted, we looked into stocking up with another jar or two from the same source.

Holy Inflation, Batman! Nine months is enough time to grow an entire human baby in a womb, and apparently the same kind of growth came to the price of Bormier mustard in the same nine-month time that had elapsed since our previous purchase. (To be fair, Amazon's level of inflation -almost- seems small when compared to another giant on-line retailer, the name of which starts with a W, where the price of Bornier mustard has increased about *600 percent* in the same nine-month time period.) So we searched for an alternative that could scratch our occasional mustard itch.

Perhaps the most renowned and revered French mustard (for that matter, mustard of any nationality) is Pommery Moutarde de Meaux, which traces its history back to the early XVII century (1632), and was an enduring staple on the tables of French royalty until the invention of the brutally efficient guillotine put an end — not to Pommery, but to royalty — with the death of the XVIth Louis in XVIII century France. (*Minor exception: the very short-lived Bourbon Restoration in the XIX century*.) According to the makers of the condiment, the secret recipe of Pommery Moutarde de Meaux has remained unchanged from 1632 until today.

Poring over the thousands of reviews of Pommery de Meaux here that accompany its Amazon listing, one was struck by the sheer volume of one specific kind of One-Star review, where the predominant complaint — almost the -only- complaint — is that the product was delivered in a jar that leaked or was completely smashed, with its contents all over the inside of, or oozing though to the outside of, the main delivery package.

Carefully examining the Amazon listing, one noted that at least five different entities are performing fulfillment of orders of Pommery Moutarde de Meaux mustard here. Clicking serially on Amazon's links to those sellers, one could not help but notice that a select few of them sport unblemished records of delivering on the promise of full satisfaction. Therefore, we carefully and intentionally sought out from among the sub-listing of "other sellers" of Pommery Moutarde de Meaux one that would be fulfilled by vendor「VerSure」. There MAY BE OTHER very reliable fulfillment vendors of Pommery Moutarde de Meaux selling via Amazon, but we wanted to purchase from a seller who was 「for sure」 and it appeared to us that 「VerSure」 is at least ONE of the 「for-sure」 vendors.

A week later, we have received delivery of our 17.6 fluid ounce (500 ml) crockery jar of Pommery Moutarde de Meaux, and it arrived in pristine condition, with the top lid double sealed — no leaking whatsoever — and the crock itself fully intact. Unlike what is shown in many of the photos appended to One-Star reviews, the primary *outer* packaging was a sturdy cardboard box, inside of which sat the crock of mustard wrapped in a strip of about 5,280 feet (of course, coming from France, the original length would have been specified as 1,609.344 meters, rather than as 5,280 feet — we did not make a precise and calibrated measurement) — of bubble wrap, applied in the Egyptian Mummy Style: around, AND around, AND around the entire crock in about six different axes of wrapping, and secured by more tape than an NBA superstar has applied to his leg after a major joint injury.

We are NOT going to subtract a star from our satisfaction Rating for the half hour or so of our time that was required to unwrap the crock of Pommery Moutarde de Meaux from its sarcophagus. We are just happy — *very* happy — that it arrived here in such excellent condition. Incidentally, the mustard itself fully lives up to its exalted reputation.

Knowing one's seller can save one lots of grief.

title: Good Variety Of Quality Products; A Bit Pricey
text:
Product: BUNNY JAMES Premium Charcuterie Board Gift Box, Crackers, Cheese, Dried Fruits & Beef Jerky

This charcuterie board gift box has a good variety of quality, brand name food products. The board is cute, but it is almost too small to be functional. It also actually looks cheaper in reality than in the pictures. It’s the weakest part of this gift set.

I liked the food products and there is variety. I used this set for two people and there was enough choice for everyone to find something they liked. There was also more than enough food for two people, with some left over. I would have liked to have another cracker product and maybe one less meat product. My favorites were the crackers (very hearty grain crackers), the asparagus (not fibrous), olives and figs. I could have eaten the figs all day.

While these types of gift sets tend to be pricey, this set was pushing the high end for me ($45.99). That said, it did contain good quality food products that are probably priced higher on their own. It’s definitely better quality food items than you would see with some lines like Hickory Farms or Swiss Colony. This set is giftable.

title: Strawberry Almond Quinoa Joy Bol
text:
I had mixed feelings about trying the Strawberry Almond Quinoa Smoothie Bowls - I love the idea of it, but wasn't sure how it would actually turn out.
The biggest thing going for this is portability and convenience - it's the perfect 'on the go' snack if you're in a hurry, need something to stash in your desk for the day you forgot to grab lunch, or even for camping it would be great. Each bowl comes with it's own spoon, all you need to do is add water to the fill line that is marked on the inside of the bowl. The first time I tried one I added water to the fill line, and overall I found it to be way too soupy and runny, nothing at all like a smoothie. But on the upside I was very pleasantly surprised by the taste - a nice bright strawberry taste, not too sweet or tart. The nuts, granola clusters and quinoa add a wonderful crunch to balance things out. The second time I tried one I used a little less water so it was a thicker consistency and I liked this much better. If you let it sit for a minute or two that will also help it thicken as more of the liquid will be absorbed.
The downside to these - 260 calories for one little bowl, and these are pretty small, definitely a snack and not a meal substitute. 35g carbs, 15g sugar definitely make this not your healthiest option out there for portable snacks.
Overall I like them (at least the strawberry flavor, can't speak for the other flavors) and will definitely consider them for an occasional snack on the go, but not something I'll want to consume frequently.

title: Some of the best Ceylon tea I have ever had
text:
The glowing reviews of this tea are all true: The tea is in big whole leaves with just a very small number of broken leaves. You have to use 2 to 3 teaspoons of tea because the leaves are so giant that they don't pack together in the spoon.

Once you get the right amount of tea leaves, the resulting tea is very malty and rich with a nice deep brown color. I always know I have good tea when I can see the shiny oils sitting on top of the liquid after the tea brews and cools.

The flavor really is some of the best I've ever had. I find the value for the price I paid to be enormous. I'm tempted to order more right now, just to have it in case this product goes out of stock. Easily 5 stars.

title: salty tasty seasoning for use on anything, no oregano,
text:
SALTY! Not necessarily a bad thing depending on what you are using it in/on. I would say that it is Salty first, then a punch of garlic, followed by black pepper and turmeric equally, and more subtle. The aroma reminds me of some chicken broth bouillon I use. If you are new to Adobo, it may seem a little bland in some ways, but not far off at all from other versions. Makes it a tasty seasoning for just about anything.

While Adobo seasoning is typically comprised of salt, black pepper, turmeric, and garlic, there are variations out there that add in other stout spices for flavor or color. The stuff I normally buy has oregano. This does not. In some ways I like this version better as I am not always a fan of oregano. This is just what I listed, and the salt is very forward tasting, with garlic lingering, and everything else sort of settled in the background.

I like the small containers, that it is organic, NO MSG (unlike some Adobo blends). I have some [[ASIN:B09CQF7Z3K McCormick Organic Harissa]] that I like a lot, so I kind of expected to be wowed by this as well. It falls a little short for me, but I still like it.

I review this based on my experience of other adobo blends. BTW, there is no nutritional info anywhere, inc their website. Usually I like to know how much sodium is in something, alas no way to know.

Two words that do not go together...'Oreo' and 'Sophisticated'.

Until now!

The taste is exactly the same as the full size version, like I needed a reason to savor both, heh heh. If you cringe at the Double Stuf Oreos, you'll be delighted to know that the filling is just as slimmed down as the cookie.
I expected them to have a lot more crunch, but any difference is negligible.
Four cookies are 140 calories, 60 fat calories, but who's counting? There are 160 in three regular Golden Oreos, with the same 60 fat calories. About 40 per package.
The only stat you might care about is that they do contain high fructose corn syrup.
The packaging has that familiar lift-up-easy-close, important on humid days.

And for the kid in you, yes, you can still twist them apart to get to the creamy filling.

title: Good honey. Honey is usually sold by weight, not volume.
text:
Lots of people know a lot more about honey than do I. All I can say is that this honey tastes as I expected it to taste and the price is reasonable. I simply unscrew the top and pour it into a smaller bottle for table use. I will buy these again when I run out if the price stays reasonable. My bottles all arrived intact.

It should be understood that honey is normally sold by weight and NOT by volume. This was not my idea, so don't be angry with me. It's been done that way for years but that fact tends to fly under a shopper's radar. So each of these bottles are two pounds as shown in the photo of the label and that is accurate.

Amazon perhaps should have said "2-lbs per bottle" which makes the amount more clear to the shopper.

This is a good basic set of food coloring additives. They provide all the basic, primary colors, plus useful, popular colors. The set includes: Yellow, Blue, Red, White, Black, Rose Pink, Leaf Green, Purple, Brown and Orange. Of course you can mix the colors to get new colors/different shades; also adding white to lighten up shades.
The food coloring is a concentrate, so a few drops goes a long way towards creating rich, robust coloring in frostings, icings and baked goods. The food coloring also comes in very handy when making home made slime and playdough.
It’s also a nice way to teach children about colors and how they combine to form other colors.
10 ml bottles offers an ample supply of the assortment of food coloring. I feel the product details provides accurate pictures and statements, with a fair representation of the product. It meets expectations, receiving a 4.75 star rating.
