title: Check around your local ethnic groceries first.
text:
This caviar is very salty, and not like the kind you find in sushi restaurants. The eggs are small and not plump and large like it's supposed to be, but kind of shrunken and marinating in the broken eggs liquid. I didn't expect much though, after all it's from a can. It tastes pretty fresh, but just not visually appealing. Very salty so you need to drain before enjoying. The can comes with a plastic seal cover so after you open the metal top, you can still seal it. It keeps longer that way, though it's probably a good idea to transfer it to another container.

For the price I can't complain, it arrives really quick with a pack of ice (2 days for me). However, if you are a salmon roe fanatic like me, look around your area and see if you can find an Eastern European market. They will usually have fresher salmon roe, sometimes with a better price. I have found a 1kg plastic tray of much fresher and plumper salmon roe in a Russian market for $46 (the same 1kg tray is listed at $130 here on Amazon). So see if they have it. Alternatively, go to an Asian market and look for Ikura. These will be sold in the sushi section, and though the price is not as competitive for the amount you get, it is usually fresh and tastes the same.

This can is a great price but don't expect too much. Check around your local ethnic groceries first.

title: Tasty, chewy and fresh! Contains added sugar.
text:
I'm always looking for new snacks to try, and I love fruit, so I decided to order these lemon-flavored cherries. I have to say, these definitely don't disappoint! The lemon flavor is really strong, but I adore lemon, so that's just a plus. The flavor of these cherries is also strong; They're equal parts sweet, tart, and sour. These are one of the cherries used in making cherry pie, and it really shows. If you like lemons and cherry pie, then you'll absolutely adore these.

These cherries taste fantastic, and are absolutely great for when you're craving something sweet. They do contain a lot of sugar, however, both added and natural, so I'd recommend snacking on them in moderation! They're also very sticky, so it helps to wash your hands, or have a wet wipe available after eating some. These are the tastiest dried cherries I've had, and I'd definitely be interested in getting more of them in the future.

title: Works as advertized.
text: This works as advertised.  I made apple mead and was at 15.2% in 48 hrs and finished with 18.3 in five days in 85 degree heat.  You will need to set your carboy or bucket in a container as this yeast will blow through the air lock.  It looks like boiling water as opposed to the happy percolation of fermentation with regular yeast.  One could get the same results with a champagne yeast and enough nutrients and warmth but I figured I'd test this to see if it worked as advertised and it does.  It takes about another week to clear so you can drink in about two weeks after you start if you want.  It may be slightly different with beer or another wine but I think it will work about the same regardless.  Good stuff for a quick batch.

title: Fruit Flies and Fungus Gnats gone!!

Electrocuting them was very effective, especially after placing pest tape on the bottom.  This product has eradicated my pest problem in less than 24 hours!  I bought two of these, yes I know they are harmful to humans and probably domesticated animals, but at this point it was worth the risk to rid my home of fruit flies and fungus gnats. title: BRIGHT, flavorful, very easy to use
text:
The is an extremely vibrant red, so if you are looking for something really, REALLY pops against a white frosting, this would be a fondant to consider.

Regarding the taste, it's a pleasant vanilla that has a slight marshmallow undertone.

As far as how working with it is; I would say very easy.
I typically struggle when working with fondant, but found this easy to roll out and mold.

Like most fondant, this will dry out/set quickly, so it will help to either be quick when working with this or keep a little water nearby.
You also want to store any unused portions in a way that locks out as much air as physically possible.

Lastly, the vibrant red of this fondant will stain your hands/fingers as you work with it.
You can either live with the color until it fades away or wear gloves when handling the fondant.

In the end, I would recommend this fondant based on color, consistency, and taste.
It's definitely a solid choice for decorating desserts.

title: Tasty, But Not Really "Robust"
text:
So my "relationship" with olive oil may be a little different than the average person's.

I grew up in an area where among hip tapas bars & fancy specialty pizzerias, a boom of literal Olive Oil Stores erupted. They are literally like wineries and besides filling your order from real wood barrels that have a TAP in them, they also have tastings! Believe me, I rolled my eyes at these establishments as much as the next middle-income-ranged person, however I did wander into a few of them over time for the free tastings to see what all the fuss was about. In addition, 2 friends of mine were pseudo chefs who perpetually stocked a delightful array of olive oils with broad, distinctive flavor ranges for their guests' delight at every get-together, so I've got a bit of a "palate" when it comes to olive oil now.

I've come to despise the cheapie stuff that pretty much just tastes like vegetable oil. And I adore a heavy tasting (aka robust) olive oil with some salt & pepperred crackers.

The stronger olive oils tend to have a more bitter taste. It's kind of like a craft beer with extra hops.

That's what I was hoping for with this olive oil, since it calls itself "robust." Robust is the same word they used to describe the more heavily noted, more bitter tasting oils in the olive oil lala fancypants places, so that's sort of what I was expecting here.

Because I know Pompeian is usually a less expensive brand, though, I kind of knew I was taking a gamble.

And yes, I was not wrong. The Pompeian "Robust" is a far cry from any authentic robust flavored olive oil. However it is a decent tasting oil, it has a nice consistency, it says it's organic, and is totally useable in any situation olive oil may be called for.

So I'm glad I tried it. My favorite olive oil is a stronger tasting one from Costco that brings with an S but the name of it escapes me now. Similarly priced to this one, the Pompeian just simply does not measure up. But it's versatility & *slightly* stronger taste than the flavorless dribble of the cheaper supermarket brands give it some hope.

It's got a weak, nutty flavor that maybe resembles pine nuts in the far away distance... and it does have a small bright sweetness.

I probably won't buy it again, but I'm not furiously disappointed with my purchase & may grab it once more in a pinch.

Happy hunting!

title: I have discovered that sprouted lentils are a great treat to eat
text: I purchase these for sprouting.  I have discovered that sprouted lentils are a great treat to eat.  They are much more yummy than the cooked ones.  They take only 4 days to sprout.  These seeds were nice and viable and sprouted right on schedule.  They came in this neat bag and were well worth the cost of purchase.  I also liked the fact that they were grown in the US in Washington State and that they are organic and not irradiated or treated in any way.  They were quite clean and did not need constant rinsing.  Just for fun for the next reader I will post how I sprout them.  I soak them for 8 hours  1/2 cup of lentils to a quart of water.  Then I drain them and rinse them a couple of times in a quart jar with tiny plastic screening rubber banded over the opening.  I leave the jar on its side and continue to rinse them every time I pass the sink by -- about 2 times a day.  On day 2 you will notice the sprouts appearing on them.  By day 4 they are good and ready to eat.  Sprinkle on salads, top soups, or eat by the handful as a snack.  I keep them in the fridge in a ziploc bag with a bounty towel folded in the bottom.

title: Not so much anymore.......So glad Amazon started offering this again
text:
2017 May - This is the second time I ordered this product. I had to downgrade the stars from 5 to 2 due to the significant reduction in quality from my first order to this one. I really hope the batch I recently received was mislabeled because I hate to think that Margaret's Hope Darjeeling has drop in quality this much. I've had better Lipton teas. I will be scrutinizing the reviews to see if the quality has returned before I reorder. It's a shame. This WAS a very good tea. I hope the quality returns soon. I miss my Darj in the morning.

2014 - My first online tea purchase was 5 years ago with one lbs of Margaret's Hope Darj. I was pleasantly surprised with the quality and value. Unfortunately, Amazon stopped offering it soon after. I switched to a Darj from Davidson and Coffee Bean. Both of those were adequate. I wasn't impressed but both were cheaper so they were still a decent value. I was happy to see Amazon start to offer a Margaret's Hope Darj again. And it's a 2nd flush!! The aroma is everything I expected from a high quality Darj. Also, the complex flavors make it interesting each morning. Some times I taste a hint of peach some times apricot. Of all the 4 versions of Darj I've purchased, this one is the best. Even the original M Hope Darj wasn't as good. Maybe the 2nd Flush made the difference. (The first version wasn't labeled as 2nd Flush.) I hope Amazon continues to offer this particular M Hope tea. It's even reasonably priced...for the quality. I'm getting more soon.

title: Amazon, GET MORE PLEASE!
text:
I've been a huge fan of Maitre Jacques Champagne Vinegar for years, but when my last case ran out, I discovered that the company no longer offers it. So while searching for a substitute, I came upon this, and, since it wasn't available back then, I clicked "Notify Me" in the hopes that Amazon would get more. On Tuesday, I received an email saying that it was available, and immediately ordered this case of 6 for a fair price of $20.94.

The order arrived the next day, yesterday, but I knew instantly that the box was too small to contain 6 bottles. There was only one in the box! I contacted Amazon and a refund was processed (thanks Amazon!) BECAUSE, there's none left to reorder from (there were 6 cases when I placed my order)! So, once again, I'm on the "Notify Me" list. But these went super fast because this vinegar is that good.

Tarragon is one of my most favorite herbs, with the light licorice taste that enhances things like bernaise sauce. I wasn't sure if it would be so great on salad, but I trusted the Maitre Jacques brand. And it's delicious on salad and chicken salad: the licorice scent is very present when you open the bottle, but the licorice taste is light and subtle. It's now my favorite vinegar.

If you eat a lot of salad, you don't EVER use bottled dressings (only fresh on fresh!), and you're really picky about your EVOO and Vinegar, you'll love this product. I just hope that Amazon gets more soon!

title: Very nice gift assortment, but some of the blends are problematic
text:
I buy Yogi's Kava Sress Relief tea with some regularity, because I find it effective (and tasty!), as well as a couple of other bookends of theirs. So I was eager to check out this assortment of their teas, most of which I hadn't tried yet.

The presentation is attractive and well designed...the slip case and internal cover keep the teas secure (although there had been some shifting of some the teas when I opened it)....it would certainly make a nice little gift for the tea lover in your life. I'm especially interested in seeing how the Honey Lavender Stress Relief compares in efficacy (and taste) to the kava one I'd been getting, but I haven't needed it yet, so I haven't tried it. (I'll try to remember to update this review once I have...same with a couple of the other blends that I should be able to judge the effects of, like Bedtime and Sweet Tangerine Positive Energy.)

However, there are a few blends that I won't be trying, either because I don't want the effect they have (for example, the DeTox blend has diuretic and laxative ingredients ) or that my research indicated might not be as safe as I'd, like Garcinia Cambogia (in the Green Tea Blueberry Slim Life blend), which the FDA considers unsafe (although the amount in the tea might not be enough to cause issues). So, if you're buying this for yourself, I'd suggest researching each blend to make sure that they're safe for you (especially if you're pregnant or breastfeeding) and that the potential side effects of the ingredients aren't of concern to you.

While this might make a nice gift, as I mentioned previously, the per-teabag cost is almost double what it costs to get the individual teas in their usual box of 16, so, unless you're not really concerned about cost and are eager to try a tea "buffet," it's not the best way to purchase these teas for your personal consumption. (Given that I'm only really interested in maybe six out of the nine varieties, I could have gotten 96 bags of tea for about the same price as these 48 by just buying them individually.)

But, despite some of my reservations, I'm giving this assortment four stars as a gift-giving option for what I know to be high-quality, tasty, and effective teas.

title: Still Tasty After Almost a Decade!
text:
At a cafeteria where I ate, they had a sushi bar that had these soy sauce packets available. Before trying these, I used to consume the free-with-order clear soy sauce packets that came from my local chinese fast-food restaurants. Once I tried these, there was no going back!

The soy sauce is way better than the cheap salt-water you get from the cheaper places. So much better that it ruins them forever.

I bought the 500-pack because I didn't want a bottle in the fridge going to waste (drying out, absorbing any smells from other foods in the fridge, etc.). I stowed it in the pantry, where it's nice and cool, to prevent any possible spoilage. The flavor is still delicious through the nine years I've had them.

I occasionally eat chinese fast-food and sushi (probably once a month or so), and I reach for these every time.

The packets are nice and portable, and single-serving size (although I generally use more than one per meal), so there's little worry about any extras. There are other manufacturers that do taste better than the aforementioned clear packets, but the ones I've tried don't hold a candle to these.

If you're an avid Kim Lan fan, or just enjoy a good soy sauce (and have the money), these packets are great, and last a long, long time.

title: Decent taste and texture
text:
Quick warning: They messed up printing the box on this one. Under nutritional information it lists a 100g serving as 70 calories and 16g of carbs, and a "serving" (ie: packet) as 212 calories and 46g of carbs. These are reversed: One serving is 70 calories. They also appear to have messed up on some of the information, since the one column reads 46g of sugar and 4g of fiber for a combined total of 23 g of carbs...which is mathematically impossible.

Printing issues aside, this tastes exactly as described: a mix of coconut and banana. I haven't had energy gels in a few years. I have tried a number of them, most notable the "gu" variety, and they've all been sickeningly sweet and tasted very poor. This wipala brand is also very sweet, but it's not gross like the other kinds I've had. It has a thick, gel texture like a thickened jelly or jam. It's easy to squeeze out and highly palatable (if you like sweetened coconut and banana flavor). Definitely good for some quick energy, since it's mostly just sugar. There is nothing "special" in this for energy except the sugar, though that can be said of a lot of other gels. Some of the more advanced energy gels have a mixture of fast-digesting and slow-digesting carbohydrates. In my opinion, it's probably not going to make a big difference for most people, and palatability takes precedence. The packets also look pretty sturdy for sporting events.

My only concern is that the ingredients contain only "banana puree, coconut water, and potassium sorbate". The potassium sorbate is just a preservative, but it looks and tastes like there's more than just banana puree and coconut water in it. It's definitely been sweetened, but what it's been sweetened with is not listed. That, along with other printing and math issues on the label would make me a little concerned about what's actually in it. The labelling clearly didn't pass any kind of good quality control. I only took off one star because it's probably just sweetened banana puree, and probably some pectin or other thickening agent that's missing. If they got these issues fixed I'd add the 5th star back on. I don't think this is anything sinister, just poor labelling on the part of the manufacturer. I also like the lack of caffeine.

title: Similar to a high quality green tea, without the caffeine. Yum!
text:
I hadn't had Soursop tea before, but after trying this, I'm definitely a fan! I brewed it for the recommended 5 minutes by putting a bag into a mug, and pouring water over it that I heated to boiling in my tea kettle.

This tea smells nice and fresh as soon as you open the package, and the flavor and color of the brewed tea reminds me of some of the high quality green teas I've purchased in the past. It has a nice mild herbal flavor that will make you feel all warm and cozy, without the bitterness of some other tea varieties. I was a little shocked that the tea wasn't 'sour' like I expected from the name, but that just comes down to the fact that Soursop tea is produced with the leaves of the plant, rather than the fruit.

As a added bonus, you can compost these tea bags afterwards, which always makes me happy to see in a product!

Overall, this is a nice mild tea that I think anyone who likes the flavor of green tea will enjoy, especially if they're trying to limit their caffeine intake. Just don't expect it to taste fruity!

title: Not the best ever
text:
Unwrapping the "peanut butter crunch" flavor is not a pleasant sight. I'll forgive you if your first thought is that somebody took baby vomit and ran it through a processing machine. The supposedly "real food" bar looks incredibly fake and processed. My body does not register this look as potential food. My best advice is do NOT look at the bar before you put it in your mouth. That's not a good sign.

As for flavor and mouthfeel? It's not terrible. Imagine somebody took some really dry peanut butter cookies made with protein powder and whole peanuts, then used an industrial press to squash them into bar form. During random bites I either got a whole nut, or a hard bit of caked protein powder that crumbled like a dry cookie. That might appeal to someone, like imagine a candy bar made out of cookies. It could work.

Nutrition? It's okay. You get 10g of protein balanced against 170 calories. A Snickers candy bar is 5g protein against 240 calories, so this bar is definitely a healthier option compared to candy. That's okay, but certainly not "the best ever". It's also really small. It doesn't fill me up, so I need to graze on some nuts to complete my meal. Then again I'm a tall guy who lifts weights so I'm used to higher protein counts than the average person.

My usual bar is the Clif Builder's Chocolate Peanut Butter bar. The Clif one has 280 calories, but also 20g of protein. That's the exact right spot to make it feel like a meal replacement for me. Take a Clif instead of breakfast, and you get 1/2 to 1/3 of your daily protein using only about 1/10th your day's calories (assuming normal people on a 2k kCal diet). The clif bar looks and tastes like real food. It looks like a peanut butter candy bar, it tastes like peanut butter and chocolate and crisped rice cereal. At no point does my body wonder whether I'm eating "real food" when I'm munching my Clif bar.

Note to manufacturer: You can NOT use the name "best ever" and then crank out something that looks and tastes like this. You're setting the bar too high. It's not awful, maybe somebody out there will really dig it especially if they're on really restricted calories. But the "best ever" bar, isn't.

Adding this matcha powder to my daily green tropical smoothie prep added a great matcha flavor to it. I also blended the matcha powder while preparing mango, strawberry and pineapple popsicles, which were a great hit for Memorial day weekend (I got this idea after eating matcha ice cream, sold as mochi ice cream).

Although this is sold as culinary grade, not ceremonial grade (for plain tea), I tried adding the matcha powder to hot water to make tea – which tasted perfectly good to me and not bitter.

Once the tea leaves are harvested, the stems and veins are removed and the leaves are ground up into a fine powder known as matcha. Matcha contains the nutrients from the entire tea leaf, which results in a greater amount of caffeine and antioxidants than typically found in green tea. It's so good!

title: Starchy Sweet, Good to Eat, It's Yacon!
text:
When I first read about Yacon I thought, "Oh dear, what did they do to bacon this time...?" Being a pork enthusiast, I was greatly relieved to learn that Yacon has nothing to do with pigs. In fact, the yacon is a tuber that is very similar to the jicama (which my Grandfather loved). So when I was offered the chance to try Life & Food Yacon Syrup, I decided to give it a go in memory of my late Grandpa.

Taste & Texture

The bottle says this is syrup, and it is pretty dead on. It is roughly the consistency of honey, and the flavor profile is "starchy sweet". That isn't bad, rather, I can identify that this flavor comes from a plant that is underground (for me, carrots, potatoes, yams, and so forth, all have that same earthy sweetness). As a result, I find the flavor a bit too earthy to use this syrup as a lone flavor. For example, while it is possible to just pour this directly over a stack of warm pancakes, I think the starchiness is a bit strong. However...

Uses

As a flavor replacement/additive, Yacon Syrup is AMAZING! Similar to the old apple sauce/vegetable oil trick, I decided to swap Yacon Syrup for Corn Syrup while making fudge. The end result was slightly darker brown than usual, but the flavor was very, very rich. One of the side benefits is that the fudge also acted as a, *ahem*, natural laxative. It wasn't strong or embarrassing at all, just that I wouldn't recommend eating an entire plateful of fudge in one sitting if you are going to swap in Yacon Syrup.

My boyfriend also added a spoonful of Yacon Syrup to his honey tea and said that it was very soothing. While I am not normally a tea drinker, I gave it a go, and the subtle flavor profile of the sweet honey, the slightly bitter tea, and the earthiness of the Yacon Syrup was definitely a palate-pleaser.

Overall

From fudge to tea, as a condiment for pancakes, or simply a couple of spoonfuls to aid digestion and provide antioxidants and restore renal function, Yacon Syrup is a wonderful, flavorful way to add variety to your diet and some nutrients, as well. Life & Food's Yacon Syrup is also 100% Organic, so if you are concerned about things such as chemical additives, this product is safe!

In terms of digestive health, I did notice that the Yacon Syrup regulated my system after about a week's time. If I skipped a couple of days, I did notice a difference in my bathroom habits. While an 8oz bottle is not enough to run a full field test of the product in relation to my digestive health, anecdotally I can say that I did find it easier to use the bathroom, but I really had no change to my metabolism. Again, though, I would imagine that you would need to use Yacon Syrup daily and in greater quantities than I did to notice any weight change benefits.

Finally, if you have children, this is a way to introduce them to different plants of the world, if that is something that you like to do. As I mentioned at the top of the article, the yacon plant (spelled yacón in Peru, Argentina, and Chile) is a relative of the jicama, which is sold here in some markets in the United States. So, while having a delicious bit of Yacon Syrup, there can be a bit of "food history" too!

title: Excellent quality and performance for many types of baking
text:
I’m very pleased with the quality and performance of this pastry flour. The grind level is very fine and even, and it comes packed in a traditional paper sack that’s easy to deal with. The sack was encased in a plastic pouch to contain any leakage during transit (there was none).

Pastry flour is midway between cake flour and all-purpose flour in terms of protein content. It’s a great fit for many non-yeast breads, muffins and many types of cookies. It makes for a softer texture with a finer crumb that really sets it apart from the same items made with all-purpose. It especially shines with pie crusts. You can really amp up your pie crust game with pastry flour and the use of lard. It makes the crust delicate, flaky and delicious.

In the past I’ve made my own pastry flour by blending cake flour and all-purpose. However, this designed from the start pastry flour performs much better than my ersatz pastry flour. It’s hard to find pastry flour in the store so, while this is priced well above what you’d pay for a five pound sack of all-purpose, it’s not out of line with other online sources for specialty flours. The fact that it’s organic and from family-owned farms is icing on the cake (well, pastry).

I’m very pleased with all aspects of this flour – a solid five stars.

title: My Go-To for Travel
text:
I didn't even realize that yogurt powder existed as an actual entity when I first started traveling almost non-stop for work while attempting to get fit, and had to start combing the shopping sites for easy, high-nutrition, travel-friendly food to take with me. Common sense made me search for it (well, there's dry milk powder, right??) and I ordered this immediately for a long trip.

With obviously no need to carry on a liquid, and being so easy to measure out -- not to mention low in fat and high in protein -- it has become the foundation for a "fit meal travel kit" I created to take with me everywhere. I just keep a set of measuring spoons with me and a little tupperware bowl - and to be honest, you don't even need to add the Guar gum (it even makes it a little too stiff if you do; I stopped adding it) - and then use the measuring spoon for the water and stir it all in. It mixes very well even with a plastic fork. Then I add a handful of grapes or raisins or whatever is easy to take on the plane with me.

I've gone back and re-ordered this multiple times, then did some more searching on Barry Farm and have added a few of their other products to my nutritional lineup. Seems like honest to goodness great value and fine products. Love the idea of freeze-drying pretty much everything too. I'm a real fan.

WARNING, TLDR: Freeze these until you are ready to eat, and then thaw before eating. Read on for more info.

Product arrived fast, as advertised. The flavor felt a tiny bit different than I am used to when buying them for $2.99 each at convenience stores, but overall they're still amazing.

However -- these have no firm expiration dates printed. This is because this product has a unique shelf life.

The products are stored frozen, and they have an 18 month shelf life while frozen. However, obviously, they are shipped to you thawed and ready to eat.

These only have a life of about 40 days while unthawed. So if you are buying this, and you're not prepared to eat one every day religiously, make sure you put two of the boxes in a freezer and leave the other one thawed out to eat through.

I unfortunately thought the 18 month shelf life was thawed and was confused as I started thinking "these don't taste as good as before" and then "this is gross now what" lol

title: Surprisingly good
text:
I'm constantly trying out new snack bars, including gluten-free ones, even though I'm not allergic to gluten, simply out of curiosity. Often the gluten-free ones are too dry for me, however, the picture on the box for this particular bar was appealing because I love chocolate, so I bought a box of 5 of these bars.

This is how my experience progressed: the first bar, first bite, I thought it was a bit dry, though not as dry as other gluten-free, cereal bars I've eaten. However, by the time I finished the first bar, I found its taste was growing on me. By the time I'd eaten four of them across two days, I actually came to like them enough to consider buying some more of them. They have a rich, chocolate taste and satisfy me when I'm both hungry and craving chocolate. I personally find them decently chewy in texture.

The ingredients are actually fairly healthy (as healthy as processed food can be, that is). These bars are definitely small, as snack bars go, only 1 ounce (28 grams) per bar. Most other meal bars tend to be as much as twice that size. However, for people wanting to eat a snack around 100 calories (minus 8 calories for the fiber, this is about 102 calories net) that can substitute for less healthy cookies or candy--or just to have a quick meal substitute on the go--this could fill the bill.

title: DO NOT buy this product
text:
These bags do not come with a scoop and it is virtually impossible to determine serving size without one.

HUEL purposely avoids sharing information about how to measure out the product without a scoop. When asked, their 2 recommendations are either to buy a kitchen scale or order a scoop directly from the company. They simply refuse to disclose how this product can be measured out with a standard measuring cup/tablespoon.

In addition, HUEL changed the size of the scoop when they released version 3.0 a couple of years ago so most of the estimates found online are incorrect.

I have been researching for an hour and am still not sure what amount of powder to use. I have no intention of purchasing a kitchen scale for the sole purpose of trying this product.

1 star, strong recommend avoiding purchase of this product. This is either an unacceptable level of incompetence from the company or bizarrely purposeful malevolence.

Going with Soylent moving forward.

title: Mmmmmmmm
text:
This almond butter is delicious, without any added sugars, salt, emulsifiers or filler. Justin's patented grinding technique must really be special, because the oil stays blended and doesn't float to the top, resulting in a fine-grained, speadable! consistency all the way through the jar.

If you see a jar of Justin's almond butter in your market has separated into oil and sludge, don't buy it, because it must have been sitting on that shelf for quite awhile. I have had more than one jar in my pantry for three months without having to stir it up from the bottom. After opening, I keep it in the fridge so it won't get stale.

I spread Justin's almond butter on toast, bananas, pretzels, apples, rice cakes, and have mixed a tablespoon or two into banana-nut muffins and fresh fruit smoothies. I also like Justin's peanut butter, but it's much more difficult to find almond butter that is this reliably good and spreadable.

title: a bit small
text:
These were smaller than expected, I am used to Madagascar beans rather Tahitian beans, and these were about 20% smaller than I expected. Commercial grade extract is about .8oz of beans per 8oz, for "Single Fold" and these were about .6oz. This is about 6-7 of these beans.

In other words, if you want to make "Double Fold" with these, 30 beans would make you a slightly stronger than normal, but not quite as potent as it should be batch of 3, 8oz bottles. (assuming 10 beans per 8oz)

At $36 for 30, including roughly $3 per bottle, (I opted for amber glass bottles) not including alcohol (which varies, and tends to be around 12-25oz, or 59oz, so you'll end up with some extra alcohol, or not enough.) but lets say $12 for some bottom shelf 750ml. six, 8oz bottles is about 48oz, so $36+$19+$14 (after taxes) means it cost you around $11.5 for 8oz of single fold homemade vanilla. Best I can find for "tahitian" pre-made online is about $20 per 8oz, so if you're wanting to make some to last a long time then you'll save yourself a few bucks with this method. There are other kinds that are cheaper, one looks like $11 for 11oz, but it's watered down and has sugar added, amongst other things. Ignore the imitation vanilla, it's not good.

All in all, what I wanted to know, was, can you make double fold with these beans? Well, there's 3.6 oz (roughly) of beans here, and double fold expects about 1.5oz, so $36 will get you about two 8oz bottles, with some left overs. If I wanted to have enough vanilla beans to make six, 2x bottles, I'd need to buy about $108 of these beans in order to have enough, and each bottle would end up costing me $23.5 or so (less, technically because of leftover beans, if I can put those forward to a new batch. Seeing as how the alternative online is $30-60, that seems a good cost saving's measure.

As for some comments of it being moldy, mine were fine, but I also bought mine, and then immediately went to work. Just because it's vacuum sealed, doesn't mean it has an infinite shelf life.

title: Very Good and Fluffy Overall but Flavor is a Little Mild
text:
This is a pretty solid coffee cake mix that works in such a unique way. While those on Keto diets will be more than pleased with this baking mix, I do feel that it could've been a little more sweet than it was.

To start, this mix was incredibly easy to prepare as the only ingredients needed were oil, eggs, milk (or water), and vanilla extract. It only took me a few minutes to prepare and it baked perfectly in just 40 minutes.

The texture of the coffee cake was perfect. It was perfectly fluffy and smooth without being too moist or too dry. It was absolutely perfect.

My only complaint is the sweetness. While the monk fruit does a great job at giving it a little bit of sweetness, I felt that there wasn’t enough to really get the full benefit of the blueberry flavoring. For example, the smell of this when it was cooking was profound. I smelled blueberries everywhere in my house and I couldn't wait to try it. However, the first bites I took were underwhelming. As stated, the texture and everything was perfect and while I could still definitely taste the blueberries, it tasted more bitter than sweet at times.

Overall, most of that is just a personal preference. I think that for those that are already used to foods like these and/or are used to the monk fruit sweetener will definitely enjoy it.

title: Nice company, weak flavor.
text:
These pods work fine in my Nespresso machine, but they don't have a strong flavor when prepared into a latte or breve. Compared to the other pods I've tried of similar rated intensities & flavors (from Nespresso or Peet's), they are just too weak. As best I can tell their intensity scale is boosted 2-3 points higher than it should be, these should be a "light" instead of a "medium" intensity.

Rosso as a company seems quite nice though. They sent follow-up emails to be sure the pods reached me, and included a coupon for a free gift, which ended up being two espresso cups, 10 "gentleman" pods, and 10 "intelligente" pods - Quite the free gift! The free gift sort of confirmed what I was thinking about their intensity scale. The "gentleman" pods were stronger and pretty good coffee, but still only a medium intensity, maybe medium-high, not a high intensity as they claim.

I will probably buy the Gentleman pods again, but this review only gets two stars because it's about what I purchased, not what I was given as a free gift. What I purchased was just too weak and not flavorful at all, and in fact I'm giving the rest of the packages I haven't opened yet to my mother to try because my wife and I don't want them at all.

I have had mole only a few times at a Mexican restaurant and I know it is time consuming to make authentic mole so I appreciated this shortcut. In terms of taste, this is a nice mixture of smoky and sweet. It tasted like one mole sauce I had before so I enjoyed it. I made it with a Mexican chicken dish and it provided the variety of different flavors and spices you expect from a mole . There are a variety of different mole recipes with different flavor profiles but if you like smoky and sweet, you will love this.

title: If you crave salt and want the freshest seeds
text:
I just now ordered my 2nd shipment of Lightly Sea Salted Pumpkin Seeds (Pepitas). I'm thrilled to have finally found a company that has great products AND ships really fresh seeds. I tried a lot of different nut sellers here on Amazon but many of them sent products that had gone rancid. This can happen if the product is not stored correctly or if the stock is too old. GERBS know what they're doing and the pumpkin seeds I've bought from them are very fresh.

If you're trying to decide which level of saltiness to get I would recommend these Lightly Sea Salted seeds. GERBS dusts their seeds with a salt that's very fine, (more like theater popcorn salt than table salt).

I get terrible salt cravings due to a chronic illness and these Lightly Sea Salted seeds are just right. Read the label and compare the sodium content to your favorite, salty snack. You'll be surprised that you get plenty of salty taste from GERBS seeds without a heap of sodium. That's because sea salt gives much more flavor than regular salt.

A Word To The Wise : When you're ordering bulk nuts and seeds remember to watch your weather. I always order these products before our temps in Arkansas reach a steady +96 degrees. Products like this with volitile oils can spoil quicker in shipment when exposed to high temps.

Since earthworms are not part of a vegan diet, I decided to pass on this dish. My far less picky husband had no problem with it especially when covered with a spicy Asian sauce. However, it is not something that I want to look again or smell again so I won’t be reordering it and I definitely can’t recommend it.

So I am ordering again, but this time I will place the bag in the freezer for 48 hrs prior to placing in my container.

title: When you're ready to graduate from Nutella to something really good
text:
Like many of us, my first experience with "hazelnut spread" was Nutella. And it's good. But it's kid stuff, with sugar and palm oil as the first two ingredients. Only after that do you get to hazelnuts and cocoa.

This stuff, in contrast, is made of hazelnuts (the first ingredient), cane sugar, cocoa powder, vanilla bean, and sea salt. Not nearly as sweet, and no cheap palm oil (the oil comes from the hazelnuts).

You can taste the difference immediately. This has a depth of flavor nothing like Nutella. Once you have this, you may never go back.

title: More misses than hits
text:
I got a mini Keurig as a gift this past Christmas, and along with it I got this "Entertainer" variety pack of K-Cups. Lets just say I'd be embarrassed to even let guests drink most of what in this box. There's only 8 different varieties in this pack (some variety, huh?), and as someone who wanted a Keurig for purely coffee, I was disappointed to find that 3 of the 8 types weren't even real coffee. As others have said, there is a very lousy tasting Hot Coca (which I dumped out after a few sips it was so bad), a "Sleepytime" tea (I don't even really like tea, but it's OK so I've been drinking it just to use it up), and a decaf coffee (haven't even bothered trying because I only drink coffee for the caffeine). Of the 5 flavors left, 2 are vile tasting dark roasts that taste like mud no matter how much milk and creamer you load it with. The remaining 3 are the only ones that I liked: the Green Mountain Caramel Vanilla Cream, the Green Mountain Breakfast Blend, and the Donut Shop coffee.

The only good thing I can say about this "variety" pack is that it was a gift and I didn't pay for it, because I would have not been happy to have spent $36 on this. I definitely would not purchase if I were you.

title: Not packaged as I expected.
text: Today, I receive my three boxes of tea. The shipping was fast, but that is not what I am disappointed with in this order. I have purchased this brand tea for years from Amazon or elsewhere. This is the first time I have received the tea without each box being completely enclosed in cellophane or plastic wrap to keep it fresher. When I opened the shipping box, I could smell the tea, and now, I wonder how fresh the tea will be when I make it.  I will, now, have to repackage all the tea with my vacuum sealer, until I am able to consume it all. Very disappointing.

title: Can not beat the quality once each is cleaned fully
text:
Not everyone loves anchovies and mostly because if they try some on something like pizza it is almost always those lousy tinned ones from Morocco (although I have been to a pizzeria where the used top quality anchovies from Sicily but they cost ). I love anchovies , love em on pizza (not every pie I eat) and love them on Caesar Salad made in my home and sometimes sauteed in pan when making some dish or another where they melt away and impart that intense umami flavor in the end dish.
These anchovies are among the best you can get to buy here but you need to work for them if you want to enjoy them. Anchovy fillet for fillet they are super tasty after you thoroughly clean them and rinse them several times in changes of water or use milk. After my first purchase I am pretty good at cleaning the whole anchovy and getting 2 lovely fillets. 30 minutes rinse time (changing water 3 times) and drying completely and YUMMY.
When my package arrived today I immediately opened and picked out about 10 fishes , many a really nice size and then packed the remainder of tin in a Ball jar with the salt content from tin covering the anchovies and these babies will last over a year in fridge,maybe longer as long as salt covered fully. Shipper sent out tins best by sometime in 2020 so superb freshness too.Keep in mind while tin is 800 grams your actual fish content is way less at 600 grams which gets reduced even greater once each fish is cleaned fully but quality is there. So unless youre lazy or dont care about cost these are a great buy for any anchovy lover.!!!!!

title: Great...BUT...it's powder
text:
I never knew black pepper came in powder form. I thought black pepper was always the same - tiny little granules. Apparently, that's not the case.

I expected what I'm used to when I ordered this, but received black pepper in powder form. After looking at the listing again, I see that I overlooked that the first time. I'm kinda glad I did, though. This is lasting MUCH longer than the black pepper I normally buy.

The taste is what you'd expect from black pepper. There's really no difference. You just use much less than you normally would (which is great when you're pinching pennies).

As pictured, you receive a large plastic container. The included lid allows you to shake it or insert a measuring spoon, to scoop out the amount you want.

I'd definitely recommend this to budget conscious folks who cook at home.

title: second order bad, dif source reason?
text:
Hi all. After many food purchases here on Amazon, this the first time sufficiently compelled to provide feedback. Most products have been just fine, thank you.

First order of 11 oz Vita Coco was great. I was shocked.
Printed on lower right side of carton "Produced in Brazil"

Second order, this order of 2 cases, first taste...horrendous. Almost undrinkable.
If it were undrinkable I would have scored just 1 star.
In any case, "I" will not be drinking it.
This second order, lower right side states "Produced in Philippines"
Hmm.

Having been to the Philippines, I am not surprised!

Conclusion: Look for "Produced in Brazil" on carton.

"Born in Brazil" is worthless and meaningless. Ignore.

I'll be asking for "Produced in Brazil" coconut water only.

May have to settle for local shopping, since there is no way I reckon to confirm source with Amazon orders.

On the other hand, may have just been a fluke, but i doubt it.
Even freshly cut-and-served coconuts sold on Philippine streets were often so-so tasting. Probably the result of baking in the hot sun, as these fruit carts were not shaded. Poor people just trying to feed their families, can hardly blame 'em. One more example of how competition detracts from quality of life here in this 21st century.

I guess I'll be hopping between natural food stores checking labels, attempting to dodge unhealthy poor quality foods, that I thought we were paying the government to protect us from.

hmm.

T

(more on this subject at my 17 oz review, also the mini Zico's)

title: Amazing machine
text:
I got the Bambino plus instead of a grinder/espresso maker combo because I live in a condo and don’t have much room in the kitchen.
It heats up in 3 sec which is amazing. Temperature is very consistent and machine produce amazing coffee. The automatic milk frother is great. You get 3 options for temperature and 3 options of foam.
I was planning to get a separate grinder and get a non pressurized cup but honestly I don’t feel the need. I get a ground Italian coffee and I don’t feel I am missing anything.
So, If you are big on grinding your own coffee and you don’t mind spending time making your coffee then go for another model. But if you like a great coffee in less than a minute then this device is for you.

title: this second time the box is a vertical dispensing box like they have in some restaurants
text:
My son has been drinking this tea in the morning for 8 or 9 years. Once our local grocery stopped carrying it, I ordered from Amazon and got the same style box and tagless bags I had been getting from the grocery. Now, this second time the box is a vertical dispensing box like they have in some restaurants, and the bags are the "flow-through" kind with a tag on a string stapled to the top. I always pull the string and tag off those when I put them in the microwave, and I did that with the first cup of this tea I made with these this morning. When I pulled the cup out of the microwave the bag was almost completely empty and the tea had emptied into the water. I strained it twice through a fine strainer I use with loose tea, and he could still tell there were loose bits of tea floating in the cup. He said the flavor was much the same, but the tea bag definitely needs upgrading.

Revised review. I looked more closely at where the tag is attached, and it is tied loosely rather than stapled, so when I remove the tag it probably opens the tea bag. I remove the tag because I compost and the tags persist for a long time in the compost. So, while I prefer the old tagless bags, I can probably change my habit to remove the tag after I brew instead of before, and get used to this new version.

title: A REALLY great dressing!
text:
My best friend suggested I try this because I needed to lose weight but needed something with real taste! I grabbed 2 bottle and made a large salad. Opening the bottle you're hit with an aroma that recalls the best of any asian food you've may have ever eaten. With nice color and modest thickness. I sprinkled it over a large mixed salad, i mixed it noting it covered everything well. On tasting it you're hit with ginger soy and sesame with a background of vinegar. Sweet but not overly so the vinegar and soy sauce givens it a light bite and little after taste.I love the tiny sesame seeds and bits of ginger floating in it. The only salad dressing I use now. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

PROS- Great taste that you don't get tired of. As a vinaigrette its light and low fat never masking the taste of the salad but actually ramping them up! Works extremely well when used for marinating (I added a 1/4 cup of fresh orange juice!) chicken or pork and works well in a stir fry.I eat salad now about once or twice a day with this vinaigrette !

CONS- At 8fl oz a bottle it's simply not enough ! A larger bottle would be awesome!

title: These oats are excellent!
text:
I have been ordering from amazon for years and this is my first review of a product. I felt really compelled to share my experience and thoughts.

When I first received this product, I had a few questions about the outer packaging. I called someone from amazon, but she couldn't answer my questions. I then called the company of Gluten Free Harvest directly and the lady there was so helpful! I have to say the customer service was excellent! After cooking with the oats (bread, pancakes, cookies, and oatmeal), I love the quality and taste of them. What I love most is that the oats are gluten-free AND organic; I have yet to find a company that has both. Before my 41 oz bag was empty, I ordered a 25 pound box from the company directly and just received it a couple of days ago. Lastly, we have a gluten-free bakery nearby and I recently inquired about the type of oats they use in their foods. The owner said she buys her oats from a small company in Wyoming and shared the name of THIS company. We then talked a few minutes about the company and she is very happy with the fact that they are GF and organic.

text:
I love Honeybush tea and so I grabbed this at it's current price $15.00 for 16 oz. Amazon. This is as good as Numi's version in my opinion and I think I probably will end up using enough to save at least 50% by buying this loose.
For those who haven't tasted Honeybush, it is a lighter sweet tea. It has a delicate, smooth delivery. If you like Rose tea or fruit teas (I'm not talking about those that have "natural flavors" such as you find with Celestial Seasonings, which have chemicals or Lord only knows added). Likewise, if you enjoy or other light tea's such as white tea, I would suggest giving this a try. Honeybush doesn't have an aftertaste.
Honeybush is something, I sip when I want to wind down but it is good anytime you want a treat without caffeine.

title: Weak flavor, slow brewing
text:
So, I carefully weighed the recommended amount of Crio Bru and I steeped it in very hot water for several minutes. Then I poured the solution through a metal mesh coffee filter.

I have 2 issues with this product:
1 - Brewing takes forever. The mesh filter gets clogged instantly and then the brewing stops. I had to constantly scrape the sides of the filter to get some liquid to slowly percolate into the cup. It took a while.
2 - This taste like a watery, weak version of a very good cocoa. The cocoa is of good quality, and the little taste there is is delicious, but it's so weak as to be more frustrating than satisfying.

I will finish the pack by brewing it "Turkish style". The one advantage of this over coffee is that the grounds are basically cocoa nibs, and they're quite delicious.

title: Fair Trade & Great Taste
text:
I'll make this quick -
I love coffee but don't like what I've learned about the raw deal that the growers get. So, it's important to buy FAIR TRADE coffee to ensure that the growers get a decent price and that they're supported enough to develop a sustainable coffee growing plantation.
Kicking Horse Decaf Coffee is no more than I was paying for a very tasty decaf from Starbucks - the difference is that their's was not FAIR TRADE [and I assume they pocketed the difference to boost their profits].
So, if you want a great decaf coffee and you want to ensure that the growers are getting a fair deal, and you care about the planet you can't go wrong with Kicking Horse Decaf Coffee

title: So easy, very customizable. Note: said 6-pack, changed to 4
text:
Not very happy about the bait-and-switch listing. When I ordered these, the listing stated it was for a six-pack, but since then, it has been changed to a four pack, for the same price. On top of that, all of the packages expire next month. I ordered two different flavors, and both are the same. I'll never eat eight packages before next month is over.

This Kapka “Vegetable Pulao” for Instant Pot is a very quick and easy way to make dinner for yourself or your family. I love one dish meals, so I really like the idea of being able to cook these in my ninja pressure cooker.
I've never eaten authentic Indian food, so I have nothing to compare this to, but this one tastes quite good! I did make a few changes to the directions, as it has quite a bit of salt, and I wanted it to be more like a soup. I added a little over 4 cups of water, one and a half teaspoons of cornstarch, and then let it cook for 10 minutes, once it pressurized. I'm not one for waiting for the slow release, so I tried it this way, and it worked well for me. The consistency was great, a bit softer than al dente, and very soup-like. I then added some leftover chicken that I cut up into chunks and some frozen chopped vegetables, closed the lid, and let it sit on warm for another 10 minutes. It has lots of flavor, and it made a pretty good bit. There was enough leftover for the next couple of nights for two people.
I've tried several microwavable and one dish Indian packet meals that have really surprised me. These are just as tasty. I like that I can customize them by adding a bit more water, vegetables, and even a bit of meat, if I choose. It is healthy, aside from quite a bit of salt, has simple ingredients, and is easy to make. I would absolutely recommend these meal packs, if you actually get what you ordered and they are not almost expired.

title: Tastes Good- Curious As To How Much Monk Fruit VS Erythritol
text:
I only recently discovered monk fruit, and now I’m a fan. I really don’t like the taste of things like Splenda and Sweet and Low. I was excited to try this Sweet Nature Monk Fruit Sweetener. I got the 1 lb bag. It tastes good on its own when I tried it, and it is a delicious alternative to sugar in my coffee. I usually just add sweetened creamer in my coffee, but this makes it to where I can use much less creamer and still have it taste good. I haven’t experienced any bad aftertaste.

I’m pretty excited about this stuff, because I’m sure we could all benefit on cutting down on our sugar/calorie intake. This is an excellent alternative that doesn’t feel like an alternative- it just tastes good- and with no calories, so I feel it could easily be a new replacement without feeling like you are missing out! I have no complaints! There is apparently no conversion needed. It says that 1 cup monk fruit = 1 cup sugar! I haven’t tried baking with it, but I am very curious as to how it would taste in like a cake or something.

The only real question I have is: How much monk fruit extract is actually in this? I see that the first ingredient in erythritol. This seems pretty common, but should probably also be listed on the front of the bag too. I am very curious and would love to know percentages. For all I know this is only 10% monk fruit extract... just a thought.

I definitely would recommend this product. I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know- thanks!

text: Daring is pretty pricey, which is what held me off from trying this meatless chicken in the first place. But when it recently went on sale at Whole Foods, I finally took the plunge ... and definitely should not have waited so long!!  WOW!! This plant-based chicken substitute is DELICIOUS!! It sears up in a pan with some olive oil PERFECTLY!! It can easily be sliced, cubed, or shredded. It takes on whatever flavor you pair it with so nicely. And the texture is AMAZING!! It is super close to a meat chicken texture, so much so that our non-vegan and non-vegetarian family members were duped when I recently used this chicken in my baked chicken wing dip. IT IS THAT GOOD!! Now I buy Daring at full price, because even at about $8 per bag regular price, it's still cheaper than eating out, and it is a TOP-QUALITY product. PLUS, as a keto-vegetarian myself, Daring Original is ZERO NET CARBS per serving!! WOW!! It's 5 carbs - 5 fibers per serving, so a handy ZERO net carbs for keto-me, too!! YAYE!! If you are personally opposed to plant-based chicken substitutes that are too much like meat chicken, you may not like Daring. But if you prefer meat'less meats that have a meaty texture, you will LOVE Daring chicken too!!

They pack a huge flavor.  The color is almost black with just a touch of eggplant color.  The olives are pretty much ground to a paste so you don't really see many little chunks in the jar.  There are really just olives as the main ingredient, a small amount of garlic and some seasonings with olive oil to make it spreadable.  It tastes pretty much like the olives primarily.  I don't taste the garlic much so no worries if you're sensitive to garlic.  It spreads nicely on a cracker and would add a lot of rich savory flavor to any charcuterie board or just with crackers and cheese.  Unfortunately, two of my jars arrived with the seal broken so I had to throw those away, but I still have 4 jars out of the 6 that were shipped that I'll keep under close watch.  My family loves it and its going to be hard to keep them away from my stash of this tapenade.  I'm really enjoying it and will serve it this Holiday season to all my guests.

title: Very pleasantly surprised
text:
I first found this at Costco and tried it and now I get it here via Subscribe and Save. I was very surprised how much I like it b/c initially dehydrated peanut butter did not sound appetizing at all. I always think I'm not a huge pb fan, but I find myself eating apples and peanut butter a lot for snacking. I also make "banana dogs" with this (lo-cal wheat wrap, one banana, 2 tbsp PB2 mixed and used like ketchup). This is perfect for that purpose alone because it is so easy to go overboard on the amount of "real" oily peanut butter and crank up the calories.

My husband also uses it in his post workout protein shakes and that really saves on our monthly Peter Pan pb usage which we still keep around for the kids. He was killing our jars of pb every week and a lot of that literally goes down the drain if you don't mix your shakes well and have to scrub it out of your shaker cups. This stuff mixes well once you find the ratio that works for you. I use the 2:1 and that works great for me. I definitely prefer the PB2 with Chocolate over the plain PB flavor.

title: Seems like Swiss made a change
text:
After reading all the current reviews it seems like there was a period where Swiss had horrible packaging and product quality issues. Having all the k-pods not in separate boxes and having weird after tastes using the product. Based off the product I received it seems like Swiss made a change for the better.

~ Receiving the 88 count, the pods were sealed inside multiple boxes. 1 amazon box, then 1 regular cardboard box, then 4 separate containers with 22 pods in each. I would say that this is very well packaged and not even the boxes were dented to the slightest.

~ Based on it's serving recommendation, the hot chocolate is pretty thick and creamy but you can adjust that using a different size cup and water setting. I noticed a slight regular hot chocolate aftertaste but nothing out of the ordinary. The reduced calorie is not as thick and packed with sweetness as the milk chocolate but I would actually say it's the perfect mix of drinking a lot without feeling a sweetness overload.

~ my recommendation is because hotchocolate powder is thick, it will jam your machine as well as clump inside your pod. Before each use, shake the k-pod vigorously to loosen up the powder inside and once you finished dispensing the hot coco form the machine run a bit of hot water to make sure there wont be any powder jams.

Overall, hot coco on the go using my Keurig machine is a definite plus and I think Swiss made some good changes to make the product an amazing and delectable treat.

title: Great deal for great health!
text: I am a newcomer to white tea. I read that it is a fat blocker and decided to try it. It is very smooth, I drink it without any sugar of any type, natural or otherwise and it is very palatable and calorie free. It has not been the only change to my diet in the past 6 weeks but I have lost 20 lbs and I feel like this tea has helped me in my venture. You are suppose to drink an 8 oz cup of this tea with each meal or at least 3 times a day if you eat more than 3 meals a day. The price is very right here for a bulk amount of this tea. I would not be able to afford this tea if I had attempted to buy it locally and this deal made it affordable for me. Grand total you get 400 teabags, which will last one person quite some time., 133 days to be exact if you never miss a cup. Many places you cannot even find this on the shelf. This stuff is like that because it is the buds, (flowering part) of the plant it grows on in china. It is minimally processed, only laid out in the sun to dry and then packaged. The rest of the plant makes tea as well, but the next expensive tea it makes is green tea. (with more processing) The last type of tea derived from the same plant is traditional black tea. (takes the most amount of processing and is the lowest in being beneficial as well as the most common. The white tea has a very low caffeine level. The green tea has more and the black tea has the most. Southern USA tea is mainly black tea. If you are looking out for your health, I suggest the white tea with meals, and green tea when you just want something besides water at times that you are not eating and maybe a little caffeine kick.

title: Weird lid, good paprika
text:
The tin is attractive and sturdy. It does have that different looking round metal seal lid which is kind of like a paint can but inverted. I'd previously had a container of paprika actually which I never did get open with that same style, but this one pried open easily with just a butter knife at the edge. It also sealed back securely when I was finished.
I generally buy paprika and smoked paprika at the Polish store so it is the Hungarian or some kind of Eastern European variety, or just at Fresh Market or some other kind of gourmet grocery store. I use it mostly with meat, especially pork, and potatoes. Amazon is convenient though so figured this product was worth a try.
My initial impression of the smell when I opened it was that it was a little bit less smokey then ones I had bought previously, but it did still have that nice blend of smokey and sort of sweet and spicy.
I used this paprika to make a chicken paprika dish tonight, essentially a slow cooking stew with onions, garlic, red and yellow bell peppers, and chicken. The only other spices were salt and pepper. Sour cream was then added and I served our over egg noodles.
I thought it turned out very well, and was similar to the flavor I'm used to even though this is Spanish paprika. I would recommend this product and will likely buy it again when this ribs out.
I did receive a discount on this product in exchange for promising to provide a review.

title: Has particles that do not dissolve, you will have grit in your food. No label warning.  And who says that is good for you?
text: Listen, they may be nice people but they should tell you on the package that it contains particles that are not water soluble. You will experience grit in your food!  I gave them the benefit of the doubt and thought I had not rinsed my vegetables enough, especially greens and leeks. However, yesterday I used a tablespoon when I made hard cooked eggs and the eggs shells ended up coated with this undissolved grit. No consequence to the eggs except for the time I had to spend rinsing the grit off before storing them. I contend that if it does not dissolve in water it cannot be used in the body!  I am not a bird who needs gravel in my digestive system!  I put this salt in the bathroom to use as a body exfoliant, it should do a good job at that!  Don't be taken in by health claims in food that are not backed by double blind scientific studies.  If you like the aesthetics, have at it, but I am calling the emperor naked!

title: Oh, so close and yet so far away
text:
Lots of pluses with these bars: Convenient, portable, low cal, low sodium, high fiber, good protein source, no fuss/no mess. But, as others have commented, there's the taste. It isn't exactly bad, but it isn't something that will bring you back for more. It's actually very plain, almost like the smell of cardboard (and, ironically, nothing at all like the components from which its made). Given that the base flavor is so mild and unremarkable, it would seem to be a slam dunk to make a variety with some spice (maybe with some healthy capsaicins, tumeric, cinnamon, etc.) or other ingredients (yams, etc.).

I'll still buy them because of all of the pluses and because they are inoffensive, flavor-wise. But, the reach and allure of the product would be greater with some more interesting flavors. If this company doesn't do it, someone else should.

title: You get more than what you pay for
text:
This tea brews up to a nice reddish or dark yellow tint, and if steeped for an appropriate time it is quite good. I've found that I prefer a shorter steeping time vs. most other black loose teas. There is some inconsistency between batches even from the same bag. Sometimes you get more Bergamot oil flavor, sometimes more lavender and tannins. This might be a consequence of inconsistency in steeping times or tea quantity on my part, but I think it's actually the tea itself. I like the variety as it keeps me from getting bored. I tend to prefer ~2 minutes steeping in my French press and reuse it 2 or 3 times. The 2nd steeping is often the best.

For under $20 per lb, I'd be happy if this were just OK tea. However, it's actually quite good. It is certainly the best value I've found so far.

title: A Karl Pilkington favorite that I had to try...
text:
After watching “An Idiot Abroad" on Netflix, these UK snacks sparked a curiosity.

Karl Pilkington always packed Monster Munch in his bag when traveling. He also chose to eat them instead of the local cuisine of bugs, grilled rats, frogs, and/or lizards. Yikes! I don’t blame him. But Karl is quite particular and I had to find out “what all the fuss was about”.

The first place I looked? Amazon, of course. They shipped from the UK and took a month to be delivered. They arrived today.

I think these are one of those “acquired taste” type of snacks. I was expecting them to taste like Funjuns, but they are far, far away from Funjun-land. I like pickles, but these are a punch in the mouth of sour pickle flavor. They get better as you eat them and dissolve into an oniony flavor, but they are not something you’d want to eat before kissing someone. Ever.

Sadly, I have no one to kiss so I am munching away :)

title: Childhood comfort food
text:
Back in the day my mom used to get me these tamales (that was well before I had had a "real" tamale), they were in a glass jar, wrapped in parchment, and sitting in a sort of watery sauce.

The masa was more like a corn mush / gelatinous in consistency and I loved those things.

These are the closest I've gotten to finding them again.

The filling is finely ground, decent flavor, texture of the outside is a very firm cornmeal mush type consistency (normal Tamales can tend to be crumbly / dry, these aren't that.

Size, imagine a little smaller than a hot dog and that's what you've got.

Heat? I can handle medium to medium plus heat, these are by my rankings "warm".

(No, mom didn't give me the hot and spicey variant, more of a middle of the road)

Happy I found them (for the memories), and pretty much what I recall from being a kid.

text: I got a great deal on these but it was clearly too good to be true. The taste is terrific -- very zingy but I had a strong negative allergic reaction to something in the chips. And that's where the mystery begins. Either it's the presence of canola oil (probably GMO) or some undocumented MSG -- or both. I would hope by now that the large corporate organic food companies would find a healthier oil and leave out anything that could cause health problems. I also have celiac disease so it may be some kind of wheat variant not listed on the package. Clearly this product could be a real winner but it only made me hyperventilate (even overnight), needlessly so. Maybe Terra should take a look at Kettle's old black bean tortilla chip recipe (which was phenomenal and so healthy) and then develop something along those lines. I would buy that in a nanosecond. The verdict? Savvy consumers should avoid this product -- I would recommend Plocky's chips instead!

title: A Spicy Meal Alternative... But Pricy...
text:
I actually purchased a pack of NongShim Spicy Chicken bowls (pk of 12) from a local warehouse in my area. Ever since college I've been a fan of these "cup of noodles" style meals during late Autumn and Winter. Makes for quick alternative meal that warms you up. How does Nongshim's spicy chicken version stand up against other brands I've had?

Pretty good actually! Each bowl contains a fairly large amount of noodles, compared to the cup variety. The noodles are your typical standard dried Ramen noodle. I am not a big fan of microwaving these products so I make mine by boiling water. Just put some water up to boil, open the package and add the "flavor pouch" or Soup Base, add boiling water to the fill line and wait 3 minutes. Instant hot soup with noodles. While the noodles are standard , the broth is really good. It has a lot of flavor to it and a good spicy kick to it. Put the two of them together and you get a very satisfying meal that will fill you up, and wake you up.

Despite having a good spicy broth and making for a filling meal... This product does have some CONS I am wary of. For one the product contains almost 1800mg of sodium for a single bowl. This is insane! Most of these cup/bowl of noodles are overloaded with sodium to begin with, but it still needs to be pointed out. The fat content is a bit high also, at 14g for an entire bowl. Another problem I have is that most of the products I've tried usually come in a sturdy container for your product. Nongshim's Spicy Chicken Bowls come in a flimsy plastic bowl. It works fine but once prepared I would definitely suggest carrying with two hands, as it has a very cheap feel to the bowl. The price per bowl is also a bit expensive. At the warehouse I purchased this, I paid $9 for 12 bowls. I could of paid $6.50 for 24 cup of noodle varieties. Compared to the cup variety, you are paying a premium for these; And while the bowl produced better quality broth, I don't see it being worth the price increase. (12 bowls = 24 servings.. $9 for 24 servings. the cups were $6.50 for 24 servings.. so basically $2.50 more for bowls vs cups)

OVERALL I would give this product 4 stars. Despite having a flimsy bowl, and incredibly high amount of sodium the product makes up for it in the overall quality of its taste and sheer volume of noodles. You get a big meal here that will both fill you, and warm you up. It has a really nice spicy kick to the broth that lingers without becoming annoying(see NOTE). I've always enjoyed spicy foods so having a few of these laying around the house helps if I just want a quick meal. I would not recommend eating these everyday, in fact maybe I tend to aim for one a week. Products like this are not exactly the healthiest alternative meal for you, but if you need a quick emergency meal these are a good alternative.

NOTE: The product contains chicken but I really wouldn't call it chicken. You might find a few tiny little bits of re-hydrated chicken
NOTE: I do not use the entire flavor/soup base packet. The amount of sodium it contains is ridiculous! I use no more than 3/4 of the packet. I tried using the entire packet once and it made the broth start to taste far too salty, as well as making the spice in the broth overpower rather than compliment. Don't be afraid to use less of the packet...

title: It may not be like A Christmas Story duck but...
text:
I was doing a week of meal preps only using what I already had in the house (no grocery store trips allowed). Feeling a bit discouraged after scouting my options, I opened the pantry and found this semi-forgotten can. Up until this point I had been slightly avoiding breaking the seal (because let’s be honest, it’s a food concept that could make anyone a bit weary to open it). But it was one of the only protein sources I had in stock of my pantry and I decided to go for it. Upon opening the can, I drained out all the liquid and sliced the individual “duck” chunks into smaller pieces. After browning them off in some olive oil, I tossed them with sweet chili sauce, sautéed onion, and green peppers and voila! I had somehow created a meal that looked, smelled, and tasted like it came from anywhere but a can.
Moral of the story: if you have dogs break in Your house and eat your Christmas roast, save yourself some money by making this instead of going out for Chinese food.

title: Delicious and seriously spicy
text:
This suya comes in a convenient resealable stand-up mylar bag and it keeps out light. Opening the bag unleashes an enticing fragrance. It is a uniformly ground vibrant red. There's a good amount in here for many meals. I used a teaspoon to retrieve a heaping mound for each skewer.

The bag has an example recipe using beef but it's a great template for many other proteins. I used shrimp (see photo) which cooks a lot faster, 6 minutes total. The suggested thinly sliced red onion and tomato compliment it well. A fine meal under 10 minutes. If you want a carb you can't go wrong with Jollof rice.

When they say it's extra spicy they mean it! We have a high spice tolerance and it is very satisfying. The heat doesn't get in the way of flavor. It's savory, nutty, warm, deep, and complex, and enhances any protein. It's low in sodium so you can decide how much more you want, but it does not need it. If you're vegan or simply like it, try it with firm tofu (press moisture out first). Perhaps wedge some red pepper between the cubes on the skewer.

The ingredient list is based on regional names for ingredients. I asked the seller to identify "kimber" and they went above and beyond and sent me a photo of it direct from northern Nigeria. I determined it has many names, generally known in the U.S. as "Grains of Selim". There are many suya ingredient variations but this is legit and it comes down to personal taste if you're comparing it with what you're familiar with. If you've never had it before, prepare your tastebuds for a treat.

title: Sneezing Squirrels
text:
Squirrels are the bane of bird-feeding. They invade the feeders, eat the sunflower seeds and scatter the rest on the ground as the birds stand by, helpless. We fill our feeders and then scatter cayenne pepper on top. Squirrel visits, takes one taste, and flees into the woods. I like to think that I can hear them sneezing.

On the other hand, cayenne pepper is a fine diet supplement for birds. They can't smell the pepper and it is a great source of vitamins A, C, iron, potassium and calcium.

International's Cayenne is particularly potent and a cost-effective solution to squirrel-management.

And no, I am not kidding!

title: Some good tea here in a post-Teavana world...
text:
I would rate the Kiwi Cherry flavor 5 stars. I'm not sure it tastes like kiwi or cherry, but it is a great herbal/fruit tea and tastes great iced or hot.
I also love Blueberry Wild Child, Maui Mango, and Citrus Sunburst hot or iced. I'm mostly a fruit tisane person, though, and I like my teas pretty strong. Fireberry is good if you like that strong hibiscus overtone. I do but there is another hibiscus and elderberry blend that I prefer over Tiesta's.
I've also tried the Sweet Ginger Peach, which is great hot but I don't like it iced. In general the white tea (purple and blue bag) varieties are a bit too subtle for my taste. I enjoyed the Lavender Chamomile, but only hot. The Earl Grey de la Creme is also very good hot with milk and tastes almost exactly like what Teavana used to have.
I'm systematically trying some of the others and will update my review as I go.

text:
^Just FYI if you are looking for virgin coconut oil. It doesn't have that pearl/milky color when it's solid and isn't clear as a liquid. Idk if that matters, but it's just something I noticed.

As a product this works great, I was using the Nature's Way Organic Extra Virgin Coconut Oil for my hair and cooking before this. And for those who don't know about coconut oil, it melts at 76 degrees and higher. Anything less will solidify it. So the bottle is nifty if you want to use it as a liquid (granted the temp is high enough) but I would suggest that you pour it in some sort of big jar-like container if you're going to keep it some place cool so that it's easier to access.

title: So, you want a healthy snack that tastes good?
text:
These were in my Gold Box and I was tempted to buy based on reviews, but it was unusual that I couldn't read what was in them. So, I had to go looking for the info and did not like what I found. I got the following from the Kellogg website and I hope Amazon doesn't mind me posting it for everyone:

Sizes
5 ct, pouch

Ingredients:
CHICORY ROOT FIBER, ROLLED OATS, CRISP RICE CEREAL (RICE FLOUR, SUGAR, MALT EXTRACT, SALT, CARAMEL COLOR, MIXED TOCOPHEROLS FOR FRESHNESS), SUGAR, SEMISWEET CHOCOLATE DROPS (SUGAR, CHOCOLATE, COCOA BUTTER, DEXTROSE, MILK FAT, SOY LECITHIN, CONFECTIONER'S GLAZE [SHELLAC, HYDROGENATED COCONUT OIL]), INULIN FROM CHICORY ROOT, VEGETABLE OIL (HYDROGENATED PALM KERNEL, COCONUT AND PALM OIL), CANOLA OIL, FRUCTOSE, CONTAINS TWO PERCENT OR LESS OF HONEY, COCOA (PROCESSED WITH ALKALI), GLYCERIN, TRICALCIUM PHOSPHATE, WHEY, CHOCOLATE, SALT, GUM ARABIC, BAKING SODA, SOY LECITHIN, SORBITAN MONOSTEARATE, POLYSORBATE 60, VITAMIN E ACETATE, NATURAL AND ARTIFICIAL FLAVOR, ZINC OXIDE, ALMOND FLOUR, NONFAT DRY MILK, WHOLE WHEAT FLOUR, PARTIALLY DEFATTED PEANUT FLOUR, SOY PROTEIN ISOLATE, BHT (FOR FRESHNESS).

Allergen Information
CONTAINS MILK, SOY, ALMOND, WHEAT, AND PEANUT INGREDIENTS. MAY CONTAIN OTHER TREE NUTS.

Kosher Status
Not Certified

Country of Origin
Distributed in USA
****end of Kellogg info****

Now I understand why this information is not readily available. These have trans-fat, preservatives, tropical oils, artificial color. And what about the Country of Origin? Distributed in USA.......shouldn't they tell us WHERE these are made? Obviously they're Distributed in USA. There are healthier alternatives out there and these are by no means inexpensive.

Next time I'll add a little more water and I think they'll be perfect. I can't imagine they won't be fine for any purpose you'd use a shell egg for. text: My favorite !  People who mention funny aftertaste have no idea what real rootbeer flavor is !  I grew up on  Long Island NY in a house surrounded by woods.
