The roots smelled strongly from the rootbeer flavor, as these roots are what it is made from.  I believe they make the New Orleans seasoning " filo powder " used in gumbo etc from the smaller leaves.  Now I live in the south were an old woman told  me when she smelled the filo powder that it smelled exactly like the Sassafras tea her mother  made when she was a little.  I like that it is not sweetened with sugar  (but diet version ? ) because its better for my teeth.  I thought they stopped selling this because it wasn't listed last time I looked, Iwas heartbroken.  I use a rival snow cone machine to chop the ice into a cereal bowl and cover with this for my own homemade slushies.  Love !!!

title: The Perfect Chai Spice
text:
I recently ordered two canisters of another chai spice that seems to sell a lot, and it reeked of something akin to garlic. Because of this, I can't use it in tea or coffee, because the funk is very off-putting. However, it might make for a good seasoning for roasts, but we'll see.

Anyway, on to this chai spice from Beantown Tea & Spices. It is quite simply the perfect blend of spices, even adding allspice, which I don't believe is one of the usual spices in traditional masala chai, but it works to make it even richer and warmer. The spices, other than the chopped cinnamon and ginger, are whole pods/seeds, so I recommend chopping them up (I used a small coffee grinder to prepare a good amount of the spice mix for later use), but the aroma is downright divine.

I'm quite fond of Tazo chai, but I recently had to give up caffeine, and decaf masala chai is nearly impossible to find, with one of the choices I found being perhaps some of the worst stuff I've ever tasted. So, I needed to find a great spice blend to mix with decaf black tea, and this is it. I imagine it will even be great by itself without tea, but I also look forward to using it in decaf coffee.

Once I finish this 8-ounce bag of spice, which will take awhile, because it goes a lot further than you might think, I'll gladly buy a 1-pound bag. I can't recommend it enough.

This "fakiness" review stuff is rampant on the internet - especially for health foods - and it's also blatantly dishonest.

Not all people on the internet are sheep...

I was obviously wrong…I started getting headaches and vomiting randomly, so I did some testing through my doctor and discovered I had toxic levels of Cadmium, Cesium, and Thallium in my blood. We discussed possible sources, and she concluded the toxic metals were likely coming from the organic ceremonial grade matcha tea I was getting from Japan. Cesium and Thallium toxicity is extremely rare, but Cesium in particular has been discovered in matcha. Thankfully I caught it early, or I could’ve sustained long term damage. Do your research before consuming!

title: They're OK.
text:
They seem a bit on the dry side, and they don't all pop at the same time, even when well mixed. I know they say "gourmet," but I don't taste the difference. If anything, it's a bit blander than the smaller kernels I buy at farmers' markets and the Amish stores.

Not objectionable, mind you, but we eat our popcorn without butter and very little salt, which means we rely on the flavor of the popped corn to come through.

The cost isn't bad, but once we're done with these, we'll be trying a few other brands to see how they do.

Edited to Add:
upon reflection, I'm revising my rating to "4 stars". One of the reasons we purchased this is because the hot air popcorn popper blows the small kernels popcorn all over the place. These being larger and heavier, tend to fly around less.

But, that means I'm comparing this popcorn to pop in a rotating arm device, and that popper requires the addition of oil on the surface to help it pop. The oil might have enhanced the perceived flavor of that popcorn, and also by helping more salt stick to it.

In this case, the popcorn is popped with no additives, and, as a result, almost no salt sticks to it. That could affect our perception of the flavor. To that point, this popcorn tastes good enough without any flavoring at all.

This Mount Comfort coffee is single-origin Guatemalan. I tested it with my French press, which is my preferred method. The result was a full-bodied, earthy, smokey cup of coffee, with just a hint of acidity (sweet/sour) at the finish.

The coffee comes in a resealable bag, with well-written, interesting copy on the packaging. The advertising promises nutty, chocolate, and caramel notes, but as I mentioned, I tasted more earthiness in this coffee. This rich coffee was ideal for a rainy day.

This coffee is reasonably priced for an artisan roaster. And the coffee was quite good.

title: Well-Made for Coffee & Loose-Leaf Tea, Travel, Camping. Great (Hostess, Stocking Stuffer) Gift.
text:
I was looking for a new french press, when I came across this curious (& inexpensive) item. Bought on a whim, but happy that I did. Most days I make coffee for the family with the usual coffee maker. On those days when I'm the lone coffee drinker, I'd use my french press. After using the Primula many times already, it has become my primary "Brew Buddy." The coffee is just as good as french pressing it; it's easier (& easy) to clean; and it's a two-fer... brews coffee and my loose-leaf tea (never liked the tea balls for individual tea). I've never tried the pour over method of coffee making, but, of course, similar mechanism (without having to bother with paper filters).

Not a coffee connoisseur, but sometimes when I'm in the mood to pretend that I am... I use my manual burr coffee grinder, 'feed' my Brew Buddy, 'bloom' the coffee grounds with 195-degree water, and, when properly bloomed, slowly (swirly) pour water into the grounds. My 'fireplace-in-a-mug' (You know, that *comforting* feeling of cupping the mug in your hands & taking in the aroma of freshly brewed coffee!) is ready to drink... or not, depending on the strength of the coffee I want at that moment.

Highly recommend this Brew Buddy!

No bread, is what we thought until we found Simple Mills.Well let me say right now the diet has worked-She has gone from daily nausea to none. And Simple Mills Artisan Bread Mix has been a Godsend!

text:
I have used Great River Organic Flour for several months now and I am really happy with it. I make all my own bread and with four kids we eat plenty of it! I love that this is organic and GMO free. The quality is great, also when I ran out of this and went back to the other stuff in the grocery store I could really tell the difference in the consistency my bread and other baked goods came out. I would suggest this to anyone looking for a good whole wheat baking flour.

*UPDATE: I had changed my order from just standard Whole Wheat Flour to Whole Wheat Pastry Flour not really knowing what a difference it would make. My mistake, and I reviewed the Pastry flour instead of the standard whole wheat flour. THE DIFFERENCE between the two IS HUGE and NOT good. Pastry flour does not a good loaf of bread make. Cookies= awesome, waffles= great, but a nice loaf of yeast bread it will fall to pieces. IF you want it for bread making just buy the standard whole wheat flour, or better yet search out Bread Flour you will be glad you did.

text:
These actually taste pretty good...but, be warned, they are sweet, sweet, sweet and then some. The caramel flavor is better, IMO, than the chocolate ones and they are nice and soft and chewy. The only thing is that the caramel on the bar doesn't taste like real caramel so much, but I do generally enjoy the flavor, anyway.

However, despite the idea that these are good for you because of the fiber, these might not be the best snack food because of the sugar. Still, if you do want to eat something snackish and want to get something good out of it (rather than just eating a candy bar) and aren't watching your sugar carbs, at least these do have the fiber to commend them. Just don't plan on using these as your only source of fiber.

I generally buy these and a variety of other bars (some fiber and some protein) to take camping or on trips. They travel pretty good and don't get too mushy.

text:
This is a decent tea that is priced well for how many bags you get ($14.99/32 bags). I like that it is compostable- the envelopes and tea bags are made of paper and the string is glued on rather than stapled.

That being said, I'm torn on the flavor. It's very weak when brewed as instructed. I would recommend tossing in two tea bags per cup or brewing longer if you prefer darker tea. It's also much sweeter than I expected, which unfortunately covered up most of the tea flavor itself.

Overall, if you tend to sweeten your tea or prefer a milder flavor, this is a good deal for decent tea. However, I would recommend skipping this one if you do not like sweetened tea and prefer a stronger flavor.

title: Not really tea but not bad
text:
I suffered a stroke about a year ago (I'm considered a "young" stroke survivor, lucky me!), and my sense of taste was damaged. I've been looking for drinks I can actually taste, as I've been drinking a lot of water. So, I was interested in trying this flavored drink.

First off, I can taste this drink, which is a plus. It doesn't really taste like tea ... more like lemonade when mixed, and that's not a bad thing. It's easy to mix; pour one tablespoon into a glass of hot water and stir; that's it. The mixture more comes out as a gel, than a liquid; this probably is because it's thickened, and it dissolves well when stirred, so its not a problem. You get a bit of pulp with your drink; I like pulp, but I mention it in case you don't. You need to refrigerate the mix after opening.

Overall, this is a good drink/mix. Just know that it tastes more like lemonade than lemon tea. Four stars.

title: Perfect for the office
text:
I really like honey in general and have purchased several brands and several local varieties of it. This honey in particular is the first time I’ve tried the creamy spreadable form and it definitely has a great use that I did not foresee.

Not only is the flavor really good, but the consistency has made it perfect for my office environment where I only use it in hot tea. It is leaps and bounds cleaner and easier to use. No drips to worry about. No glued on lid. No sticky jar. I scoop it out with a spoon and it sticks to it like peanut butter. It melts very easily in hot tea with zero taste difference to other varieties.

The texture is not off-putting to me at all. I think I could enjoy this on toast just as much as any liquid honey. It tastes great. It’s simply a good quality honey with a slightly firmer texture until it warms up as you eat it.

title: Low FODMAP friendly, Great Taste, But Easily Broken
text:
These have a good taste and texture. So much that my husband was eating them and he hates “pretend” foods. The flavor is buttery and reminds me of club crackers.

They are not very sturdy. There are usually quite a few smaller pieces in the packet and they break very easily. I haven’t tried spreading anything on them. (For a sturdier saltine type cracker, try to find Good Graces. I find that brand at my grocery store here in the Midwest.

They are also working well on my first phase of the Low FODMAP program. I seem to be super sensitive to things and most gluten free products have tapioca flour high on the list. I think that doesn’t work for me. Anyway, if you’re doing the elimination phase of Low FODMAP, you might give them a try. (They’ve been tested at Monash University and are certified Low FODMAP.)

title: Your basic Golden Milk
text:
The instructions didn't say how much milk to dissolve it in. So I used a cup of almond milk, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, and 1 tsp of this powder. It turned out well!

It's your basic golden milk mix. It does have chilies in it, which I thought would be interesting, but aside from a little extra earthiness there's no heat or pizazz.

If I hadn't had this one other Golden Milk that is absolutely awesome, I would think this is really excellent. It has all the essential ingredients of a Golden Milk mix. It does lack any sort of peppery punch that I'm used to in other mixes, even though it says it has that sort of thing in it. So if you want a less spicy one, this one is for you.

title: Nice Whole Blossoms... From Egypt
text:
I grow my own organic calendula flowers every single year on my Eco farm. It's not a difficult plant to grow. This brand is from Washington - USA. Why not support USA organic farmers? Because it cheaper to buy from overseas & ship back here. Very disappointing.

Aside from the whole US/Egypt thing, these are very nice whole blossoms. I grow mine for the petals to make anti-inflammatory teas. Calendula is a great for autoimmune disease. I also grow for it's use as a natural/organic plant based dye.

Aside from it's uses once harvested, it also attracts pollinators & is a very pretty flower to grow. It self sows easily. If you can, try growing your own. The blooms are harvested the entire growing season. The more you removed the flower heads, the more it will produce as it is trying very hard to produce seed. And produce seed it does! The seeds look to some like dried up bugs or worms. If you see anything like this in your dried calendula blossoms, please don't panic - plant it!

title: Liquid is not the same as semi solid
text: [[VIDEOID:dec20d9dd540355bda6d0a80fc054b8d]] I have bought and used beef tallow several times in my life. The product can be semisoft like a shortening such as Crisco but not grainy and liquidy. The product that I received from this company was both grainy and liquidy. When I brought my concerns up to the company, they said to heat the product and 98% of their customers. Who do this are satisfied. Heating the product slowly and stirring Will get out the rest of the liquid that is in the product. So, essentially of course those customers would be satisfied because the liquidliness went away. This process is finishing the preparation of the Tallow. If I am paying for a jar of tallow I expect that that jar be prepared fully and me not have to continue cooking it, making it where I'm getting less product for my money. They will say and continue to say that they prepared it according to what they should have. In the end, liquid is not the same as semisoft. They may ship different batches to different people and it may be fully prepared but mine was not. I live in a climate that during this time of year it does not get over 65 to 70°. They claimed that the reason it was liquid was because it got hot on the trucks. It has a high smoking point and melting point. Therefore it should still be solid after it sits on my counter a couple of days. This was not the case and they're only offered to fix their error in preparation. Was denying that they did it wrong and telling me that I could ship it back at my own expense and they would issue me a refund for what I paid for it. This is a lot like if I went to IKEA and bought a table to build and they didn't include the screws so I had to go out and buy the screws to finish my table. The cooking process is just like this. It is finishing or me doing something to finish the product when I paid for a finished product. I hope this helps somebody they're horrible company to work with.

title: Very pleased - Kefir is easy to make
text: I have been using pro-biotics for years trying to battle digestive  and skin issues. So far no luck or improvement in the conditions, despite good eating habits.  I have spent a lot of money on those pills and don't even know if they contained any live cuItures when I consumed them.  After reading about Kefir and not finding a ready made product that impressed me,  because of all the added sugar and the high price, I decided  to make my own.  That way I know what is in it and it will be fresh. I received my Kefir grains about a week ago and they are already producing good Kefir and appear to be growing.  They arrived in a small plastic container and looked very healthy, just like a piece of  fresh cauliflower.  The seller had also included a flyer with information about activating the grains which was very helpful.  I immediately placed the grains into a glass mason jar added  approx 3/4 cup of milk, covered the jar with a small piece of cloth, held in place by a rubber band, left it sit on the kitchen counter and let them do their thing.  The first few batches separated into whey and curds and I have since figured out, that, since I live in Florida and it is very warm (my house stays around 78-80 degrees) the grains don't need 24 hours to ferment. There are lots of videos on YouTube with helpful information about making Kefir.  Yesterday I made a batch with  1 1/2 cups of milk and after approx 18 hrs I noticed a sign of  slight separation and whey at the bottom of the jar and decided to remove the grains at that point. Removal is easy.  Just pour the contents through a plastic strainer, use a wooden or plastic spoon to gently  stir the contents through the mesh until only the Kefir grains are left behind. Use the grains to start your next batch of Kefir, or place them into a small jar, cover with fresh milk and keep in the  refrigerator until you are ready to make more Kefir.  The Kefir from this batch was very good and I plan on making many more batches.  The process could not be any easier..  Definitely a good product and if all goes well these grains will continue to thrive and multiply and hopefully I will notice results in my digestive tract and overall health with regular use of homemade Kefir.

title: Tasty and effective, just needs a finish touch with packaging
text:
I've used a number of other hydration mixes like this, which contain sugar and minerals that are supposed to deliver hydration to your body much faster than plain water. They're usually a tastier version that you used to see in first aid kits.
I found this product to work well and taste good. The packets are well designed, with perforations for easy opening. Each stick is full of a lot of mix, consistent with the big brands I've tried. The mix is very finely ground, which is nice for mixing but does lead to some initial challenges. In a water bottle or blender bottle, it will mix easily with a few shakes. In a glass with a spoon, it takes a little more work, but it still mixes.
The flavor of this mix is a bit unusual, but it's good. I get the grape flavor, but I also picked up a really floral character to it. It was like a lavender grape or something like that. After the initial surprise, though, I found it was good. The drink went down easy and didn't leave much of an aftertaste. The technology requires sugar to aid in hydration, but it wasn't overly sweet. This would be an easy drink for during or after an athletic endeavor, since it doesn't leave a cloyingly sweet taste in your mouth.
I know that a lot of early products are not a finished product, and the zip lock bag these came in was no exception. It's not uncommon to review new products like this, so I wasn't surprised, and frankly I usually keep my drink sticks in bags like this so I can grab what I want quickly and go.
Overall, I'm happy with these hydration sticks.

title: Antioxidant Refresher
text:
****
This Pomegranate Green Tea from Yogi Tea is an antioxidant refresher. It's an all natural tea made from organic green tea leaf, organic hibiscus flowers, organic flavors, organic peppermint leaf, pomegranate juice powder, stevia leaf, organic burdock root, and organic dandelion root. The taste is mild, only very slightly tasting of pomegranate, tasting mostly just of green tea, with a very pleasant aroma; in fact, it's so mild, that I would definitely use two tea bags and brew it for the full six minutes. It does not get bitter. Unless you enjoy very mild tea, you should plan on getting fewer cups of tea from the box. For this reason I gave this tea only four stars.

I am definitely impressed with this tea and with Yogi Teas in general. Pomegranate Green Tea comes with an expiration date (a good thing, because it's not full of preservatives, plus you can tell if it is fresh). Yogi Tea seems to be another company (like Numi, Aspen, Traditional Medicinals) that values sustainable and healthy practices. Their web site has a helpful glossary of tea ingredients and is beautifully designed, with info about each tea they make.

Yogi Tea writes this on the box about the tea's benefits: "Green Tea Pomegranate helps reinvigorate the body through the neutralization of harmful free radicals. Delicious Pomegranate provides this tea with a powerful dose of natural antioxidants and exciting fruit flavor. This cherished fruit contains polyphenols, chemical compounds that include Epigallo-catechin-3 gallate (EGCG), an antioxidant that is nearly 100 times more potent than vitamin C and 25 times more potent than vitamin E. A favorite of the Mediterranean peoples for centuries, Pomegranate has also been linked to nourishing the skin, supporting healthy cholesterol levels already in the normal range and promoting cardiovascular health. Like Pomegranate, Organic Green Tea also supplies polyphenols that help ward off free radicals. In fact, a single cup of Green Tea has been shown to provide greater antioxidant support than a serving of broccoli, spinach or strawberries. To further complement this healing formula, we've included the detoxifying qualities of Organic Burdock and Organic Dandelion, as well as the gentle essence of Organic Peppermint. Enjoy a cup of refreshing Green Tea Pomegranate and feel renewed with the benefits of nature's most powerful antioxidants."

There are no cautions or warnings on the box except the standard disclaimer that the tea is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.

Pomegranate Green Tea has contains approximately 30 mg of caffeine per tea bag, which is just one third of what is normally found in an 8 oz cup of coffee.

I really like this tea, and it is very health-promoting. Recommended.
****

title: The smell takes some getting used to
text:
If you've never had or smelled real truffle before - you will be a bit taken aback. The entire gift box - all three tins, in their packaging - smells of the truffle. That's despite the tight cork lids on all three tins.

If you can get over that initial olfactory impression, these are quite nice! Each type of salt has visible pieces of herbs, truffles, and spices, respectively. As mentioned before, each tin has a tight-fitting cork lid that helps keep the salt fresh and prevent it from clumping too much.

I recommend using a small, clean spoon to ladle out exactly how much you want, especially if you're thinking about sprinkling some over a piping hot dish. Because these are more like finishing salts, for flavor and texture - to be sprinkled over the food right before it's eaten on the plate. And if you don't use a spoon and instead just pour, the steam from the food will defeat the purpose of having such nice cork lids.

I think these are a little too fancy for ordinary personal use - French sea salt with real French herbs, truffles, and peppers! At about $25 for the 3 tins! But it would make a delightful gift for culinary friends.

title: has the potential to make you a Baking Star
text:
i buy this from sam's club and have been using it for several years now. i consider myself an experienced home baker - i have even cooked brownies from scratch. when i used as directed, i noticed it seemed undercooked. i would even leave it in a bit longer. i realize that brownie recipes tend to err on the fudgy side, meaning that you can't always rely on the "toothpick" test to determine when it is ready to be removed from the oven. if you want a more "baked" but not dry yet rich tasting, here is how i modified the directions: substitute melted unsalted real butter for the oil, add 1 extra egg (whatever size batch you decide to use), and add 1/2 to 1 teaspoon of almond extract. i really whip the eggs before adding in the other wet ingredients. i use a ceramic corning ware pan for baking and cook it for the number of minutes on the upper end of the range suggested in the directions. also, let it COMPLETELY COOL before serving. this will allow the dough to set so that you do not end up with something resembling uncooked batter in the middle. if you cook it for the number of minutes suggested, it will wind up being fully cooked.

i get so many compliments when i do it this way! i think the extra egg gives it more "lift" and richness and still be fudgy enough at the same time.

If you're looking for a totally all natural sweetener just buy a lb of dates in the veggies section of your store, cut them in half and take out the pits/stems, soak them in like a cup of water over night (covered well over) then blend them in your blender/food processor. It will make a thick paste that you can store in a jar/container in your fridge for a couple weeks.  I know that may sound like more trouble, but really? You'd be waiting for these things in the mail and when they arrive, I know you'd be dissapointed. Dates are chemical/sugar free, all natural and totally sweet so they DO work in many recipes and even coffee/tea.  Dates, now, after trying many, many sweeteners ( I have a serious sweet tooth) are the ONLY thing I will endorse that is remotely safe for your body and also tastes GREAT.  Peace, hope this helps...

title: These are NOT good cocktails
text:
I have a friend who owns a Bartesian and has at least a hundred drink pods on hand. Last night at her house I had three: a Negroni, an Old Fashioned, and a Margarita. Each of these drinks was barely recognizable and far below the low level found in bars and restaurants. (There are bars that make these right, but not many.) Trust me. Seriously terrible drinks! Don’t waste your money.

It isn’t hard to make excellent cocktails, and it’s fun to learn how. Ten years ago, a girlfriend and I bought some good books on the topic and bookmarked the ones we wanted to try. We “kept” only the drinks we both gave five stars. Some recipes weren’t quite there, and for those, we experimented until they were just right. We used only highly rated top shelf liquor. NO mixes like margarita mix or whisky sour mix. We made our own simple syrup with cane sugar and water. We used the best seltzer or tonic we could find. We used fresh, just squeezed fruit juices.

For example:
Espresso Cocktail: 1 oz Kahlua, 1 oz Vodka, 1 oz fresh espresso. Rim glass with brown sugar (Karo on the rim helps it stick).
Gimlet: 2 oz gin or vodka, 1 1/2 oz Rose’s lime juice (which has sugar in it)
Gin and Tonic: 2 oz gin (preferably Tanqueray #10), 3 oz tonic (Q-Tonic), lime wedge, squeezed
Last Word (superb!): 1 oz gin, 1 oz green Chartreuse, 1 oz Luxardo Marie chino liquor, 1 oz lime juice, 1 lime wheel, shake with ice and strain
Margarita: 2 oz Patron Silver Tequila, 1 oz Patron Citronge or Cointreau, 3/4 oz lime juice, 1/8 oz simple syrup, shake with ice and strain, serve up or on the roxks
Martini: 2 1/2 oz of gin (#10), 1/2 oz dry vermouth (ideally Carpano Antico Classico), stir or shake very well with ice.
Mojito: 2 oz light rum, 1 oz lime juice, 2 tsp sugar, 4-6 sprite of long leaf mint. Put mints then sugar, and half an oz of seltzer in glass and muddle lightly. Add lime and rum, stir, add ice, then add only 1/2 oz of soda.
Whisky Sour: 2 oz Jack Daniels, 3/4 oz simple syrup, 1 oz lemon juice, shake with ice and strain. (As with all of these, measure! Be exact!

I guess I'd speculate that instead of elevating you, they keep you at a constant level, whatever level you happen to be at one you drink one. If you're already tired, IDK how much these would work.

Keep in mind the following after reading the above: I have, in my 30 years on this planet, taken far more caffeine than is recommended. I consider myself very tolerant of its affects now. title: Just a normal dude trying us matcha to make drinks
text:
I bought the matcha to mix with milk to make a nice dessert drink.
Matcha has a nice mild taste. There is a mild bitterness from the matcha.

I do find that I needed about a tablespoon of the match in my drink before I could distinctly taste it, otherwise I would mostly just taste the milk.

Matcha with water was ok. It just tasted like tea.

Mixing was kind of an issue. I think the best way to mix it is to strain it, pass it through a sift otherwise it clumps up as soon as it mixes. I haven't been able to successfully mix the matcha well without having to stir for a really long period.

Overall the taste is nice, just have to take some time mixing it.

title: Bean soup as it should be
text:
I have never had such delicious bean soup. I wish I had known about Bob's Red Mill's bean soup seasoning years ago, I would have had many more delicious bean meals.

The mixture is complex, balanced, and delightful but be aware that the red pepper grows very spicy as the soup ages. I use half-packets now instead of whole packets, but those who love spice will probably want the entire packet.

I can imagine other uses for this spice: Texas-style chili (no beans, no tomatoes, only meat and the spice); cornbread; meatloaf; spicy potato soup; spicy corn spoonbread, fried spicy potato patties, breading for fish and chicken, in beef and pork mardinade, in biscuits and other small breads, and for the adventurous, even in chocolate cake!

title: #1 Mixer
text:
Decided to conduct a small taste test.
The contestants were(from left to right)
Cryptoblast
Monster
Nerd Focus
Red Bull
After some sips of each, Cryptoblast came in close with Red Bull but Cryptoblast finished 1st place.

4.Monster tasted like bitter bull piss(I’m not sure how as it had the most sugar yet tasted the worst out of the bunch)
3.Nerd tasted like flat Mountain Dew(loved the detailed nutrition facts though)
2.Red Bull was second in taste but the carbonation was the ideal amount and tasted the way I thought a typical energy drink would.
1. Cryptoblast had the most sophisticated design but could be brighter shades of purple as when next to the other cans it looks a little dull/dark (less eye catching). Out of the bunch Cryptoblast was the most flavorful. However, there could be a litttttle more carbonation but the drink would be the perfect mixer for adult beverages.

But yeah, with that being said, I truly feel Cryptoblast could be up to par with Red Bull. The other brands really didn’t stand a chance(taste wise) next to those two.

I’m giving 4 stars because of the way Amazon chose to wrangle the box during shipping and put stickers all over mine. Probably needs some sort of fragile label and handling.
Upon opening the box the inner casing that separates the 3 drinks was broken but luckily the box was very strong as the drinks were in mint condition.
Another reason for the 4 stars is the can wasn’t as smooth as the other cans upon drinking from it.

A-/B+ from me. Damn near perfect!
-just being honest-

title: It works, but if you do the math... You're saving almost nothing.
text:
These things are really easy to use. Just clean off the old foil, clean out the ground and you're ready to start. It takes 30 seconds to refill them after you get the hang of it. But here's the kicker - If you spend $12/pound for Starbucks coffee, you're going to get about 15 pods per pound. That's about .80/pod + the cost of this gizmo.

So you're saving almost nothing.

But I solved this - I got two pound of BJ's Guatemalan blend for $9.99 and ground it fine. It's nothing like the Nespresso pods - it takes like cheap coffee even after fine grind, tamping it in, adding a little extra coffee.

So keep the Nespresso pods for "special occasions" and use the refills when you need 100mg of caffeine from unknown sources.

title: Great gum
text:
This gum's flavor is more akin to orange, or basically a sweet citrus taste. I chew a piece when I work out or play any type of sport, and it pastes at least 40 minutes to keep my mouth feeling refreshed. Granted, the taste is obviously not as intense after the first 10 minutes or so. A few added bonus is that unlike some other gum like Extra, the consistency of this gum doesn't degrade down to a nasty mush when your mouth's temperature gets very high. In addition, even when the fruity taste is mostly gone, there is no weird or bitter taste either.

Lastly, I'm not sure if vitamin b6 and b12 in this gum actually does anything, but for those who swear by these 2 vitamins for energy boost, they can't hurt.

title: Best Non Sugar Sweetener Ever!!
text:
I've been a Type 1 diabetic for a long time.
At the beginning there was only Saccharin and while terrible got us by.
Drinks like Tab and Pepsi Light were a disappointing.

I can remember the day when Diet Coke showed up with Aspartame in it.
This proved that life with T1D would be okay.
Finally, drinks that tasted close to the original.
After some time, this even became the preferred taste.
Coke Zero always tastes heavy and to close to the sweetened version.
Aspartame was a big deal!

Later on I started moving to natural sweeteners.
Stevia which honestly reminds me of Saccharin was not good.
We had used Monk Fruit a few time in baking and started to get it in packets.
It was interesting in coffee but still not right.
Later, I discovered mixing packets of Stevia and Monk fruit yielded good results.

After I saw Stevia and Monk fruit being premixed by Whole Earth I wanted to give it a try.
I will tell you, IMHO this is as good as any Aspartame packet and a natural product.
This is a great non sugar sweetener!

Thank you Whole Earth! ;)

title: red dye #40
text:
I was impressed with the description: spring water flavored with real juice with added antioxidents - sounds good and natural but far from it. From the description I thought I would be getting it regularly and signed up for repeat delivery.
I almost forgot to cancel that!
The worst is it has the most dangerous of all dyes, #40. My grandson now 13 had his first red dye #40 when he was 2 years old - he went from a normal playful 2 year old to a demon litterally climbing the walls. It lasted several hours. Unfortunately relatives forgot about hearing about that episode (and since they didn't witness it that was easy to forget - no one witnessing it will Ever forget) and red dye demon child emerged again. Research shows some children are more susceptible than others.
I want Black Rasberry flavored - not colored to look like the flavor.
The second issue is the sucralose. The Center for Science in the Public Interest dropped sucralose from a determination of Safe to one of Caution in June of 2013. Also research with obese individuals shows that sucralose negatively affects insuline release.
I will not be buying products from this company again.

title: Like restaurant quality noodles
text:
I was skeptical but lots of people called it the best noodles in the world. Seasoning came in two packets. First was a curry paste with some chili oil. Don't be fooled by it being labeled a curry. It has a spiced taste but the curry is very mild as it should be if you're expected to treat it like noodles in soup. No one in their right mind would shovel spoonfuls of pure curry into their mouth. This is a curry flavored broth.

Second was hydrated coconut milk to give it the curry a creamy taste. The noodles once cooked fully do not resemble any instant noodle texture you have had. It's quite similar to the fat egg noodles typically served with this kind of dish in Asian restaurants. Very chewy and dense. Make sure to cook them fully like pasta till they are al dente.

I grew up with curry laksa which is pretty similar to this and I tell you I could not believe this was instant noodles. Add some fixings like fried bean curd, some protein and green beans and you wouldn't be able to tell the difference much.

Just wow. It really blew my mind.

title: Cooking oil
text:
This is a refined vegetable oil made of avocados. The ingredients are: avocado oil. The labels suggests that 1 serving is 1 Tbs, and that there are 24 servings per container. One serving provides 120 calories, 14 g of fat, 0 g of carbs and 0 g of protein. The label says the product is certified USDA organic. The oil is steam refined. The oil is packaged in foil bags with plastic lids. It is a product of Mexico.

I find this oil works fine for cooking. Because the oil is refined, it doesn’t have the strong avocado flavor that I look for in a salad oil. The bags compact to a very small size when empty. Overall, this is a decent choice for vegetable cooking oil.

They also smell artificially, which interferes with the perception of their taste... although I can't tell if they have any taste, besides some sweetness. Where did orange, ginger, and chocolate go?

It's also irritating that the manufacturer doesn't talk about the ingredients in a simple and straightforward manner. Why say "low glycemic monosaccharide" and "low glycemic fruit concentrate"? title: 5 pounds of Organic Ceylon Cinnamon for the trash can
text:
I've been using Organic Ceylon cinnamon for several years for health reasons. I know how Ceylon cinnamon is supposed to look, smell and taste like. I have ordered the 1 lb package from Naturevibe Botanicals before and was very happy with the product. I was excited to see that Naturevibe offered 5 packs of 1 lb for a substantial discount. When I opened the first bag, I immediately noticed that the cinnamon powder looked pale. I smelled the bag and noticed that it only had a faint cinnamon smell. When I tasted it, I came to realize that this is NOT the same powder that I've received from this company before. I could barely taste any cinnamon. The spicy-sweet flavor I've come to expect from Organic Ceylon cinnamon was missing. The powder has a strange flavor with a subtle hint of cinnamon
and a bitter aftertaste. I gave a sample to my wife and she immediately asked "What is this???". Needless to say, I am extremely disappointed with this product and would not recommend it to anyone. I am now stuck with 5 pounds of worthless "cinnamon". I don't know what to think of this powder. Is it a fake cinnamon, a stale or inferior product? I've tried to return the product but it is "NOT ELIGIBLE FOR RETURN". 5 pounds of mystery cinnamon will now wind up in the trash can.

title: I love some, can't stomach others.
text:
Alright, overall this was a good value. I liked several of the flavors and absolutely hated others. Here's a rundown of my thoughts on each flavor:

Zen: The teabag smelled as if the tea would be nasty, but it was surprisingly okay. It tasted like a mild form of green tea, with a hint of lemon. Thumbs up for Zen.

Calm: This tea is basically chamomile, it tastes really good. It relaxes me.

Passion: My favorite tea, by far. It tastes like some kind of berry drink, almost like fruit punch. I was really shocked with the flavor, it's delicious.

China green tips: Awful. This tastes like grass, I mean it is really awful. My least favorite tea in the box.

Earl grey: Umm, I have never had earl grey tea before, and TAZO did not give me a good first impression. Before brewing, the teabag smelled really good, like black licorice really. However when I took a sip I couldn't stand the taste. I might try another brand of earl grey, I wanted to like it.

Awake: A tasty blend of black teas, what can I say. It is a little bitter if you brew the full 5 minutes, I suggest doing just 3 minutes of steeping time.

Chai: Well, chai is chai, it tasted good. Chai tea lattes have always been my favorite drink at Starbucks, this tea is great.

title: Just as good as 7-11
text:
I usually like my hot chocolate and certain foods/beverages made with milk to have a richer/creamier taste. But with the Pumpkin Spice Latte, it calls for hot water and I've tried it with both, it tastes great with just hot water.
The Pumpkin Spice has a flavor more subtle than pumpkin pie does. It has a lot of flavor without being sweet or overpowering. It has the taste of pumpkin, cinnamon, nutmeg and subtle coffee flavor. I like the mix, you can measure it to taste and it does taste just like the flavor you get at 7-11. With the price and shipping and handling, it still comes out cheaper than going to the store. I like being able to make a little or a lot and each time it's perfect. For a 16 ounce i use 1/4 cup (about 6 heaping teaspoons) and it comes out perfect. The standard is 12 ounces with 3 heaping teaspoons, then add a little more at a time until you get it to how you like it.

title: Not very good
text:
Some things should have never gotten past the focus group and this is one of them. It needs much more work in the test kitchen.

Comparing with a typical box of mac and cheese, by volume the Cheetos pasta spirals are about 50% less. They also break easily and tear into stringy pasta bits after cooking.

The cheese sauce packet doesn't have much in it. The directions also have you add roughly half the butter of a competing mac and cheese product. With the small cheese packet and milk you end up with a runny and watery cheese goo in the bottom of the bowl and not mixed with the pasta. The flavor is a bit stale, similar to a bag of Cheetos that was left open for a few weeks.

Can you eat it? Yes, but not very enjoyable.

It had promise but it needs more pasta and more creamy sauce to compete with other products.

Almond milk was easy to make.  We just put them in the Nutribullet or you could use a blender and add 4 times as much water and blend then use a nut milk bag or cheese cloth to strain the almond milk out and then you can drink the milk and use the almond meal for flour if you put it in the oven on a baking sheet at a lower temperature.

text:
I saw a bag of this just tonight at a local store that's good at stocking International and Foodie favorites that aren't so easy to find, and, oh my God, I swear this was love at first bite!

The lemon flavor here is the prevalent one when the candy first hits your palate, if you opt to bite down and chew these up. Just after that initial burst of lemon flavor, the ginger works its way through a rather woodsy flavor, so you get the pleasure of lemon segueing into ginger, with a final spicy ginger bite at the end. The sanding sugar adds just enough sweetness and great crunchy texture to a soft, delicious gummy that is my ABSOLUTE favorite gummy that I've EVER had the pleasure of eating! I'm not a fan of overly sweet candies (friends tease me because I've been known to shave 3/4 of the chocolate off of regular Snickers bars, since they're too sweet for me), and these are absolutely PERFECT!

Dang! Send me five 12 pack boxes of this stuff STAT!!! SO good!!! If you're a lover of ginger, and already know the deliciousness that comes with pairing ginger with lemon, don't wait to get your hands on this candy - it's SO what you're looking for!!! YUMMY!!!

title: Not Doing It For Me And Can't Return.... SAD
text:
Well I had to drastically reduce caffeine for medical reasons and I LOVE my coffee. I swear I've been served decaf in restaurants by mistake and not noticed right away, but whenever I brew a pot at home it's undrinkable. This is coming from drinking several cups of Starbucks whole bean freshly ground Pike's Place, which is high in both caffeine and IMHO flavor. I decided to get some decent decaf so that I could still have a cup or two in the mornings, enjoy the taste and ritual even if I can't have the "real stuff". I know it won't *feel* the same, but is it too much to ask that it just taste like coffee and not brown water? I didn't like the Starbucks decaf beans, so I googled best decaf and found an article that said "There's no inherent reason decaffeinated coffee should taste bad", and I thought DING DING DING! That's exactly what I was wondering, is there a bloody reason decaf can't taste remotely like coffee? So I got to the point of the article that mentioned the best tasting decaf beans. The #1 was a small specialty bean that cost $30 for a small bag plus S&H. No thanks! The #2 was this stuff, $17 for huge 2 lb bag here on Amazon. And it had great reveiews, almost a 5 star average! It must be good!

Well, maybe I'm the biggest snob on the planet, but it wasn't good. I brewed to specifications and it tasted like sad brown water. Then I experimented with putting more grounds in for a stronger taste. Meh, it just never tasted right. It boasts low acidity, maybe acidity is what makes coffee taste and feel in the mouth like coffee? I really don't know, all I know is this stuff is just sitting in my cupboard now, it feels like a huge waste. If I hate something I buy on Amazon I usually send it back, but coffee isn't a pair of shoes, you're not allowed to return it. Even at Whole Foods if you hate a product they'll give your money back.

Later someone mentioned that Sprouts had decent organic coffee beans in bulk section. Dammit, should have tried that first because I could buy just enough beans for one pot for fifty cents, and I would have discovered their beans are better than this stuff.

Confused why this product is rated so high. Had to let you know in case you're in the same boat and I could stop you from wasting your money too.

title: Great Product, but price has gotten too high
text:
I've been a Monster drinker for over a decade, and I've always bought in bulk. In the good ole early days of amazon I was happy to get 24 packs at nearly the same price as a 24 pack at one of the big-box membership stores, and it saved me a trip. After those prices slowly crept up I was able to get it back down to normal with Subscribe and Save. Then out of nowhere the subscribe and save canceled the 24 pack, and I was able to replace with a 20 pack for nearly the same price. Granted, by this point I'm paying about the same for a 20 pack (with subscribe and save discount) as the other stores have 24 packs but it's still less than normal price at the gas station and saves the trip out. Fast forward to today, and after nearly a decade of ordering on Amazon I'm finally calling it quits. Even with the 15% subscribe and save discount, this item has gotten more expensive than what I typically pick them up for at the gas station. It's much more than what i get them at the big-box membership, and even more than they are sold for in 4 and 10 packs at the grocery store. It's a sad day to come to realization that your old pal Amazon has let you down on pricing. You either die a hero or live long enough to become the villain.

The Monster is great, the price is terrible. Look elsewhere.

title: Rich Flavor, Super Fresh, Ultra Smooth - Dr. Mojo Medicine
text:
I have been ordering MOJO delivered to my front door since 2018, prior to that, I was a daily customer in their store and purchased my bean on-site. Mojo is the only coffee I buy. I even grind my own coffee and take it to work now that I left Chicago. Don't buy the stale coffee sitting on the shelf at the grocery store, pick up MOJO and never have regrets about how fresh these beans are. On the whole, DMM (Dr. Mojo's Medicine) is hands down my go-to favorite (also what I ordered in this transaction, although it seems to show as 12oz of Feelgood, it was 5lb of DMM), but I have enjoyed the Injection and Feelgood blends as well as several of their single-origin coffees. I always return back to DMM. It is just so smooth with just a touch of sweetness in the blend that I enjoy it immensely just black and sometimes with 3 oz of steamed milk.

A little history, back in 2017, Mojo opened up a coffee shop in my building in downtown Chicago across from the Willis Tower. They had a soft opening for the tenants of the building and offered small samples of their coffee drinks. At the time, I was caffeine-free but decided one drink couldn't hurt. Well... one drink turned into a weekly visit (typically on Fridays), then into multiple visits during the week, then nearly daily. I recall asking if I could just purchase the beans so I could enjoy Mojo coffee at home on the weekends and they said "absolutely, but we aren't set up for that right now, so the bags will just be plain without labels". I didn't care. I have since moved out of state, and now they send my coffee to my house. I miss the days of drinking a Flat White in the shop, but I still enjoy my Mojo every day!

So we decided to order the "full count" of 100 to give them a try again and I would say my initial "3" moves to a strong "4" now as that light, blonde type body still exists in a good way to start your day.

title: Strange odor
text:
This product has a very strange odor to it. The odor reminds me of wet cat food, something I haven't smelled in decades. It is not nearly as strong as an open can of cat food, and it also mostly dissipates during cooking. Unfortunately, if you have a very acute sense of smell, it is always there in the background and ultimately makes the product unpalatable to me. I won't rule out the possibility that This may be one of those foods that triggers different reactions in people based upon genetics like cilantro.

I ate it in the form of a burger with a very strongly flavored topping made from ketchup, mayonnaise, mustard, chopped cherry peppers, and a beet-cabbage sauerkraut. That almost completely masked the strange odor, which resulted in a pretty enjoyable burger at the time. That being said, I shouldn't have to drown my food and strong flavors to mask some thing that is offensive about it.

I also crumbled up some and sautéed it like ground beef to use as a taco filling. Even though I mixed it with a fairly strongly flavored spicy chipotle salsa, the smell was still readily apparent. My stomach also feels a little bit queasy after eating it, and now that I think about it, my stomach was a bit off from the burger, as well. This is not normal for me.

I might think that I have gotten a bad package, but I have read about the strange cat foot odor in several other places before coming here to write this review. It is possible what we were all referring to is a batch that was spoiled. Oh well. I was hopeful but will probably be reluctant to try this particular variety again.

I will say that I very much enjoyed their Italian sausage but will not continue to buy that, either. That is because I suspect that underneath all of these strongly flavored spices I would find the same cat food odor.

title: I don't have tons of food like some do
text: This is my review for Freeze-dried Fruit 120 serving Sample Pack by Nutristore.  I never lived in a disaster area, but if it ever happens I want to be prepared. I don't have tons of food like some do, but I am fairly confident I have enough to last my family 6 months or so.  My stash is mostly those prepackaged monthly buckets, rice, beans, wheats, and oatmeals... so I am lacking fruits and vegetables as they tend to be more expensive to buy and you get less than buying a bucket of rice or something. So I dont have a ton of them like the other stuff. So when I seen that I could review these for a discount, I was super excited. I decided to keep 2 of them for emergency purposes and open one of them for review. These come in sturdy number 10 cans and they are sealed just like any other can. I had no issues with shipping and they arrived dent free.  The bananas are 16.9 ounces, raspberries are 7 ounces, and the strawberries are 5.6 ounces. I opened the strawberries to sample the taste and I am pretty impressed. The strawberries taste exactly like the ones in Special K Cereal. They have a nice sweet strawberry taste to them. They are kind of addicting.  Unopened they will last for 25 years and the items that I recieved where recently manufactured. Personally, from what I tasted these are good. I have no complaints other than at full price they are kind of expensive and not really that much of a bargin and I know many companies that have been in the business for years you can find there stuff cheaper if you find it on sale or have a bulk membership club and shop online at there site.

30 (I counted) individually foil-wrapped strips about 2x4".

title: Easier on the body? Definitely tastes better than mined salt.
text:
I love this stuff! If you buy it, be careful until you get used to it. It has a stronger flavor than mined salt. To me, it just plain tastes better and you don't need as much. I'm a techie rather than having a medical background, so I don't understand the principle behind it, but sea salt is supposed to be easier for the body to process. My doctor seems to agree. My sodium counts went down pretty drastically after I switched to this salt. I didn't change anything else. I still eat chips and crackers and french fries and all those other salty foods that I'm not supposed to have - but just using this salt for my home use made a huge difference! I don't know if it is just that I don't use as much, or if "they" are right that this is easier for the body to process. I still use the same amounts that are called for in recipes, but I don't feel the need to add salt to the food on my plate because it doesn't taste like it needs it.

It does have a tendency to clump a bit, but I put some in a grinder and some in a regular shaker with a few kernels of rice - and they both work pretty well for those times when there is no recipe for what I am doing. If you shake it directly from the canister when the humidity is high, as it is here along the Gulf Coast, it will land in small splats instead of as individual grains, but this is a very minor thing compared to the flavor and benefits I have gotten from using this salt. If you are mixing something, like a sandwich-salad or a pasta salad, even that doesn't really matter.

title: These guys make baking fun!
text:
I am not sure that the red color is worth the difference in price, but I am new to Quinoa and I love it! I was using chia, which gave a very nice texture but the omega 3 oils may break down in baking. Now that I've found Quinoa, I still have lots of low temperature applications for chia.

I tried Quinoa flour, and it is a perfect replacement for wheat flour. The whole Quinoa seeds give a wonderful texture that no flour matches.

I started out using these Quinoa seeds with no prep. (They are pre-rinsed) My brownies were quite nice with the quinoa making something like a graham cracker crust, but the rest of the brownie, while tasty, wasn't very stable.

My last experiment was to simmer a cup of seeds for 20 minutes in 2 cups of water. The quinoa expanded to fill the water, and gave me a much lighter texture while vastly improving the consistency of the brownies overall.

Next off I'll make brownies with some quinoa flour plus some whole seeds. I'm looking forward to it.

Did I mention high protein, or gluten free, or low starch?

title: Extremely Inconsistent Product
text:
I've had this licorice product on subscribe & save delivered every month for about 6 months, and it is the most inconsistent delivery we get by far.

It seems to me like there are two formulations of this product - or something much weirder going on.

One version of the product is a very flavorful licorice but rock hard. The taste of this one is honestly the best tasting gluten-free licorice I've ever had. But it does require lightly gnawing on each individual piece for a few minutes to soften it up before it can be eaten.

The OTHER version of the product has a more edible texture - soft like traditional licorice although still lacking gluten-level chewiness - but tastes like wax with a very weak licorice flavor.

It seems to be total luck of the draw as to which batch we end up getting. So either quality control at the YumEarth factory is absolutely horrible, or they are delivering batches from two different suppliers with dramatically different formulations or perhaps handling (maybe some batches are getting superheated while sitting on a truck somewhere??).

Personally, I actually really love the super-chew strong-licorice version but I hate the wax-flavorless version so much that we're going to cancel the S&S. It's just not worth it to roll the dice on whether the product you receive is edible or not, especially in such large-quantity deliveries.

text:
This gelato mix is stupidly easy and convenient to make. The result is also very good gelato that's super creamy. It's a fair bit pricier than making it entirely from scratch, but the convenience really is huge. The 3 flavors you get here all knock it out of the park and leave you wanting seconds. It's also easy to add in anything else you want while preparing the mix or after it is served. The gelato is a great base that takes on additional flavors very easily.

I don't know if I'd recommend most people to stock up on a huge amount of this mix, but it's definitely nice to have a bit on hand. It's easy to make and also makes for a fun activity in the kitchen with a helper. I might reorder once.

title: Just needs a little doctoring
text:
I bought a box of this stuff a year ago and didn't like it very much, thinking it was too watery tasting. I complained about it and immediately got an email from the seller saying they were sorry I didn't care for the product and issuing a full refund.

Since then I've been experimenting with the product. At first I was setting the Keurig brewer for either a 10 or 12 ounce brew. I've since experimented with the 6 and 8 ounce settings and have found they, of course, produce a much fuller tasting hot chocolate. Additionally, I tried adding a teaspoon full of Hershey's Chocolate Syrup to the cup prior to running the product through the Keurig and stirring it in during the brief brewing process. While the added syrup isn't really necessary at the 6 ounce setting, I've found that adding it to the 8 ounce setting produces a steaming cup of hot chocolate that is very much to my liking. Today I placed a second order for a product that I did not like when I first tried it.

I'm glad I kept working with the product and gave it a second chance. This is a top notch seller and I'm happy to be able to give them my patronage.

title: MMM, Chicken in Water!
text:
I like Chicken. Sometimes I buy a raw whole one from the supermarket. Other times I buy it ready cooked so I can just nom down on it as soon as I get back. So, when I discovered that Hormel produce this product I was skeptical but intrigued. As I said I like chicken, and I am partial to water so surely I would like chicken preserved in water. When the tins arrived I had my can opener ready and waiting. I polished the tin off and felt I had satisfied my poultry needs for the day. To summarise, if you like chicken and you like water then you should have no problems with this product.

Also, don't forget that you get 12 tins. So if Bobby, Lisa Marie, Jayden, Kaitlin, Maggie, Ellie, Joanie, Ritchie, Phil and Laura all need feeding as well as yourself and Mummy/Daddy then that's your evening meal sorted in one pop - easy.

title: High Quality Beans, Delicious Complexity
text:
These are very high quality beans. I've never actually seen beans in such amazing shape- they're huge and virtually all the same size. They give you a nice even roast. The profile is quite intense on the cacao side, with a chocolatey sweetness and not very much fruit or 'brightness.' I over roasted it the first few times and didn't like it very much, but then I did a perfect light roast and really tasted the complexity of this wonderful bean.

I'm sure that blended with an African or a brighter Guatemalan would be quite delicious indeed. Overall very impressed with this supplier, they definitely care about the quality of their product.
